author: 100yenadmin
body:
## What does this PR do?

Allows a messaging plugin that removes its native callbacks during unload to opt into wiring its replacement registration against the same live client after a plugin reload.

Platform handlers are currently deduplicated by plugin name and factory qualified name. That protects legacy plugins from duplicate callbacks, but it also suppresses a replacement factory with the same qualified name. This change keeps that legacy behavior by default and adds an opaque registration generation only when the plugin explicitly passes `reload_safe=True`.

## Related Issue

No dedicated issue. This replaces the platform-handler reload slice from draft PR #121036.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/plugins.py`: add the default-off `reload_safe` registration flag, track platform-handler registrations through unload, and expose an opaque generation without changing the existing factory accessor shape.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py`: include the opaque generation in the live-client deduplication key only for opted-in registrations.
- `tests/gateway/test_platform_plugin_handlers.py`: prove opted-in unload/reload rewires exactly once and legacy qualified-name deduplication remains unchanged.

## How to Test

1. With the new tests applied to base `f7a861379f5ea06fdbf1e561c666958fc606602b`, run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_platform_plugin_handlers.py`: 13 passed and the two `reload_safe` tests failed because the opt-in did not exist.
2. On head `2f0e8478af3c0803f462d0824317a88171442e86`, run the same command: 15 passed.
3. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/gateway/test_late_plugin_rewire.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_ownership_ledger.py`: 32 passed.

## Checklist

### Code

- [ ] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — focused files passed; the full suite was not run
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6.2 arm64

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — the API docstring records the unload obligation
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A, no config change
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — Python-only registration bookkeeping
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A, no model tool change

## Screenshots / Logs

Not applicable. The evidence packet contains the raw red-on-base, green-on-head, and neighbour test outputs.

Disclosure: extracted from a larger product host change; the remaining pieces will follow as independent PRs.

What this PR does NOT change: other registration paths, tool registration, capability registries, configuration, or documentation beyond the platform-handler API docstring. It does not silently remove native callbacks; a plugin that opts into reload safety remains responsible for removing its prior callbacks during unload.

author: uchihathai105
body:
## Summary

Sends a push notification to your phone through [ntfy](https://ntfy.sh) when any coin's BUY / SELL / HOLD signal changes.

- **`report.py`**
  - The report now ends with a hidden `<!-- signals: {...} -->` marker.
  - When `NOTIFY_PATH` is set, the script reads the previous report (`PREV_REPORT_PATH`) and writes one line per changed coin, for example `BTC HOLD → BUY at $85,210.00 (score +3, 24h +2.40%)`.
  - Nothing is written when no signal changed, or when the previous report has no marker (such as the first run after this merges).
  - `NOTIFY_ALWAYS=true` includes every coin, for testing.
- **Workflow**
  - A new first step loads the current issue body as the previous report.
  - The last step posts the message to `https://ntfy.sh/$NTFY_TOPIC`: high priority, and tapping it opens the report issue.
  - If the `NTFY_TOPIC` secret is missing, the step logs a warning and skips the push instead of failing.
  - A manual run has a new **test_notification** checkbox that forces a push with the current signals.
- **README:** adds phone setup steps (install ntfy, subscribe to a topic, add the `NTFY_TOPIC` repository secret, run a test).

The branch briefly held a commit that called the Claude API from the workflow. It has been reverted, so the net diff is the notification change only. Claude-written notes will come from Claude Code routines instead, which need no API key.

## Testing

- **Offline:** the marker survives a round trip. The script sends nothing when signals are unchanged or when there is no previous marker, lists each changed coin as "old → new", and lists every coin when forced.
- **Live:** [run 36082283082](https://github.com/uchihathai105/cryptuch/actions/runs/36082283082) from this branch with the test checkbox ticked succeeded end to end. It hit the "secret not set" warning because the `NTFY_TOPIC` secret wasn't visible to Actions.

## After merging

Add the `NTFY_TOPIC` repository secret, then run the workflow by hand with **test_notification** ticked to confirm the push arrives.

body:
Tabs were built from local usage only, so quota-only providers (Copilot, Antigravity IDE) had no tab and Antigravity CLI/IDE could not share one. This follows macOS (`tabClients(present:quotaIds:)`, #349, #345/#348).

- **Rust**: `required_card_source` — Codex/Antigravity report `"unconfigured"` when their absence marker is the failure (was hard-coded `"oauth"`).
- **Interop**: `IsSetupPlaceholder`, `ConfiguredClientIds`.
- **Core (ClientRegistry)**: Antigravity group only; tab row = present ∪ configured, grouped; hidden/order folded on every read (settings never rewritten); every hidden-set consumer via `HiddenTabClients`; Overview selects present usage minus hidden, not the tab row.
- **App**: tab labels via `TabLabel`; a quota-only stored tab is not normalised to Overview before the quota lane arrives; Settings toggle/move canonicalise legacy `antigravity-cli` entries.

cargo test 425 passed; Core tests 1234 passed; WinUI built on the x64 host. Awaiting the user's check of the tab row.

author: techitechi0331-svg
alextitanium
body:
**Let one process run several `runner.run()` calls at once, and upstream the studio fal patch, so the studio can drop its bun patch on 0.3.0.**

| Problem | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| A second `run()` throws "A run is already active" ([api.ts#L63](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/4840782ac206d11d01ac86dabd96bbbb6579d35d/src/plugins/runner/api.ts#L63)). Two studio Render clicks wait for each other. | New config `runner.maxActiveRuns`, default 1 ([index.ts#L20](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/index.ts#L20)). Only an integer >= 1 is accepted, with no upper cap ([api.ts#L70](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/api.ts#L70)). |
| A caller cannot follow only its own run. | `run`/`resume` take `onStart(runId)` ([api.ts#L143](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/api.ts#L143)). Every `RunEvent` has `runId`. `events({ runId })` follows one run, `events()` follows all ([api.ts#L630](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/api.ts#L630)). |
| Two runs with the same item would pay twice. | A claim map lets one item per artifact key reach the provider ([claim.ts#L190](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/claim.ts#L190)). The other run waits and copies the result: reuse at cost 0, or the same flagged/failed verdict. |
| `resume()` with no id could pick a run that is already running. | `journal.latestResumableRun({ exclude })` skips the active runs ([journal/api.ts#L425](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/journal/api.ts#L425)). |
| fal "sensitive / likeness / nsfw / moderation" errors were not flagged ([client.ts#L216](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/4840782ac206d11d01ac86dabd96bbbb6579d35d/src/plugins/fal/client.ts#L216)). | They count as content policy ([client.ts#L93](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/fal/client.ts#L93)). |
| A 400 on the fal result or download was retried ([handler.ts#L294](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/4840782ac206d11d01ac86dabd96bbbb6579d35d/src/plugins/fal/video/handler.ts#L294)). | It is a terminal job verdict, like 422 ([handler.ts#L55](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/fal/video/handler.ts#L55)). |
| A retryable error that used up its attempts was copied to the other run as failed. A 503 can pass on a later try. | The claim settles `open`, so the other run tries itself ([pipeline.ts#L777](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/31b72fb20f8fed7ece20ba6b069c3866aba0a7f6/src/plugins/runner/pipeline.ts#L777)). 4xx and content policy are still copied. |
| `app.stop()` closed the journal under active runs. The run rejected instead of pausing. | Runner `onStop` pauses every active run and waits for it, before core plugins stop ([index.ts#L82](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/31b72fb20f8fed7ece20ba6b069c3866aba0a7f6/src/plugins/runner/index.ts#L82), [state.ts#L67](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/31b72fb20f8fed7ece20ba6b069c3866aba0a7f6/src/plugins/runner/state.ts#L67)). Jobs stay adoptable by `resume()`. |
| 7 fal models existed only in the studio patch. | `seedance-2.0-mini`, `seedance-2.0-mini-ref`, `seedance-2.0-ref`, `wan-3.0-ref`, `veo-3.1-fast`, `vidu-q3`, `vidu-q3-ref` with 20 prices ([models.ts#L661](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/fal/models.ts#L661), [prices.ts#L42](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/fal/prices.ts#L42)). |

```ts
// studio config after the upgrade
// now
// (no field: a second run throws)
// fix
createApp({ pluginConfigs: { runner: { maxActiveRuns: 4 } } });
await app.runner.run({ files }, { onStart: runId => follow(app.runner.events({ runId })) });
```

Limits lanes are not changed. They are global plugin state, so all runs share one lane budget.

## Before / After
| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runs at once | 1 | `maxActiveRuns`, default 1 |
| Default config, second `run()` | throws "A run is already active: <id>." | same first line |
| Same item in two runs | not possible | one submit |
| `RunEvent` | no `runId` | `runId` on every record |

## Breaking for code that builds `RunEvent` literals
| What | Migration |
| --- | --- |
| `RunEvent` variants carry `runId` | Add `runId` to literals, for example in test mocks. Readers need nothing. |

## Verification
| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint` | pass |
| `bun run test:coverage` | 986 pass, branches 91.54% |
| `bun run build`, `bun run validate` | pass |
| 2 runs at once, own totals | [test#L279](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L279) |
| 3rd run refused at cap 2; default refuses the 2nd | [test#L305](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L305), [test#L325](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L325) |
| 4 runs, lane concurrency 4: 4 in flight, peak 4 | [test#L367](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L367), 5/5 repeats |
| Same job item in 2 runs: 1 submit | [test#L402](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L402) |
| Abort one run, the other finishes | [test#L450](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L450) |
| Abort the leader: the follower adopts its job, 1 submit | [test#L482](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L482) |
| 503 exhausted on run A: run B calls the provider itself | [test#L474](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/31b72fb20f8fed7ece20ba6b069c3866aba0a7f6/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L474) |
| `app.stop()` pauses both runs, a new app resumes and adopts the job | [test#L557](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/31b72fb20f8fed7ece20ba6b069c3866aba0a7f6/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L557) |
| Budget per run | [test#L507](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L507) |
| `events({ runId })` vs `events()` | [test#L572](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L572) |
| Same bytes from 2 runs: 1 store object | [test#L645](https://github.com/moku-labs/ai/blob/436f6920501a2624bf5c1308a6c1dfcb1a57590f/src/plugins/runner/__tests__/integration/concurrent-runs.test.ts#L645) |

## Release
Minor. This repo has no `.changeset/`. Run the Release workflow with `release_type: minor`. Not published by this PR.

Release note: `runner.maxActiveRuns` lets one process drive several runs. `app.stop()` now pauses active runs and waits for them. Each record from `events()` carries `runId`, and `run`/`resume` accept `onStart(runId)`. The same artifact key is submitted once across runs. fal gains 7 video models and two error rules from the studio patch.

Next: review and merge, then run Release with `minor`. The studio then upgrades and deletes `patches/@moku-labs%2Fai@0.3.0.patch`.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
Present-tense sweep for bead rf2-tv5ac.73 (epic rf2-tv5ac, applying the CALIBRATION rulings R1–R10). Every comment and prose line was read in the fence: `spec/010-Schemas.md`, `spec/011-SSR.md`, `spec/013-Flows.md`, `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`, `spec/015-Data-Classification.md`, `spec/Privacy.md` and `spec/Security.md`. The PR also covers the bead's three ALSO-IN-SCOPE items, one of which extends the fence to `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc` and `docs/api/re-frame.http.md`.

There is one commit per file, per R7, and the branch is rebased on trunk `0fc0de6b0e`. No keyword or identifier changed, and no heading was renamed.

## Census, before and after (`scripts/present_tense.py census`, same seven files)

| | lines | bead-id lines | history lines |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| before (trunk copies) | 6546 | 81 | 66 |
| after | 6470 | 3 | 27 |

The 3 bead-id hits kept, with reasons:
- `011:643` `"rf2-root-"`: an emitted id prefix.
- `011:1767` `rf2-ssr-streaming-<frame-id>`: a thread name, which is an identifier.
- `011:1755`: a heading that carries `(rf2-t72b1c)`. Headings are not renamed; it is listed below.

The 27 history hits kept, with reasons:
- In 014, most are the domain term *supersede / superseded* for a same-`:request-id` reissue.
- "no longer exists / resolves" appears as a present-tense counterfactual in 011:765, 013:488, 015:344 and 015:500.
- "already" is used in the present tense in 010:368, 010:825 and 011:1575.
- 011:147, 011:318, 011:889, 011:1016, 011:1708, 011:1737 and Security:272 were read and are present-tense.
- One heading is listed below.

## Items

- **Present-tense sweep, all seven files:** fixed. The rewrites follow the calibration kinds:
  - Bead ids and PR numbers are removed. Bug stories become counterfactuals ("would"). Retirements become "There is no X". Change narration becomes plain present tense. "Ruling A", "pre-alpha", "graduated", "Finding #8", "(parent finding)" and "45-bead" are dropped.
  - The Resolved-decisions narratives in 010 and 013 now state the reason rather than the history.
  - The Security decisions-log row "The split executed | Keystone bead …" is deleted: it was pure process history.
- **ALSO-IN-SCOPE 1, spec/011 §Failed-root isolation:** fixed. The section no longer cites the removed client duplicate-root registry. It now scopes to the per-root server-emit arms and the 004C §7 payload rule.
- **ALSO-IN-SCOPE 2, spec/011 `v/html`:** fixed.
  - The trusted-markup sentence names the structural UI-tree tier's `{:html s}` node variant, linking to 004B §The node schema — version 1, and Fresco's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
  - The two-dispositions paragraph is kept. It now states the tree tier's refusal of keys that canonicalise onto `:children`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `:key` and `:ref`. This was verified against `re-frame.ssr.ui-tree` `reserved-attr-names` / `reject-reserved-attrs!`.
  - It links only to 004B anchors, and 004B is not edited.
- **ALSO-IN-SCOPE 3, the `:rf.error/http-no-reply-target` message:** fixed.
  - The retired-pre-alpha sentence now reads "The framework never addresses a reply implicitly, because an implicit target can swallow failures." The rest of the message and its "Per Spec 014 §Reply addressing" pointer are kept.
  - `docs/api/re-frame.http.md:93` matches it.
  - No test asserts the old sentence. Two out-of-fence docs still carry the same "retired pre-alpha" narrative and are reported below.
- **Stale prose, fixed only where code verifies the new sentence:**
  - 013, 015 and 011 described an "`:errors` stream of `register-listener!`". `re-frame.core` says "There is no `:events` / `:errors` stream". `re-frame.observability` says "`register-listener!` carries no `:errors` stream". SSR installs through the internal `re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener!`. The prose now names the `:observability :errors` sink route or the internal substrate registry.
  - 010 called `:boundary?` "the interceptor". It is the step-1 validation site; 010 itself says it is not a chain entry.
  - In the Privacy.md composition diagram:
    - It had a "sub-output propagation table". `re-frame.classification` says there is no propagation.
    - It had "schema-sourced migration-import" registry entries. `re-frame.elision` writes only `:effect`, `:flow`, `:machine`, `:route` and `:resource` sources.
    - It listed `redact-interceptor` under API.md §Privacy. `re-frame.core` says there is no public `redact-interceptor`.
  - 014 had stale prose about trace hoisting, canned stubs and the `:after-ms` envelope. Each fix was checked against `re-frame.trace` and `re-frame.http` test support.
  - 011 had four sections that describe removed re-frame.ui / Freehand machinery. They are deleted, per the mayor's REMOVED-machinery note on the bead, and nothing links to their anchors (see Gates).

## Reported, not changed

- **Historical headings, not renamed:**
  - 011 `#### Fn-form :root-view invocation count under streaming (rf2-t72b1c)`
  - 014 `### :reply-to is the unified authoring key; the co-located default is retired`
  - 013 `### A flow throw aborts the event — atomic commit boundary (RESOLVED, Mike 2026-05-24)`
  - 010 `### Boundary-validation interceptor naming`
  - 015 `## What is removed (and what is kept)`
  - Privacy `## Removed surfaces`
  - Security `### Pragmatic stance (the nine policy beads)`
- **SA-4 terms kept.** "no tracking bead is filed yet" in 010 and 013 is the SA-4 classification vocabulary.
- **R8 contradiction 1, not settled.** The docs disagree on whether per-slot schema props classify durable data.
  - These passages treat per-slot `:sensitive?` / `:large?` schema props as a classification route for machine `[:schemas :data]` / resource data, or as a feeder of the `[:rf.runtime/elision …]` registry:
    - Privacy §re-frame.schemas, §Per-slot schema props, the transition-payload paragraph, and the "Composition is additive" rule.
    - Security §Privacy / secret handling, the epoch "Sensitive rollup" bullet, and the always-on "Per-path elision" bullet.
    - The Security meta-keys `:sensitive?` row, the trace-egress and epoch matrix rows, and the decisions-log row "Schema walker populates the sensitive-declarations registry at boot".
  - These say schema props drive validation-failure-trace redaction only:

author: adewale
body:
## Summary

Mermaid 11.16 parses in-range fractional Journey scores such as `3.5`, but Agentic Mermaid's shared parser previously rejected them, leaving the agent source opaque and the native renderer unable to render. This PR makes finite scores from 1 through 5 continuous across native/agent parsing, serialization, mutation, facts, SVG position, and terminal output. It promotes the existing #248 fractional-score receipt from diagnosed to native.

This is deliberately bounded: Mermaid also parses out-of-range and non-finite spellings, but the documented 1–5 rendering domain still rejects them with targeted diagnostics. Existing integer Journey output remains byte-identical (including both committed SVG snapshots).

## Visual evidence

Baseline: merged base `49cbd03ac1a3df5c23920305a4bc424daa8e406f`. Current: implementation head `e4af4e6c9b2822953d9c2739a9c0ed4e7ff59e04`.

At the baseline, the public renderer fails on the exact source below: `Journey task "Review" has invalid score 3.5. Expected an integer from 1 through 5`. There is no successful “before” image.

```mermaid
journey
  title Fractional Journey scores
  section Work
  First: 3: Me
  Review: 3.5: Me
  Last: 4: Me
```

After, the [SVG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/e4af4e6c9b2822953d9c2739a9c0ed4e7ff59e04/docs/pr-assets/issue-248-journey-fractional-score-after.svg) and PNG show Review at the exact midpoint between 3 and 4:

![Journey chart with Review at score 3.5 between the 3 and 4 gridlines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/e4af4e6c9b2822953d9c2739a9c0ed4e7ff59e04/docs/pr-assets/issue-248-journey-fractional-score-after.png)

The [reproduction and artifact provenance](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/blob/e4af4e6c9b2822953d9c2739a9c0ed4e7ff59e04/docs/pr-assets/issue-248-journey-fractional-score-evidence.md) run the same input against an independent checkout pinned to the exact base and this branch.

## Verification and scope

- The pinned-base reproduction proves the authentic pre-fix failure. The focused test probes Mermaid 11.16 itself and checks exact native/agent/facts/serialize/mutate semantics, strictly ordered midpoint SVG geometry, Mermaid's fractional face sentiment, exact terminal score text, and rejection of malformed/out-of-range/non-finite values. It also rejects quadratic backtracking on 64 KiB malformed task/score fields. The #248 receipt now reads emitted SVG geometry and verifies the mutated diagram after serialization/reparse, with agent/render/serialize/mutate sabotage tests.
- Focused Journey and fidelity tests, both typechecks, the exact npm package-file manifest (172 files), and all nine evidence freshness checks pass. The three refreshed gallery PNGs were regenerated by [Linux CI](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/actions/runs/36083336504); visual review found unchanged layouts and only minor browser/font rasterization differences (mean absolute channel difference <1/255). Section B's approved PNG is byte-identical. The [final-head hosted CI run](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/actions/runs/36085455625) passed every check, including browser E2E and payload verification.
- A final [Linux/x64 gallery and browser capture](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/actions/runs/36085188853) at code commit `114f9eb27e6f5e863b98f8c26defa905885450ff` pins the exact request graphs and bytes for all four routes. Its captured JSON is byte-identical to the checked-in baseline; all four gallery PNGs are byte-identical to the previously reviewed images. The final head only tightens the measured budgets, refreshes gallery receipts, and removes the temporary capture workflow. The local macOS Chromium launch is sandbox-blocked, so Linux is the authoritative browser result.
- The required independent semantic, architecture, test-strength, security, and evidence audit/fix/re-audit loop approved the exact final head/base in all five lanes. The detailed [final audit addendum](https://github.com/adewale/agentic-mermaid/pull/293#issuecomment-5825625613) records the verdicts and separately tracked #294/#295 follow-ups.

Refs #248.

author: ksingh31
body:
## What

Implements story `consumer/03-estimate-rate-limit.md`:

**Dedicated estimates pipeline (AC1/AC2):** `POST /api/v1/estimate` moves off the general 100-req/60s limiter onto its own pipeline — **20 requests/hour per client IP**. The 21st estimate in an hour → `429` with `Retry-After` header and RFC 7807 `RATE_LIMITED` body (existing `rateLimitedProblem` + `problemResponseHeaders` — reused, not rebuilt). A real-user flow (≤ 5/hr) never touches the ceiling.

**Per-tenant aggregation for embeds (AC3):** the pipeline gains a generic `extraLimiters` mechanism — secondary limiters, each enforcing an independent budget on its own key dimension, checked after the primary limiter (first denial wins). The estimates pipeline adds a per-tenant bucket (also 20/hr): two IPs sharing one tenant key hit the tenant cap even though neither IP is near its own. Non-embed traffic (no `tenantKey`) skips the tenant limiter entirely. The adapter forwards `tenantKey` from the request body (same pattern as the leads adapter); the body itself is never logged, and denial logs carry a key hash, never the raw tenant key or IP.

**Frozen registry, not hardcoded (AC4):** all four numbers are zod-validated env config (`ESTIMATE_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`/`_MAX_REQUESTS`, `ESTIMATE_TENANT_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`/`_MAX_REQUESTS`), defaulting to the frozen values from the canonical registry (TECH_PLAN.md §13.3, public-anon tier: estimates 20/hr/IP). No literal limits in routes/services. Note: api-mcp/08 (machine-readable registry + conformance) isn't built yet — when it lands, these config defaults are the seam it supersedes; the doc comment says so.

**Docs:** `docs/security/rate-limits.md` — the estimate endpoint moves from the generic-limiter row to its own enforced row (20/hr/IP + per-tenant); the 'planned' row for it is removed; the reusable-mechanism paragraph now describes `extraLimiters`.

## Frontend capability unblocked

None directly (behavioral hardening), but the web app's estimate calls now inherit the documented contract: bursts past 20/hr/IP get a `429` with `Retry-After` the client should honor — the frontend retry/backoff story can rely on it.

## Verification

- `npx tsc -b` (root, all projects): clean
- `npm test -w @feasly/api`: 23 files / 236 tests pass (twice in a row; one earlier full run failed with an unreproduced error — treated as flake, both reruns fully green)
- `npm run lint -w @feasly/api`: clean
- `npm run bundle:functions`: estimate adapter bundles
- Layer-boundary tests pass (no new db/env/URL imports in routes or middleware)

New tests: `estimate.adapter.test.ts` (dedicated-pipeline wiring, tenantKey forwarding), 5 new pipeline cases (21st-request 429 + Retry-After, real-user non-interference, two-IPs-one-tenant cap, tenant-skip for non-embeds, key-hash log hygiene), config defaults + overrides, composition wiring.

## Merge-conflict pre-check

Branch is fresh from `origin/main` (post-#55); the only shared file with the active report-redesign branch is `docs/` prose. Will merge main again before merge if it moved.

On 2026-09-25 UTC, a same-run check against the pinned CAJSamples revision passed **546/546 generic-only tool comparisons and 546/546 Rust comparisons**, zero failures/skips, 27 source hashes before and after, and no semantic/toolchain drift. author: benkirk
body:
## Summary

Follow-on to #616. Adds a bulk lead/admin membership remediation that you run yourself, and scopes every reconcile path to **active resources** and **active users**.

**Why active resources.** `account.deleted` is never set in practice: zero soft-deleted accounts on any of 29 resources, back to Bluefire in 2013. "Non-deleted accounts" therefore meant every retired resource too. On prod, pressing "Reconcile all" on CESM0020 added 26 Cheyenne rows.

- **`Project.live_accounts`** means non-deleted accounts on a `Resource.is_active` resource (commissioned, not decommissioned). `ensure_members`, `reconcile_project_access` (and so the web **Reconcile all** button) and `--validate` all use it. Cheyenne is excluded even though five of its allocations still end in 2026–2029.
- **Active users only.** Reconcile, in the CLI and on the web, skips users who are not `User.is_active` (inactive or locked). `--validate` doesn't flag an inactive lead or admin. An explicit lead or admin assignment through `Project.update` still seeds them whatever their status.
- **`reconcile_project_access(lead_admin_only=True)`** seeds only the lead and admin.
- **CLI:** `sam-admin project <PROJCODE|--all> <--reconcile|--reconcile-lead-admin> [--dry-run]`
  - it prints one row per (project, user) with role, prior history on the project (`never a member` / `partial` / `ended DATE`) and resources, plus totals and a history breakdown;
  - `--format json` gives the same result as a `project_reconcile` envelope;
  - `--dry-run` rolls back its own savepoint, so it writes nothing;
  - a real run commits per project.
- CLAUDE.md is updated: the invariant now says live accounts and active users, and the CLI block shows the bulk command.

### Local dry run (dev snapshot, about 10 s each)

| mode | memberships | users | projects | never a member | ended | partial |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--reconcile-lead-admin --all` | 1,235 | 405 (160 leads, 245 admins) | 340 | 167 | 152 | 86 |
| `--reconcile --all` | 2,257 | 1,065 | 379 | 167 | 152 | 746 |

The `account_user` count was unchanged after the dry runs: 163,030 before and after.

### What the "ended" dates are (triage)

- **2024-11-12 08:46 is the Cheyenne shutdown.** 19,614 rows for 8,610 users on 2,270 projects ended in one minute, 99.9% of them on Cheyenne. A lead or admin whose rows "ended" that day only ever held Cheyenne access on that project. They never got rows on the project's Derecho or Casper accounts, which is the same seeding gap as CESM0020.
- **2025-10-09 14:23–25, 2025-12-05 08:41–48 and 2026-01-28 15:12–13 are batched whole-user deactivations.** Each user's rows on every project and every resource closed in the same minute, which is the legacy `userlifecycle/deactivate` shape. About 75% of those users are still inactive and hold nothing, which is correct. The rest were reactivated later without their memberships (the sam-ldap-syncd#3 defect).

With the active-user filter, the lead/admin pass reaches only leads and admins who are active today, which is what precedent says they should have. Non-lead members who were reactivated after a deactivation sweep are **not** covered, and remain a separate decision.

Nothing was run against prod.

**Add member modal** (second commit). The End Date note now reads "Usually blank; access follows the allocation duration", and the start date stays prefilled with today. Since the webapp began adding members, 8 adds (44 rows) have set an end date at insert, all starting at midnight (this form's fingerprint). Two of them equal the project's allocation end, e.g. UCSD0060 ahoudou. XRAS never passes dates.

**How legacy SAM handles membership end dates** (from reading `legacy_sam/`)
- **Adding a member:** legacy never sets an end date. The only insert, `Account.assign` → `new AccountUser(...)`, hard-codes `end_date = NULL`. That covers the UI, XRAS and AMIE. An end date chosen at insert exists only in the new UI.
- **Removing a member:** legacy never deletes a row. Every removal end-dates it with the server's "now":
  - UI member removal;
  - AMIE InactivateAccount;
  - user deactivation: `PUT /protected/admin/userlifecycle/deactivate/{username}` → `User.unassignFromAccounts()`, run by something outside the tree, which fits the batched bursts;
  - the Quartz `AssignmentsOnDecommissionedResourcesSweeper`, daily at 02:15, for resources decommissioned within the last 90 days.
- **This app is the opposite:** `remove_user_from_project` and `revoke_user_resource_access` **hard-delete**. So the two apps follow different removal conventions.
- **The Cheyenne close does not match the sweeper.** It happened at 08:46, not 02:15, and 10+ months after the recorded 2023-12-31 decommission, outside the sweeper's 90-day window. It was a manual run, or the decommission date was edited afterwards.


### Test Results

`make check-all`:
- MySQL: 9711 passed, 43 skipped, 1 xfailed.
- Postgres: 9674 passed, 80 skipped, 1 xfailed.
- Perf: 57 passed.
- Helm renders: all OK.
- e2e: 109 passed, 18 skipped.

New tests:
- `test_project_lead_membership.py`: decommissioned resources are skipped by `ensure_members` and by reconcile; `lead_admin_only` leaves other members alone; both modes skip an inactive user.
- `test_htmx_handler_routes.py`: the add-member form prefills today's start date, leaves the end date blank and shows the note.
- `test_project_admin_membership.py`:
  - the flag guards;
  - a single-project `--reconcile-lead-admin --dry-run` reports and writes nothing;
  - `--all` in JSON then for real, with the project list substituted;
  - `--validate` ignores an inactive lead.

body: ## What / why `dueItems()` takes every scheduled row whose time has passed on the very next scheduler tick — by design, that is how an item that went overdue gets caught up. But `POST /items/:id/schedule` accepted **any** instant, including one in the past. So on the Publishing screen: - the datetime-local picker is prefilled from the item's old `scheduledFor` (retry flows, a laptop that slept past the date), and - pressing **Schedule** with that stale value published to the live audience seconds later. This contradicts the area's own stated contract ("nothing is scheduled that is not approved… nothing publishes by accident" — Publishing.tsx header, routes.ts): an approval + a click labelled *Schedule* must never mean *publish now*. ## Change - **Server** (`routes.ts`, the human/agent door): a past instant → 400 *"That time has already passed, and a schedule in the past publishes on the next tick — which is publishing now, not scheduling it. Pick a time in the future, or use Publish now if you meant now."*; an unreadable date gets its own refusal. `schedule()` itself stays permissive — the auto-scheduler's `nextSlot()` is always future and the scheduler/retry machinery legitimately deals with overdue rows. - **Client** (`Publishing.tsx` + new `scheduleTime.ts`): Schedule is disabled while the picker holds a past (or unparseable) value, with the reason in the button title; the server message is the same wording for older tabs and API callers. ## Testing - `publishing.test.ts` — new route test: past → 400 with the message, item untouched (still `approved`, `scheduled_for` null), future → 200, junk → 400. **Verified failing without the guard (41/1) and passing with it (42/0).** - `scheduleTime.test.ts` — 6 unit tests incl. the exact-minute-is-past rule and local-time parity with the call site. - Gates: server 1421/1421 (1 skipped = baseline), client 245/245, `tsc --noEmit` clean both packages. Images: mockups rebuilt in HTML with the repo's real card/button CSS, not live screenshots. ### Before / after | Before | After | |---|---| | | |

author: gojatora
body:
## Summary

Adds soft deactivation of an existing Resident (Active → Inactive). The Resident record stays in SQLite, and only its `status` column changes.

## Resident Deactivation Behavior

`ResidentDeactivationService::deactivateResident(id)` finds the Resident by its persisted ID, then handles one of three outcomes:

| Outcome | `success` | `stateChanged` | `residentNotFound` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Newly deactivated | true | true | false |
| Already Inactive | true | false | false |
| Not found | false | false | true |

- **Active-to-Inactive rule:** only an Active Resident triggers a database write.
- **Already-Inactive handling:** the Resident is returned unchanged with no database write, so repeating the operation is safe and leaves it Inactive.
- **Resident-not-found handling:** a normal result, not an exception or a validation error. Nothing is inserted or deleted, and no ID is generated.
- **No status toggle, no reactivation:** an Inactive Resident is never changed back to Active.

## Implementation

- **Persistence:** `ResidentRepository::deactivateById(int)` runs a parameterized `UPDATE residents SET status = ? WHERE id = ?`.
  - The status value is fixed to `Inactive` in code, so callers cannot set an arbitrary status.
  - It returns `true` when a row matched (via `sqlite3_changes`).
  - It never deletes rows.
- **Service layer:** the new `ResidentDeactivationService` and `ResidentDeactivationResult` reuse the existing `ResidentRepository`.
  - It takes no validator because personal information is never touched.
  - It does not use registration or T06 update.
- **ID preservation:** the same row is updated in place, with no delete-and-reinsert.
- **Personal/contact information preservation:** only `status` is written. First name, last name, address, contact number (including the leading `0`) and email are unchanged.

## Files Changed

- `repositories/ResidentRepository.h` and `.cc`: add `deactivateById`
- `services/ResidentDeactivationResult.h`, `ResidentDeactivationService.h` and `.cc`: new
- `CMakeLists.txt` and `test/CMakeLists.txt`: register the new `.cc` file
- `test/test_main.cc`: 10 new T07 tests

## Integration Verification

- **T03:** `findById` still returns the deactivated Resident, with the same ID and information and `status = Inactive`.
- **T05:** the deactivated Resident still appears in both `listResidents()` and `searchResidents(...)` with `status = Inactive`. T05 is unmodified.
- **T06:** unmodified. It still preserves status during information updates.
- **Isolation:** deactivating one Resident leaves the others unchanged.

## Automated Tests (all ten required scenarios)

1. Active Resident can be deactivated
2. Inactive status is stored in persistence (checked through a fresh repository instance)
3. Resident ID is preserved
4. All Resident information is preserved (including the leading zero)
5. Deactivated Resident stays retrievable, and the row count is unchanged (no deletion)
6. Deactivated Resident stays available through T05 search and listing
7. Already-Inactive Resident is handled safely, including repeated calls
8. Nonexistent Resident returns `residentNotFound`
9. Nonexistent ID neither creates nor deletes records
10. Deactivating one Resident does not affect another

## Regression Result

Full `ctest --output-on-failure` run: **100% passed, 60/60** (the 50 starter–T06 tests plus the 10 new T07 tests). No existing tests were removed, disabled or modified.

## Application Verification

The application starts and `GET /health` returns:

```json
{"application":"Community Services Management System","status":"ok","version":"0.1.0"}
```

## Out of Scope (not implemented)

No deactivation UI or REST endpoint, no physical delete, no reactivation or status toggle, no audit fields (reason, date, user), and no active/inactive search filters.

## Known Issues

None.

body:
Fixes #976
Fixes #975
Fixes #1012
Fixes #1082

Four independent small fixes, one commit each, so they can be reviewed or reverted separately.

- **#976 (a309584):** `DEFAULT_POOL_ROOT` is now `/mnt/shared/prismabuild-fleet/pb-queue`, the queue that `pbrun.SH / "pb-queue"` names. `PRISMABUILD_POOL_ROOT` still overrides it. A bare `PoolQueue()` now raises `PoolContractError` naming the path when that default is not a directory, instead of reading it as an empty queue. Explicit roots are unchanged and add no stat. `retire_worker` reports the refusal and exits 2 instead of printing "no worker record". `docs/design.md` records the default and the refusal.
- **#975 (791125e):** a `pbtest --gpu` run with neither `--timeout-s` nor `--test-timeout-s` exits 2 before submitting anything (option 1 in the issue). `--test-timeout-s 0` still works because it is a declared choice. CPU shards are unchanged. No prismaquant or tessera script calls `pbtest --gpu` without a timeout. *Not covered:* a CPU-only run tagged `gb10` with neither flag still derives 86370 s from the ceiling; that needs its own decision.
- **#1012 (2476dba):** pbrun's `queued` / `attached to` line now prints the full 64-character key; later lines keep the 12-character prefix. pbtest prints `shard N action <key> (queued): <files>`, and its ending line repeats the key. `--json` records gain `action_key` and `receipt_path`. Only the first such line counts, so a test's own output can't replace the shard's key. `PrismaBuildCAS.receipt_path()` is new. *Limitation:* SLURM submission lines still print only the prefix.
- **#1082 (7b5dfca):** campaign rows accept `residency`, `residency_ram`, `residency_prefetch_depth_gib`, `residency_read_mb_s` and `cpus`, each passed through as pbrun's flag of the same name. They are checked when the manifest loads, using pbrun's own rules; the allowed residency words are now constants in pbrun that both tools use. *Pre-existing gap, not introduced here:* under `--transport slurm`, pbrun ignores `--residency stage`.

Docs for all four are in `docs/design.md` and `docs/operating_prismabuild.md`.

Validation: **local pytest in a cloud container (Python 3.12, no fleet). The pbtest run through PrismaBuild is still owed, including #1082's full 20-shard suite and a check that a real two-shard run's printed keys match its records; there are no receipts.**

author: jobbyist
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes two SEO issues flagged in audits.

### 1. Language markup that isn't an ISO code
`SEO.tsx` emitted `<meta name="language" content="English">` on every Helmet page, and prerendering baked it into the static HTML. It now emits `content="en"`, and `SEO.tsx` also sets `<html lang="en">` through Helmet. `index.html`, the SSR root, the AMP stories and the email layouts already used `lang="en"`. Three things were left as they are on purpose: JSON-LD `inLanguage: "en-ZA"`, the podcast RSS `<language>en-za</language>` and the `en-ZA` date formatting. They are valid BCP 47 values and aren't HTML language markup.

### 2. GSC: "Review has multiple aggregate ratings" (in `review` / in `aggregateRating`)
I confirmed this on production before changing anything. `/reviews/:slug` served `aggregateRating` as an **array of two**:
- an "editorial" aggregate built from our own single review (`reviewCount: 1`). That rating is self-serving, not an aggregate.
- a 1–5 member rating from `getMemberRatingStats()`. It is **hash-generated** (for example "854 members"), not real data.

There were two more sources of bad data:
- `SitewideSEO.tsx` added a second `Product` node on review pages rendered by the SPA.
- `ProductReview.tsx` could fall back to a seeded average, and it counted comments instead of ratings.

**After this PR:** each review page has one `Product`, one editorial `Review` (0–10) and **at most one** `aggregateRating` (1–5, `ratingCount`). The `aggregateRating` appears only when real `review_ratings` rows exist. The SSR route now loads that aggregate on the server.

## Verification
- `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` exits 0 and `npm run lint` exits 0.
- `bun test`: all tests pass, including 11 new ones in `src/lib/__tests__/productReviewJsonLd.test.ts`.
- I built a local node-server SSR bundle and ran it against live data. A rated review (`pc-dermaceutical-retinol-serum`) gets one `aggregateRating {ratingValue 5, ratingCount 1}`. Unrated reviews get none. `<html lang="en">` is present.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- After deploy, run "Validate fix" in Search Console.
- `ReviewsGrid.tsx` still *shows* the hash-generated member ratings on `/reviews` cards, and the pages still use seeded like/rating fallbacks. Both conflict with the "never fabricate ratings" principle, so a product decision is needed.

author: nasarajoe
body:
## What Changed

Implements four testing/reliability issues for the protocol:

- **Contract state snapshot testing (#1064)**
  - New `scripts/snapshot-test/` — record golden snapshots of contract state
    (positions, pools, governance) and fail when current state diverges.
  - Order-insensitive sha256 hashing, row-level add/remove/change detection,
    leaf-path diffing, `--allow` allowlist for expected volatile fields, `--record`.
  - Committed golden snapshot `snapshots/lending.snap.json` + fixture state.
  - CI: `.github/workflows/snapshot-tests.yml` (unit suite, golden verification, negative gate).

- **Gas regression testing in CI (#1065)**
  - New `scripts/gas-regression.sh` — builds + runs the benchmark suite and
    compares against the committed baseline, failing beyond a configurable
    threshold; reuses `run-benchmarks.sh --compare`.
  - `run-benchmarks.sh` now honors `GAS_REG_MAX_PCT` for `--max-regression-pct`.
  - CI: `.github/workflows/gas-regression.yml` — cold-cache rebuild for a fair
    comparison, fails job on regression, comments on the PR.

- **Contract deployment verification scripts (#1066)**
  - New `scripts/deploy-verify/` — offline structural verification of deployment
    manifests: Stellar `C…` address format, per-network uniqueness, uninitialized/
    duplicate detection, bytecode authenticity (recorded wasmHash vs locally built
    artifact sha256), `--update-hashes` to regenerate hashes.
  - Fixed broken `jq | length` invocations in `scripts/verify-deployment.sh` and
    added a `manifest` mode that wires in the Node verifier.
  - CI: `.github/workflows/deployment-verification.yml`.

- **Differential testing between implementations (#1067)**
  - New `scripts/differential-test/` — runs identical scenarios through two
    independent implementations and asserts output equivalence (relative numeric
    tolerance, leaf-level findings, allowlists).
  - Bundled reference pair (continuous vs daily-discrete interest accrual) and
    scenario set as the working gate.
  - CI: `.github/workflows/differential-tests.yml` including a negative gate.

## Why

These close the loop on protocol reliability: snapshots pin contract state
against silent drift, gas gates catch performance regressions before merge,
deployment verification prevents deploying bytecode/address mismatches, and
differential testing proves reimplementations behave like the code they replace.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests updated or added (16 passing: snapshot, deploy-verify, differential)
- [x] Relevant local checks passed (`node --experimental-strip-types --test …` on all three suites)
- [x] Manual verification completed when needed (CLI record/compare, verify, differential run/negative run)
- [ ] Committed baseline present for gas gate (`stellar-lend/benchmarks/baseline.json`)

## Related Issues

Closes #1064
Closes #1065
Closes #1066
Closes #1067

body:
This PR addresses a `GraphQLError` where clients attempted to filter repositories using `private: Boolean` within the `RepositorySetFilters` input type, but the field was not defined in the GraphQL schema.

Previously, repository visibility filtering was only supported via `isPublic: Boolean`. This change adds `private: Boolean` to the `RepositorySetFilters` input type and implements its corresponding filtering logic in `apply_filters_to_queryset`.

This makes the GraphQL API more robust and user-friendly by accepting a common and intuitive filter name, preventing `GraphQLError` for clients using it, and maintaining full compatibility with existing `isPublic` usage.

body:
## What

Task: #1833

The Feed's delete confirms now tell the truth. `SocialProfile` inherits `paranoid: true` from the global define and production `social_profiles` has `deleted_at`, so `destroy()` generates `UPDATE "social_profiles" SET "deleted_at"=$1 WHERE "deleted_at" IS NULL AND …`. That is a soft delete: no row is removed, no FK cascade fires, and a profile is restorable by clearing `deleted_at`. The Recycle Bin does not list profiles, so restore is not available from any screen today.

**UI copy (`SocialProfileGenerator.jsx`):**
- `deleteProfile`'s confirm: "Delete this profile permanently?" → "Delete this profile? It'll be hidden from the Feed. It can be restored, though not from this screen yet."
- `BulkDeleteDialog` title: "Permanently delete N profiles and their follows/relationships? This cannot be undone." → "Delete N profile(s)? …". With one profile it reads "It'll be hidden from the Feed. Its follows and relationships are kept. It can be restored, though not from this screen yet."; with several, "They'll … Their … They can …".
- The typed-count requirement and the "Locked, crossed and entangled profiles are kept automatically." note are unchanged.

**Comments (`socialProfileRoutes.js`, no code change):**
- `DELETE /:id`: "Permanently delete a profile" → "Soft-delete a profile: SocialProfile is paranoid, so destroy() sets deleted_at. Restorable by clearing it."
- `/bulk/delete` guard: "Entanglement rows cascade on delete, so a profile with any is kept." → "Delete only sets deleted_at (no cascade fires), but an entangled profile hidden from the Feed would leave story rows pointing at it, so a profile with any is kept."

**History:** the single-delete confirm has said "permanently" since it was written. The bulk dialog's wording, and the "cascade" rationale for the entanglement guard, came from #1827/#1830 and were wrong. The guard itself stays, for the true reason above. No behaviour changes: no backend logic, no restore UI, no Recycle Bin change.

**Test:** `tests/unit/models/SocialProfile.softDelete.test.js` (offline, no DB) pins that the app define is paranoid, the model does not override it, and `destroy()` generates an UPDATE setting `deleted_at`, never a DELETE.

author: angryjay91
body:
[SID:4276]

## 문제(민 기기 하네스 · 배포 27 · 결재 탭 첫 진입 ×3)
탭→정착 중앙값 1728ms · 요청 8. `/inbox` RSC 460~600ms를 다 받은 **뒤**에야 데이터 요청이 출발(탭 +608~946ms) · 각 0.6~1.06초 — 폭포.

## 원인(코드)
결재 화면(`inbox/page.tsx`)은 클라이언트 컴포넌트라 요청 넷이 전부 하이드레이션 뒤 `useEffect`에서 출발한다:
| 요청 | 자리 |
|---|---|
| `gates/inbox?status=pending…` · `?status=held…` | `components/inbox/approvals-queue.tsx` `fetchGates` |
| `notifications?`(1쪽) | `inbox/page.tsx` `fetchInboxNotifications` |
| `workflow-executions?project_id…&member_id…&limit=10` | `inbox/page.tsx` 워크플로우 실행 effect |

## 방법 비교(AC1)
| 방법 | 출발 시각 | 드는 것 | 판단 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. 로딩 경계에서 선출발 + 화면이 1회 넘겨받기** | 누른 즉시(로딩 스켈레톤이 뜨는 순간) — RSC 대기와 겹침 | 작은 모듈 하나(`inbox-prefetch.ts`) · 소비처 셋이 같은 주소로 넘겨받기 | **선택** |
| B. 서버에서 초기 데이터 싣기(RSC에 데이터 포함) | 요청 시각(서버 → BE) | 큰 클라이언트 화면(`inbox/page.tsx` · 결재 큐)을 서버 데이터 받는 모양으로 재구성 · 401 재시도(`fetchWithAuth`) 경로가 서버에 없음 | 비용 큼 — 이득(RSC 대기와 겹치기)은 A와 같은 크기 |
| C. 탭 누를 때(탭바 onClick) 선출발 | 누른 즉시 | 탭바가 결재 화면 요청을 알아야 함(결합) · 메뉴 · 링크 · 알림으로 오는 길은 못 덮음 | A가 같은 시각에 모든 길을 덮음 |
| D. gates/inbox 두 상태를 한 요청으로 | — | BE 계약 변경(`list_gates`가 status 하드 필터 · «held 최하단» 요건은 두 목록 이어붙이기로 충족 중) + 소비처 | 지연은 안 줄어듦(둘은 이미 병렬) · 요청 수만 1 감소 — 이 PR 밖(필요하면 별 카드) |

로딩 경계는 4274(PR 4643)로 누른 즉시 그려지고, 이 PR 전에도 `inbox/loading.tsx`는 있었다(결재 탭이 44~193ms로 빨랐던 이유) — 그 순간을 요청 출발에 쓴다.

## 넘겨받기 규칙(오래된 값이 화면에 서지 않게)
| 규칙 | 내용 | 왜 |
|---|---|---|
| 1회용 | 넘겨준 항목은 바로 지운다 — 그 뒤 새로고침 · 15초 폴링 · 더 보기 · 재시도는 늘 새 요청 | 화면이 붙은 뒤의 데이터는 원래 경로 그대로 |
| 기한 | 선출발 시각부터 **10초**가 지나면 버리고 새 요청 | 화면 폴링 주기(15초)보다 짧아 «폴링이 보여 줄 값»보다 오래된 값이 설 일이 없다 — 선출발 뒤 화면이 늦게 붙는 경우(느린 망에서 RSC가 10초 넘게 걸림)도 이 규칙으로 새 요청 |
| 범위 | 항목마다 선출발한 사람(member) · 프로젝트를 적고, 넘겨받는 쪽의 현재 값과 다르면 버린다 | 그 사이 프로젝트 · 계정 전환 |
| 탭 | gates 두 요청은 결재 탭(`?tab=gates`)으로 올 때만 선출발 · 알림 1쪽 · 워크플로우 실행은 모든 탭이 첫 화면에 쓰므로 늘 | 다른 탭으로 오면 안 쓰는 요청이 된다 — 안 쓴 항목은 기한이 지나 버려짐 |
| 중복 | 같은 범위 · 기한 안의 항목이 있으면 다시 출발하지 않음 | 개발 모드 StrictMode 이중 effect |
| 실패 | 선출발 실패는 «처리 안 된 거부»로 새지 않게 막고, 넘겨받는 쪽은 원래 promise로 실패를 그대로 받는다(기존 실패 표시 경로 무변) | — |
| 인증 | 선출발도 같은 `fetchWithAuth`(401 → refresh → 재시도) | story #2689 경로 유지 |

## 변경
- `components/inbox/inbox-prefetch.ts`: 주소 만들기(화면 · 선출발 공용) · `prefetchInbox` · `takePrefetchedOrFetch` · 위 규칙.
- `components/inbox/inbox-prefetch-starter.tsx`: `inbox/loading.tsx`에 얹는 클라이언트 조각(현재 member · 프로젝트 · `?tab=`).
- 소비처: `approvals-queue.tsx` `fetchGates` · `inbox/page.tsx` 알림 · 워크플로우 실행 — 같은 주소로 넘겨받기. 범위는 ref로 넘겨 기존 콜백 · effect 의존성은 그대로.

## 테스트(`inbox-prefetch.test.tsx` · 9)
- 결재 탭이면 넷 · 다른 탭이면 gates 없음 · 중복 출발 없음.
- 1회용 · 기한(10초 · 폴링 15초보다 짧음) · 범위 불일치 · 선출발 실패(거부 누출 없음 · 넘겨받는 쪽은 실패 그대로).
- 실제 `inbox/loading.tsx`를 그리면 넷 출발 · 선출발 뒤 `ApprovalsQueue`가 붙어도 pending · held 각 1건(넘겨받음).
- 뮤테이션 RED 다섯: 기한 검사 제거 · 범위 검사 제거 · 1회용 제거 · loading에서 선출발 조각 제거 · 결재 큐가 넘겨받기를 건너뜀.

## 남는 것
- AC2(민 기기 결재 탭 첫 진입 전후 ×3 — 요청 출발 시각 · 정착 ms)는 배포 뒤.
- D(두 상태 한 요청)는 이 PR 밖.

## 검증
- `pnpm lint` 0 errors · `tsc` · `verify:*` 전부(build-schema-integrity 제외) · inbox 묶음 8 files / 144 PASS. 전체 vitest는 CI 판(PO 지시 · 머신 줄).

author: aeplay
body:
Stacked on #3446. Fixes #3366.

Before: a delta that doesn't qualify for the bulk path (for example, same-index replacements, whose indexes aren't unique) runs sequentially. Every splice then reindexed all later positions, so a frame cost O(changes × rows). At 10k rows, 500 same-index replacements took 131 ms on main and 198 ms on the undo log.

After: during a sequential delta, the ordered-id index goes stale only from the lowest touched position, and it is rebuilt once at commit. Lookups on a stale entry search outward from the recorded position, no further than the number of splices since the index was last exact, because each splice moves any id by at most one position. Added or Updated changes whose row is already at its target index skip the remove and reinsert. At 10k rows:
- 500 same-index replacements: 131 ms (main) → 18.5 ms
- 500 in-place updates: 16.2 → 12.6 ms
- 1-row update: 6.0 → 0.65 ms

**Invariants**
- Positions below `staleFrom` are always exact. A stale id lies at or after `staleFrom`, within `staleSplices` of its recorded position. A run of removals counts one splice per removed row.
- The index is exact again after every committed delta. Rollback resets the stale markers along with the journal.
- Output is unchanged. My randomized comparison with main ran 24,518 checks with none different. The independent review's ~64k runtime-shaped frames also matched main and #3446 exactly.

**Unchanged:** the bulk path's own criteria, reset frames, and the delta sent to listeners.

**Worked examples**
- 40 rows. One frame moves r39 to the front, replaces every fourth row at the same index, updates the row after each replacement in place, then updates r38 at index 39. The final order matches a straightforward array model, and replaying the emitted deltas reproduces `all()`. The next frame then removes and moves rows by id, which checks that positions are exact again. This test fails if the splice counter never counts; it does not catch a wrong count.
- `subscription-manager.ordered-index.test.ts` (added after review) pins the rest:
  - A row shifted by two inserts earlier in the same frame is still found. Fails if lookups search only one position either side.
  - A row shifted by a batched run of removals is still found. Fails if the run counts as one splice.
  - A moved row is restored and findable after a later terminal edit fails. Fails if the undo log keeps the latest prior value instead of the first.
  - 300 random frames, some failing and rolling back, check that the index is exact after each one. Fails if both reindex calls are removed, which otherwise only makes lookups slower.

**Follow-up (not in this PR):** the final reindex runs while journaling is on, so a front insert into 10k rows journals 10k index entries per frame. That is still cheaper than the old snapshot. Rebuilding the index from the restored `orderedIds` on rollback would avoid it.

body:
## Summary
- **GPT-6 aliases**: `astra`, `sol`, and `luna` now resolve to `gpt-6-*`. The legacy aliases `sol-5.6`, `terra`, `luna-5.6`, and `spark` still work.
- **Sol is the default model** for fresh tasks and reviews (override with `CODEX_COMPANION_DEFAULT_MODEL`). Before this, an omitted `--model` inherited `~/.codex/config.toml`, which is `gpt-6-astra` at `high` effort. `continue` and resume keep the thread's model.
- **Astra effort guard**: `high` is rejected (cost policy), `none` and `minimal` are rejected (Astra doesn't support them), and Astra defaults to `medium`.
- **Launch race**: the job record is now written before the worker spawns, and the worker retries its lookup for up to 3 s. Back-to-back launches used to kill the first worker with "No stored job found".
- **Stray thread on early connection close**: the retry reuses the thread it already created and logs why the connection closed.
- **Search progress**: web-search progress lines now show the query and the URL of opened pages.
- **Reconciler false-kill**: a live worker pid now blocks read-side finalization, and a non-completed turn must stay stable across two samples at least 30 s apart. Broker teardown skips brokers that belong to live workers, and a worker's terminal write overwrites a false `failed`. On 2026-09-25 this bug killed a live Sol turn: the job was falsely finalized and SessionEnd then shut down its broker.
- **Prompting skill**: the internal `gpt-5-4-prompting` skill is replaced by `gpt-6-prompting`.

The work was done by `gpt-6-sol` jobs and steered live; Claude Opus 5.5 reviewed it and ported the prompting skill.

- [x] `pnpm run typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test`: 23 unit and 137 integration tests, including new regression tests for concurrent launches, the reconciler with a live pid, two-sample finalization, worker overwrite of a false failure, the Astra effort policy, and alias resolution

author: yasyf
body:
In a monorepo with about 4,400 local branches and Graphite squash-merge landings, three `ccx vcs` paths broke down. A spent GraphQL budget failed a ship after its push and submit had already landed. `prune` missed squash-landed branches. `ship --dry-run` on an untracked branch took about 5.5 minutes.

**Pull request writes go through REST.** A ship's title and body restate now runs `gh api -X PATCH repos/<nwo>/pulls/<n>` in place of `gh pr edit`, so it draws on the REST core budget. The GraphQL budget no longer matters here. The body goes in as `-F body=@<path>`. gh reads an `@` value as the file's raw string, with no type coercion: `POST /markdown` with `-F text=@file` rendered files holding `true` and `123` back as text.

`stack drop` moves to REST the same way. Its branch lookup uses `pulls?head=<owner>:<branch>` (newest first, the PR `gh pr list --limit 1` resolved), its read-back uses `pulls/<n>`, and its retarget and reopen use `PATCH pulls/<n>` with `base=` and `state=open`. REST reports a merge as `closed` plus `merged_at`, so reads map that back to `MERGED`, the state the drop logic already compares against.

If a restate still fails, the error says the push (and on the graphite lane, the submit) already happened. It then names the `gh api` commands that finish only the restate: the one that failed and every one after it. A caller can finish the job without re-running the whole ship. Each argument is single-quoted for the shell, a body read from stdin retries as `-F body=@-` because ship deletes its temp file on exit, and a pending `--draft`/`--publish` transition is appended as its `gh pr ready` command. `gh pr ready` failures get the same wording; REST has no draft toggle, so that call stays on GraphQL.

**`prune` finds squash landings on the graphite lane.** `git branch --merged` never matches a squash-landed branch. Prune now also asks Graphite's `pull-request-info` about every live branch that ancestry didn't already mark as merged, 100 head refs per request with up to 4 requests in flight. A branch counts as landed only when its PR is `MERGED` and the PR's newest version (by `createdAt`) has exactly the branch's local head as its head. A branch carrying a commit the merged PR didn't is kept. Branches that gt reports as diverged, or that a worktree holds, are excluded the same way ancestry-merged ones are. `--dry-run` reports landed branches as `would delete N branches whose pull request squash-landed: …`.

`git branch -d` refuses a branch that never reached trunk, so landed branches are deleted in one `git update-ref --stdin` transaction. Each `delete refs/heads/<b> <sha>` in it carries the merged head as its old value, and if any branch moved after the plan, git refuses the whole transaction. `update-ref` deletes a checked-out branch without complaint, so the worktree holders are read again right before it and a branch checked out since the plan stops the apply. The graphite rows of landed branches are forgotten, and their children are reparented through the existing `pruneReparent` path.

**`ship --dry-run` asks git once for contained branches.** `dryRunNearestTracked` used to fork one `git merge-base --is-ancestor` per tracked branch. Now one `git for-each-ref --merged=refs/heads/<branch> refs/heads/` lists the branches the ship branch contains. That list is intersected with gt's tracked set, and only those survivors are ordered. The answer and the name-order tie-break don't change.

Tests: the `stack drop` fake now serves the REST routes. The ship tests assert the PATCH argv and cover a restate failure on both lanes. The Graphite API stub can report MERGED PRs with versions, listed newest first so a reader that takes the last entry fails. New prune tests cover landed, moved, held, diverged, and open branches, a squash branch that moves between plan and apply, and the 100-ref batching. A dry-run test checks that no ancestry check runs on a tracked sibling the branch doesn't contain; that test fails against the old loop.

author: w0nder-official
body:
> Stacked on #242. Review in order: #242 → this → the approvals PR.

## Summary

- Adds `docs/specs/2026-09-25-ota-release-control-design.md`, the decided scope and order for the OTA product (#99). The five phases are:
  1. **Gate existing OTA tools.** Mocco releases the team's EAS, hosted CodePush or hot-updater publishing token only to a resumed run.
  2. **Version policy and native force update.**
  3. **Expo Updates hosting**, as already designed.
  4. **A CodePush-compatible device layer**, with the three device endpoints only.
  5. **Crash-driven auto pause.**
- **One direction rule for all phases.** Changes that add risk are gated. Changes that remove risk apply at once, are audited, and get a post-hoc review.
- Adds CodePush research: `research/codepush-technical.md` covers the protocol, read from the archived Microsoft sources, and `research/codepush-market.md` covers npm demand, Korean migration cases, 2026 pricing per MAU and Korean program-control rules.
- The existing OTA design is now scoped to phase 3, with a pointer to the new spec. The roadmap's Wave 1 entry and its competitor claim are updated.
- **Not here:** code. The approvals slice (#114) and the version policy slice come next in the stack.

## Why

The research changed the plan.
- **Delivery is a commodity:** Cloudflare self-host costs about $5–20/month at 1M MAU, and Bitrise CodePush is free up to 100K MAU.
- **The gap is specific.** Competitors now sell audit and roles on enterprise tiers. None offers an approval gate before an OTA push, customer-verifiable audit, or CI publishing without a long-lived token.

Starting with Expo hosting, as the old design did, would spend the longest build on the commodity part. Phases 1 and 2 deliver the differentiated part first and reuse existing code: the credential broker, the gates and the audit chain.

Alternatives weighed:
- **Hosting first:** slowest to ship, and it competes on price.
- **CodePush compatibility first:** it starts on the weaker protocol, where signing doesn't cover the selection metadata and replays are possible.
- **Full CodePush management API and CLI compatibility:** this would bring back long-lived tokens and ungated promotion, which is what Mocco sells against.

Trade-offs, stated in the spec:
- In phase 1 the publishing token is static once released to a runner.
- In phase 1 the direction rules are procedural rather than cryptographic. They become enforced in phase 3, where Mocco owns the channel state.
- Mapping OTA to the Korean Art. 29 program-control rule is an interpretation that must be confirmed with a fintech security team before it is used in marketing.

## Verified

- `yarn docs:lint`: 76 docs, 0 errors.
- No Korean characters in the added research. Korean terms were translated, and Korean URLs were percent-encoded.
- The full `yarn verify` mirror passed in pre-push.

- Introduced a cohesive color palette (`C` object) for consistent theming across map elements (ground, blocks, parks, water, streets, etc.)
- Completely rewrote the `lightStyle()` function to:
  - Filter out 3D extrusions, raster/hillshade layers, and noisy symbol layers upfront
  - Remove non-vector sources to reduce data overhead
  - Apply granular color and opacity rules for different feature types (fills, lines, symbols)
  - Add pattern removal for hatch patterns that look pixelated when tilted
  - Implement zoom-dependent opacity for buildings (fade out at lower zoom levels)
  - Add text halos and custom colors for labels and waterway text
- Updated lighting configuration with warmer tones and adjusted intensity/position for better depth perception
- Added sky configuration with fog and atmosphere blending for enhanced 3D effect
- Refined building extrusion colors with a gradient from warm stone (low buildings) to cool glass (tall towers)
- Increased building extrusion opacity and adjusted minzoom from 13 to 14

**Performance Optimizations:**
- Implemented scroll event throttling with a `ticking` flag to prevent excessive `onScroll()` calls
- Reduced intersection observer root margins (1200px → 600px for init, added explicit 600px for visibility)
- Added visibility check in `onScroll()` to prevent map redraws when section is off-screen
- Added `pixelRatio` capping (max 2x) and increased tile cache size for better performance on high-DPI displays
- Reduced map section height from 330vh to 240vh (200vh on mobile)

**UI/UX Refinements:**
- Adjusted journey section padding, gaps, and spacing for better visual hierarchy
- Refined timeline styling with smaller dots, adjusted positioning, and reduced padding
- Updated typography sizes and line heights throughout the journey section
- Added `decoding="async"` to pin card images for non-blocking image loading
- Removed backdrop-filter from glass cards over the map canvas (performance optimization)

**CSS Optimizations:**
- Consolidated spacing values using `clamp()` for better responsive scaling
- Reduced overall padding and margins in the journey/timeline sections
- Adjusted font sizes and line heights for improved readability at different viewport sizes

body:
## Phase 11 — persona-conditioned fly circuits (shadow-first, final build phase)

**Design (non-negotiable):** persona changes neural initial conditions and gains, **never** final action scores. `playfulness → +0.2 to play action` is forbidden; the implemented pattern is `playfulness → CX engagement gain / MB plasticity / DN vigor → changed circuit trajectory → changed behavioral preference`.

**Architecture:** SOUL.md (untouched, non-drifting) → documented persona defaults → per-identity Neural Personality State → CX/MB/GF/DN circuit modulators → Aiko-specific neural trajectory → behavior → Phase-10A dopamine/eligibility → bounded personality update.

### New: `cognition/fly_persona/`
- `state.py` — per-identity traits (curiosity, playfulness, attachment, calmness, exploration ∈ [0,1]); defaults documented from SOUL.md's Personality section; JSON persistence under `~/.aiko/data/fly_persona/`; save/load/reset/describe; drift clamp ±0.30 around defaults; **never modifies SOUL.md**; never raises
- `modulators.py` — trait→gain mapping, all multiplicative factors on existing circuit params clamped [0.5, 1.5]: curiosity→CX novelty gain/threshold, exploration→heading persistence, playfulness/attachment→engagement gain + MB plasticity + DN vigor, calmness→GF urgency sensitivity (functionally a higher interrupt threshold)
- `plasticity.py` — the **only** trait writer, called from `credit_event`; per-event |Δ|≤0.02, 3-event cooldown, DA-gated, `scope="real"` only (sim/replay never reshape personality)
- `trace.py` — per-turn JSON explainability record (trait → gain → effect) into the NeuralState influence ring; data for a future Studio panel (panel not built)

### Mode: `AIKO_FLY_PERSONA_MODE=off|shadow|live` (default shadow)
Shadow computes + logs gains, applies nothing. Hooks (all fail-soft, identity in shadow): `TemporalCX.step(gains=...)`, `tick_cx_temporal` fresh-urgency scaling, `teach_gain_for` × MB plasticity, `_gf_urgency` × urgency sensitivity, `body_drive` × vigor, per-turn trace in `apply_turn_priors`.

### QA
- 27 new tests (`tests/unit/test_fly_stage11_persona.py`): defaults, clamps, rate caps, cooldown, shadow-no-modulation, persistence round-trip, reset, dopamine-only plasticity, **seeded FlyWorld A/B** (same scenario, only curiosity 0.7→1.0 via the dopamine path → CX trajectories `[0.0,0.276,0.525]` vs `[0.107,0.500,0.873]`, winner flips familiar→novel with identical LLM priors, no reward shaping), conscience-veto supremacy (veto flag uncleared in live persona mode; fly never applies override toward vetoed candidate)
- Neighboring suites: 260 passed; 11 failures byte-identical to clean `origin/dev` (pre-existing env issues: missing optional deps)
- Full `tests/unit/`: 70 failed / 826 passed on branch vs 70 failed / 799 passed on clean dev — **identical failure and error sets**, delta is exactly the 27 new tests
- Per-turn overhead: ~65µs live, ~45µs shadow, 0 off (measured, not estimated)
- Caveats: no Jetson measurement; no live behavioral validation (shadow default); Studio panel not built; prior-fallback on veto/ambiguity is pre-existing action-selection behavior, unchanged

**Do not merge yet — user merges Aiko-chan PRs.**

Second phase 1 PR from the [RPP Debt Ledger](https://claude.ai/artifact/NjkGa4wzYbRHb4oxZb3jcd).

## untrusted-input-gaps
- **Imported scans:** ranks are renumbered 0..n-1 in their order. A rank of 4e9 made `slots` a sparse array that every render walks (the tab froze), and a repeated rank hid a card. Duplicate usernames, and post authors that aren't a name or `[deleted]`, are rejected.
- **Archive manifest** (`parseManifest`): the subreddit name must match `\w{2,21}`, and each file must sit under its own `r/<key>/`. A `*_to_utc` more than a day past the page's clock is rejected, because it would make `beforeFacts` skip the API for recent activity.
- **API:**
  - `getPost` throws on a bad `created_utc`, a bad subreddit or a mismatched id, instead of sending `before=NaN` on every later query.
  - A 200 reply with no `data` field is retried as a bad response, rather than read as "post not found".
- **Links:** subreddit names and post ids from the API are `encodeURIComponent`-ed in reddit.com links (`redditPostUrl`, `redditSubredditUrl`).
- **Options:** `clampScanNumbers` (tested, in `core.js`) also clamps `maxUsers` and `cacheDays`, so `cache=Infinity` or `max=1e400` from a share link falls back to a sane value.

## csv-unknown-vs-zero
- When the post is older than the `years` window, the target `*_before` cells are empty instead of `0`, which read as "no activity".

author: identity-wael
body:
Closes #366.

Per ADR-0006, Cloud Tasks queues now **store** IAM policies. **No RPC consults a stored policy**, and dispatch is unaffected.

**IAM.** `GetIamPolicy`, `SetIamPolicy` and `TestIamPermissions` on `projects/*/locations/*/queues/*` use the shared `internal/iampolicy` from #365, so the semantics are identical:
- a stale etag is ABORTED;
- conditions and audit configs are UNIMPLEMENTED with the field named;
- version 3 without conditions is accepted;
- every requested permission is returned.

The policy is kept on the queue record. Every queue write is a read-modify-write of the whole record, so pause, resume and purge keep it. It goes with `DeleteQueue`, is cleared by reset and is captured by `state save`.

**The gap the Terraform item exposed: Cloud Tasks had no JSON API.** Terraform's `google_cloud_tasks_queue` and `_iam_member` use REST. So:
- `grpctransport.Server.ServeHTTP` optionally serves a JSON handler on the gRPC port. An h2c split sends `application/grpc` requests to gRPC and everything else to JSON, the same split Secret Manager already uses. `TestServeHTTPSharesThePortWithGRPC` covers it.
- `tasks.RESTServer` transcodes the existing gRPC methods: create, get, list and delete queues; the `:pause`, `:resume` and `:purge` verbs; and `:getIamPolicy` (GET and POST), `:setIamPolicy` and `:testIamPermissions`. It uses protojson and refuses unknown fields.
- `PATCH` (UpdateQueue, not implemented over gRPC either) and every task method over JSON return **UNIMPLEMENTED**.
- `apierror.From` now keeps a gRPC status's code, so an embedded-Unimplemented method answers 501 over REST instead of 500. The gRPC path already passed statuses through, so it's unchanged.

**Terraform, measured locally first.** With the Tasks server in-process behind a logging proxy, and egress blocked with `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:1`, `google_cloud_tasks_queue` plus `google_cloud_tasks_queue_iam_member` applied, a second plan found **no changes**, and destroy removed both. The provider's calls were POST queues, GET queue, POST `:getIamPolicy`, then POST `:setIamPolicy` with `version: 3`. `cloudburrow terraform` now sets `cloud_tasks_custom_endpoint`, and the env golden is updated.

**Tests**
- Compat: `TestQueueIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced` uses the official `cloudtasks` client for the round trip, a new etag, a stale etag ABORTED, a condition UNIMPLEMENTED, and TestIamPermissions.
- Compat: `TestTerraformAppliesAndDestroysThroughTheWrapper` now also applies the queue and its iam_member. It reads the binding back through the SDK, checks the targeted plan is clean, and checks the queue is gone after destroy.
- Unit: `TestRESTQueueAndIamPolicy` replays Terraform's JSON calls in order, plus 409, 400 for an unknown field, and 501 for PATCH, tasks and an unknown verb.

**Docs:** `compatibility.md` gets ***Stored, not enforced*** rows, a JSON API row (Partial) and the Terraform rows. README and `status.md` are updated, and the coverage registry now marks the methods implemented.

`make check`, `go run ./tools/coverage -check` and `go vet -tags compat ./test/compat` pass.

author: sdcb
body:
## Summary

Adds a `cuda` backend (`--backend cuda`) for NVIDIA GPUs, mirroring `MetalBackend`'s structure. On this machine (RTX 3080 Ti, Q4_K_M, threads=8) it measures **~6.1k tok/s prefill** and **~172 tok/s decode** vs CPU's 420/29 — and vs llama-bench's 14378/336 on the same model (currently ~42%/~51% of llama).

## Architecture

- **Vendored TensorSharp CUDA kernel set** (`native/cuda/vendor/tensorsharp_kernels.cu`, verbatim @ `fe0be2749b6e3055543c33e36d76f7468d8947e4`, see `vendor/README.md`): dp4a/MMQ quantized matmuls, cuBLAS prefill GEMMs, GQA decode/prefill attention, RMSNorm/RoPE/SiLU, plus the driver/cuBLAS interop layer under `Backends/Cuda/`. Loads committed PTX via the driver API — no CUDA toolkit needed at runtime, only `nvcuda`.
- **HyMT-specific kernels** (`native/cuda/hymt_kernels.cu` → `native/ptx/hymt_kernels.ptx`, built by `native/cuda/build-ptx.ps1`):
  - `hymt_rows_to_head_first_*`: flat `[seq][heads*dim]` → head-first `[head][cap][dim]` KV layout (f32, bf16 for `UploadKv`, and a `dyn` variant that reads the write position from device memory so it works inside a captured graph).
  - `hymt_add_rmsnorm_f32`: fuses `h += b` + following RMSNorm (one node instead of two).
  - `hymt_attn_prep_f32`: per-layer megakernel doing rope(Q,K) + per-head rmsnorm + KV-cache append in one launch (grid = `heads + 2*kvHeads`).
  - `hymt_matvec_q4k/q6k_q81_f32`: warp-per-row decode matvecs — the vendored one-CTA-per-row vec kernels measured ~2–3x off DRAM bandwidth; `HYMT2SHARP_CUDA_MATVEC=0` reverts to them.
- **CUDA-graph decode**: after the first scalar step the whole decode step (~450 nodes) is captured once and replayed with one `cuGraphLaunch` per token. Per-step values (token id, kv-write pos, rope pos) travel via pinned host buffers re-read by captured HtoD nodes + a `dyn` device buffer read by the prep/attention kernels; `HYMT2SHARP_CUDA_GRAPH=0` disables.
- **Node-count reduction**: same-type weight rows are concatenated at load (`qkv`/`qk`/`gu` fused weights) so each projection is one matmul, and the q8_1 activation quantize is shared between consecutive matmuls reading the same buffer.

## Perf (Q4_K_M, this machine)

| | HyMT2Sharp cuda | llama-bench |
|---|---|---|
| pp512 | ~6150 tok/s | 14378 |
| tg128 | ~172 tok/s | 336 |

Remaining gap is dominated by kernel-granularity: ~450 serialized nodes/token (~4µs/node floor) plus matvec exec — reaching llama parity needs flash-attention-style KV fusion / fewer kernels per layer. Prefill uses the vendored dequant→F16→cuBLAS path; llama's int8 MMQ kernels don't exist in the vendored set, so ~14k is out of reach without writing Q4_K MMQ.

STQ1_0/Q2_0C have no CUDA kernels — they throw and the fallback is `--backend cpu`. `HYMT2SHARP_CUDA_TIME=1`/`=2` print GPU ms/tok and a per-op breakdown via events.

PTX is committed; `build-ptx.ps1` rewrites `.version` 9.4→8.7 because driver 13.0 rejects nvcc 13.4's PTX (CUDA error 222).

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/909f163fbac444c6a46a6d5c6008651f
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/909f163fbac444c6a46a6d5c6008651f?variant=devin
