author: kimgyuilli
body:
## Why

`main` 보호 규칙이 존재하지 않는 `build` 체크를 요구해 정상 CI를 통과한 PR도 필수 체크를 충족하지 못했습니다. 기존 관리자 우회 설정 아래에서는 이 규칙이 실패한 CI를 막는 보장도 제공하지 못했습니다.

## What

- GitHub 브랜치 보호의 필수 체크를 `build`에서 실제 CI의 `gate`로 교체
- D-037 계획, API 적용 결과, 검증 기록을 문서화
- D-043의 선행 조건과 현재 게이트 범위를 실제 상태에 맞게 갱신

## How

PR #140 head에서 `gate`가 GitHub Actions 앱 `15368`의 성공 체크로 발행된 것을 확인했습니다. GitHub API의 필수 체크 설정만 `gate`와 앱 ID `15368`로 바꾸고 `strict=true`를 유지했습니다. 관리자 우회, 대화 해결 요구, 강제 푸시 설정은 변경하지 않았습니다. CI 워크플로 코드는 변경하지 않았습니다.

## Test plan

- 변경 후 GitHub API 재조회: `contexts=[gate]`, 앱 ID `15368`, `strict=true` 확인
- 전체 보호 설정 재조회: `enforce_admins=false`, `required_conversation_resolution=false`, `allow_force_pushes=false` 유지 확인
- `scripts/ci-release-gate-lint.sh`: 실제 워크플로 통과
- `scripts/ci-release-gate-lint.sh --self-test`: 실패 주입 포함 6/6 통과
- `./gradlew test`: 성공, 4분 36초, 49 tasks 중 2 executed와 47 up-to-date
- `hpx_consistency_precheck`: 경고 0건

## 리뷰 이력

- 등급: M
- 별도 Codex 리뷰 미호출

## 관련

- D-037, `docs/plans/task-d037-branch-protection.md`
- D-043: 최종 필수 검증과 이미지 승격 경계 재설계
- PR #140: 실제 `gate` 체크 발행 근거

## 미충족

- 실제 실패 PR의 병합 UI는 새로 재현하지 않았습니다. 보호 설정 읽기 결과, 실제 check-run, 실패 전파 lint를 각각 확인했습니다.
- 기존 `enforce_admins=false` 정책은 유지했습니다. 현재 필수 `gate`는 test와 guards를 집계하며 lint, 이미지, e2e는 D-043에서 판단합니다.

author: rieki777
body:
## What changed

This fixes defect 12 in the Governance Canvas plan: the Village Brain audience does not stick. That becomes a leak once canvas sections open to members.

1. **A section's audience is now a stored choice.** `briefWrite` in `server/lib/villageBrain.ts` used to write `input.audience ?? spec.audience` on every save. So a section an admin opened to members closed again on its next text edit. And if a registry default ever became "member", the same line would reopen a row an admin had closed. It now writes `input.audience ?? existing?.audience ?? spec.audience`. A text-only save keeps the stored audience, and only a new row takes the registry default. A revision row is still written on every change, including a change that only touches the audience.
2. **An admin can close a section again.** `PUT /api/admin/brain/:section` accepts `"admin"` as well as `"member"`, through `briefAudienceFromBody`. Any other value, or no value, means "keep the stored audience", so a bad value can never open anything.
3. **Strangers read an allowlist.** `briefForPublicPrompt`, which builds the public guide's prompt on /work-with-us and /propose-quest, now reads only `STRANGER_READABLE_SECTIONS` (aims, vision, values, language). Each section must also be member-audience and confirmed. The list can only remove rows. A section added to the registry later stays off the public prompt until someone adds it to the list by name.
4. **An account that has not been admitted gets the stranger's view** (review fix). `GET /api/village/brain` served the member view to every signed-in account. It checked `authedUser` and `isAdmin` and never read `hasMembership`. Once the audience sticks, an opened `economy` stays open. Without this fix, an invited account that has not been admitted yet could read it, and so could anybody on a fork with `membership.invite_only` off. The new `briefRowsForViewer` limits those accounts to the allowlist. Admins and members see exactly what they saw before.
5. **The audit line records the audience** (review fix). The PUT's audit text is now `brain:write:<section>:r<n>:<audience>`, so every open and close shows up in the audit log. Nothing parses this text: a grep found only the line that writes it.
6. Two comments said the strangers' prompt carries every member-audience, confirmed section. They now name the allowlist: `server/index.ts` above the public guide call, and the `server/lib/proposalPrompt.ts` header.

`server/index.ts` is line-neutral: 27070 of 27089 lines and 390 of 390 routes, the same before and after. Every edit in it is in place. The ledger row in section 27c records this claim. There is no migration, capability key, game variable or baseline change.

## Tests

- New `server/lib/villageBrainAudience.test.ts` (MySQL):
  - (a) An opened section stays open after a later text-only save.
  - (b) An explicit "admin" closes a section, and that close sticks too.
  - Revision rows are kept for every change.
  - (c) The strangers' prompt: every registry section is opened to members, with a distinctive marker in each. No non-allowlisted marker appears in the prompt, and all four allowlisted markers do. A setup check confirms those rows really were opened, so the "not present" checks cannot pass by accident.
  - The rows the GET route builds: an account that has not been admitted reads only the allowlisted markers, and a member reads the opened `economy`.
- `server/lib/villageBrain.test.ts` (no database):
  - The allowlist is pinned to exactly those four sections, and each one exists and defaults to member.
  - `briefAudienceFromBody` accepts both values and nothing else.
  - `briefRowsForViewer` narrows only a viewer who is neither admin nor member.
- Controls. Each one broke a single fix, ran the tests, watched the named tests fail for the stated reason, and restored the fix:
  - With the allowlist filter removed, only (c) failed, with `work reached a stranger's prompt`.
  - With the old `input.audience ?? spec.audience` put back, exactly (a) and (b) failed.
  - With the helper accepting only "member", only the both-directions test failed.
  - With `briefRowsForViewer` returning every row, exactly its two tests failed, with `an unadmitted account read a section a stranger may not` and `work reached an account the village has not admitted`.

Ran on the final head, each with exit 0:
- `npx vitest run` on villageBrain, villageBrainAudience, villageBrainPublic, villageMemory and proposalPrompt: 5 files, 63 tests, none skipped (local MariaDB).
- `pnpm check`
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`
- Every `node scripts/*.mjs` gate in `ci.yml`, one at a time. `check-governance-doc` passed after the restamp, which is the last commit.
- `node scripts/validate-module.mjs --diff=origin/main`: PASS, 9 checks.
- `node scripts/sql-burndown.mjs`: 714 of the 714 ceiling.
- `node scripts/dependency-audit.mjs`
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`: merges clean.

**Not run:**
- The full suite, following the repo's rule: the integrator runs it once on the composed tree.
- `pnpm build` and any e2e file. No existing e2e covers the brain routes. So three `server/index.ts` lines are not driven by any test: the PUT's `briefAudienceFromBody` call, its audit text, and the GET's `hasMembership(viewer)` argument. The library functions behind them are tested.

## Review findings

Two adversarial reviews ran on this lane.

**Fixed:**
- Medium, confirmed by both reviews: `GET /api/village/brain` gave an opened section to any signed-in non-member (item 4 above).
- Medium, confirmed by both reviews: an open or close left no trace in the audit (item 5 above).
- Low, confirmed by both reviews: the two stale comments about the strangers' prompt (item 6 above). This is a comment-only, in-place change that this lane's own diff had made necessary.

**Deferred:**
- Low: the member index (`renderIndexMarkdown`) picks sections by registry default, not by the row's audience. After an admin closes `values`, a member's index calls it "not yet written", and an opened `economy` is missing from the index even though its body is rendered. This leaks nothing, and only a direct API reader sees it. The fix belongs with the canvas lane that adds the open/close control.
- Low: no e2e drives the PUT's audience line, and a revert would stay green. That needs a build and the machine-wide heavy lock. The canvas lane should add one step to an existing e2e file when it wires the UI.
- Not a finding, noted while fixing: the GET index also lists the three newest `village_record` titles per section to every signed-in account. That predates this lane and is outside the brief.

**Refuted by the reviews:**
- Example-row audience inheritance: no code seeds example brief rows.
- The ETag counting admin rows: it reveals counts only, and it predates this lane.
- Other brief readers: none exists outside the ones listed above.
- Something relying on the old snap-back: nothing does.
- Live rows needing a backfill: none do.
- The tests passing without the fix: each control failed its named test.
- Ratchet growth or merge conflicts: none.

## Open questions for Rye

- Should the stranger allowlist stay at exactly aims, vision, values and language? Suggested answer: yes. Widening it takes a deliberate edit plus the pinned-list test.
- Should an unknown `audience` value get a 400 instead of being treated as "keep"? Suggested answer: keep ignoring it. Ignoring can only keep a section as it is, and a 400 would cost a `server/index.ts` line that has no headroom.

author: ariofrio
body:
Clamps `dimming` to each bulb's `minDimLevel` from `getModelConfig`, instead of the global floor of 1 from #207.

Bulbs report their lowest supported dimming as `minDimLevel`, and it varies by hardware, not firmware. Two of my single-head color bulbs on firmware 1.38.0:

| Product | Module | `minDimLevel` | `setPilot` with `dimming` below 10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A19 60W eq., 800 lm, Color | `ESP25_SHRGB_01` | 1 | Accepted, and 1% is visibly dimmer than 10% |
| A23 150W eq., 2550 lm, Color | `ESP24_SHRGB_01` | 10 | Accepted and read back by `getPilot`, but brightness stays at 10% |

On home-assistant/core#177502, the Mobile (`ESP20_DHRGB_01`) rejects values below 10 with `-32602 Invalid params`. So with a global floor of 1, low brightness either fails or leaves callers reporting a level the bulb isn't at.

Changes:
- `turn_on()` and `set_state()` raise `dimming` to `get_min_dimming()`. This is the bulb's `minDimLevel`, or 10 when the bulb doesn't report one (the behavior before #207).
- `getModelConfig()` remembers when the bulb doesn't support it, so bulbs on older firmware don't get asked again on every `turn_on()`. When `get_bulbtype()` has already fetched the model config, clamping needs no extra requests.
- Test fixtures for both bulbs above, using their real `getModelConfig` responses. The fake bulb now also answers `setState`.
- `test_PilotBuilder_brightness` goes back to expecting 26. Its fixture doesn't report `minDimLevel`, so it falls back to 10%, as its "10% == 26 in Hex" comment says.

Tested: `pytest` (96 passed), plus black, flake8, and mypy with the CI settings. I also ran it against both bulbs above: `turn_on(PilotBuilder(brightness=1))` sent `dimming` 10 to the ESP24 and 1 to the ESP25.

author: kazu-yamamoto
body:
`gcmFullEncrypt`, `gcmFullDecrypt` and `gcmFullEncryptMask` take three
`ByteArrayAccess` arguments and were marked `NOINLINE`. That is this module's
habit, and it is right for a wrapper called once at startup. **These are
called once per packet.**

Without specialisation the dictionaries are passed at runtime, so every
`withByteArray` and every `length` inside them is an indirect call.

## Measured, Apple M4, through the Haskell interface

| | 100 B | 400 B | 1200 B | 1440 B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0.265 | 0.343 | 0.529 | 0.661 |
| after | **0.128** | **0.175** | **0.363** | **0.412** |

The same work measured in C is 0.114 µs at 100 bytes. So the Haskell layer
was costing **0.15 µs and now costs 0.014** — the dictionaries were more
expensive than the encryption they wrapped.

## How this was found

While putting quic's packet path on this interface. The obvious suspect was
quic's own wrapper, so I measured it separately: it accounts for 0.026 µs of
the 0.291. The rest was here.

In quic, a 100-byte packet goes from 0.291 to 0.161 µs with this, and from
2.25 µs with the path it replaces.

## Scope

Six functions: the three in `Crypto.Cipher.AES.GCM` that a caller reaches
for, and the three in `Crypto.Cipher.AES.Primitive` beneath them. The other
twenty-five `NOINLINE`s in `Primitive.hs` are left alone — they are on
wrappers where the pragma costs nothing.

## Testing

3401 examples, 0 failures. quic's own suite, which includes the RFC 9001 and
RFC 9369 test vectors for Initial, Retry and short-header packets: 135
examples, 0 failures.

author: eldartri
body:
## Что здесь

Английская главная — `/en/index.html`. Переключатель языка в шапке обеих страниц.

Продукт переводится на английский (#4236), бот уже отвечает по-английски, а страница, с которой человек к нему приходит, говорила только по-русски.

**Мержить нельзя без отдельного слова Eldar: `main` в этом репозитории — это прод.** Cloudflare Pages заливает fizkult.ai с мержа.

## Имена взяты у бота, а не придуманы

Иначе человек, пришедший со страницы, не узнал бы в боте то, что ему обещали. Английские имена вычитаны из `locales/en.yaml`:

| русский | английский |
|---|---|
| норма | baseline |
| Разбор | breakdown |
| Разбор недели | Weekly breakdown |
| Готовность | Readiness |
| Утро | Morning |
| Тренерская | Coach's room |
| Часы и данные | Watch and data |

## Почему отдельный файл, а не общий `/assets/site.css`

`<style>` и `<script>` перенесены в английскую страницу **побайтно**.

Вынести общее наружу стройнее, и в обычном проекте так и надо. Здесь нет: русская страница на проде и зарабатывает, а вынос стилей даёт ей ровно один новый способ сломаться — приехать к человеку без оформления, причём не на моей машине, а у него. Ради стройности такой размен не делается.

Плата — дрейф. Она принята сознательно, и под неё сделан прибор.

## Прибор: `scripts/check-locale-parity.py`

Сверяет всё, кроме слов, — слова обязаны различаться, на то и перевод.

Оформление и скрипт побайтно · состав и порядок тегов · якоря разделов · классы · внешние ссылки · якорные ссылки · живость каждого пункта меню · переключатель языка · карта `hreflang` · `<html lang>` · кириллица в английском тексте.

### Восемь намеренных поломок, каждая покраснела нужным пунктом

| поломка | ждали красным | |
|---|---|---|
| класс потерян | классы разные | ✅ |
| якорь раздела переименован | якоря разделов разные | ✅ |
| один байт оформления разошёлся | `<style>` разъехался | ✅ |
| карточка выпала | состав тегов разный | ✅ |
| ссылка на бота испорчена | внешние ссылки разные | ✅ |
| кусок остался непереведённым | непереведённый текст | ✅ |
| меню ведёт в мёртвый раздел | ведёт в несуществующий раздел | ✅ |
| переключатель ведёт не туда | переключатель должен быть один | ✅ |

Дерево после каждой восстановлено по **md5 содержимого файла** — размер тут не годится: подмена строки на строку того же размера размеру не видна.

Первая редакция стола была негодна, и стол сказал это сам: возврат обратной заменой на поломке-удалении вырождается — искать в файле пустую строку бессмысленно («якорь возврата встречается 55642 раза»). Возврат переписан на запись сохранённых байт.

## У прибора нет привода, и это сказано вслух

`.github` в этом репозитории нет, бюджет Actions закрыт с 21.09 (#4113). Прогон, который не создаётся, — стена без привода, а не проверка. Привод — человек: запускать руками перед каждой правкой любой из двух страниц. Так и записано в `EN.md`.

## Проверено на месте

Обе страницы отданы локальным сервером и сняты headless-Chrome на 1440 и 390 px: `en/` HTTP 200, оферта, политика и фавиконка с английской страницы открываются. На 390 px переключатель виден — ради этого он и не прячется, в отличие от `.est`: там уже скрыто меню, и спрячь мы ещё и его, человек на чужом языке не нашёл бы свой вовсе.

Горизонтальный обрез на 390 px в headless есть — **и он одинаков на обеих страницах**, то есть английская ничего нового не сломала. На живом телефоне я не проверял и не утверждаю, что проверил.

## Чего здесь НЕТ

- **`whitepaper.html` не переведён, намеренно.** На него никто не ссылается (проверено грепом), он обращён к тестерам перехода v1 → v2, которого больше нет, и в переводе соврал бы прямо: обещает ответ «одним сообщением, **на русском**». Перевод устаревшего документа даёт две устаревшие страницы вместо одной. Решение про русскую — за Eldar, в `EN.md` оно зафиксировано, а не принято.
- **Оферта и политика — по-русски**, идут последними отдельным решением. Английская страница зовёт их от корня и помечает «(in Russian)», чтобы человек не упирался в них молча.

## Расхождение, найденное попутно

Русская карточка зовётся **«📅 Итоги недели»**, а бот в том же месте говорит **«📅 Разбор недели»**. Расхождение старое, английского не касается — на английской стороне стоит имя бота. Русскую карточку стоит привести к имени бота отдельной правкой; здесь не трогаю.

Refs #4236

author: hneyra
body:
Closes #317

## Que cambia

Solo pruebas: el codigo de produccion de hoy es correcto en las diez horas publicadas. Esto es para que una regresion **futura** se note.

`NingunaHoraSePublicaSinSuDesfaseTest` (#188) miraba el **tipo** de cada campo publicado. `sesion.inicio().atOffset(ZoneOffset.UTC)` deja el tipo bien puesto (`OffsetDateTime`) y publica `…Z`. Se hacen las dos formas que el issue proponia:

1. **Guarda de bytecode** (`ningunaHoraPublicadaEligeSuDesfaseAMano`): ninguna llamada a un metodo de `java.time` que **devuelva un `OffsetDateTime`** (`atOffset`, `ofInstant`, `withOffsetSameInstant`, `toOffsetDateTime`, `now`…) desde **lo que se publica**: los controladores y cada record al que llega el tipo de retorno de una operacion, con el mismo recorrido que las pruebas de tipo. Queda como unico camino `ZonaHoraria.conSuDesfase`.
   - **Medido antes de escribirla**, en todo `backend/*/src/main`: 9 llamadas (`ZonaHoraria`, los cuatro `atOffset(UTC)` inocuos de Ref #273, tres `OffsetDateTime.now(reloj)` que van a JDBC y un `OffsetDateTime.of` de `DatosDePrueba`), **0** dentro del alcance (274 clases). Barrer todo el arbol daria ocho excepciones para vigilar cero casos; el alcance es lo que las separa: si sale por HTTP.
   - Centinela `lasHorasQueNoSalenPorHttpQuedanFuera`: el detector ve los cuatro de #273, y el alcance contiene los siete Resource con hora y no contiene a `AplicarUnEventoDeIdentidad` ni a `ValorMasivoRepositoryJdbc`.
2. **Por campo** (`LasHorasDeSeguridadLlevanSuDesfaseTest`): siembra las 20:00 del 4 de marzo (`2026-03-05T01:00:00Z`, escrita en UTC) y afirma `2026-03-04T20:00:00-05:00` en las cuatro horas que no tenian prueba de desfase: `SesionResource.inicio`, `AuditoriaResource.fecha`, `RespaldoResource.inicio` y `.fin` (y `ultimaRestauracionVerificada`). Las otras cinco ya la tenian: panel, trabajo parado, historial de placas y los dos del pago.

**Lo que la guarda no ve**, y lo dice su javadoc: un `OffsetDateTime` que llegue ya hecho (el de pgjdbc, en UTC) y se publique tal cual no deja llamada que leer. Eso lo cubren las pruebas por campo.

## Pruebas

**El RED, medido.** La mutacion literal del issue (en `AuditoriaResource.de`) **ya caia** en `main` desde Ref #327, pero de casualidad: `elRecorridoDelBytecodeVeLasLlamadas` nombra a `AuditoriaResource` entre los que llaman a `ZonaHoraria`, y a los otros cuatro Resource no. La misma mutacion en `SesionResource.de` salia **verde**: `:kamayuk-rentas-seguridad:test` 142 pruebas y la guarda 4, 0 fallos, rc=0. El hueco seguia abierto.

## Roturas (una cada vez, restauradas con `cmp`)

1. **La del issue**, `registro.fecha().atOffset(java.time.ZoneOffset.UTC)` en `AuditoriaResource.de` → prueba por campo roja «expected: "2026-03-04T20:00:00-05:00" but was: "2026-03-05T01:00:00Z"» y la guarda «Expecting empty but was: ["…SesionController$AuditoriaResource.de(…):399 llama a Instant.atOffset(), que le elige el desfase a mano"]».
2. La misma en `SesionResource.de` (la que antes salia verde) → 1 de 145 y 1 de 6 rojas, con `SesionResource.de(…):351`.
3. `hora.atOffset(java.time.ZoneOffset.UTC)` en `RespaldoResource.publicada` → 2 de 145 (`«fin» but was: "2026-03-05T04:30:00Z"` y `RestauracionVerificadaFronteraTest`) y la guarda con `RespaldoResource.publicada(…):451`.
4. En la prueba: quitar `records.add(clase)` del recorrido, **con la rotura 2 puesta** → la guarda sale verde (el alcance se queda en los controladores) y la centinela roja: «[el alcance: los controladores y los records que publican] Expecting TreeSet: […] to contain […]».

## Verificacion local

Contra PostgreSQL 16, rebasado sobre `e94bf21`: `:kamayuk-rentas-seguridad:build` 145 pruebas (3 nuevas), `:kamayuk-rentas-aplicacion:build` 293 (2 nuevas) mas 5 de arranque, 0 fallos y Spotless; `verificarArquitectura` rc=0. Sin cambio de produccion ni de API (`docs/50-api` intacto); frontend sin tocar.

Fila en `docs/agent/HISTORY.md`.

author: andrewchra
body:
## **Description**

In Swaps → Markets, the sort bottom sheet renders each option as a label on the left and the currently selected direction (with its chevron) on the right. The row had no truncation rules, so long translations pushed the direction off screen. In Greek, `Κεφαλαιοποίηση αγοράς` ("Market cap") consumed the whole width and the `Υψηλότερη πρώτα` value was clipped, leaving the user unable to read which direction was active.

This fixes the layout rather than the strings, so it holds for every locale:

- Each option label (`Price change`, `Volume`, `Market cap`) is now `flex: 1` with `minWidth: 0`, `numberOfLines={1}` and `ellipsizeMode="tail"`, so it shrinks and ellipsizes instead of pushing its sibling out of the row.
- The direction container is `flexShrink: 0`, so the selected value and chevron always keep their intrinsic width and stay fully visible.

All three rows get the same treatment, so the first and second options truncate too when a translation does not fit.

## **Changelog**

CHANGELOG entry: Fixed the Markets sort options so long translated labels truncate instead of hiding the selected sort direction

## **Related issues**

Fixes: N/A — UI polish found during localization review

## **Manual testing steps**

```gherkin
Feature: Markets sort options truncate long labels

  Scenario: user opens the sort sheet in a locale with long labels
    Given the app language is set to Greek (or any locale with long sort labels)
    And the user is on Swaps

    When user opens the Markets tab
    And user taps the sort control
    Then each sort option label is rendered on a single line
    And a label that does not fit is truncated with an ellipsis
    And the selected sort direction and its chevron remain fully visible on every row

  Scenario: user opens the sort sheet in English
    Given the app language is set to English
    When user opens the Markets sort sheet
    Then the labels render in full with no visual change from before
```

## **Screenshots/Recordings**

Tested in Greek on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator.

### **Before**

`Κεφαλαιοποίηση αγοράς` fills the row and `Από το υψηλότερο στο χαμηλότερο` is clipped, so the active direction is unreadable.

<!-- before.png -->

### **After**

The label truncates to `Κεφα...` and the full direction plus chevron stay visible. Same behaviour on the `Αλλαγή τιμής` row when it is the selected one.

<!-- after-market-cap.png -->
<!-- after-price-change.png -->

author: nicolaszurbuchen
body:
Steps 2 and 3 of #63. The dataset half was already there -- all 314 abilities with both halves of their effect text, `variantAbility` populated, `insertAbility` already running -- so this is the Kotlin slice and the two screens.

`core/ability/` rather than the feature, because it models the subject and the Pokemon detail will read it too when abilities join its Moves tab (#27).

## The list

A column, not the two-column grid the dex and the moves list use. An ability is a sentence, and a sentence in a half-width card wraps to four lines and stops being scannable; the design file asks for rows here for the same reason. The short effect is clamped to two lines -- the longest runs to three and a half at this width, and a card that grows to fit the worst one leaves a hole under every short name.

**The tile carries the ability's initial and is the same colour on every card.** The design tints it by category and there is no category: three attempts were built against the real 314, measured and rejected (`DECISIONS.md § Rejected for now: a classification for abilities`, #65). Tinting by generation instead would put a colour on the card meaning *when*, which is not what a reader scanning for an effect is looking for, and a hue per generation is a taxonomy wearing a palette. The letter is a real job in an alphabetical list of 314: it is what says where you are as you scroll.

**No search and no filter, which departs from #65.** That ticket wants a generation filter here, on the grounds that the list is the instrument for working out what a category axis should be. The author's call is that this list matches the other two for now and both arrive together later. Commented at the screen so the next person finds the divergence rather than the ticket.

## The detail

The sheet the other two details have -- arc, handle, nested-scroll, name rising into the toolbar -- with **the hero in the accent from the first frame**. A move's hero waits for its type before it has a colour and opens grey; an ability has no colour of its own to wait for, so there is nothing to find out.

**Details** is three figures, the effect, and the paragraph behind it. The third figure is hidden-holder count, which is the one worth a tile: "96 Pokemon, 4 of them hidden" and "96 Pokemon, all of them hidden" are different answers to the question someone opened the screen with.

**In depth is dropped where upstream's long entry repeats the short one verbatim**, which it does for 46 of the 314. A heading over a repeat of the line above it reads as a rendering fault rather than as an ability with little to say. The data layer keeps both strings; the screen decides.

**Known by** is the move detail's Learned by grid with `isHidden` in place of the learn method, `cardSlug` joined for the same reason -- only default forms are dex cards, so Alolan Sandshrew opens Sandshrew's card with the Alolan form selected.

The transition in is a **push**, per #11. A move's name travels from its card because card and hero are the same colour; an ability card is a surface with dark text on it, so the same word would change colour in mid-air.

## The tab row

`8c7019a`, its own commit. `MoveDetailTabRow`'s KDoc named the trigger -- three call sites is evidence, two is a coincidence -- and this is the third. `AppTabRow` takes labels and an index; each screen keeps its own tab enum and maps back with `entries[index]`.

## Also

`variantAbilityByAbility`, because the primary key leads with `variantSlug` and this reads the table the other way. Note that an index added to a `.sq` reaches a device only on a fresh copy: the stamp is `schemaVersion:sourceSha` and an index changes neither, so existing installs keep the unindexed table. Correctness is unaffected, and the same is already true of `moveLearnerByVariant` from #68.

## Verified

All five local checks green, plus `:androidApp:assembleDebug`. **Not yet run on a device** -- happy to install and walk both screens if you want that before merge.

## Not in here

Abilities on the Pokemon detail's Moves tab (#27). `core/ability/` now exists, so that is unblocked and small.

author: devthejo
body:
Was stacked on #1753 (it needs `secrets.ProviderMoonshot` and the anthropic-wire facade slots); #1753 landed as `76aeef26`, so this is now rebased onto `main` and stands alone — 2 commits.

Arbitration this implements: at the org and platform tiers, a **pinned provider funds its own slot**.

## The gap

The shared tiers fill one credential per **wire family**, so a tenant whose org or platform holds both an Anthropic and a Moonshot key is served anthropic alone — and a node pinned `provider: moonshot` is then refused, correctly, with its funding one row away. Measured on the platform tier before this change:

```
platform holds anthropic AND moonshot -> anthropic="platform-anthropic" moonshot=""
platform holds zai AND moonshot       -> zai="platform-zai"             moonshot=""
tenant holds BOTH (team scope)        -> both funded  (never gated, unchanged)
```

Not specific to the provider that exposed it: the same rule already did this to z.ai.

## The rule, and the three properties that make it safe

**A run that pins nothing keeps the one-key-per-wire-family rule, byte for byte.** The exception is keyed on a set derived from the run's own routes; an empty set leaves the fills exactly as they were.

**A key filled this way serves only the routes that NAME its provider.** It rides its own channel, `RunBundle.PinnedAPIKeys`, rather than `APIKeys` — so the delegates' default precedence cannot see it by construction, not by a guard every reader has to repeat. That is load-bearing: the anthropic wire ranks the facade slots **first**, so a Moonshot key in the default map would reroute every *unpinned* node of the run onto Kimi, past the tenant's own forfait, on the deployment's account. The read sites are the ones that already know the route names the provider — the `claude_code` delegate under an explicit `provider:` hint, a claw node whose model spec carries the `<provider>/` prefix, and the in-process registry lookup, which is called with the provider its spec named.

**The pinned set is frozen at launch** (`store.Run.PinnedProviders`) and replayed by every resume. A resume re-resolves its source, so re-deriving would let a program the launch never approved decide what an in-flight run is funded with.

## One chokepoint, not one guard per launch path

`resolveAndSealCredentials` is the only caller of both shared fills, and it has exactly two callers: `SubmitLaunch` and `SubmitResume`. Schedules, the dispatcher and triggers all publish through the launch (they differ in `spec.SourceRef`, not in the funding path); local non-cloud launches have no tiers at all. So the set is derived once at the launch, stamped, and replayed — the resume never re-derives.

The derivation is `model.EffectiveProviders`, the walk the pool's wants derivation and the run-doc fingerprint stamp already share, so the three surfaces cannot disagree about what a run targets. It reads `Providers` and deliberately ignores `NarrowSafe`: narrowing a request must fail **open**, funding must fail **closed**. An unresolvable route — a subbot's inner nodes, an explicit `auto`, a `{{vars.…}}` provider — therefore contributes no pin, its slot stays unfillable, and its node is refused by name. A missing pin costs a loud refusal; an invented one would hand a run a credential nobody asked for.

`iterion remote credentials preview` applies the same exception, so what it lists is what the launch will grant.

## Found by grepping the class, not by reading the diff

- the output **secret guard** seeded itself from `APIKeys` alone — a pinned key would have appeared **unredacted** in node output and logs (now `EveryKeyForRedaction`, named so a default-precedence reader cannot mistake it for spendable credentials);
- the usage-cap **scope** walk read presence from `APIKeys`, so a run funded only by an org's pinned key metered on the **platform** ledger instead of the org's;
- `supervise.ctxFundsProvider` and `secrets.SubscriptionOAuthOnly`, both asked per **named** provider, answered "not funded" for a funded one;
- the forfait crossing's `heldAnthropicWireAPIKey` must **not** count a pinned key — it asks whether the tenant brought its own instrument. Verified, with a test.

Left alone on purpose: the per-credential **spend ledger**'s default walk (it cannot see a `provider:` hint at all — a pre-existing imprecision this does not touch), and `backend: pi` / `codex` (pi would need the task threaded into `piResolveEnv`; until then a pinned pi node is refused rather than mis-routed).

## Falsification — seven mutants, each red on its own assertion

Every bench carries both directions on one bank, so neither half can pass inertly.

| mutant | red |
|---|---|
| the pinned exception removed from `fillable` (both tiers) | `PinnedAPIKeys[moonshot] = "", want the platform key` |
| the pinned key landed in `APIKeys` (the naive form) | `APIKeys[moonshot] = "platform-moonshot" — a pinned-only key in the default map reroutes every unpinned node onto another vendor` |
| the delegate's default precedence allowed to read pinned keys | `an unpinned node was served "platform-moonshot"`, and the run's forfait lost |
| the meter's bundle default no longer skipping a pinned slot | `forSource("") = …fp:fp-moonshot`, want the run's own credential |
| claw forwarding a pinned key to every node | `MOONSHOT_API_KEY crossed for an anthropic node` |
| the resume re-deriving instead of replaying | red in **both** directions: a source that gained a pin funds it, one that dropped it loses it |
| the launch stamp dropped | `run.PinnedProviders = [], want [moonshot]` |

The controls — the unpinned-run bench and the tenant-key bench — stay green under all seven.

## Review round

Three findings from the first review are fixed in the second commit, each falsified by a mutant — all three were the same class this branch closes (a reader walking `bundle.APIKeys` alone), and all three newly reachable because a pinned key is the first credential to live outside that map:

- **`[high]`** the required-credential gate refused the launch this feature exists to enable (`no tier holds a credential for any of them`, with the key sealed in the same bundle);
- **`[medium]`** the run recorded the pinned key's fingerprint while `credential_tiers` and the granted-credential audit line named nothing — the line now says `pinned-routes-only`;
- **`[medium]`** a shared tier's pinned key metered on the *tenant's* private ledger; the scope now travels with the slot (platform key → platform scope, org key → org scope, the run's own → the run scope).

The other `bundle.APIKeys` readers were judged one by one rather than assumed, and the account is in the commit message: two `taken` constructions and three "does the run hold anything?" predicates are provably unaffected, and the review-topology families are left on `APIKeys` **deliberately**, with the reason at the site — those vars shape the program, and widening a run's family set because one node pins a provider would switch a mono topology to dual behind the author's back.

## Gate

Container (golang:1.26.0, no network, vendored modules): `go build` 0, `go vet -mod=vendor ./...` 0, `golangci-lint run` (v2.12.2, CI's pin) **0 issues**, `map:check` 0, `gofmt -l` empty. The touched packages' suites are green except the two failures `main` also has in this container (no `node` binary, no ssh signing key).

author: hakimlabs
body:
Build 4, founder-decided (proposal §5i; the record is also in #754). Build 3 (#753) was withdrawn for two departure regressions against main (C1, C2).

## The rule
- **Serving is evidence-only.** The §7.6 bundle, the identity log and `GET /api/v1/agents/:id/succession` (`current_public_key`) read the holder `identity_keys` and nothing else. Only evidence writes the holder:
  - **E-sov:** the id is exactly the sovereign commitment to the key, and the request proves current possession of it;
  - **E-link:** a succession link from the key the holder holds;
  - **E-mig:** a migration's binding;
  - **E-op:** an operator registration of a bare service identity;
  - **E-main:** the v42 transplant of main's registry key only.

  This half held under every review of build 3.
- **Departure is the holder, else main's rule byte-for-byte.** This covers `departureFrom`, the registration succession check, and every signature reader (`verificationKeyFor`). Main's rule is registry → chain head → exact device row.
- **Found while building (§5j):** main's rule needs main's inputs, so a keyless registration writes main's exact registry value again. The registry is never served now, so R3's harm stays closed.

## Proof
- **Differential** (`scripts/differential-vs-main.ts --probe services/relay/src/__tests__/identity-keys.probe.ts`, 12 scenarios including the decisive round's C1/C2/C3): **every rotation, recovery and admission result equals main's.** The only differences are in serving:
  - W2: a stranger's non-canonical plant is refused, and the owner's evidence-proven key is served;
  - `''` for identities no evidence has proven (the stated cost, precisely in §5j).
- **Tests:** identity-keys 31, including C1/C2/C3 regression tests; relay 1726/1726; CLI rotation 21/21; every pre-push check passed.

## Stopping rule for this PR (proposal §8)
A wrong answer is a key served that the identity never proved, or a rotation or recovery refused (or a stranger accepted) where main differs. One round of fixes is allowed; a second finding of that kind means withdraw.

Deploys migration v42 to the production relay on merge.

body:
## Summary

Split out of #6130 (PR #6258). `routes/agents/pamReconciliation.ts`'s `consumePamReconciliationRateLimit` (Redis round-trip) ran inside `agentAuthMiddleware`'s request-long `withDbAccessContext` transaction — the same #1105 shape #6258 fixed for `heartbeat` / `reliability` / `commands` / `eventlogs` / `elevation-requests`.

It was left out of #6258 because `/:id/pam/reconciliation-bindings` is a **two-segment** action, and the self-managed opt-out matcher (`isCoreAgentPath` + `SELF_MANAGED_DB_CONTEXT_ACTIONS` in `middleware/agentAuth.ts`) only handled single-segment actions.

## Changes

- `middleware/agentAuth.ts`: adds `SELF_MANAGED_DB_CONTEXT_TWO_SEGMENT_ACTIONS` (absolutely anchored the same way as the existing single-segment set — exact path length AND both segments must match, so a crafted extension-gateway tail can't opt out) with one entry, `['pam', 'reconciliation-bindings']`. ## Summary

`cost --summary` now names the repository and branch it covers in its `Scope:` caption. The scanned-files column now says what it counts. An agent reading the cost block in a PR body can no longer mistake a one-repo, one-branch figure for an account-wide one and ask for per-PR re-approval.

Fixes GH-1088.

- **Caption.** `Scope: this repository only, <branch clause>. This account only, <window>.` The branch clause has four shapes: `branch X`, `branches a, b`, `all branches`, and `no branches`. It reflects the same `--branches` filter that produced the figures.
- **Column label.** The first column of the scan table reads `Transcript files scanned (before branch/date filters)`. Columns 1 and 2 ignore `--branches` and `--since`; columns 3 and 4 apply both.
- **Pre-clearance pointer.** `pr-description/SKILL.md` ties the "embed without asking for per-PR approval" rule to exit 0 and the opt-in sentinel, and cites `docs/private-project-redaction.md` § "Publishing a tooling measurement".
- **Docs.** `docs/transcript-analysis.md` is the single home for the caption shapes, the echo hazards, and the disclosed-fields paragraph. `README.md` and `docs/hooks.md` now point to it instead of listing fields. `docs/scripts.md`, the `transcript-analysis` and `review-loop-cost-audit` skill bodies, and `CHANGELOG.md` carry the new caption and header text. The changelog entry also records that `/pr-description` embeds the exit-0 block without per-PR approval.
- **Tests.** New tests in `test_transcript_cost.py` cover the four caption shapes end to end, the header, and the `--since` window keeping the full scanned-file count. `test_transcript_analysis.py` pins the `--branches` parsing that the caption documents (`""`, `","`, `"a,,b"`, absent).

## Context for the reviewer

- **Branch echo is a new disclosed field.** The caption prints the wrapper's local branch name, taken from `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`. It is unescaped and can differ from the pushed head ref. Git's ref grammar bars whitespace and control characters, so the echo stays on one line. Everything else git allows renders as-is. A comma splits the name into separate entries. A non-UTF-8 ref name raises under a strict UTF-8 stdout, the wrapper exits 3, and the block is omitted. The residual is accepted and documented in the echo-hazards list in `docs/transcript-analysis.md`.
- **Owner: please re-read `docs/private-project-redaction.md` and re-clear the pre-clearance.** The doc gained one sentence: the caption echoes the wrapper's local branch name, the pre-clearance covers the wrapper path only, and a change to what the block prints reopens the bar. This change alters what the block prints, so the pre-clearance needs your explicit re-clearance.
- **Slug-collision pooling.** `--this-repo` matches project directories by lossy slug (`/` and `.` become `-`), so a checkout whose path maps to the same slug is read as this repo's and counted under the `this repository only` caption. The scanned-files count includes it whatever the filters. Priced sessions, turns, tokens, and dollars include only turns matching the branch and date filters. The pooling predates this change and is now documented in `docs/transcript-analysis.md`. The follow-up is a `cwd` identity check in `scope.py`, a fix to the `_repo_scoped_project_slugs` docstring (`scope.py:92-97`), which overstates its guarantee, and a re-check of `claude-skills/skills/transcript-analysis/SKILL.md:24` ("always scoped to this repository"). No ticket is filed yet.
- **Frozen header wording.** The scan-table header is frozen at `Transcript files scanned (before branch/date filters)` by the engineer's choice.
- **Preserved record.** The merged plan `.claude/plans/clarify-pr-cost-section.md` (row 7) says something different about this column. It is a preserved record and is not edited.

## Alternatives considered

- **Put "repo" in the column label, as the ticket words it.** The label omits it because the `Scope:` line directly above already carries the repository, and the label states the part the caption cannot: the count is taken before the branch and date filters.

- `ruff check claude/.claude/ claude-skills/` passed clean.

author: abdulrahmancodes
body: ## Context While investigating the lost-authenticator lockout (a member with 2FA in several workspaces cannot recover one workspace from another), three weaknesses in the existing 2FA code came up that are independent of any recovery feature. This PR fixes them first; the admin-issued recovery code will follow in a separate PR. ## Changes **Refuse impersonated sessions on the 2FA self-service mutations.** The impersonation branch of `getAuthTokensFromLoginToken` never runs the target's 2FA check, and `initiateOTPProvisioningForAuthenticatedUser`, `verifyTwoFactorAuthenticationMethodForAuthenticatedUser` and `deleteTwoFactorAuthenticationMethod` had no `NoImpersonationGuard`. An impersonator (workspace-level impersonation needs no 2FA at all) could therefore replace or remove a member's authenticator from the member's own Profile page, attributed to the member. All three mutations now carry `NoImpersonationGuard`, like `impersonate` and `updateServerAdminAccess` already do. **Rate-limit OTP verification.** `getAuthTokensFromOTP` had only the captcha and the settings verification had nothing. `TwoFactorAuthenticationService.validateStrategy` now consumes a token from a `ThrottlerService` bucket keyed by `(userId, workspaceId)` before any lookup (10 attempts per 15 minutes, `constants/two-factor-authentication-otp-rate-limit.constant.ts`). Both the login exchange and the settings/step-up paths go through it. `ThrottlerGraphqlApiExceptionFilter` is added to the 2FA and admin-panel resolvers so `LIMIT_REACHED` comes back as a user-input error. **Audit 2FA changes.** New `TwoFactorAuthentication` workspace event (`event-logs/emit/events/workspace-event/two-factor-authentication/`), emitted on `method_provisioned`, `method_verified` (pending → verified), `method_deleted` and `otp_rejected`, with the same `EventLogEmitterService` pattern as impersonation and server-admin events. Supporting changes: - The delete logic moved from the resolver into `deleteTwoFactorAuthenticationMethodForAuthenticatedUser` on the service so it can emit the event. Guards, checks and error codes are unchanged. - `TwoFactorAuthenticationExceptionFilter` is now applied on the 2FA resolver, so an invalid code on the settings page maps to `INVALID_OTP` instead of a generic error. ## Tests - New `two-factor-authentication.service.spec.ts`: throttle ordering and propagation, `otp_rejected` / `method_verified` / `method_deleted` events, delete ownership and not-found checks. - Resolver spec updated for the service-backed delete. - New integration suites: `impersonation/failing-impersonated-two-factor-authentication` (the three mutations are denied under an impersonated session) and `auth/two-factor-authentication/two-factor-authentication-otp-rate-limit` (limit reached after exactly 10 attempts, isolated on a user no other suite verifies codes for, Redis bucket cleared before/after). - Existing 2FA, impersonation, user-session and auth integration suites pass locally against Postgres + Redis, including two consecutive runs. ## Notes for reviewers - No schema change, no config variable, no translation catalog churn. - The per-user bucket means an attacker holding a member's password could exhaust that member's OTP attempts for up to 15 minutes. That is the standard trade-off of per-account throttling and is still gated by the captcha on the public mutation. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01DQN6YDCPTjufVtjgxS8Hrz)_

author: yahya-fazeli
body:
## What

Adds high-value unit tests for two under-covered, business-critical modules. Test-only change: no production code was modified.

## Why these targets

I measured coverage first with `node --test --experimental-test-coverage` rather than guessing, then picked targets that were both genuinely under-covered and load-bearing.

- **`src/core/concurrency.js`** — 43.75% branch coverage, the lowest of the core helpers. It backs *every* fan-out in the pipeline: the per-segment TTS loop (`stages-tts.js:61`), the alignment/timing loops (`:200`, `:268`), and the batched translation calls (`stages-ai.js:203`, `:243`). `mapLimit`'s `onSettled` hook is what drives incremental job persistence, so a regression there silently loses or duplicates progress.
- **`src/pipeline/alignment.js`** — 71.43% branch coverage on a headline feature (fitting synthesized speech into the original segment window). The uncovered branches were the timing-subtlety ones most likely to regress.

I deliberately skipped `Mutex`/`Semaphore` being unused in `src/` today — they are exported public helpers, so they still warrant coverage.

## Scenarios covered

`test/unit/concurrency.test.js` (new, 15 tests):
- `mapLimit`: `onSettled` fires exactly once per item, in index order, including for rejected items; no callback for work skipped by `shouldStop`; limit clamped to `[1, itemCount]` (a `0`/negative limit would otherwise start zero workers and hang); iterable inputs; `forEachLimit` halts at first rejection; `mapLimitStrict` rejects instead of recording.
- `Mutex`: serialization order, value propagation, and recovery after a task throws.
- `Semaphore`: bounded concurrency, FIFO permit order, clamping, and release in a `finally`.
- `sleep`: no-signal resolution, abort before and mid-flight, non-`Error` abort reason wrapped in a real `Error`, signal-like objects lacking `addEventListener`, and listener cleanup once the timer fires.
- `chunk`: batch-size clamping to at least one.

`test/unit/alignment.test.js` (+9 tests):
- Sample-rate conversion happens *before* duration is measured (44.1kHz response against a 16kHz timeline).
- Zero-length-window guards in both `alignSegment` (neutral ratio, infeasible) and `fitSegmentToWindow` (early return, no WAV encoded).
- Tempo exactly at `minTempo`/`maxTempo` is feasible (the tolerance matters at the boundary).
- Centered padding vs. front-loaded padding when `respectNaturalPauses` is off — asserted by locating the first non-zero frame.
- `gradeFit`: clipped warns, and silence takes precedence over clipping.

I wrote these by probing the implementation's actual behavior first (boundary inputs, abort timing) and asserting what it really does, rather than what it looked like it should do.

## One test I dropped

I initially added a test that `alignSegment` accepts a raw WAV buffer. It failed: the function only special-cases `typeof audio === 'string'` (base64), so a `Buffer` falls through to `toMono` and throws. Rather than document behavior the code does not have, I removed the test. (Treated as out of scope — flagging, not fixing, since the brief is test coverage.)

## Verification

```
node --test test/unit/concurrency.test.js   # 15 pass, 0 fail
node --test test/unit/alignment.test.js     # 22 pass, 0 fail
npm test                                    # 375 tests, 360 pass, 15 skipped, 0 fail
```

Coverage, measured with `node --test --experimental-test-coverage`:

| File | Lines | Branches | Functions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `concurrency.js` | 73.04 → **100.00** | 43.75 → **98.08** | 43.75 → **100.00** |
| `alignment.js` | 92.24 → **100.00** | 71.43 → **86.57** | 100.00 → **100.00** |

The 15 skipped tests are the pre-existing opt-in real-ffmpeg/Gemini suites, unchanged by this PR.

## Remaining gaps

- `alignment.js` retains ~13% uncovered branches: the deadband boundaries in `fitSegmentToWindow` and `silenceRatio` interval edges. Low value relative to what is now covered.
- `cancellation.js` (77% branches) and `stages-media.js` (47%) remain the next-best candidates. `CancelToken.register/child/race/createController` are only exercised indirectly via the orchestrator, and the `vocalSeparationStage` branches need an engine double.

author: valerielinc-ops
body:
Refresh evergreen di `costo-pendolare-auto-ticino-2026` (issue corpus #1810, parent sito valerielinc-ops/frontaliere-si-o-no#9629). Il costo annuo dell'auto poggiava su un prezzo della benzina «ipotizzato» e su una tariffa Arcobaleno approssimata, e la FAQ fiscale prometteva detrazioni che non esistono. Sono cambiati solo i fatti verificati su fonte ufficiale; parcheggio, assicurazione, manutenzione e ammortamento restano stime redazionali, ora dichiarate come tali.

## Implementato

- **Benzina, nelle 4 lingue.** Il prezzo «ipotizzato» di 1,85 €/l diventa la media nazionale della benzina self-service rilevata dal MIMIT il 24-09-2026, cioè 2,154 €/l (https://www.mimit.gov.it/it/prezzi-carburanti-media-nazionale). La spesa annua per 13.200 km a 6,5 l/100 km passa da 1.590 € (1.550 CHF) a 1.850 € (1.740 CHF). Il cambio è quello di riferimento BCE dello stesso giorno, 0,9409 CHF per euro (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/eurofxref-graph-chf.en.html). Aggiornati il blocco «Fatti chiave» e la risposta FAQ sul carburante.
- **Assicurazione e bollo, nelle 4 lingue.** La stima di 950 € resta invariata. Al cambio BCE del 24-09-2026 vale 890 CHF invece di 920 CHF.
- **Vignetta, nelle 4 lingue.** I 40 CHF sono verificati e restano invariati. Si aggiungono la fonte UDSC/BAZG e la validità della vignetta 2026, dal 1° dicembre 2025 al 31 gennaio 2027 (https://www.bazg.admin.ch/it/faq-contrassegno-e-acquisto-e-vignetta).
- **Abbonamento Como-Lugano, nelle 4 lingue.** «TILO/Arcobaleno circa 1.900 CHF» diventa l'abbonamento annuale transfrontaliero Arcobaleno da 1.638 CHF (2a classe, tariffa valida dal 14.12.2025, https://arcobaleno.ch/it/home/abbonamenti/abbonamento-annuale-transfrontaliero). In DE, FR ed EN la forbice dei «Fatti chiave» passa da 1.300-1.900 a 1.300-1.638 CHF.
- **Totali ricalcolati, nelle 4 lingue.** Costi visibili da 3.390 a 3.580 CHF (1.740 + 40 + 1.800). Costi nascosti da 5.120 a 5.090 CHF (890 + 900 + 3.300). Totale da 8.510 a 8.670 CHF. Risparmio con il treno da «6.000 CHF» a «oltre 7.000 CHF» (8.670 - 1.638 = 7.032).
- **Excerpt e og:title.** Negli excerpt di `content/blog-meta-{it,en,de,fr}.ts`, «fino a 7.500 CHF» (in contraddizione con il totale dell'articolo) diventa «circa 8.670 CHF». In `content/seo/seo-blog.ts`, l'`ogTitle` italiano passa da «fino a 8.500 CHF» a «quasi 8.700 CHF». Titolo SEO, slug, URL e `canonicalPath` restano invariati.
- **Riga delle fonti, nelle 4 lingue.** «Analisi redazionale basata su dati TCS e stime di mercato 2026» non era verificabile: l'articolo non riporta alcun costo chilometrico TCS. Al suo posto ci sono le fonti ufficiali (MIMIT, BCE, UDSC, Arcobaleno), e la riga dichiara parcheggio, assicurazione e bollo, manutenzione e ammortamento come stime redazionali indicative aggiornate a settembre 2026.
- **FAQ fiscale, nelle 4 lingue.** La vecchia risposta diceva: «I frontalieri possono beneficiare di detrazioni fiscali per le spese di trasporto, come il costo del carburante, assicurazione e manutenzione, nelle dichiarazioni dei redditi in Italia». La nuova dice che non esiste alcuna agevolazione specifica per l'auto. In Svizzera l'imposta alla fonte comprende già deduzioni forfettarie. Chi rientra nell'Accordo CH-IT del 23.12.2020 non può più chiedere la tassazione ordinaria ulteriore, perché l'imposta alla fonte è definitiva (art. 3 par. 3; Divisione delle contribuzioni TI, https://www4.ti.ch/dfe/dc/dichiarazione/imposte-alla-fonte-1/richiesta-di-correzione-dellimposizione-alla-fonte). In Italia il reddito di lavoro dipendente è costituito da tutte le somme percepite (art. 51 c. 1 TUIR, https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.del.presidente.della.repubblica:1986-12-22;917~art51), e per carburante e manutenzione dell'auto usata nel tragitto casa-lavoro non sono previste deduzioni. Le risposte DE/FR/EN, che traducevano «frontalieri» con «Grenzen», «frontières» e «frontiers», sono riscritte con la stessa sostanza.
- **Registry.** In `content/blog-articles-data.ts` la voce `costo-pendolare-auto-ticino-2026` riceve `updatedAt: '2026-09-24'`, legato a un cambio fattuale.
- **Osservatore.** `generator/tests/evergreen-costo-pendolare-auto-ticino-2026-refresh.test.mjs` contiene 14 test. Nelle 4 lingue fissa cifre, date di rilevazione e fonti, la FAQ fiscale, excerpt, `ogTitle` e `updatedAt`. Vieta inoltre i valori superati (1,85 €/l, 8.510, 1.550, 1.590, 3.390, 5.120, 6.000, 920 CHF, la citazione TCS e la promessa di detrazioni). Sui file di `origin/main` fallisce 14/14; sul branch passa 14/14. Il test è registrato in ordine alfabetico in `CONTENT_GATES` di `scripts/ci/content-gates-main.mjs`.
- **Verifica locale dopo il merge di `origin/main`.** Con `env -u FORCE_COLOR node --test` sui 35 file di `CONTENT_GATES`: 646 test, 645 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip. `generator/tests/content-gates-main.test.mjs` passa 27/27. `faq-locale-consistency`, `faq-ts-literal-escaping`, `faq-key-anchoring` e `blog-body-syntax-gate` sono verdi, e il JSON delle FAQ si parsa nelle 4 lingue. `tsx scripts/build-api.mjs` completa (28 file, gate verdi, `updatedAt` presente in `articles.json`). `git diff --check` è pulito.

Closes #1810

## Non implementato (ancora)

- Rimisura della metrica `scripts/audit-evergreen-articles.mjs` (sul sito) (atteso 0 target stale per `costo-pendolare-auto-ticino-2026`) dopo publish-api e sync del corpus. **Stato:** `blocked: misura post-pubblicazione`
- «Da Varese a Mendrisio circa 1.300 CHF» resta invariato. L'abbonamento annuale transfrontaliero Arcobaleno copre Como, Milano e Malpensa ma non Varese, e non ho trovato una tariffa ufficiale per quella tratta. **Stato:** `blocked: nessuna tariffa ufficiale pubblicata per Varese-Mendrisio`
- Restano invariati i parcheggi (80-100 CHF a Mendrisio, 250-300 CHF negli autosili di Lugano, media 1.800 CHF), la forbice assicurazione più bollo (800-1.200 €), la manutenzione (900 CHF) e l'ammortamento (15% di 22.000 CHF). Motivo: sono stime di mercato che nessuna fonte ufficiale sostiene o smentisce, e ora sono dichiarate come stime redazionali datate. Prossimo passo: sostituirle al prossimo refresh se UST/USTAT o il Cantone pubblicano valori medi citabili. **Stato:** `per scelta`
- Costo chilometrico TCS, pedaggi autostradali italiani ed eventuale tassa sul transito non compaiono nell'articolo, quindi non c'è un fatto da correggere. Anche la deduzione svizzera per chilometro dell'auto privata non riguarda questi lettori, perché i frontalieri sotto l'Accordo 2020 non possono chiedere la TOU. Motivo: aggiungere nuove voci di costo sarebbe una riscrittura, non un refresh fattuale. Prossimo passo: valutarle in una issue editoriale dedicata se il proprietario vuole ampliare il calcolo. **Stato:** `per scelta`
- «Quasi 80.000 frontalieri» resta invariato. Il dato UST del secondo trimestre 2026 riportato dalla stampa (79.121) lo conferma. Le domande FAQ tradotte in DE/FR/EN restano goffe ma non contengono fatti errati. Motivo: nessun fatto da cambiare, e il brief vieta le riscritture di stile. Prossimo passo: issue di localizzazione separata per le domande FAQ. **Stato:** `per scelta`

body:
主人 2026-09-24 说「合」——服务端那一半（[ideahub-server#80](https://github.com/TianbinLiu/ideahub-server/pull/80)）已合并部署、线上健康，这是客户端这一半。

## 为什么

出片时真正读的是 `idLine`（`types.idLineOf`），而简介自 2026-09-18 起一个字都不进提示词。于是那天之前铸的卡出片时**只剩一个卡名**，长相由模型自己编、每段都可能不一样 —— 而产品里没有任何地方补得上（服务端那条 PATCH 今天才收下这一位；顺序不能反，反了就是「发了、被 strip、零报错」）。

## 改了什么

| 位置 | 改动 |
|---|---|
| `pages/CardDetailPage` 编辑窗 | 多一格「出片句」，`maxLength` 用 `ID_LINE_MAX`=60。标题与入口键跟着改（「改名」→「编辑」） |
| 「🎯 出片身份句」那一块 | 没写出片句的**自己的卡**从什么都不显示改成琥珀提示 + 「写一句」——老卡唯一能被发现的入口；别人的卡照旧什么都不摆 |
| `data/account.updateCardMeta` | 回滚快照改成**按这次真给了的那几位**存（原来写死三位，漏一位就是远端失败、本地留着新值，下次冷启动又变回去） |
| `api/branch.updateCardMeta` | payload 类型多一位 |

⚠ 上限两个数**有意不等**：客户端 60（产品口径，按提示词预算反推）、服务端 200（安全上界）。别顺手统一。

## 验了什么

- 本机离线全链：空出片句 → 琥珀块 +「写一句」→ 编辑窗第三格（上限 60）→ 保存 → 落库、`idLineOf` 不再兜底成卡名、那一块翻成正常显示。
- 远端那一跳对着**内存服务端**真走了一遍（与 app 同一个 payload 形状）：PATCH 200、回包带 `idLine`、**回读**也是它、`summary` 没被动。
- 服务端侧 `tests/branchAssetPublish.spec.js` 31/31（含新增 A15c）。
- `npm run build` 全绿（含 i18n 棘轮，5 条新文案已带英文）。

body:
Roadmap: RepresentationTheory

**Two `@[simp]` lemmas in `Symmetric/Specht/Extremes.lean` never fired; this PR makes them fire.** It is the `RepresentationTheory` part of the simp-firing audit of the files changed on main since 2026-09-25T00:00Z. The bug class is the one fixed in #8315 and #8722; #8722 fixed the other Specht lemmas of this file but not these two.

**Scope of the audit**
* **Files.** Every `.lean` file under `NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory`, `RepresentationTheory`, `GroupTheory` and `Algebra/Category/ModuleCat` changed on main since then (main snapshot `364643e53`). Files touched by an open PR (#8695, #8699, #8752, #8763) and `Clifford/{Correspondence,Equivalence}.lean` are skipped. That leaves 37 files.
* **Lemmas.** The 124 simp lemmas declared in those files, including the ones generated by `@[simps]` and `reassoc`.
* **Split by roadmap.** The findings in `ClassFieldTheory` and `CFSGStatement` files are in two sibling PRs. This PR has the `RepresentationTheory` ones.

**Method.** A scratch meta-program imports all 37 modules. For each simp lemma, it takes the lemma's own statement at generic arguments and runs `simpTarget` twice: once with `simp only [lemma]`, once with the default simp set. It then reads `Simp.Stats.usedTheorems` to see whether the lemma was used. I confirmed each finding by hand with `example`s in an importing file, restating the goal from the source text. Comparing the discrimination-tree keys stored for each lemma with the keys of its own left-hand side in an importing file shows the cause.

| declaration | problem | fix | before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `YoungTableau.permutationModule_ρ_polytabloid_of_rowSubgroup_eq_top` | The carrier `(permutationModule _).V` is indexed unreduced, as `Rep.V` of a `Rep` structure literal. `simp` reduces it to the monoid algebra before the lookup, so the lemma is never found. | Left-hand side stated through `dsimp% only`, the convention of #8315. | `simp only [·]`: no → yes; `simp`: no → yes |
| `YoungTableau.permutationModule_ρ_polytabloid_of_colSubgroup_eq_top` | Same. | Same. | no → yes; no → yes |

The other 6 simp lemmas of the file already fire under both `simp only [·]` and `simp`.

**Nothing else changes.**
* The proofs are unchanged. The only statement change is the `dsimp%` restatement of the two left-hand sides, which is the accepted convention; each elaborated statement is the `dsimp`-reduced form of the old one.
* The change carries a `--` code comment that says why.

**Things a reviewer should weigh**
* `Extremes.lean` has no reverse dependency in the repository, so no downstream simp lemma can be pushed out of simp normal form by the change (the failure mode of #8719). The environment-wide `simpNF` check below covers every module that mentions the polytabloids or the permutation module.
* Both lemmas have a hypothesis (`rowSubgroup t = ⊤`, `colSubgroup t = ⊤`), so `simp` fires them only when it can discharge it, e.g. `simp [h]`.

**Provenance.** Original work. The convention comes from #8315.

**Verification**
* **Build:** `lake build TauCeti.RepresentationTheory.Symmetric.Specht.Extremes` is green. Its reverse-dependency closure, computed from `import` lines, is the module itself, and it has no direct importers.
* **Lint:** full `#lint` on the changed module gives 0 errors (23 declarations, 15 linters).
* **`simpNF`:** a legacy (non-module) driver, the kind `scripts/lint-env.sh` generates, imports the 23 modules that mention `polytabloid` or `permutationModule` (all of `Symmetric/Specht`, `Symmetric/Dominance`, the permutation-module files) and runs `#lint only simpNF in TauCeti`: 0 errors in 1515 declarations.
* **Fire tests** from an importing file, on each lemma's own statement restated from the source: `simp only [lemma, h]` and `simp [h]` close both goals.
  * Control: the same `example`s against unchanged `main` all fail with unsolved goals, with the lemma reported as an unused simp argument.
* **Style:** `lake exe lint-style` exits 0. `scripts/lint-dot-notation.py` reports 0 new findings. Lines are at most 100 codepoints, and the diff has no U+0124.

author: jumplink
body:
## Summary

The socket.io integration suite passed 70/70 on GJS but printed ~24 lines like
`libsoup-CRITICAL: soup_websocket_connection_close: assertion '!priv->close_sent' failed`.
A CRITICAL is a programming error on our side, and under `G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals` it aborts
the process.

Root cause: when the peer sends a Close frame, libsoup answers it on its own right away. It
emits `closed` only after the TCP stream ends, one round trip later. Our wrappers left
`readyState` at OPEN during that gap. So a `close()` or `send()` made then reached Soup after
Soup had already sent its Close frame. In the socket.io suite the caller is the **client**:
engine.io-client closes a failed upgrade probe in exactly that gap, through
`@gjsify/websocket`. Stack traces I added while debugging showed no call from the server side
in this suite. `@gjsify/ws`'s server-side socket has the same gap, and `terminate()` after
`close()` hits it every time, so this PR fixes it there too.

## What changed

- `@gjsify/websocket` (W3C client): Soup's `closing` signal now sets `readyState` to CLOSING.
  `close()` and `send()` check the connection's own `get_state()` before calling into Soup.
  `send()` while CLOSING or CLOSED now follows the spec: the data is dropped and
  `bufferedAmount` grows. It no longer throws. A connection that ends without a Close frame
  now reports code 1006 instead of Soup's 0.
- `@gjsify/ws` server side: the same `closing` and state checks. `send()` after close hands an
  error to the callback, as ws's `sendAfterClose` does. `terminate()` never worked before,
  because Soup rejects code 1006 with its own CRITICAL and sends nothing. It now shuts the TCP
  socket down under Soup, found through the SoupIOStream's `base-iostream`. Soup then reads
  EOF and closes with 1006, the same as ws.
- `@gjsify/ws` client wrapper: before `send()`, it copies the native socket's CLOSING state,
  so the callback still hears about dropped data.
- Tests:
  - `ws/src/close-lifecycle.spec.ts` runs against npm `ws` on Node and `@gjsify/ws` on GJS,
    in both `{port}` and `noServer` modes. On GJS it also counts libsoup log records through
    `GLib.log_set_handler`.
  - `websocket/src/index.spec.ts` adds a test with a hand-rolled server. The server sends a
    Close frame and keeps TCP open, so the client stays in the closing window for as long as
    the test needs.
  - Three sockets in `ws/src/index.spec.ts` had no `error` listener. Their late connection
    error was landing in whichever test ran next.

## How it was tested (macOS 27 arm64, Homebrew gjs 1.88.1)

Fresh worktree, then a full `gjsify run build:infra` + `gjsify run build`.

- Both new tests fail without the fix. On GJS, 6 of 45 in ws: the log count is 1, and
  `terminate` times out. In websocket, `readyState` stays 1 during the closing window.
- `@gjsify/websocket`: 19/19 (gjs).
- `@gjsify/ws`: 19/19 on Node and 45/45 on GJS, with no CRITICAL or WARNING lines.
- `@gjsify/http`: 393/393 on Node and on GJS.
- socket.io integration: 70/70 on Node and on GJS, with **0** libsoup lines. It also passes
  70/70 under `G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals`. Before the fix there were 25 CRITICALs.
- devtools-cdp integration passes. undici's GJS leg can't load on this Mac, because the
  `Gda-6.0` typelib is missing; that is unrelated to this change.
- `gjsify lint` passes; `gjsify format` and `check` pass on both packages.

## Review follow-ups (second pair of commits)

- `@gjsify/ws` client `terminate()` works now. It used to call the W3C `close(1006)`, which
  throws, and the swallowed error left the socket open. `@gjsify/websocket` gains an internal
  `[kAbort]()` hook (`Symbol.for`, `@internal`, not W3C API). The socket-shutdown path is now
  one shared `abortConnection()`, used by the client hook and the server's `terminate()`.
- The server reports 1006 for every close without a Close frame, as ws does. Before, a peer
  tearing the socket down gave 1005. Soup already reports an empty Close frame as 1005.
- `CloseEvent.wasClean` follows the closing handshake, not `code === 1000`.
- Specs restore the libsoup log handler in `finally`. New cases cover `[kAbort]` and the
  client-side `terminate()`; the second is checked against npm ws on Node.
- Re-run on macOS 27 arm64: websocket 20/20; ws 21/21 on Node and 47/47 on GJS; http 393/393
  on Node and GJS; socket.io 70/70 on Node and GJS. GJS legs also pass under
  `G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals`, with 0 libsoup lines.

author: kory-io
body:
## Summary

Batch 5 — precise note→code links, links that no longer silently vanish, and correct project membership.

- **nw-674 — project membership by stable identity.** Declared project repos were matched only against the URL-derived display name (plus a URL-substring fallback), so repos indexed as `web-app` / `service` / `docs` / `website` never joined their projects (6 of 43 on a real config: `project_context` returned none of their code). One resolver (`resolve_declared_repo`) now matches by `[[repos]]` alias, path/URL, then one derived-name tier (stored name, checkout dir, URL name) with a single distinct-remote ambiguity check, then a disclosed substring fallback. Ambiguous, unresolved, alias-not-indexed and substring matches are disclosed in `list-projects`, `project-context` and MCP `project_context` (`repo_issues`). Links and features use the same resolver; a feature whose repos don't resolve no longer silently widens to every repo.
- **nw-675 — links a refresh or re-index dropped are rebuilt.** A full `brain refresh` removed every note→code link until each note was edited again, and a code re-index dropped links into changed files. A level-triggered `CodeLinkReconciler` (like the trigram/embedding reconcilers) diffs each note's stored links against what its committed text should produce and rewrites only the notes that differ — scanning off the write lease, chunked flushes, a non-blocking publication. Routes that change what links should exist record debt (vault index/refresh, repo index, materialize, project/instance removal/merge/purge, code watcher, remove/prune). Passes are spaced ≥ 10 s and log their duration; notes whose files are unreadable keep the debt and are disclosed; notes deleted on disk are treated as a stale index.
- **nw-670 — link notes to code only for real code mentions.** Every ≥ 4-char prose word was matched against every symbol in every repo (≈39 M note/section→symbol edges on a 2,000-note vault; median 12 K per note; ~3 % precision). A note now links to a symbol only when it names it as code — backticks / code fences, identifier shape (snake_case, camelCase with ≥ 2 humps, `name(`) — resolved within the note's project repos, with plain words only in exact backtick spans to types/constants, test and value definitions de-prioritised, and names defined in more than 5 files in scope linking nothing. One implementation serves the bulk pass, the vault watcher and the reconciler (watcher/bulk parity test kept). Design: `docs/architecture/project-brain.md` §5.4/§10.
- **Migration.** On first start after upgrading, the daemon drops and recreates the two `REFERENCES_CODE` tables in one transaction and one publication (1 M-edge fixture: 113 ms), then relinks every note in chunks; resumable; recorded as rules version 2 (also recorded by a fresh full index, and backed up / sealed as a compatibility-stamp artifact).
- **nw-673 — `[cross_domain]` config applies.** It was parsed but every caller used defaults; it now reaches the reconciler, both watchers, the server worker and the publication path.

### Behaviour changes (also in the README table)

- Far fewer note→code links (roughly 700× fewer on a large vault); notes link only to code they name as code, within their project.
- First start after upgrading runs the link migration in the background; `brain status` shows a `Note→code links: being rebuilt …` line (new `code_links` status object, proto field 23) and ranked reads (`brain_context`, `project_context`, `investigate`, MCP and CLI) carry `code_links_incomplete` / `code_links_pending` until it finishes.
- Six repos that were silently outside their projects join them after `nestweaver materialize-projects --config …`; ambiguous or unresolvable declared repos are reported instead of silently attaching nothing (or the wrong repo).
- Configured `[cross_domain]` stoplist/thresholds now take effect.
- Server mode and the direct code `watch` do not run the reconciler yet (tracked separately; README caveat).

## Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Enhancement
- [x] Refactoring
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Build

## Checklist

- [ ] `cargo test` passes — targeted `--all-features` crate suites locally (below); full suite in CI
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean — engine/daemon scoped clippy locally; workspace in CI
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- [x] Commit messages follow conventional commits (`type(scope): description`)
- [x] Added/updated tests for new functionality

## Testing

Each fix written test-first (failing on the prior code for the stated reason), with counterweights; mutation checks on every rule guard (14/14), reconciler guards (6/6), config propagation (2/2) and the review fixes. Locally: engine, parser, store, daemon and MCP `--all-features` lib suites for the touched areas; engine+daemon clippy; fmt. The root-binary tests (incl. `brain_context_json_keeps_code_links_disclosure` and the status renderer tests) and workspace clippy run in CI — local disk could not hold another build.

**Live evaluation (release build, on a copy-on-write clone of a real ~2,000-note / 45-repo graph):**
- Migration: old links dropped in one step (0.19–2.98 s); relink 400–430 s; 53,118–53,544 scoped links (was ~39.1 M); WAL peak ~11 MB; no corruption or checkpoint errors (`repair --dry-run` clean).
- Ranked reads during the relink: 16/16 answered, each with `code_links_incomplete` disclosure (15–36 s while chunks publish; migration-only).
- Retrieval: a note seed that names ~18 identifiers in code spans went from 0 to 8 linked symbols in its top 20; symbol seeds now return the notes that name them; `project_context` returns member code again (e.g. 0 → 111 / 169 / 19 symbols for three projects).
- Persistence: clean restart does not re-migrate (0 rewrites); crash replay (`kill -9` 10 ms after the purge) reopens cleanly and completes the migration; removing and re-adding a repo restores its project's code without a restart or manual materialize.
- Steady state vs the previous release on the same clone: settled query 0.37 s (was 0.44 s); first query after an edit 1.50 s (was 1.43 s; 1.84 s if it overlaps the per-edit link pass, tracked as a follow-up).

This PR also fixes nw-678: project→symbol membership was erased by every code re-index and only restored by a manual `materialize-projects`, so `project_context` could return no code for any project. Membership is now a durable Project→Repo edge, kept current by the daemon.

## Related Issues

Internal backlog: nw-674, nw-675, nw-670, nw-673, nw-678. Follow-ups filed: nw-676, nw-677, nw-679, nw-680, nw-681.

body: ## Sammanfattning Bekräfta i Fota väljer konto i en ren funktion (`chooseCaptureAccount`) som servern kör om: - Förvalt konto i samma valuta som kvittot behålls. - Annars används ett aktivt konto i kvittots valuta: det enda, eller det senast använda när det finns flera. - Ett nytt konto (t.ex. Bankapp SEK) skapas bara när inget aktivt konto i valutan finns. Arkiverade konton väljs aldrig. - Granskningen före Bekräfta visar konto och datum, båda redigerbara. Om ett nytt konto behövs står det «Nytt konto skapas: Bankapp (SEK)». - Vision-prompten får returnera Resor, Travel och Transport som `categoryHint`. Det går in i befintlig mappning till Transport, även på ett kvitto utan händelserader. - «Alla N rörelser finns redan» räknas från listan som visas, med singular för en rad. Kända rader visas på Inget nytt så meningen och listan är samma tal. - En makulerad rörelse (`status = voided`, schemats soft delete — ingen `voided_at`) räknas inte som «finns redan sparad». Bara en levande transaktion blockar samma fingerprint. - En confirmed-kandidat vars kanoniska transaktion är voidad, saknas eller har null-id är död. Omuppladdning med samma fingerprint uppdaterar den raden till `needs_review`, nollställer kanon-länken och skriver den nya extraktionen. Ingen ny insert, så det unika indexet `numa_candidates_user_fingerprint_unique` krockar inte. En levande kanonisk transaktion ger «Den här rörelsen finns redan.» utan insert. - När en rörelse makuleras i appen sätts länkade kandidater till `rejected` (befintligt statusvärde). Inget nytt enum och ingen migration. - Råa databasfel visas inte vid Fota-uppladdning. En levande krock blir «Den här rörelsen finns redan.» Övriga fel blir «Kunde inte spara bilden. Försök igen.» Det verkliga felet loggas med `reportError("ocr.upload")`. - Bankapp-datum som inte är full månad eller ISO släpps igenom: korta svenska månader (jul, sep., okt), engelska (Jul, July, Sept), dag-först, Idag/Igår/Today/Yesterday och enbart klockslag (uppladdningsdagen i appens tidszon). Prompten ber om ISO 8601 lokal tid och ISO 4217-valuta. Samma modell, inget extra vision-anrop. När ingen rad går att importera loggas en rad `[fota-vision]` med modell, läge, detectedKind, radantal och vilka av amount/currency/occurredAt som var null — aldrig belopp, butik eller bild. - Sparar…-låset är kvar och kompletterat med samma synkrona dubbeltryck-spärr som övriga pengaformulär. Ingen databasändring. Ingen ny miljövariabel. ## React #185 Felet återskapades inte i granskning/bekräfta. `ReceiptCaptureFlow` skriver om state under render bara när `resumeKey` (observation eller läge) byts — samma mönster som tidigare, inte en effekt som beror på värdet den skriver. Formuläret har ingen `useEffect` som sätter konto eller datum. Närmaste max-update-depth-spår medan Fota är öppen sitter i Hem, inte i granskningsformuläret: `HomeDashboard` (`src/components/home/HomeDashboard.tsx`) har en effekt som anropar `rememberHomeSnapshot` när `snap` ändras. `rememberHomeSnapshot` (`src/features/home/last-snapshot.ts`) kör `applyLeftoverLivingBaseline` (ny objektidentitet) och, när snapshottet inte är dirty, `adoptAccountsLastKnown(null)`, som kan notifiera kontolyssnare. Effektens beroenden är server-props, inte den lagrade snapshottet, så den loopar inte av sig själv om inte en förälder skickar ny `snap`-identitet varje render. Den rör saldo och är orörd i den här ändringen. ## Risker - Ett SEK-kvitto med förvalt THB-konto landar på befintligt aktivt SEK-konto (t.ex. Test-SEK) i stället för ett nytt Bankapp. Det är avsikten. - Saknas aktivt konto i valutan skapas Bankapp och, för ett kvitto som inte är THB, ett startsaldo 0 med växelkurs innan utgiften sparas. Bankapp-batchen behåller sin tidigare bootstrap utan att kräva kurs. - Bank-SMS är kvar på THB. - Flera aktiva konton i samma valuta: det senast använda (senaste icke-makulerade transaktionen, annars `updatedAt`) väljs. Användaren kan byta i listan innan Bekräfta. - Resor är fortfarande inte en egen chip-kategori. Hintet blir Transport. - En raderad utgift kan fotas in igen. Den gamla confirmed-kandidaten skrivs om. En levande kopia säger att rörelsen redan finns. - Enbart klockslag («16:46») hamnar på uppladdningsdagen i Asia/Bangkok, inte på transaktionens verkliga dag om den saknas i bilden. Tip: `301200f67ab7a5eb4c77bf2726c661e52f7f9c73`

Cola de moderación de reportes: cada reporte pendiente se ve como tarjeta con el análisis original completo, con acciones confirmar/descartar.

## Cambios
- `resources/views/pages/staff/⚡reportes.blade.php`: componente Livewire con la cola de reportes `pendiente`. Cada tarjeta muestra tipo, nivel, contenido analizado, razones, explicación y el comentario del reporte (o "Sin comentario"). Confirmar/descartar quita la tarjeta sin recargar. Estado vacío cuando no queda nada por revisar.
- `resources/views/layouts/staff.blade.php`: agregado el link "Reportes" al sidebar, **visible para cualquier staff sin restricción de rol** (a diferencia de "Gestión de staff", que solo ve el admin).
- `routes/web.php`: agregada `GET /staff/reportes` (Livewire), **TEMPORAL**, sin middleware.
- **Detalle de seguridad no pedido explícitamente en el issue:** el contenido reportado (links, texto de QR) se muestra siempre como texto plano, nunca como `<a href>` clickeable — para que el moderador no abra por accidente un link de phishing mientras lo revisa. Verificado con test.
- 12 tests nuevos en `tests/Feature/Staff/ReportesTest.php` (54/54 en total).

## Cómo probé
- `php artisan test`: 54/54 pasan.
- Mock con 3 reportes de ejemplo (texto/riesgo, link/dudoso, qr/seguro). El reporte #3 simula el caso "otro moderador ya lo resolvió" (422), para poder ver ese estado en el navegador sin depender de timing de doble clic.
- **Pendiente:** no lo vi en un navegador real todavía — falta confirmar que la tarjeta desaparece sin recarga, que el foco pasa al aviso tras cada acción, y que los botones se deshabilitan durante la demora simulada.

## Pendiente de coordinar con backend
- Los nombres de estado `confirmado`/`descartado` son una suposición del mock (marcados `// MOCK:`) — si backend usa otros nombres, es un cambio de una línea.
- Lo que hay que reemplazar: el array `$reportes` por `GET /staff/reportes`, y `resolverMock()` por los dos `POST` reales. La vista no debería necesitar cambios.
- No implementa nada de la lógica de `casos_confirmados` — eso es 100% de backend al confirmar.
- Igual que en HU1.2, el test de "visible sin restricción de rol" simula `rol` en memoria porque la columna todavía no existe en `users`.

Closes 2.3
