author: jondgoodwin
body:
## What this does

A library compile now writes its package's **include file**: `<package>.cone` in the output directory. That is the Cone source a program compiles against in place of the package's source. It is written when the build description says `output: library`, or when the new `--emit-include` switch asks for it, after type check and only when there are no errors. This follows the seven rulings of 25 Sep (`Incubator\Cone\Ruminations\include-file-generation.md`, section 6).

**How the text is made.** The generator copies the author's own source text; it prints nothing from the IR except an inferred type. The parser now records a span for every module-level statement and every member of a type's braces (`ir/dclspan.h`): where it starts (at `pub`), its keyword, where its body or value starts and ends, and where it ends. The spans live in a side list on the module or type. `--spans` prints the root's spans, and I checked them by hand against `module_build_link`'s `q.cone` before anything used them. The IR then decides, statement by statement (`ir/incfile.c`):

- **Whole**: a body an importer expands. That is an inline or generic function, a macro, a trait's methods, a generic type, or an enum's own methods.
- **Cut to `extern`**: a definition the object exports. `extern` is written in before the keyword, and the body (from `{`) or the value (from `=`) is left out. A global's fold clause is kept (Q4).
- **Out**: everything else, together with the comments directly above it.

**What goes in is the exported set (Q5).** The generator and code generation now call one function, `dclIsExported`, moved unchanged to `ir/export.c` along with `dclIsInstance` and `typeHoldsExpanded`. `fnDclIsExpanded` is no longer private. Types keep every field, private ones included. The `mod` line and all imports and `use` lines go in as written (Q7). A global with an inferred type gets its type printed (Q6). Every comment in the kept text is kept, under a banner that says the file is generated, from which files, and not to edit it (Q2, Q3).

**Q1 (submodules) is refused, as the brief asked.** Three kinds of reach into a submodule are detected and refused with the new `ErrorIncSubmodule`:
- a type named by an included declaration's signature, type or fields;
- a declaration that the root's expanded body names. Name resolution now marks these `DclSubReached`, beside `DclExpandReached`.
- a `pub use` of a submodule's names, or of an enum a submodule holds.

**Self-check.** Before the file is written, it is parsed and name-resolved as the package's module, beside the program. Its imports are answered by the root's own import lines (`parseIncludeCheck`, `pgmNameResAlone`, `modFoldAlone`). A failure is `ErrorIncCheck`, and the text goes to `<package>.cone.rejected`, where the errors are located. A path that is a source of the compile is refused before anything is generated (`ErrorIncWrite`). New codes 1147–1149 are appended at the end of `error.h` and `codes.toml`.

## Tests

- **Round trips.** Each package is compiled alone and writes its include file. The runner's new `include` key requires that file to equal a golden file byte for byte, and checks it as soon as the package is compiled. The program's build description names the golden file, so the program compiles against exactly what the package generated. Then everything is linked and run.
  - `module_build_link` now compiles against q's generated file. Output is unchanged.
  - `module_init_link` and `module_generic_link` now compile against generated files too. `module_init_link` also drops a `lib.Handle` now.
  - New: `module_include_roundtrip`, with three packages. `base` is extended, `dep` is re-exported with `pub use` on its import, and `t` has one of each kind of declaration:
    - enums with variants, including a variant that meets its enum's requirement privately;
    - a trait with a default;
    - a macro that reaches a private function;
    - a `@c` function;
    - a default fold on the `mod` line, and `extends` of an imported module;
    - a global that folds its type's members in;
    - globals with inferred types: a number, an imported type, and t's own type;
    - a private type that a public type holds;
    - a typedef and a const;
    - `init` and `final` in a second file, whose import is moved up into the header;
    - a private function and a private type that nothing reaches, which are left out.
  - I wrote the `.out` by hand from the source before the first run, and it matched.
  - I checked every golden file by eye against its source.
- **Refusals.**
  - `module_include_refuse` pins `ErrorIncSubmodule` at six reaches: a signature, a global's type, a field, two `pub use`s, and an inline body naming a submodule function. It also shows that a private signature, a public body and a private `use` are not refused.
  - `module_include_check` pins `ErrorIncCheck`: the self-check catches a submodule macro that the generator cannot see.
  - `driver_include_over_source` pins `ErrorIncWrite`.
- Suite: 309 passed + 1 expected failure → **313 passed + 1 expected failure**. Congo: **17 → 17 OK**. A Congo build now leaves generated `core.cone` and `stdio.cone` in `build/<mode>/`. I checked them by eye: `stdio.cone` declares exactly what the hand-written file does, including `pub extern mut print IOStream;` with the type printed from the inferred one.

## Judgement calls (each one yours to veto)

1. **How the round-trip test works.** The program compiles against a golden copy that the runner verifies is byte-identical to what the package just generated. The alternative was pointing descriptions into `build/testrun/...`. `--bless` records a generated file that differs.
2. **Three existing scenarios converted.** `module_build_link`, `module_init_link` and `module_generic_link` now use generated include files. `module_build_transitive*` and `module_build_fold_extern*` keep their hand-written ones, because hand-written include files are still legal and still what Congo uses.
3. **Comments.** Every comment in the kept text stays. That includes section comments between declarations, even when everything under them is gone, and the source's file-header comment. A comment block directly above an omitted declaration (no blank line between) goes with it, and so does a trailing comment on the same line.
4. **A few things go in beyond the exported set**, because an importer's compile reads them without naming them:
   - a global that the module's finalizer drops, so the importer derives `drop` as the package does;
   - any root type that an included signature, type or field names, even a private one (needed for layout).
5. **Two changes to what a library exports.** Both are measured failures without the change, and both only make more symbols external.
   - A reachable type's `final` and `clone` are exported whatever their visibility (`fnIsTypeLifecycle`). Without this, a program dropping a `lib.Handle` failed to link: LNK2019 on `lib.Handle.final`.
   - A method that meets a requirement of a trait its type is (its base or a mixin) is exported and declared (`fnIsTraitMethod`). Without it, the importer's type check failed: "Type must implement area method, as required by Shape".
6. **Private typedefs, consts, macros and module traits are kept.** They have no symbol, and nothing records what reaches them. The one exception: a private typedef that names a submodule's type is dropped.
7. **Standalone `use`.** It stays when it names a kept enum or something from another package. A private `use` of a submodule's names is dropped. A `pub use` of one is refused.
8. **Several files in the root.** They are concatenated in parse order, and a later file's imports move up into the first file's header. The banner names the files by basename.
9. **A module-level `static` global becomes `extern`**; the word `static` is dropped.
10. **Where a body reach is reported.** It is reported where the submodule's declaration is, not at the body, becau

author: ruledicaprio
body:
Refs #453. **Report-only**: the M4 synthetic bench now counts wrong accepts, meaning Tier-1 hits where any of the 12 scored fields differs from the generator's exact truth.

**Why:**
- A hit proves only a checksum-consistent zone whose document number matches.
- Line 1 (document type, issuer, both names), nationality and sex carry no check digit.
- A check digit on the other fields is consistency, not proof. #454 measured three wrong reads that had been counted as hits.

**What it adds:**
- per document: `wrong_accept` and `wrong_fields`;
- per run: `wrong_accepts` and `wrong_accept_rate`, with hits as the denominator;
- a summary line printed after the strict-hit line.

It reuses the per-field CER comparison that `strict_hits` already uses. `hit`, `hit_rate` and `--min-hit-rate` are unchanged, and nothing gates on the new counter. Whether to gate is a separate decision, left to the architect.

**Measured:** the gate's own M4 command (`--count 50 --seed 0 --profile clean`, TD3) gives 39 hits, of which **23 are wrong accepts**. That matches the analyst's count by hand. Wrong fields across the 23 (one document can have several):

| Field | Wrong accepts |
| --- | ---: |
| given_names | 16 |
| surname | 15 |
| personal_number | 5 |
| issuing_country | 3 |
| document_type | 3 |
| nationality | 1 |

**Tests:** 4 new unit tests:
- all fields equal: not a wrong accept;
- one scored field differs: a wrong accept;
- only `mrz_lines` differs: not a wrong accept;
- a non-hit: never a wrong accept.

**Gates:** fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`), `cargo test --workspace`, the doc-link check and the changelog check all pass.

**Also:** a changelog fragment (`.added`); the new field documented in `knowledge/benchmarks/README.md`. The real-specimen equivalent is #443 and isn't touched here.

author: syntaxwanderer
body:
## Commits

1. **Reject host-less redirect targets a browser resolves off-site** (`ResponseRenderer`)
   - **Defect:** the VULN-006 guard treated any target where `parse_url()` finds no host as relative. Browsers follow WHATWG URL parsing: they read `\` as `/` and drop TAB/CR/LF. So `/\evil.com/`, `\\evil.com/`, `/<TAB>/evil.com`, ` //evil.com`, `https:/evil.com` and `javascript:…` all passed the guard.
   - **Fix:** these targets now fall back to `/`. `/path`, `?q=1`, `#frag` and `page` are unchanged.
2. **Keep the default-locale prefix redirect on the current host** (`LocalePhase`)
   - **Defect:** with `LOCALE_URL_PREFIX=true`, `GET /en//evil.example/x` answered `301 Location: //evil.example/x`, which is protocol-relative and leaves the site. `/en/\evil.example` had the same effect.
   - **Fix:** the target is collapsed to a single leading `/`.
3. **Carry the resource's headers onto redirect responses**
   - **Defect:** the redirect path returned a bare `HttpResponse::redirect()`, so `Cache-Control: no-store` on a login or `Clear-Site-Data` on a logout were silently dropped.
   - **Fix:** the handler's headers now go out with the redirect. A handler-set `Location` (in any case) is dropped, so the validated target is always the only one.
   - Cookies were already applied by `SessionPhase::finalize()` and are not duplicated.
4. A one-line follow-up puts `isSiblingHost()`'s docblock back on its method.

## Verification

- New `RedirectTargetGuardTest`: 10 attack targets, all failing before the fix, plus 9 accepted-target cases.
- New `LocalePhaseTest`: uses the real `semitexa/locale`. 3 of its cases fail before the fix.
- New `RedirectKeepsResourceHeadersTest`.
- The full core suite ran in a `semitexa-ultimate` app with Swoole: 1759 tests. The only failures are the 22 environmental ones already failing on `develop`.
- Merges cleanly together with semitexa/semitexa-core#149, which touches another hunk of `ResponseRenderer`.

## Suggested CHANGELOG entry (Unreleased → Security / Fixed)

- Redirect targets a browser would resolve to another host (`/\evil.com`, a control character, `https:/evil.com`) fall back to `/`.
- The default-locale redirect can no longer be steered off-site with `//` or `\`.
- A redirect keeps the headers its handler set.

author: genematx
body:
SQLAlchemy 2.1.0 changed how `JSON.as_string()` renders on SQLite (it now text-extracts such that a stored JSON integer 0 compares equal to the string "0"). So `Eq("number", "0")` — which must not match a node whose number is integer 0 — now matches. This causes [tests failure](https://github.com/bluesky/tiled/actions/runs/36111071642/job/107994413166#step:9:4821) in `test_queries.py::test_eq` with `assert ['a'] == []`. The map backend uses Python comparison (not SQL), which is why `test_eq[map]` passes and only `[sqlite]` breaks.

author: sanjays2402
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-37362

#### Branch description

Fixes a sentinel collision in `identify_hasher()`. When a stored password hash's algorithm segment is the literal string `"default"` (e.g. `default$$$$`), the old code handed that string to `get_hasher()`, where it matched the `"default"` sentinel and returned the first configured hasher instead of being treated as an unknown algorithm. The mismatched hasher then failed in `decode()` with a bare `AssertionError`, rather than the `ValueError` that `identify_hasher()`'s docstring promises. This is reachable through `check_password()`, the exact function `User.check_password()` and `ModelBackend.authenticate()` call on every login attempt.

The fix looks the algorithm up in `get_hashers_by_algorithm()` directly, so any unrecognized name (including the literal `"default"`) raises `ValueError("Unknown password hashing algorithm ...")` as documented, and `check_password()` fails closed by returning `False`. The public `get_hasher("default")` sentinel behavior is unchanged.

Reproduction (on `main` before the fix):

```python
import django
from django.conf import settings
settings.configure(
    SECRET_KEY="x",
    PASSWORD_HASHERS=["django.contrib.auth.hashers.PBKDF2PasswordHasher"],
)
django.setup()
from django.contrib.auth.hashers import check_password
check_password("some guess", "default$$$$")  # raised bare AssertionError
```

After the fix, that call returns `False`, and `identify_hasher("default$$$$")` raises `ValueError: Unknown password hashing algorithm 'default'. Did you specify it in the PASSWORD_HASHERS setting?`

Tests: added `test_default_algorithm_sentinel_collision` to `tests/auth_tests/test_hashers.py` covering both `identify_hasher()` and `check_password()`. Ran the full `auth_tests.test_hashers` suite (SQLite): all tests pass.

Refs #37362

AI tools used: Muse (Meta's personal AI agent). I fully reviewed and verified the change and its tests.

author: windchargerj
body:
**Keep XMake DAP breakpoints working on IntelliJ Platform 2026.3.**

## What Changed

- Replaced the direct `DapBreakpointsDescription` constructor call with runtime constructor resolution.
- The debugger descriptor now supports both the 2026.2 two-argument constructor and the 2026.3 three-argument constructor.
- When the new function-breakpoint parameter is present, it is passed as `null`, preserving the existing line- and exception-breakpoint behavior.

## Why

IntelliJ Platform 2026.3 removes the old two-argument constructor used by this plugin. Since the plugin is still compiled against 2026.2, directly calling the new three-argument constructor would break the supported 2026.2 runtime.

Resolving the available constructor at runtime keeps one plugin distribution compatible with both platform versions without changing breakpoint behavior.

## Impact

*XMake debugging continues to install its DAP breakpoint description on both IntelliJ Platform 2026.2 and 2026.3.*

body: ## 概要 `internal/app` に `Auth` を足し、初回設定・ログイン・ログアウト・セッションの確認・見る人の状態を受け持たせる。HTTP にはまだつながない（#299 でつなぐ）。 工程の選択: sdd-autopilot の implement。子 #298 の前提の #295（PR #309）は feature ブランチにマージ済みで、#298 を Refs するマージ済みの PR は無い。 ## 関連 Issue Refs #298 ## 変更点 - `internal/app/auth.go`: `Auth` と、`Auth` 自身が定める `AuthStore`・`PasswordHasher` の interface を足す。時計・乱数・照合の空きを待つ時間は差し替えられる。 - 初回設定: 設定済みかを先に確かめ、設定済みなら Argon2id を計算せずに `ErrAccountAlreadyConfigured` を返す。値は `domain.ValidateUsername`・`ValidatePassword` で確かめる。 - ログイン: 誤りの原因（ユーザー名・パスワード・両方・空欄・上限超え・未設定）はどれも同じ `ErrInvalidCredentials` になり、どれも照合を1回だけ行う。未設定のときは固定のダミーのハッシュと照合する。ユーザー名は SHA-256 を定数時間で比べる。照合は同時に2つまでで、空きを 5 秒待っても得られなければ、失敗に数えずに `*ThrottledError`（`errors.Is` で `ErrLoginThrottled` と一致し、`RetryAfterSeconds` を持つ）を返す。セッションには照合に使った `account.version` を書き、形式の合う現在の Cookie の行は消す。 - セッション ID は 32 バイトの暗号学的乱数を base64url（パディングなし）にしたもの。形式の合わない値は保存先に問い合わせずに無効とする。確認で DB が失敗したら、無効とせずに誤りを返す。 - `State` は `owner`・`guest`・`setupRequired` を返す。未設定なら Cookie によらず `setupRequired`。 - `internal/app/login_throttle.go`: 送信元ごとの試行制限（Plan の Structural Decisions 6）。照合の前に1回分を予約し、「予約 + 直近 5 分の失敗」が 5 以上なら制限する。IPv4 はアドレスごと、IPv6 は /64 ごとに数える。送信元は 10000 まで覚え、超えたら最も長く使われていない送信元から捨てる。 - `internal/app/doc.go`・`ARCHITECTURE.md`: `internal/app` の説明に `Auth` と、その interface を足す。 ## 確認 - `go test -race -count=3 ./internal/app/` が通る。完了の条件の各項目にテストがある。 - `task check` と `task check-docs` が通る（最初の `task check` の1回目は、関係の無い `web/src/player/VideoPage.test.tsx` が負荷で一度だけ失敗した。単独では3回とも通り、再実行の全体も通った）。 - 完了の条件の「保存されるのはそのハッシュだけ」は、`internal/app` では確かめられない。偽物の保存先は ID をそのまま持ち、ハッシュにするのは保存先の役目だからである。これは `internal/store` の `TestAuthStoreStoresOnlyTokenHash`（#295）で確かめている。`internal/app` のテストが確かめるのは、ID が 32 バイトの base64url であることまで。 ## 残るリスク - `dummyPasswordHash` のパラメータ（m=19456,t=2,p=1）を `internal/password` の既定に合わせているのはコメントだけである。depguard で `internal/app` から `internal/password` を import できないので、両方を import する組み立ての単位（#299 の `cmd/mdm`）で、ダミーのハッシュと新しいハッシュのパラメータが一致することを確かめるテストを置くとよい。 - ログインで消す古いセッションは、有効かどうかを確かめずに、形式が合えば消す。無効な行は元から使えないので、見える振る舞いは data-model §5 と変わらない。 - 試行制限の記録はメモリにだけあり、再起動で消える。送信元が 10000 を超えると古い記録から捨てる（どちらも Plan の Structural Decisions 6 のとおり）。 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_012GYHQLEZhowbtMofywhf3s --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_012GYHQLEZhowbtMofywhf3s)_ ---

author: lexasoft123
body:
## The problem

Launching `Shitty.app` (or `Pretty.app`) from Finder, the Dock or `open` gives a shell that can't find Homebrew commands, and a prompt that opens at `/`:

```
➜  / htop
zsh: command not found: htop
```

Both come from the launch context, not from the terminal:

- launchd starts the app with a bare `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` and no shell environment to inherit, in `/`.
- `login` defaults to `false`, so the shell runs non-login and never reads `.zprofile`, which is where Homebrew's `eval "$(brew shellenv)"` conventionally lives.

Running the raw binary from another terminal hid it, because the child then inherits that terminal's environment. Since #120 ships an app bundle, a desktop launch is now the normal path.

## The fix

Only when launchd is the parent process (macOS only):

- `login` defaults to **true**, unless the user set it, in the config file or on the command line. `+login` and `login = false` still win.
- A working directory of `/` becomes `$HOME`.

Launches from a shell are untouched. The predicate takes the parent pid as a parameter (`launchedFromDesktop(pid_t)`), so it is unit-testable; the login default is read off the option's source (`HardDefault` means the user never chose).

I went with "only when launched from launchd" rather than making every macOS launch a login shell (as Terminal.app and iTerm2 do), because it changes nothing for people who start `st` from a shell today. Happy to switch if you'd rather follow the other convention.

## Verified

Launched the built binary orphaned to launchd (`ppid 1`) with a small C probe as the shell, so it could report its true `argv[0]` and cwd:

| launch | login shell | cwd |
|---|---|---|
| launchd-style, default | yes | `$HOME` (was `/`) |
| launchd-style, `+login` | no, so the explicit setting wins | `$HOME` |
| from a live shell, default | no, unchanged | untouched |
| from a live shell, `-login` | yes | untouched |

- New `Startup` unit test; the whole unit suite passes through `./build`'s own runner.
- **Not verified:** a real double-click of the bundle. In my session `open` started the app but never spawned the shell, so the launchd case is covered by the orphaned-process test above rather than by an actual Finder launch.

## Avant

La carte du kanban ne montrait du risque que sa référence, sur un fond coloré par la cotation, et le même triangle d'avertissement pour tous. La cotation chiffrée et la catégorie de danger n'étaient lisibles qu'au survol, dans l'infobulle.

- La vignette de la catégorie de danger (`img/categorieDangers/<thumbnail>.png`, la même que dans les listes de risques et les documents) remplace le triangle générique.

La vignette est posée sur un disque blanc, les pictogrammes étant dessinés pour un fond clair alors que les cotations ≥ 51 donnent un badge sombre.

author: amir-arad
body:
## Play change

A ship now dies only when its **capsule** is breached. The capsule is the hull's internal core, a hit-point counter that loses 0.1 integrity per defect, so it breaks after 10 defects. Broken systems past `systemKillRatio` (`healthRatio` 0) are now a **mission kill**: the ship is disabled but stays alive and does not become a derelict.

- Every hull config carries a `capsule` design (internal, not electronics). Its `damage50` is `FIGHTER_CAPSULE_DAMAGE50` (100, in `configurations/capsule-class.ts`) times the hull class: dragonfly-MK1/MK2 x1, gravitas/predator/demo-ship x2, glaive/freighter/cataphract x3, stations x4.
- What reaches it: internal-hitting weapon damage (HiExp, for example) through either hit area, as one penetration candidate at the worst exposure, so a hit spanning both areas never counts it twice. Collision damage reaches it the same way. External-only damage (Frag) never touches it.
- The capsule is not in `ShipState.systems()`. The kill ratio does not count it, station UIs do not list it, and no repair protocol can restore it.
- Docs: `systemKillRatio` / `healthRatio` JSDoc and the GM tweak panel's Health readout comment now say they measure mission kills, not death.

## Source

Extracted from #2271:
- starwards/starwards@2fd730e: capsule mechanism, configs, damage/attack resolution, specs
- starwards/starwards@e323cbc: fighter base 100, hull classes scale from one constant
- starwards/starwards@a190d5b: docs, healthRatio/systemKillRatio are mission-kill measures
- starwards/starwards@48eb7ad: fighter half-life specs; kill-window specs assert mission kills
- starwards/starwards@0e1a8a3: half-life pins measured with a fresh id sequence per seed
- starwards/starwards@e504040: core `resetIds` only, so each headless seed starts from a fresh id sequence

## Tests

Copied from `training-harness`, and each one failed on master:
- `core/test/damage-manager-death.spec.ts`: copied. I dropped one line, the fake SpaceManager's `state: { get }`, because it only serves the aggro feature. On master it fails with `state.capsule` undefined (TypeError) in every capsule case.
- `core/test/ship-kill-window.spec.ts` and `station-kill-window.spec.ts`: copied. The dangling "ADR-0004" reference is replaced with a pointer to `Capsule` / `damage-manager-death.spec.ts`. On master they fail with `<model> must survive a mission kill: expected true to equal false` for dragonfly-MK1, gravitas and all 3 stations, because master turns the ship into a derelict at the ratio.
- `core/test/armor-layers-examples.spec.ts`: copied hunk. It changes the die seed from `ShipDie(2)` to `ShipDie(6)` (the capsule now joins the single-scope pick) and adds `capsule.integrity === 1`. On master it fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integrity')`.
- `core/test/npc-ammo-doctrine.spec.ts`: copied. The "ADR-0004" reference is reworded. It checks that a GVTS kills a pinned dragonfly-MK1 with HiExp. On master it fails with `killedAt: null` (`maxBroken: 5`): internal-only HiExp never reaches the broken-system ratio.
- `server/src/test/training/fighter-half-life{,-mk1.spec,-mk2.spec}.ts`: copied, then re-pinned (see below). On master both fail with `half-life Infinity s` because none of seeds 1-16 kills within the cap.

These specs need a minimal harness: `test/headless-game.ts` (start/tick only: no restore, save, crewed player or recorder), `test/damage-tap.ts` (`tapDerelicts` only), `scenarios/training.ts` (the T1 map only) and `test/training/training-scenarios.ts` (the T1 and T1-MK2 rungs only).

### Half-life re-pin

Measured the spec's own way: seeds 1-64, 60 Hz, 300 s cap, the `timeToKill` loop, one fresh id sequence per seed.

| Rung | #2271 pin (all changes) | master + capsule only | **This PR on current master** (all 8 merged) | Kills | TTK p10 / p50 / p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | 98 s | 123 s | **98 s** | 63/64 | 51 / 98 / 223 |
| T1-MK2 | 69 s | 149 s | **69 s** | 61/64 | 32 / 69 / 267 |

With the other seven extracted PRs on master, both rungs reproduce #2271's pins, so the split lost nothing the half-life can see. 16-seed blocks span 0.7x-1.45x the pin (inside the ±50% band CI checks on seeds 1-16).

## Changed existing specs

- `ship-kill-window.spec.ts`, `station-kill-window.spec.ts`: the ratio threshold is now a mission kill (`healthRatio` 0), and the ship must survive it.
- `damage-manager-death.spec.ts`: death is now a capsule breach, and a ship past the ratio is a mission kill only.
- `armor-layers-examples.spec.ts`: with the capsule as a candidate, the die seed that reproduces the documented magazine case moved from 2 to 6.
- `orbit-capture.spec.ts`: the station now rolls a seeded `ShipDie(1)`. With `MockDie`, roll 0 made every defect land, so the capsule would breach in ten hits and the fight would end before any orbit. The spec's other change on #2271 (the hold window) belongs to a different feature and is not taken.
- `armor-ammo-matrix-report.md`: regenerated. HiExp through faraday now reaches 4 penetration-channel systems (was 3), the capsule included. It is identical to the #2271 report.

## Evidence

Harness and balance evidence lives in https://github.com/starwards/starwards/pull/2271

## Left out

- Recorder, DuckDB analysis, wave-defence balance harness, the `run-*.ts` runners, the README, crew proxies, `HeadlessGame.restore`/`saveGame`/`crewedPlayer`, and the T0 / T1-missile / T1-predator / T1-noweave rungs.
- `labNoCombatWeave`, the aggro threat table, the gravitas reactor retune, energy brownout, impact exposure, line of fire, obstacle avoidance and NPC gunnery.
- The removal of `selectAmmoForTarget` / `peerState` in 2fd730e: that doctrine is not on master.
- The wave-defence harness hunks in 2fd730e, 48eb7ad and a190d5b: that harness is not on master.
- The T0 parity fixture recapture in e323cbc: the analysis layer is not on master.

author: bsikar
body:
Closes #1183.

`check_sg_offsets.py` was wired into exactly one app, the parked `examples/ek_ra8d2/hil_needs_revalidation/tz_nsc_cgc_usb`. The two other apps that emit a CMSE import library, `apps/board/stand_alone/ereader` (the production TrustZone app) and `examples/ek_ra8d2/hw_pending/tz_threadx_demo`, never ran it, even though both linker scripts claim the slot offsets are "verified AFTER the link ... by scripts/checks/check_sg_offsets.py, run as a POST_BUILD step in this app's CMakeLists.txt".

The checker could not simply be attached to them. `EXPECTED_OFFSETS` pins three symbols at 0/8/16, which is the parked app's layout. `ra8d2-ereader.elf` globs all of `libs/ra8_nsc/src`, so its `.gnu.sgstubs` holds 40 stubs in 320 B with `ra8_nsc_cgc_get_clock_hz` at +96; pointing the old checker at it would report drift on a correct link.

## What landed

A structural rule that holds for any secure image: find each veneer by its `__acle_se_<name>` companion (the definitive `cmse_nonsecure_entry` marker, independent of which `ra8_nsc` sources the app compiled), then require every gateway to sit inside `[g_ra8_ls_sgstubs_start, g_ra8_ls_sgstubs_end)` at an exact multiple of `SG_STUB_BYTES`, one veneer per slot, no slot empty, region sized exactly for the veneer count.

The pinned `EXPECTED_OFFSETS` table now applies only to an ELF whose veneer set equals its keys, so the `tz_nsc_cgc_usb` ABI pin keeps its full strength while other apps are held to the structural rule alone. `ereader` and `tz_threadx_demo` run the checker POST_BUILD, so `build-cross` enforces the contract on every build.

It also corrects a claim both the checker and the sg-offsets gate made: ld does not emit the stubs in ascending symbol-name order (the 40-stub e-reader layout opens `acmphs_init`, `pdm_init`, `adc_init`); only the stride and the one-per-slot packing are dependable.

Six files: `scripts/checks/check_sg_offsets.py` (+238), the two app `CMakeLists.txt` (+19 each), `scripts/ci/gates/analysis.sh`, and one entry each in the non-auth and scope suppression registries. No C source and no library touched.

## Why this branch rather than `ci/1183-sg-offsets-coverage`

That branch carries this commit stacked on three others that are not on `dev`: the `#1048` commit (now merged here as #1598) plus two unrelated ones, `#900` @since checking and `#953` media_download cross-build. Merging it as it stands would drag both unrelated commits in and break one-commit-per-PR. This is the `#1183` commit alone, cherry-picked onto `ra8ci/dev`, author and committer unchanged. Both registry hunks auto-merged and are the new entries only.

## Verified in this box

- `python3 scripts/checks/check_sg_offsets.py --selftest`: all 10 cases pass, both directions (clean layout, missing and displaced veneer, pinned set recognised as its own image, a wider set not held to the pinned table, packed region of any count, off-stride gateway, out-of-region gateway, slot collision, oversized region, empty NSC region).
- `python3 scripts/checks/suppression_nonauth_registry.py` and `suppression_scope_registry.py`: exit 0.
- `bash -n scripts/ci/gates/analysis.sh`: clean. `shellcheck` and `ruff` are not installed in this box, so neither was rerun here.

Not reproduced here, and stated plainly rather than assumed: the original commit's run against a real `ra8d2-ereader.elf` built with the pinned arm-gnu-toolchain 13.3.rel1 (reporting "NSC SG-veneer layout OK (40 veneer(s))"). This box has no cross toolchain, so the two POST_BUILD hookups are unexercised until a `build-cross` runs.

No Go file is touched, so the `tools/ra8ci` build and test set is unaffected.

author: com-junkawasaki
body:
Fixes the two kexe loader holes the C3 differential recorded (superproject adr-2609251400). Only mechanism changed in C; op 8 and the generated decision region are byte-identical (`test-loader-decisions` passes).

**1. Directory symlink escape.** Every `:fs/app-data` / `:fs/browse` open now goes through the new `kexe_scope_open`. It asks op 8 which scope entry to use, then opens the rest of the path relative to that entry's root:
- Linux: `openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS`.
- macOS: `openat O_RESOLVE_BENEATH`, probed once.

A kernel refusal counts as a failed containment. The old containment check still runs after the open.

Behaviour change: an absolute symlink is refused even when it points inside the scope. The static image refuses it the same way.

**2. seccomp.** With a wire-35 scope the filter now admits:
- `mkdirat` for MKDIR
- `unlinkat` for UNLINK and RMDIR
- `renameat` for RENAME (x86_64 264, aarch64 38, both measured)

With any fs scope it also admits `openat2`. `renameat2` and `fchmod` stay denied. CHMOD dying with SIGSYS is kept as the negative case.

**Evidence**
- Linux differential: 270 checks, 0 failed. The symlink and mutation cases no longer need recorded differences. The same expectations fail 14 checks against main's loader.
- macOS (arm64 and x86_64 under Rosetta, with and without Seatbelt): all escapes trap, and nothing is created outside the scope.
- Other suites: run-tests 237/0, test-nbb-js the known 10, jdk-free-native, package-command 40/40, loader-warnings, and fuzz (ASan+UBSan, 20,000 cases) all pass.
- The artifact pin moves to eff17393 (loader identity 9c2bbcee).

## Summary
This brings the DPDPA pack, its prompts and the client-facing copy into line with the DPDP Act 2023 and the DPDP Rules 2025. Everything was checked against the primary MeitY and e-Gazette texts. Full edit list: `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-25-p6-0e-dpdpa-pack-correctness.md#results`.

- **Section references:**
  - 14 `section_ref` corrections.
  - The CHILD.1 and CHILD.2 references were swapped; they are now the right way round.
  - SDF.4 cited s.10(2)(d), which doesn't exist. It now cites s.10(2)(c)(ii).
  - The questionnaire guidance references are corrected too.
- **Breach timeline:**
  - The Act's s.8(6) sets no deadline.
  - The first notice to the Board and to affected people is due "without delay" (r.7(1) and r.7(2)(a)).
  - The 72 hours applies only to the detailed report to the Board (r.7(2)(b)).
  - Fixed in the prompts, the red-flag description, the scope profiler and the guidance.
- **Requirement text:** three descriptions and two titles no longer misstate the law: ACCURACY.1, CORRECT.2 and NOTICE.1.
- **Penalty table:**
  - BN.NOTIFY: ₹250 Cr → ₹200 Cr.
  - CH4.SDF: ₹50 Cr → ₹150 Cr.
  - CONSENT.5 (parental consent) → ₹200 Cr.
  - The "per incident" wording is replaced with the s.33 framing.
- **Readiness note:** fiduciary obligations and penalties commence on 13 May 2027 (G.S.R. 843(E); Rules r.1(4)). The note appears only when DPDPA is in scope and the report predates that date. It shows in:
  - the board PDF (Scope & Limitations)
  - the integrated PDF
  - the web summary
- **Unchanged:** IDs, criticality, weights and red-flag `pattern` keys. The golden `score.json` and analyzer output are unchanged. The golden fixtures were regenerated with the offline capture only; only the call key and the PDF text hash changed.

## Test changes to review
- **`test_p5_3` scenario 12:** the guard now exempts only `definitions/dpdpa.py`, and still requires that identifiers and weights are unchanged.
- **`test_p5_3` scenario 3:** updated the pinned prompt hash and request key.
- **`test_p5_6` scenario 22:** the guard excludes `pdf_export.py` and `scope_profiler.py`, which this task has to edit.
- **`test_validation_harness::test_app_files_are_untouched_by_harness`:** PR #47 made this fail on every branch that changes `app/`. It is now scoped to branches that also change the harness (separate commit `d14fa4d`).

## Test plan

- [x] 9 new tests in `tests/test_p6_0e_dpdpa_pack_correctness.py` pass.
- [x] Smoke test on a seeded DPDPA assessment:
  - The penalty tile shows ₹200Cr with the new wording.
  - The readiness note appears under the Executive Summary.
  - The board PDF shows "Regulatory Commencement" in Scope & Limitations.

## Open questions for Saqlain
- **No statutory basis:**
  - CB.TRANSFER.2 (contracts for transfers).
  - CM.RECORDS.2 (periodic consent refresh).
- **Duplicates:** whether to merge CONSENT.2 and GRANULAR.1.
- **Scope gaps:**
  - IT Act s.43A / SPDI Rules coverage until May 2027.
  - The s.17(3) startup exemption.
  - Rules r.3(a) and r.8(3).
- **Date:** 13 vs 14 May 2027. Both documents are dated 13 Nov on their face, so the PR uses 13 May.
- **CH2.NOTICE.3** still cites s.5(1).
- **Question text** still repeats the old wording for NOTICE.1, ACCURACY.1 and CORRECT.2.
- **The `missing_timeline` prompt** flags "without undue delay" as vague. The Rules themselves use "without delay".

author: oscorped
body:
## Scope

Reduce public Ethereum native direct-transfer RPC usage without changing signed transaction economics.

- Reuse the existing pinned, canonical batch reader for chain 1 native prepare and approval. Batch rejection stops without scalar fallback or a retry.
- Retain the fresh post-sign balance check, but reuse the validated frozen execution-only fee upper bound. The signed gas limit and max fee per gas already cap that on-chain charge.
- Persist an accepted send as `submitted_pending`; inspect its receipt through explicit observation.
- Arm the existing 24-physical-POST, persisted 750 ms provider pacing guard on Ethereum direct prepare, approval, and resume. BNB remains on the same guard.

## Modeled physical POSTs

| Clean path | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Prepare | 17 | 8 |
| Approve through accepted send | 17 pre-sign + 9 post-sign + 1 send = 27, so the 24 cap interrupts before send | 8 pre-sign + 3 post-sign balance + 1 send = 12 |
| Explicit native receipt observation | Up to 8 scalar reads | Up to 8 scalar reads |

The observed operation previously used 90 physical POSTs across eight invocations, including failed approvals, resume, and separate balance/observation reads. These are clean-path modeled counts; no live RPC was used for this PR. Observation remains scalar and is outside the approval invocation.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build:ts` passed.
- Focused batch transport, direct EVM, and guard suite: 66/66 passed. The transport test counts actual mocked HTTPS POST bodies: 17 Ethereum prepare read envelopes in 8 POSTs, with reversed response IDs. Existing parser tests reject malformed, missing, and conflicting duplicate IDs. A 429 batch stops after one POST.
- Signed Ethereum regression covers fresh funding loss before send, unchanged frozen fee reuse, signed-not-submitted resume with exactly one broadcast, and explicit receipt observation.

No live RPC, wallet, signing, or transaction submission was performed.

author: kixelated
body:
## Problem

`spawn retention > an effect that never reruns drops settled tasks` (added in #4085) fails CI's Test job intermittently with ~8191-8194 retained promises (runs 36104628091, 36104280755). It blocks #4095.

The implementation is correct: `spawn` deletes each task from its set once it settles. The test is not. It counted `Promise` cells after `Bun.gc(true)`, called from inside the test's own async stack. JSC scans that stack conservatively, so a stale pointer can keep dead cells alive. The ~8192 is most likely a discarded storage table of the task set (it grows to 10000 promises before any are dropped), pinned with every entry it still holds. Whether such a pointer survives depends on stack/register reuse, which differs by arch (CI is arm64) and load; bun is 1.3.13 in both CI and the local dev shell.

The sibling `race > many races against a long-lived promise keep the heap flat` (same PR, `objectCount`-based) has the same flaw. It reproduces locally under parallel load: ~1900 extra `Cell Butterfly` and ~95 `Structure` cells after the GC, gone once the stack unwinds.

## Approach

Assert on the bookkeeping itself instead of observing the GC. Both tests spy on `Set.prototype.add` to find the set in question, then check its `size`:

- spawn: the effect's task set holds all 100 tasks while pending and none once they settle.
- race: `closed`'s listener set received all 1000 listeners, and every set touched is empty afterwards.

Both fail deterministically with the respective `delete` removed, and passed 160 parallel runs locally.

## Impact

- Tests only. No public API or wire change.

## Alternatives

- Measure after `setTimeout` so the stack unwinds, or spawn one task at a time so the set never grows: less flaky, still GC-dependent.
- Loosen the thresholds: papers over it.

## Follow-ups

- `js/binary`, `js/json`, `js/watch` (`sync.test.ts`, `retention.test.ts`) have end-to-end heap-count tests from #4085 with the same exposure. They have not failed in CI yet; left for a separate change since they have no single set to inspect.

(Written by Claude Opus 5.5)

author: gsoultan
body:
Plan item 3: the console at 375px. Measuring it properly turned up two defects that had nothing to do with width, both shipped in v0.4.0, so this is four commits.

## The console at phone width — `02254f45`

At 375px the sidebar kept 232px and left the page ~145px, inside a document 662px wide. Below `md` the nav is a drawer behind a burger. It's the same component as the column, on the same `--s-nav` plane, and it closes on the scrim, Escape, or navigation. Headers drop their secondary text, and page actions stack under the title.

**Tables were clipped at every width up to ~1300px, not only on phones.** `.panel` clips, so columns past its edge were unreachable. At 1024 People, Grants, Audit and Applications were cut off; at 1280 Audit lost 19px. `DataTable` now measures itself and sets `data-wide` only while the table doesn't fit, and only then does `.tbl-body` scroll sideways. A table that fits keeps its sticky header. A table that scrolls gives it up, because CSS can't make both work (overflow on one axis makes the other a scroller too).

Two follow-on bugs from that trade-off, both fixed:
- In a scrolling table, the sticky header sat 44px **over the first row**: against a box that never scrolls vertically, sticky only applies its offset. It's `static` there now.
- The toolbar rail crushed its controls ("Via membership" became "Via me"). It wraps now, and the header's sticky offset follows the rail's measured height.

Also: a person's page gave Access **35px**, under the Identity panel. It, Playground, Structure and the sign-in page editor now stack below `lg`. The attributes modal's value field was 38px; three buttons had clipped labels; a long permission key could push past its drawer.

## A person's page was blank on refresh — `e20e787b`

The bundle loaded assets by relative URL. From `/identities/<id>`, `./chunk.js` resolved to `/identities/chunk.js`, the SPA fallback answered with HTML, and the browser refused it. Clicking through from People worked; **a refresh or a shared link gave a blank page.** Assets are now root-absolute (`publicPath: '/'`). A `<base href>` wasn't an option because the shell's CSP sets `base-uri 'none'`. The build now refuses a shell with relative asset URLs; on the old config it failed naming both assets.

## Create drawers read their own form as a snapshot — `71d01783`

`form.state` is a snapshot, and typing re-renders the field, not the drawer.
- **Add a permission** could never be submitted: the preview stayed empty and the button stayed disabled, however the form was filled.
- **Add person** never showed the population's facts and never offered a category, so nobody added from the console had one.
- Axis, identity and role worked only because a validator happened to flip `canSubmit` after the relevant keystroke.

Render now subscribes (`useStore` or the `Subscribe` selector). The new `scripts/check/console-form-snapshots.sh` lists all six reads against `dev` and passes here.

## Memory — `673f7081`
Updated the Serena memories for console tables, the person page and the create drawers.

## Verification
- **Routes:** all 17 authenticated routes at 375, 800, 1024, 1280 and 1440. Each run asserts the page rendered, then that nothing overflows the document or `<main>`, no panel clips, no hidden overflow, and no header is displaced at rest. All green. (The first version of this check passed a blank page, which is how the refresh bug surfaced.)
- **Sticky headers:** at 1440 the People header pins exactly under its rail, and Audit and Roles pin to the top. At 1024 the wide tables scroll their header away and Roles keeps it.
- **Drawers:** all 7 create drawers at 375 are clean. The permission preview wraps a 69-character key inside the drawer, submitting shows the "declared by the manifest" explanation, and a categorised population shows its Category field.
- **Shell:** the nav drawer opens, its list scrolls to the last link, and choosing a destination closes it. Sign-in and setup are fine at 375.
- **Screenshots:** light and dark, at 375 and 1280.
- **Build and gates:** `bun run build` (tsc included) is clean, and all 14 `scripts/check` gates are green.

## Trade-off to know about
**Audit at 1280** is 19px too wide with the current data, because its Detail chips don't wrap and the widest value sets the column. It now scrolls to reach them instead of cutting them off, but its header doesn't stick at that width. From 1366 up everything fits and sticks.

## Found, not fixed
- The permission drawer rejects resource and action names over 31 characters with "Lowercase snake_case, starting with a letter." The message doesn't mention length, and the rule mirrors nothing on the server: manifests accept any non-empty value.

author: jurajmajerik
body:
## Problem

Experiment metrics recalculate once per day per team. A customer wants results refreshed twice a day, and the single `experiment_recalculation_time` column cannot hold a second time.

## Changes

- Adds `experiment_recalculation_times` to `TeamExperimentsConfig`: a list of `"HH:00:00"` UTC strings, at most 2 entries, distinct, at least 6 hours apart (circular, so 23:00 and 01:00 count as 2 hours). Includes a backfill from the legacy column.
- The `experiments_config` serializer validates the list and keeps both columns in sync: writing either one updates the other.
- Nothing changes for users yet. The hourly workflows still read the legacy column; the read path and the flag-gated UI come in follow-up PRs.

Design notes:

- A list column instead of a second time column, so raising the cap later is a serializer constant change, not a migration.
- Entries must be on the hour because scheduling is hour-granular (24 hourly Temporal schedules). The legacy column silently ignores minutes; the new field rejects them instead.
- The write path ships before the read path so there is no deploy window where new code reads a column old code does not write.

## How did you test this code?

- Extended the `experiments_config` tests in `test_project.py`: a sync round-trip test (catches dual-write drift, which would make recalcs run at the wrong hour) and parameterized reject cases (sub-hour times the scheduler would ignore, overlapping times, too many entries, empty list).
- `sqlmigrate` confirms the migration is a plain nullable `ADD COLUMN` on the extension table.
- Not tested: the backfill migration (trivial hour extraction on a small table).

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None. The setting gets docs with the UI PR.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Fable 5

Skills invoked: /wt, /django-migrations, /improving-drf-endpoints, /writing-tests, /writing-user-facing-copy, /writing-code-comments, /writing-pr-descriptions, /reviewing-with-coderabbit.

CodeRabbit CLI: signed out in this worktree; the human chose to skip, so the PR opened without a local pass.

Session decisions: the stored format moved from a single `TimeField` to a list of hour-granular strings after weighing ints vs time strings; strings keep the schema open for sub-hourly scheduling while validation rejects precision the scheduler does not honor. `hogli build:openapi` produced no generated-type changes because the `experiments_config` action has no `@extend_schema` (pre-existing; the frontend calls it with raw `api.get`).

author: m-ikmal-hisham
body:
## Summary
Organisers who don't have full player details could not start a match: Start Match stayed disabled until both lineups held registered players. Scores can now be saved against the team, and the player attached to the same score later.

**Frontend** (`MatchDetail`, `MatchControls`, `PlayerPicker`)
- **Start Match:** no longer blocked. Without both lineups it shows an amber note and asks for confirmation.
- **Picker:** the team-only option reads "Team only, add player later". With no lineup, the picker lists the team's **squad for this tournament** (club roster if no squad is registered), not the whole organisation. Everything it offers is accepted by the backend, so a school's U14 players no longer appear under its U16 side.
- **Match Events:** a score or card saved without a player shows "Team", and for admins a "+ Add player" button that opens the picker ("Who scored this?"). This also works after full time. Scrums and lineouts stay team-only.

**Backend**
- `PUT /matches/events/{id}` accepts `playerId`:
  - present: attaches or changes the player;
  - explicit `null`: removes the player;
  - absent: leaves the player unchanged.
- The player must be on the team's roster or its tournament squad. This is the same check as recording an event, now in one shared `resolveTeamPlayer`.
- Failures go through `GlobalExceptionHandler`:
  - not in the squad → **400**: "<Name> is not in <Team>'s roster or squad for this tournament. Add them to the squad first, then try again.";
  - unknown player → **404**.
- Same permissions as other edits: after the 5-minute grace period, only super admin, match manager, supervisor or the assigned referee.
- Attaching a player does not change points. Scores are recalculated as for any edit.

## Testing
- `MatchEventServiceImplTest` (new, 6 tests):
  - attaches a roster player;
  - attaches a tournament-squad player;
  - rejects another team's player (with the message);
  - an explicit null removes the player;
  - a minute-only edit keeps the player;
  - the grace-period lock still applies.
- Full backend suite: 383 passed. `tsc -b`, `vite build` and `eslint` on the touched files: pass, no warnings.
- Admin match screen: typechecked, not viewed in the browser (needs a login).

author: lexasoft123
body:
## The problem

Holding Cmd+T makes Shitty exit: every tab and the window vanish, with no crash report.

Nothing caps the tab count, and each tab costs a pty and a forked shell. When the system refuses one (out of file descriptors, ptys or processes), `Pty::spawn` calls `sysError()`, which calls `exit(1)`. launchd gives GUI apps a **256 descriptor soft limit** and a tab costs about one, so key repeat reaches it in well under a minute.

Reproduced through the real `Pty::spawn` (test mode's `NEW_SESSION` uses a fake pty and does not exercise it) with a 128-descriptor limit; tab 124 printed

```
Error: can't open slave pty: open(): Too many open files (errno=24)
```

and the process exited with status 1. That this is the reported crash is an inference from the symptoms (no crash report, needs sustained key repeat); I don't have a stack for it.

## The fix

- `Pty::spawn`'s pty-open steps and `fork` now throw through `raiseError()` (the recoverable path `newSession()` already cleans up for) instead of exiting, and close the master descriptor the failed step still held, so a refused attempt leaks nothing.
- The new-tab action catches it, prints `Warning: cannot open a new tab: ...` to stderr, and leaves every existing tab alone.
- A failure of the very *first* tab at startup still ends the run, with the same `Error: ...` line the top-level handler printed before.

`sysError()` is unchanged and still used for the genuinely fatal drain-thread setup.

## Test

`Pty::RefusedSpawnThrowsAndLeaksNothing` runs the real `Pty` under a tight `RLIMIT_NOFILE`. Spawning must be refused with an exception, and a second round must open at least as many terminals as the first (a master left open by a refused attempt would shrink it). Against the old `pty.cpp` it kills the test binary with the error above; with the fix it passes. The `Error: F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC` lines in its output are forked children reporting on their own stderr at the starved boundary.

- The full unit suite passes through `./build`'s own runner, and `tst/test_tabs.py` passes (26/26).
- **Not verified:** the Cmd+T catch in `session.cpp` was read and compiled but not exercised, since test mode substitutes its own pty and I couldn't synthesize key events in a real window.

## Not in this PR

No tab cap, and no raising the descriptor soft limit at startup. Once the limit is hit, other things that need a descriptor can still fail, so raising `RLIMIT_NOFILE` at startup is probably worth a follow-up.

body:
## Summary

In nightly run [36109907148](https://github.com/BentoBoxWorld/bbox-test-harness/actions/runs/36109907148), 26.3 reported **48 failures** that all came from one bug:

1. Boxed failed to enable (BentoBoxWorld/Boxed#135).
2. That left a game mode with a null world, so `bbox v` threw an NPE (BentoBoxWorld/BentoBox#3089).
3. The `bbox v` output stopped before the world and addon lists, so every addon and world check failed.

When `bbox v` output contains a command exception, the harness now does this:
- **Core Load** reports the exception once as `'bbox v' completes without an exception`. It no longer also fails the addon-list and no-ERROR checks for the same reason.
- **Addon Load** reads BentoBox's startup log instead. An addon counts as enabled if `Enabling <Addon> (...)` appears and no `Skipping <Addon>`, `has dependency on`, `Cannot load`, `is disabled.` or `Addon <Addon>:` message names it.
- **World Registration** passes a world if its owning addon enabled and the world appears in the log. Otherwise the failure message gives the owning addon's reason.

Each fallback result says `(from startup log; 'bbox v' crashed)`, and the runner prints a warning with the exception. Runs where `bbox v` works are unchanged.

## Testing

Replayed against the server logs saved from run 36109907148:

| Log | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 26.3 (bbox v crashed) | 15 passed, 48 failed | 57 passed, 5 failed: Boxed in Core Load, Addon Load and World Registration (`Skipping Boxed due to an unhandled exception...`), plus the Boxed ERROR and the expected BentoBox compatibility WARN in Console Health |
| 26.2 | no crash | no crash detected; Core 4/4; fallback agrees with `bbox v` on all 33 addons |
| 1.21.5 | no crash | no crash detected; fallback agrees with `bbox v` (only TradeWinds not enabled) |

author: alundgren
body:
New operators could receive internal function names and invented workflow instructions. Directed requests could also prepare a broader review than requested or claim a preview was ready after preparation failed.

This change keeps Ministral 3B and Jev. The Work module owns onboarding, recorded order and queue facts, and review explanations. One bounded Jev selection request chooses a maintained reply or sends the request to Ministral's normal tool loop. Mixed requests and supported actions still reach that loop. Human acceptance remains the only way to commit a reviewed business change.

- Replace API-oriented instructions with the actual operator workflow and explicit tool call conditions.
- Derive preview, failure, and tutorial acknowledgements from validated application results. Retain useful order details when compacting tool responses and keep unexpected diagnostics in Audit.
- Let the model request whole-receipt Undo through an order ID and expected operation kind/count. The server resolves the latest receipt and checks those values; existing version checks reject intervening edits. The tool cannot target an earlier historical receipt.
- Document the experiments, model comparisons, costs, failure cases, and reusable guidance for other domains. Keep the existing temperature setting and require provider support for requested parameters.

Start with the [reusable engineering guide](https://github.com/alundgren/parcel-hopscotch-playground/blob/9546dfc261e94b3e2fe259a1d994db4f607a1338/docs/tool-assistant-engineering.md). The [investigation report](https://github.com/alundgren/parcel-hopscotch-playground/blob/9546dfc261e94b3e2fe259a1d994db4f607a1338/docs/tool-assistant-investigation-2026-09-25.md) and [structured evidence](https://github.com/alundgren/parcel-hopscotch-playground/blob/9546dfc261e94b3e2fe259a1d994db4f607a1338/docs/tool-assistant-evidence-2026-09-25.json) retain configurations, scenario grades, source fingerprints, and limitations. Raw paid-call artifacts and credentials are excluded from this PR.

Validation completed locally:

- Build, typecheck, guidance boundary checks, and whitespace checks passed. Independent completion review found no material defect.
- The final 240-test server run passed 239 tests and failed one existing one-second timing assertion at 1,266 ms. The isolated 18-test provider-audit rerun passed, including that assertion at 749 ms. All 240 unique tests passed across those runs.
- All 54 Browser Mode tests passed at desktop and narrow widths before the final server-only Undo changes. The attached PNGs were visually inspected. All 22 affected E2E tests passed on the final application source.
- The final targeted live Undo regression passed 3/3 using the retained models, fresh synthetic databases, and simulated UI acknowledgements. No measured assistant turn accepted a business change. The earlier 26-case release screen and separate six-case holdout were not rerun on the final source. The repository's human-invoked live suite was not run.

The selector adds a Jev request to each standard live chat turn, with corresponding latency, cost, and availability dependency. Classification and free-text responses remain fallible. Receipt kind/count checks establish consistency, not user intent. These small synthetic experiments do not establish a production success rate.

The attached screenshots show maintained onboarding at 1440×1000 and 320×900, an address preview with its human acceptance control and separate packing explanation, and a held preview whose acceptance control is disabled. They use rendered application components with synthetic fixtures; they are layout and wording evidence, not live-model measurements.

author: eastlondoner
body:
A value bound in a `match` that isn't in tail position was held until its function returned. Examples are the scrutinee of `match make() {...}`, what an arm binds, and temporaries. This affected every heap value, and was found through GPU handles in #1.

## Cause
A `match` whose value is used, rather than returned, lowers to a `LetJoin`. `core_ir/perceus.rs` treated a `LetJoin`'s body as opaque, and its own comment said no drops were inserted inside it. The `join_body_defers_drop` golden recorded that gap.

## Fix
Perceus now works through the `LetJoin` with the same rules as any other branch:
- At the end of each arm, everything the code after the match reads counts as live. Each arm drops everything else it owns, through guards, fallthrough jumps between cases, nested matches and early exits.
- A value that an arm's final expression reads for the last time is handed over to the match's result instead of being dropped. This is Lean's and Koka's rule that a jump to a join point consumes its argument. It adds `Atom::Move` to Core IR (printed `move %x`) and a VM instruction, `Take`, that hands over the register's reference instead of copying it.
- A freed cell stays available for reuse after the match only if every arm leaves it free, so reuse also works inside matches. The loop-reuse test still makes 1 cell and reuses 1,000.
- `is_heap` now answers `true` for a type variable, so a value passed through a generic parameter is dropped at its last use. The VM's `Drop` already does nothing for a plain value.
- Strings are now dropped too. They are always cells in the new VM, but were never dropped.

## Tests
- **New test built-in:** `internal.cells_live()`, like `cells_made`.
- **Exact tests of the live-cell count after a match:**
  - in each arm, behind a guard, in a match nested in another, in a loop;
  - a value an arm returns survives, including a closure that captured it;
  - a value still read after the match is kept until then;
  - every kind of cell (array, closure, tuple, binary, string);
  - a generic value, and a string;
  - three matches in a row hold 0/0/0 (previously 2/4/6).
- **Randomized:** 300 seeded programs with nested matches, guards and matches inside arms. After every statement, the live-cell count is checked against a model of what is still reachable, along with each program's printed answer.
- **Core IR goldens** show the new drops and moves.
- **Proof the tests bite:** with the old `perceus.rs` and `rty.rs` restored, all 11 new VM tests fail.
- No committed allocation count changed.

## Performance (best of 5, back to back)
| Program | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `bench_heavy` | 1.81 s | 1.66 s |
| `bench_typed` | 1.05 s | 0.99 s |
| `bench_map` | 4.59 s | 4.33 s |

All 45 examples and test programs print the same output and exit the same way as before.

## Checked together with #1
I merged this onto #1 (`metal-handles`, at `0c7b84e`) in a scratch tree. The only conflicts were both sides adding to the lists of built-in functions, and keeping both resolved them.
- #1's three lifetime tests, which are ignored while they wait for this fix, then pass on both the fake GPU and Metal: 6 of 6.
- The reviewer's reproducer then prints 0 handles held after each match, instead of 2.
- The full suite passes: 1,317 tests, 0 failed.

## Checks run locally (M1 Max)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | exit 0 |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |
| `cargo test --workspace` | 1,266 passed, 0 failed |
| hawk (host target) | 0 findings |
| mordant | exit 0 |
| `bun run corpus` | exit 0 |

Not done: an arm whose value is a constructor built from values it reads for the last time costs an extra drop and a `Take`, because a constructor copies its fields. Having a constructor take ownership of its fields would be a separate optimisation. Big Ints are still held until the frame exits, by design.

🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL/HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** Uncast `req.query` and `req.body` parameters across multiple routes (`placements.js`, `events.js`, `notices.js`, `materials.js`, `auth.js`) allowed NoSQL injection via object payloads, Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) via unescaped special characters, and Type Denial of Service (Type DoS) crashes when non-string inputs hit `.toLowerCase()`.
🎯 **Impact:** Malicious actors could crash the server by passing arrays/objects to string methods, cause severe CPU spikes via crafted regex inputs (ReDoS), or manipulate database queries via NoSQL object injection.
🔧 **Fix:** Explicitly cast vulnerable inputs to `String()` before applying string methods or regex constructors, and properly escape regex characters where dynamic strings are used for MongoDB regex matching.
✅ **Verification:** Verified that variables are explicitly cast to string safely before methods are applied, which turns object payloads to `"[object Object]"`, effectively stopping crashes and logic injections. Node native syntax validation passes. Tests are currently missing in the workspace.

author: xiaods
body:
## Summary

Three of #592's remaining merge gates, of which one turned out to be a live
defect rather than cleanup. Related to #592; does not close it.

- The ~30 unrouted etcd handlers were dead code, not a registration gap.
- `Maintenance.Status` is now served, and it was worth serving.
- The snapshot reconcile loop logged an error every second on a Tandem node.

## The unrouted handlers were unreachable, not merely unregistered

`grpc-lite` looks the method path up in its handler table before dispatch and
answers `unimplemented "method not found"` for anything missing
(`tandem/vendor/grpc-lite/src/server.zig:3358-3360`). A request for
`Cluster/MemberList` therefore never reached `processRequest`, so the handler
behind it had never run. The Cluster(5), Auth(17) and remaining Maintenance(6)
handlers were dead code — about 230 lines — and most of them answered with a
constant: an empty member list, a fabricated leader and raft index of 1, a
hash of 0, an `AuthEnable`-shaped reply to `UserList`.

That is the opposite of what registering them would have achieved. Today's
answer is an honest `Unimplemented`; wiring those handlers up would have
replaced it with something that looks like success, which KIP-29 forbids for a
call the layer does not serve. They are deleted, and a comment on
`routeRequest` records that re-adding one means building it against rqlite's
`/nodes` and membership endpoints rather than restoring a placeholder.

Two were kept. `handleSnapshot` returns `SnapshotNotImplemented` rather than an
empty body — it is the model the rest should have followed, and deleting it
would have removed the only in-tree instance of that rule.

## Maintenance.Status is now served

This is the one registration that was actually worth making. The apiserver calls
`Status` on **every start**, from `etcd3.New` through `CheckClient`
(`apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go:205`), to read the endpoint version and
decide whether `RequestWatchProgress` is supported. While it was unrouted that
probe failed on each boot, logged at error level, and left watch-list initial
events disabled.

The handler was not a stub — its `db_size` is a real page count and its
`version` is the string the apiserver parses. But its `leader`, `raft_index`
and `raft_applied_index` were the constant 1, which is a fabricated answer in
exactly the place an operator would look during an incident. They now come from
rqlite's `/status`.

Reading them required parsing that response structurally. rqlite nests `leader`
and `raft` inside `store`, and both carry a `node_id` and a `term`, so the
existing first-match string scan returned whichever appeared first in the
document rather than the one being asked for. Two tests cover the nesting.

The leader is reported as present-or-absent rather than by id: rqlite
identifies a member by string and etcd's `Status` reports a numeric member id,
so there is no honest number to put there. `known_differences.go` records that
along with what would make it comparable.

## A live defect: the snapshot reconcile log flood

`Cluster.Start` polls `ReconcileSnapshotData` once a second and logs whatever
it returns, retrying until it succeeds
(`pkg/cluster/cluster.go:77`). The Tandem driver returns an error
permanently, because there is nothing for it to reconcile, and
`--etcd-disable-snapshots` defaults to false. Every Tandem node without that
flag therefore logged

```
Failed to record snapshots for cluster: tandem snapshot reconciliation is not implemented
```

at error level, once a second, for the life of the process.

A driver with no counterpart for an operation now returns
`managed.ErrNotImplemented`, and the loop treats that as terminal — it is not a
failure and retrying it cannot succeed. A test asserts the sentinel is
distinguishable from a real failure, because the loop must still retry the
latter.

Also fixes a hardcoded `Managed etcd` in the cluster-reset message, which would
have pointed an operator at the wrong data directory under the Tandem backend.

## Dead Go code

`pkg/etcd/etcdproxy.go` (143 lines) was the kine intermediary KIP-29 removed,
with no callers left anywhere, and `GetAPIServerURLsFromETCD` had none either.
`ClientURLs` was checked and **kept** — an audit classified it as dead, but it
is called from `pkg/etcd/etcd.go:575`.

## Not in this PR, deliberately

- **Switching the default backend.** It is still embedded etcd. #592 is explicit
  that this must not happen before the M3 gate, so the driver registration
  order is untouched.
- **`pkg/embedw` and `tests/etcdrobustness`.** The differential suite starts its
  embedded etcd through `tests/etcdrobustness`, which imports `pkg/embedw`.
  Removing it would remove the ability to check Tandem against etcd at all.
- **Three-node lifecycle.** Separate round; the scoping is in `m1-status.md`.
- **Re-wiring Cluster/Maintenance/Auth.** That is feature work against rqlite's
  membership API, not cleanup.

## Verification

- `zig build test`: 165/165
- `go test -tags=tandem_differential ./pkg/tandem/differential`: 23/23 against a
  real embedded etcd and a real rqlited on Linux arm64, including the new
  `Status` case on both backends
- `go test -tags=tandem_integration ./pkg/tandem`: 34/34, no regression
- `go test ./pkg/cluster/... ./pkg/etcd/... ./pkg/tandem/...`: pass
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./pkg/...`: clean

The differential suite passing after the deletion is the load-bearing check:
those handlers were unreachable, so removing them cannot change observed
behaviour, and it does not.

author: panosrepoussis
body:
Found by asking whether header casing mattered while debugging the Claude.ai connector (#53). Header *names* don't. The **scheme in the value** does, and shouldn't.

## The bug

Verified against the live hosted endpoint:

| `Authorization` value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Bearer <key>` | **200**, valid handshake |
| `bearer <key>` | **401** |
| `BEARER <key>` | **401** |

RFC 9110 §11.1 defines `auth-scheme` as a **case-insensitive token**. `readApiKeyFromRequest` used `authorization.startsWith('Bearer ')`.

Header *names* were never affected — Node lowercases them before they reach `req.headers`. Confirmed: `Authorization`, `authorization` and `AUTHORIZATION` all handshake.

## Why it matters more than the status code suggests

The rejection message is actively misleading:

> Missing VerifyAX API key. Send `Authorization: Bearer sk-ver-api-...`

A client that normalised the scheme is told the header is *missing*, sending whoever reads it hunting for a header they did send. That's an expensive wrong turn for a one-character difference.

## Fix

`/^Bearer[ \t]+/i`, which also tolerates a tab or repeated spaces between scheme and token.

## Tests

`readApiKeyFromRequest` had **no coverage at all** — that's how this survived. Now covered:

- the scheme as `Bearer`, `bearer`, `BEARER`, `BeArEr`
- extra spaces and a tab after the scheme
- the `X-VerifyAX-API-Key` fallback, and `Authorization` taking precedence
- falling through to `X-VerifyAX-API-Key` when the Bearer token is empty
- `undefined` cases: no headers, `Basic`, a bare `Bearer`, empty `X-VerifyAX-API-Key`, and **`Bearertoken`** — which a prefix match without the mandatory separator would wrongly accept

All 14 cases verified locally against the new logic. (Local `vitest` can't run on this Windows checkout — a `#module-sync-enabled` resolution failure in the pnpm store, unrelated to this change — so CI is the authority on the suite itself.)

## Relationship to #53

This is **not** established as the cause of the Claude.ai connector failure, and I'm not claiming it is. It's a real bug found while investigating one. If Claude.ai does send a normalised `authorization: bearer …`, this would have been the cause — worth re-testing the connector once this ships, before assuming OAuth is required.

## Summary
Performance fixes for the 3D preview, based on a comparison with 3dome.tw's renderer. Only changes that don't affect continuous playback or the look of the scene.

- **Geometry leak (main fix)**: `StageObjectRenderer` called `node.geometry.clone()` on every render and never disposed the copies. Each content or render-mode switch uploaded new GPU buffers. It now uses the cached GLTF geometry directly and memoizes the mesh lookup.
- **Dispose**: replaced materials and image textures are now disposed. Also fixes the video-texture cleanup, which disposed a stale state value instead of the texture it created.
- **Removed per-render `console.log`** from the render path.
- **Removed the unused shadow map pass** (`shadows="soft"` + `castShadow`): no mesh casts shadows, so this has no visual change.
- **`antialias: false`**: the SMAA pass in EffectComposer already handles anti-aliasing. Native MSAA only applied to the final blit.
- **DPR capped at 1.5 on touch or small screens.** Desktop stays at 2, which is also what recordings use.

### Intentionally unchanged
- `frameloop` stays `always` while video plays or recording mode is on, so playback and animations keep running.
- Bloom stays on (LED glow look).
- `preserveDrawingBuffer: true` stays, for `captureStream()` recording compatibility.

author: maxprain12
body:
## Why

2.9.0 and 2.9.1 crash at startup with `Cannot find module 'once'`. It is not an asar/unpacked issue: `once` is simply not in `app.asar`, and neither are 14 other packages (`debug`, `ajv`, `express`, `cross-spawn`, `string-width`, …). Fixing only `once` would have crashed on the next one (`debug` is needed by the auto-updater).

Root cause is electron-builder 26.15.3's pnpm collector (still present in 26.16.1):

- It marks visited packages by `name@version`. pnpm installs two peer-dependency variants of `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.29.0` (zod 3 under shadcn, zod 4 under @google/genai) and prints the full subtree only under the second one. The collector skips it, so every `deduped` reference to `express`, `ajv`, `once`… is dropped with a warning.
- `string-width@4.2.3` is printed in full only under its npm alias `string-width-cjs`, so the same thing happens.

#1711 tried to copy `once`/`wrappy` by hand, but its copy filter excluded every file (the real path always contains `node_modules`), leaving empty folders.

## What

- `patches/app-builder-lib@26.15.3.patch`: key visited packages by store path and resolve deduped references by path. `electron-builder` pinned to `26.15.3` so the patch cannot silently stop applying.
- Removed the #1711 workaround (`once`/`wrappy` direct deps + `materializeHoisted`).
- `pnpm run check:packaged-deps` (CI Lint): runs electron-builder's collector without packaging and fails on any unresolved dependency. Before: 15 unresolved. After: 0.
- `scripts/after-pack.cjs`: fails the build if any package in `app.asar` cannot resolve a non-optional dependency (logic in `scripts/verify-packaged-app.cjs`, tests in `test:packaged-deps`). Also checks ffmpeg against the target arch and warns when native prebuilts (sharp, lancedb, canvas, ffmpeg) do not match it. The macOS x64 build currently ships arm64 prebuilts; that stays a warning until a follow-up fixes it.

## Verification

- Gate run against the installed 2.9.1 `app.asar`: reports exactly the 15 missing packages.
- Unsigned `electron-builder --mac --arm64 --dir`: after-pack reports every dependency resolves; `once`, `debug`, `ajv`, `express` present; the packaged app boots with an isolated `DOME_PROFILE` (DB, init, updater) with no `Cannot find module`.
- `typecheck`, `lint`, `check:asar-unpack`, `check:sonar-patterns --diff`, `test:packaged-deps`.

author: n4k3l0
body:
Firecrawl's credits ran out, and every scrape now returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Three sources that go through it stopped adding jobs, including **MyJobMag, the main source of Nigerian jobs**. The logs were full of the failures.

Those pages load fine for a plain request that says who we are, so they don't need Firecrawl.

No migration.

## What changes
- **Direct first.** `scrape_url` and `scrape_html` fetch the page directly with an honest user agent (`JobHuntPipeline/1.0`). The HTML is turned into the markdown shape the source parsers already read, with links made absolute.
- **Firecrawl only as a fallback**, when a direct fetch fails. After a 429 it's left alone for an hour, so one run doesn't hit it once per page.
- **Wellfound company names.** The company and location now come from the `JobPosting` record the page embeds (new `discovery/jobposting.py`). Before, most Wellfound jobs arrived as company "Unknown".
- **MyJobMag company names.** Its pages are titled "Finance officer at First Ally Trust MFB", which now gives title "Finance officer" and company "First Ally Trust MFB" instead of "Unknown".
- **DailyRemote is off.** Its job pages now show the company as "[Hidden Company]" and no longer carry the job data the parser reads, so every run fetched pages and kept nothing.
- **No workarounds.** A site that blocks direct requests or shows a human check is never worked around; it just falls to Firecrawl or is skipped.

## Checked
Ran each source live with Firecrawl switched off (read-only, nothing saved):

| Source | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| MyJobMag | nothing (429) | 3 of 3 sampled; e.g. "Finance officer" at First Ally Trust MFB |
| Wellfound | nothing (429) | 3 of 3; e.g. "AI Engineer" at Redule Ai, Dubai |
| Undutchables | nothing (429) | 3 of 3 |
| DailyRemote | nothing | off; the site now hides what we need |

- Tests: 229 pass, 5 of them new in `test_page_fetch.py`: a page that answers is read directly without touching Firecrawl; Firecrawl is the fallback and rests after a 429; no key means a blocked page is simply skipped; the JobPosting record is parsed; MyJobMag titles split into role and company.

A note on duplicates: MyJobMag jobs that are still listed will come in once more with their real company name, since the old copies say "Unknown". That settles on its own as the old copies expire.
