author: santhoshcharanbolt
body:
## Summary

Bolt is migrating its asset and API domains from `bolt.com` to `boltapp.com`. This points the Bolt integration's asset host at the new apex.

Scripts served from `bolt.com` are third-party in a `boltapp.com` context, so cookies they set are partitioned and shopper recognition degrades. Bolt's API layer has already moved; today a single BigCommerce checkout page loads Bolt assets from `connect.bolt.com` while calling `api.boltapp.com`. This change makes the two consistent.

## Changes

`getDomainURL()` now returns the `boltapp.com` apex for the production, staging and sandbox branches:

| Branch | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Production | `connect.bolt.com` | `connect.boltapp.com` |
| `StagingMode` | `connect-staging.bolt.com` | `connect-staging.boltapp.com` |
| Sandbox / no developer config | `connect-sandbox.bolt.com` | `connect-sandbox.boltapp.com` |
| `DevelopmentMode` | `connect.${developerDomain}` | unchanged |

`DevelopmentMode` is deliberately untouched — it interpolates the caller's `developerDomain`, which is already a fully qualified host.

Every Bolt asset the SDK injects derives its host from this one function, so all of the following move together:

- `connect-bigcommerce.js` and `track.js` (`loadBoltClient`)
- `embed.js` (`loadBoltEmbedded`)
- the product-page checkout button `v1/checkout_button` URL (`BoltButtonStrategy`)

## Verification

The `boltapp.com` hosts are live and serve byte-identical bundles to their `bolt.com` counterparts:

```
connect.bolt.com/connect-bigcommerce.js             200   1,489,437 bytes
connect.boltapp.com/connect-bigcommerce.js          200   1,489,437 bytes
connect-staging.bolt.com/connect-bigcommerce.js     200   1,489,459 bytes
connect-staging.boltapp.com/connect-bigcommerce.js  200   1,489,459 bytes
```

Locally, on this branch:

- `nx test bolt-integration` — 9 suites, 88 tests passing
- `nx lint bolt-integration` — clean
- `tsc --noEmit` — 10 pre-existing project-reference errors, identical count on `master` with the change stashed

## Risk

Merchants whose Content Security Policy names `connect.bolt.com` explicitly will need `connect.boltapp.com` added before this reaches them. Bolt is tracking that rollout separately.

author: casualarclamp
body:
Seven bugs turned up while auditing what the project is missing. Each is one commit, with tests, and each commit message says why in full.

## What changes

1. **V.42bis: a far end's P1 below the minimum is refused, not built** (`b7d9abd`). A far end's XID offering V.42bis with a P1 of 259 or less crashed the line thread as the dictionary was built. `Xid::resolve` now settles such an offer to no compression, as V.44 already does below its own minimum, and the answer says P0 = 0 so the far end does not compress at us.
2. **ZMODEM: every file of a batch, `sz -e`, and names Windows cannot misread** (`a7b7319`).
   - **Batch:** of a batch, only the last file used to be kept. Each file is now kept as its ZEOF lands, via `take_arrived()`.
   - **ZSINIT:** it is answered now. Also, `sz` ends a hex header with a line feed that has its parity bit set (0212), so the header's tail is now matched on seven bits.
   - **Names:** `safe_name` now defuses drive-relative names (`C:x.dll`), alternate streams and device names.
   - **Test:** new `tests/lrzsz.rs` runs the receiver against real `sz` where lrzsz is installed, and passes quietly where it is not.
3. **Proxy: the answering end goes to the internet and nowhere nearer** (`753f2bb`).
   - **Destinations:** a caller can no longer reach the answering machine's loopback or LAN; such requests get a 403.
   - **Behaviour change:** CONNECT is limited to port 443, per RFC 9110 9.3.6. A plain request may go to 80, 443 or any port above 1023.
   - **Tests:** the tests with a loopback web server opt out with `reach_anywhere()`.
4. **SIP: RTP follows the call's stream, not whoever sends to the port** (`4c0ad57`). After a call's first packet, a packet from a new address is followed only if it continues the call's own stream (same SSRC, sequence carrying on), per RFC 3550 8.2 and A.1. Anything else is dropped and counted in `strangers`.
5. **Far-end panel: which compression the call is running, V.44 included** (`bdb0da1`).
   - **Offer and answer:** the stack keeps the far end's XID command and response apart.
   - **Panel rows:** the panel shows what the far end offered and what the call is running. It said "none offered" on every call running V.44.
   - **README:** this removes the "compression in V.90 not offered correctly" work-in-progress item. That item came from live calls; the fix is confirmed only in simulation.
6. **Fax: a page the far end could not read is sent again** (`c402330`). Per T.30 5.3.6.1.7 and Figure 5-2, RTN now leads to retraining a rung down and resending the page, up to twice. After that the call moves to the next page instead of hanging up at the first RTN. Under ECM, RTN still ends the call.
7. **V.44: ECM starts the dictionary again, and leaves the ESCAPE alone** (`861d29c`). V.44 7.5 and 7.14 set ESCAPE to 0 only at initialisation, but both the encoder and the decoder reset it on ECM. The new test builds its stream from the clause and fails on the old code.

## Testing

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude datapump --exclude dsp` passes in debug: 1312 passed, 0 failed. Neither excluded crate uses the changed code (datapump takes only `ec::hdlc` from ec), and datapump's debug tests passed through `v32_call` before that run was stopped for time.
- The modem call, fax and V.90 tests also pass in release.
- Every run was on Linux; the Windows CI job has not run yet.
- None of it has been on a live call.

author: pierrebrisorgueil
body:
## What
OAuth signup (Google / Apple) now provisions the user's workspace, like email signup does — but only for a genuine new signup.

## Why
OAuth users landed on the org-required page and had to create a workspace by hand; many stopped there.

## How
- `checkOAuthUserProfile`'s create branch (new account) marks its result so the caller can tell a brand-new signup apart from an existing/linked user.
- The Google/Apple strategy wrappers relay that as `info.created` through passport's verify callback.
- `oauthCallback`'s passport callback is now `async` and reads that 3rd `info` argument. After the `!user` guard, it calls `AuthOrganizationService.handleSignupOrganization(user)` only when `info.created` is true (best-effort try/catch, same pattern as `verifyEmail`). An existing user — whether on a normal login or one with no current org right now (removed from their org, org deleted, a pending join request) — is never re-provisioned.
- The whole callback body is wrapped in an outer try/catch routed to `oauthErrorRedirect`: passport never awaits the callback's promise, so any other throw would otherwise become an unhandled rejection. That fallback redirect now also checks `res.headersSent` first, so a throw after the success response already started writing can't attempt a conflicting second redirect.
- Error-logging for the callback deduped into one helper.

## Tests
`modules/auth/tests/auth.oauth.signup-org.unit.tests.js` (9 cases): provisioning fires on `info.created`, is skipped for an existing user with no current org, skipped for an existing user with a current org, skipped when `info` is absent entirely, skipped on `err` / `!user`, a provisioning rejection still sets the cookie and redirects, a throw past provisioning hits the outer catch, and a throw after headers are already sent does not attempt a second redirect. `auth.oauth.signup.analytics.unit.tests.js` extended to assert the new create-branch marker is set only on branch 4.

## Known gaps (out of scope)
- `suggestedJoin` (domain-match hint) is not carried through the OAuth redirect.
- A provider-unverified email with the mailer on still gets `emailVerificationRequired`.

Reviewer: /critical-review fallback (CodeRabbit rate-limited on this repo's Free review quota during this PR's review window). Finding: gating provisioning on "no current org" would have re-provisioned any existing org-less user on every OAuth login — fixed by gating on `info.created` instead.

Closes #4115

author: archledger
body:
## Summary

`irlume-gkr-unlock` reads the sealed GNOME keyring token from stdin and
sends it to gnome-keyring's control socket in an UNLOCK packet. Both
buffers now wipe themselves on drop:

- `read_token` reads the token into one fixed `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` of
  `MAX_TOKEN_LEN + 1` bytes, so it never reallocates, and locks its
  pages with `memlock::lock_slice` (best effort). The empty, length and
  printable checks and their messages are unchanged.
- `read_token_from_stdin` hands `read_token` an unbuffered `File` on a
  clone of the stdin descriptor, as `irlume-kwallet-init` does, so no
  copy stays in `Stdin`'s process-wide buffer.
- `gkr_wire::encode_request` returns `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`, allocated at
  its final size. This also covers the CHANGE packet `irlume keyring arm`
  and `forget` send. `gkr_wire::call` keeps its signature.

`irlume-gkr-unlock` now depends on `zeroize` directly (already in the
lockfile). Exit codes, messages and the wire format don't change.

## Testing

- The unit-test binary gets a copy of irlume-pam's `freed_blocks`
  allocator. It zero-fills every block and, while a test enables it,
  searches each byte buffer that test's thread frees for a marker.
  `the_freed_block_check_sees_an_unwiped_copy` checks that the allocator
  is installed.
- `the_unlock_packet_is_wiped_after_it_is_sent` drives `gkr_wire::call`
  against a scripted daemon. On main it fails with `the UNLOCK packet was
  freed without a wipe` (`left: 1, right: 0`). With the change it passes.
- `the_stdin_token_is_read_unbuffered_and_wiped` feeds a pipe to two
  fresh-exec children that run the real `run()` up to the user lookup and
  requires `1 passed` from each. On main, the accepted token fails with
  `left: 1, right: 0` and the oversized one with `left: 2, right: 0`. With
  the wipe check off, the oversized child also fails on main: the pipe has
  0 bytes left instead of 43, because `Stdin` drains it. With the change
  both children pass.
- `read_token` unit tests: exact, at-limit, over-limit, empty and
  non-printable input, a retried `Interrupted` read and a failed read.
  `read_token_joins_one_byte_reads` serves one byte per read and checks
  the exact token, a 256-byte token in order, and a refusal after exactly
  257 bytes. A read loop that writes every chunk at offset 0 passes the
  other tests and fails this one.
- `cargo test -p irlume-gkr-unlock -p irlume-common`: 9 + 178 passed.
  The gkr-unlock tests also pass under AddressSanitizer (nightly).

- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` passes (not run; `-p irlume-gkr-unlock -p irlume-common` above)
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (not run; `-p irlume-common -p irlume-gkr-unlock --all-targets` clean on 1.88.0)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean
- [ ] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` clean (not run; both crates clean)
- [x] Docs/CHANGELOG updated if user-facing
- [ ] Hardware-validated (not run: `scripts/gkr-token-check.sh` needs a live gnome-keyring session)

Brings the installer from 2.0.4 to mx-mac's 2.0.10. Stacked on #3; GitHub retargets it to `main` when #3 merges.

The ten mx-mac commits that touched the installer after the extraction (`maralcbr/omarchy-mx-mac` `4db862da..92a9054f`) are replayed with `git format-patch --relative=apps/omarchy-apple-installer` and `git am`. Authors, dates and messages are kept, and each message names its source commit. Two conflicts with #3 were resolved in place: the descriptor fixture line and the Release README. One last commit moves the new identifiers onto `identity.conf`: the engine-failure error domain, the stderr queue label, the user log folder and the wording that names it. Apart from #3's identity derivation, every ported file is byte-identical to mx-mac at `92a9054f`. Identity and hosting stay mx-mac and aicodelabs.

2.0.10 parity, item by item:
- [x] 2.0.6, 2.0.8 and 2.0.10 version bumps; the app is now 2.0.10, build 27 (mx #195, #225, #262)
- [x] rc-aurora retired: two channels, stable and rc, in `ReleaseChannel`, the descriptor, `make-release-descriptor` and `build-app.sh` (mx #197, #198)
- [x] the window shows which channel the download fetches (mx #223)
- [x] the app opens on Stable every launch; a channel switch lasts only for that session (mx #223, #228)

- [x] engine failure diagnostics (mx #259, `EngineFailureDiagnostics.swift`). The helper keeps the engine's stderr, bounded and redacted, in root-only diagnostics. It returns a typed reason and a journal-proven disk-unchanged flag over XPC. The app shows plain wording, offers a re-plan for a size refusal and saves a user log.
- [x] a refused Mac is named, and the supported models are listed by name (mx #259, `MacModelNames.swift`)
- [x] runbook note from mx #232 and #263, with its links pinned to the mx-mac revision
- `scripts/publish-channels` still knows rc-aurora, as mx 2.0.10 does. The live bucket still serves that catalog.
- Not included: mx #265 (retry a dropped payload download). It landed after 2.0.10 and is unreleased.

Testing (M4 Pro, Xcode 26.6, Swift 6.3.3):
- `swift test`: debug 440 tests, release 434 tests, all passing. `swift-format lint --strict` is clean.
- `test/all` (Bash 5) passes, including the identity test.
- The live stable, rc and rc-aurora catalogs verify against the trust root (`publish-channels channel-status`). Stable lists `apple,j416c` (the M2 Max) as enabled.

- CI (portable and macOS checks) passed on `a03f256` through a manual run, since PR checks only run against `main`: https://github.com/omacom/omarchy-mac-installer/actions/runs/36111137456
- Nothing was signed with real credentials, notarized or published.
- Not done: an install on the M2 Max. The test Macs are unreachable, and it needs a Developer ID build. Steps are below.

Second review: two rounds. The first compared every ported file with mx-mac `92a9054f` and found no code problems. Its one verified finding was a stale channel guide link in the Release README, now pinned to the 2.0.10 guide. The second round found nothing.

Overlap with draft #2: `9899e0d` (channels from the bundled default per launch) and `924084f` (payload downloads coherent across replanning) are that branch's own versions of mx #223 and #228. They touch the same files: `ReleaseChannelPreference`, `InstallerSession`, `PayloadPrefetch`, `LiveInstallerEnvironment`, `OnePageInstallerView` and their tests, plus `build-app.sh` and `docs/extraction.md`. When #2 is rebased (ticket 21), the mx versions here should win and those two commits should drop.

M2 Max acceptance (owner):

4. Choose a new size while the payload downloads; the download should not restart. Install, then boot Omarchy.

body:
Closes #1874 Closes #1880 `ast::Directive` had no `title` field, so the parser discarded the opener's quoted title and every stage downstream inherited the loss: the wire could not carry it, `carve fmt` rewrote `::: toc "Contents" [T]` to `::: toc [T]` - deleting authored text from the user's own file, which is #1880 - and no placed element rendered it. The field is added and each stage carries it, implementing `CARVE-P9-072` (markup-carve/carve#2266). ````carve Intro[^a]. ::: footnotes "Notes" [End] ::: [^a]: first note ```` ````html

Intro1.

Notes

End

```` The TOC nav takes the same shape in place of the `tocNav` default. `glossary` places a `
` and `index` a `
    `, neither of which admits a paragraph, so both emit the tokens immediately before the generated content and name nothing. ## What moved besides the field - **Placement is decided the same way for every marker**: the document has a note, and no marker has placed yet. A marker in a document without one falls through to the ordinary typed-div rendering, which carries its title, its label and its own blocks, replacing the hand-written `
    ` that was shorter than the div every other empty container renders. Two tests expected that string. - **The id comes from the one `adm-{n}` sequence** a titled admonition already uses, reserved before the marker's children render, so a titled `::: note` written inside a titled marker takes the later number. - **A degraded div takes neither generated naming attribute and mints no id**, because ARIA prohibits both on role `generic`. The author's own `aria-label` survives verbatim, casing included, which is what carve-js and carve-php emit. - **`tests/spec` moves to `0cc4dbae`**, the commit that gave `directive` its `title`, so ingest accepts the field, and `src/wire_fields.rs` is regenerated from it with `tools/generate-wire-fields.py`. ## A reference in the title A footnote reference written in a directive title rendered as literal `[^a]` and produced no endnotes section, while the same reference in an admonition title worked. Collecting from `Directive.title` was not enough: the title MOVES onto the `ExtensionCarrier` that renders in the container's place, so collection reaches it there. Numbering it on the container alone numbered a copy nobody emits. ## The nav fragment stays at column 0 Extensions §8b.3 makes the `
    ` fragment the cross-impl contract. An earlier draft of this change indented the list whenever a title was present, and its own test pinned that indentation; both are corrected, and the fragment is byte-identical to carve-js again. ## Measured Fourteen shapes against carve-js `82f85e4ea`: placed titled, placed untitled, no marker, degraded titled, degraded untitled, a second marker, a titled admonition beside and inside the marker, an author-written name, markup in the title, escaping in the title and in the label, an empty title, and a bibliography marker. All byte-identical. `cargo nextest run -E 'not binary(perf_regressions)'`: 6512 of 6512 passing. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. Verification ran in a target dir of its own, because a concurrent build of another carve-rs checkout into the shared dir twice served this worktree a stale `carve-lang` rlib and produced two confident wrong readings; the isolated dir is deleted after this lands. ## Not in this PR Inside a heading section carve-rs indents the `
    ` opening tag where carve-js does not. That predates this change - an untitled `::: toc` shows it - so it gets its own ticket rather than riding here.

author: fabian-geyer
body:
The Binary and CoP shaders rendered into their num_pixel x num_pixel ID texture without setting the viewport, so they used the default viewport: the size of the hidden GLFW window. The OS clamps that window to the screen, so any num_pixel larger than the screen was silently rendered at the clamped, non-square size. Visibility then stopped improving with num_pixel, and small or thin triangles that never won a pixel were dropped from the hybrid loads (1.7 % of the projected area of the 61440 triangle shuttlecock on a 1536x960 screen).

Both shaders now set glViewport to num_pixel before drawing, as the per-pixel calculator already does.

test_viewport.cpp renders with a 64x64 window and num_pixel 800; before the fix Binary lost 11 of 20 sub-cell triangles. The CoP tetrahedron test used axis-aligned flow, where edge-on faces put a centroid exactly on another face's edge; it only passed with the old viewport, so its flow directions are now tilted slightly off the axes.

author: vicrdguez
body:
## Summary `skl propose cleanup` is now the explicit, ledger-backed cleanup for projects that have adopted the private Workflow Ledger. It has two independent outcomes: - **Ledger archival** (`ledger/archive.go`, `ArchiveTerminalProposals`). Inside the existing serialized ledger mutation, cleanup moves every whole Proposal whose slices are all Merged or Superseded and unclaimed. The directory moves from `projects//proposals/

` to `projects//archive/

` in one rename, followed by one local commit and an ordinary push attempt. - All-Merged Proposals report `fully_delivered`. Mixed or wholly Superseded Proposals are retired without full delivery. - Lifecycle, reports, and embedded references are never rewritten. - Ineligible Proposals stay whole and report the reason they were kept. - Each of these cases is a repair outcome that overwrites and discards nothing: a committed or uncommitted distinct destination, a dirty proposal, an unexplained partial tree, staged index content under the source or destination that is not exactly the committed record renamed, and a failed commit. A failed commit restores the original location. - An interrupted move is finished on retry, but only when the uncommitted tree matches the committed record exactly (paths, bytes, and modes) and the index either matches head or holds exactly that committed rename. - **Source cleanup** (`workflow.CleanupSource`, shared with the legacy forge path; authority comes from `ledger.TerminalSourceWork`). - A local worktree and branch are removed only for confirmed Merged, unclaimed work whose Submission, Completion, and Target are consistent and whose branch has a single owner. The worktree must also be clean, registered at `/.worktrees/`, and have HEAD equal to the recorded accepted source head. - Every slice directory under `proposals/` or `archive/` is a member whose state must be read. A missing or malformed `state.json` withholds all source deletion, and the reason names the unreadable items. - Squash merges need neither ancestry nor an upstream. - These are preserved with a reason: Superseded, claimed, contradictory or duplicate ownership, a missing or unreadable sibling record, dirty, wrong location, and unknown or changed head. - Removal failures are reported under `failed`, never as removed. - Remote branches are never touched. Supporting changes: - **Archived identities stay resolvable.** `ShowItem` and dependency reads (`readStateByReferenceAt`) resolve active or archive locations directly. Acceptance accepts an archived dependency. Branch ownership checks also scan the archive. An archived proposal name cannot be accepted again, which would create a second copy. - **CLI** (`cmd/skl/cleanup.go`). Output uses Markdown by default, and `--format json` is honored on both the ledger and legacy paths. Status is `completed`, `no_work`, or `fix_required`; any repair or failed removal forces `fix_required`, so it cannot hide behind overall success. Archive results, kept proposals, repairs, replication, and removed, preserved, and failed source work are shown separately. The old "unsupported for adopted projects" gate for cleanup is replaced; `adoptedLedger` is factored out of `gateUnsupportedDelivery` and reused. - **Propose** (`skills/dev/propose/SKILL.md` step 6.1) runs `skl propose cleanup` before preparing new slices and routes all mechanics through `skl`. The README's adopted-project note is updated. - **No automatic archival.** Status, completion observation, and Watchdog never call archival. Because they build on the predecessor ledger slices, the branch merged `origin/main` at `b496da5` before implementing. This rework round merged `origin/main` at `b6525c9` (see Verification). ## Rework Rework: 6228eb555d8db2eeb8f1dd046cfa414000794117...eefc9a1f9ba8512a2d4430fd7aa29670474a3933 - W1 resolved — fcbd9c5b9ee0e393a2787a4d707caf32274e9336; covered by `TestUnreadableRecordWithholdsSourceDeletion/missing` (and `/malformed`). `TerminalSourceWork` used to find records by listing existing `state.json` files. It now counts every `/` directory in the active and archive locations as a member, and a missing or unreadable state withholds deletion for every candidate. The hold reason names the item, for example `missing or unreadable Work Item state (damaged/only) could own branch safe-only`. The subtest reproduces the Watchdog case: a clean, exact-head Merged `safe/only` sits beside a committed `damaged/only` whose `state.json` was removed with `git rm`. The test asserts `source.removed` is empty and one preserved entry names `damaged/only`. It also asserts that the branch ref, the exact head, and a committed worktree file survive, that `safe` is still archived, and that `damaged` is kept for `unknown state`. Sensitivity: skipping slices that lack `state.json` (the old behavior) fails `/missing` only. - W2 resolved — fcbd9c5b9ee0e393a2787a4d707caf32274e9336 (classification refined in eefc9a1f9ba8512a2d4430fd7aa29670474a3933); covered by `TestCleanupArchiveFailuresKeepOneCompleteProposal`. Before touching anything, `moveProposal` classifies the index under the source and destination against head: - **Unchanged:** proceed as before. - **Exactly the committed rename:** unstaged losslessly, but only after the working-tree resume match, and then finished as a resume. - **Anything else:** a repair outcome, with no staging, commit, reset, or rename. Staging and the rollback `git reset` therefore only ever run from an index equal to head, so they cannot discard distinct content. The test adds three proposals: - `staged` is the Watchdog reproduction: distinct `intent.md` staged at the destination only, with working-tree bytes restored to the original. - `renamed` stages the whole rename with distinct content. This is the case where the absent-source staging failure triggered the reset. - `matching` hits the commit-hook failure and rollback in the first run, and then, as a staged exact rename, resumes with `resumed_interrupted_move` in the retry. Across both runs, `staged` and `renamed` are kept as `staged changes` repairs, and `git show :/only/intent.md` still returns the unique staged content. Their committed records are unchanged. Sensitivity: disabling the distinct-index guard fails the test. ## Verification Remote `origin`. This round's late pre-Audit integration: `git fetch origin main` → `FETCH_HEAD` = `b6525c96297e5900717a6eaf7867be96ff4a9789`, merged in `bd7e360`, which is this round's integration cutoff. Integration effects: - One conflict in `skills/dev/propose/SKILL.md`. It was resolved by taking the target's step text verbatim, renumbered 2–8 after this branch's cleanup step 1. - The target removed durable `PublicationState.Issue`: issue publication no longer persists pending facts. `TestCleanupArchivesWholeTerminalProposals` asserted that such a fact survived archival. It now seeds an ordinary pending `Publication.Push` fact on `widget/core` and asserts it survives. The archive tree ID still equals the active tree ID, so all bytes moved unchanged. - Known interaction with the inherited `skl ledger publish` (not part of this Contract): see F21. Tests (all in `cmd/skl`, real temporary source and ledger Git repositories, local bare remotes, and a forge server that fails the test if contacted during cleanup): | Evidence | Obligations | |---|---| | `TestCleanupArchivesWholeTerminalProposals` | B1 (all-Merged → fully delivered, Merged+Superseded → retired; archive tree ID equals the prior active tree ID, so every document, state, report, and pending publication fact moved byte-identically; all 7 ineligible outline rows, plus a dependent proposal, kept whole with observable reasons and no archive children). B2 (a Watchdog-cited `commit/path` of an earlier implementation report returns v1 bytes after the move; the current report at the archive path returns v2; the review file is unchange

#97: a drift reference is now built from a window that ends where the comparison window starts. The window it was built from is stored in the parquet, and every drift report states its baseline and whether that baseline overlaps the window under test.

author: arnaudprioul
body:
Ferme la moitié « radius » de #294, corrige le défaut signalé sur capture, et **corrige un fait faux** qui circulait dans #934 et dans le titre de son spec.

Closes #944.

## Mesuré — Chromium réel, marketing, viewport 1280×900, 8 identités × 2 modes

Menu « Introduction » ouvert, entrée « Changelog » survolée. ⚠️ Le rayon du menu se lit sur **`.origam-menu__content`** : `.origam-menu` est la racine du téléport et n'en porte aucun — une mesure qui la vise rend `0px` partout et conclut, à tort, que rien n'est arrondi.

| identité | menu `__content` | ligne | ligne / hauteur (48px) |
|---|---|---|---|
| origam | 8px → 8px | 0px → 0px | 0 % |
| editorial | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 % |
| ecom | 4 → 4 | 4 → 4 | 8 % |
| geek | 4 → 4 | 4 → 4 | 8 % |
| apple | 12 → 12 | 12 → 12 | 25 % |
| **cartoon** (clair + sombre) | 20 → 20 | **20 → 8** | 42 % → 17 % |
| **glass** clair | 22 → 22 | **22 → 10** | 46 % → 21 % |
| **glass** sombre | 30 → 30 | **30 → 16** | **63 %** → 33 % |
| **material** (clair + sombre) | **28 → 4** | **28 → 4** | **58 %** → 8 % |

Au-delà de 24px sur une ligne de 48px, le navigateur ramène les rayons et la ligne devient une **pilule pleine** : c'est le cas de `material` et de `glass` sombre. **Dans les 8 identités, la ligne portait exactement le rayon du conteneur** — les thèmes donnaient le même rung (`rounded: 'lg'`) aux deux.

## ⛔ Le point de design — une forme de TIROIR posée sur un MENU

Vérifié dans les **sources de tokens Material**, pas de mémoire :

| surface | token M3 | valeur | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| conteneur de **menu déroulant** | `corner-extra-small` | **4px** | material-web `tokens/versions/v0_192/_md-comp-menu.scss` → `'container-shape': … 'corner-extra-small'` ; `_md-sys-shape.scss` → `'corner-extra-small': … 4px` |
| **item de liste** | `corner-none` | **0** | `_md-comp-list.scss` → `'list-item-container-shape': … 'corner-none'` |
| destination de **tiroir de navigation** | `Corner.Full` | pilule | material-components-android `navigation/res/values/styles.xml` → `<item name="itemShapeAppearance">@style/ShapeAppearance.Material3.Corner.Full</item>` |
| — | `corner-extra-large` | **28px** | `_md-sys-shape.scss` |

Le `28px` que `material.theme.ts` déclare en `rounded.lg` **est** `corner-extra-large`, et la pilule **est** le traitement de tiroir. L'hypothèse se confirme.

⚠️ `origam-list` porte bien `nav: true`, mais **ce n'est pas le canal** : dans le DS, `nav` ne touche que le padding et la typographie (`OrigamList.vue:411`, `OrigamListItem.vue:743`), jamais le rayon.

## ⛔ Il n'y a PAS de rognage — #934 et le titre de son spec sont faux sur ce point

| sonde | résultat |
|---|---|
| la ligne déborde-t-elle de `__content` ? | **non** — bord droit `351.5` pour un conteneur à `363.5` |
| `scrollWidth` vs `clientWidth` du conteneur | `180` vs `180` |
| forcer `overflow: visible` sur `.origam-menu__content` | **zéro pixel de différence** (deux captures du coin bas-droit, `deviceScaleFactor: 8`) |
| coin bas-droit de la pastille à 8×, avant correctif, material et glass sombre | **extrémité arrondie intacte** |

Deux arcs de **même rayon** laissaient au coin bas-droit un croissant très fin, qui se lit comme une coupe à l'échelle 1×. Le défaut réel est l'**ampleur du rayon**.

## Ce qui change

**`material.theme.ts`**
- `vars.rounded.xs: '4px'` — le rung manquait (retombait sur le primitif DS à 2px) ; `4px` **est** `corner-extra-small`.
- `'origam-menu': rounded 'lg' → 'xs'` · `'origam-list': 'lg' → 'none'` · `'origam-list-item': 'lg' → 'xs'`.

**`glass.theme.ts`** / **`cartoon.theme.ts`** — `'origam-list-item': 'lg' → 'sm'`. Le rayon du **conteneur** est conservé : c'est leur signature, et M3 ne les régit pas.

**Consolidation #294** — `glass` déclarait `--origam-list-item---border-radius: 11px`, `cartoon` `9px` : **ces déclarations n'ont jamais peint**. `useRounded` émet, pour un rung utilitaire, la classe `.origam--rounded-{rung}` **ET** un `border-radius` inline (relevé sur l'attribut `style`), qui bat toute feuille. Les 4 déclarations mortes sont retirées ; la valeur visée vit dans la prop. `--origam-menu---border-radius` est **laissé en place** (même mécanisme, mais `marketing-theming-isolation.spec.ts` le sonde).

**Gouttière de la ligne** — `paddingInline: 12` sur les trois identités. `padding-inline-start` valait `0px` sous les 8 identités : `calc(12px − 8px d'indent `nav` − 8px de densité compacte)` clampé à 0, `titleLeft === itemLeft` au pixel près. La pilule le masquait. #934 a corrigé la gouttière de la **liste**, pas celle de la **ligne** — défaut DS résiduel, à traiter à part.

## ⛔ Deux arbitrages pour le propriétaire

**1. Ligne de menu carrée (M3 strict) ou arrondie 4px ?** M3 donne `corner-none` aux items **parce que sa surbrillance est pleine largeur** ; la nôtre est encartée (12px de gouttière). Un rectangle à angles vifs flottant dans un conteneur arrondi n'est une forme M3 ni d'un côté ni de l'autre. **Livré : 4px**, aligné sur le rung du conteneur. Les trois rendus (0 / 4 / 12px) sont dans la comparaison visuelle.

**2. Un item de menu et une destination de tiroir ne sont pas distinguables.** `components['origam-list-item'].rounded` est un **défaut global** de thème. Le site n'a aujourd'hui aucun tiroir (tous les `origam-list` du marketing vivent dans un `origam-menu` — vérifié), donc la question est théorique ici ; mais un futur tiroir héritera du rayon de menu et devra redemander la pilule (`rounded="full"`). Si la distinction doit exister dans le DS, c'est un chantier à part.

## Vérification

- `marketing-primary-nav.spec.ts` gagne **6 cas en valeurs absolues**. Pas de nouveau fichier → `spec-coverage` inchangée. ⚠️ Ce fichier n'est **pas** dans `MARKETING_GREEN_SPECS` : la CI ne l'exécute pas.
- **Témoin positif** : 6/6 **ROUGE** contre un serveur servant `develop`, sur l'assertion de valeur (`28px` / `22px` / `30px` / `20px` reçus), pas sur une expiration.
- **Stabilité** : `--repeat-each=5 --retries=0` → **30/30**, 1,2 min. Fichier entier : **22/22**.
- `pnpm -F origam guards` **29/29**, `guards:self` **16/16**, `lint` vert — vrais `$?` hors pipe.
- Serveur de dev isolé sur `:3099` (jamais le `:3000` du propriétaire), tué avant de rendre la main.

⚠️ **Aucune modification du DS — pas de release.**

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Comparaison visuelle

Avant/après du menu ouvert avec une entrée survolée, **8 identités × 2 modes**, plus les trois rendus de l’arbitrage 1 et les zooms 8× qui montrent l’absence de rognage :

**https://claude.ai/artifact/3ijGkKMrJxPUzpDUm2grBC**

---

## Second commit — la spec est branchée

Le fichier n'était exécuté par **aucun** job : il était inscrit dans `e2e/_support/baseline/spec-coverage.json` comme non exécuté, donc `spec-coverage` restait verte et rien ne le signalait. Il est maintenant dans `MARKETING_GREEN_SPECS`.

Mesuré **sur le fichier entier**, pas seulement les 6 cas ajoutés — brancher un fichier qui contient des cas instables rendrait la CI rouge en permanence, ce qui est pire que pas de garde :

| mesure | résultat |
|---|---|
| fichier entier, `--repeat-each=5 --retries=0` | **110/110** (22 cas × 5), 2,3 min, load 3,3, serveur isolé sur `:3099` |
| suite `MARKETING_GREEN_ONLY=1` complète (forme exacte du job CI) | **51/51**, 1,1 min |
| dont `nav-link-availability.spec.ts`, signalé flaky dans l'en-tête de la config (3 échecs sur 5 exécutions) | vert sur cette exécution |
| sélection vérifiée avec l'instrument de la garde (`playwright test --list` sous `MARKETING_GREEN_ONLY=1`) | fichier retenu, 22 cas |

Baseline `spec-coverage` : **177 → 176** entrées. La garde a bien signalé l'entrée devenue obsolète (`FAIL — 1 STALE baseline entry`) ; `--update-baseline` la retire, puis 176 known / 0 new.

`run-guards.mjs` **3/3** · `guards` **29/29** · `guards:self` **16/16** · lint vert — vrais `$?` hors pipe.

author: danishhaiderau-maker
body: Draft only. Do not merge. Do not deploy tip. Overnight freeze stays in effect: no master merge, no tip deploy. Soft B is not in this change. ## Why [Run 36109823110](https://github.com/danishhaiderau-maker/doxed-founders-website/actions/runs/36109823110) (`apply=true`, `expected_epoch=epoch-v22-51e7a8d95b4a233813fa`, `expected_revision=37f3a57a36db`) died in the force-bootstrap step: - Guest printed `{"phase":"store_ready"}` and was then SIGKILL'd (`RC=137`, OOM) during the first advance. - `/tmp/force_chunk_status.json` stayed missing, so it never reached `BOOTSTRAP_PARTIAL` / `BOOTSTRAP_FORCED`. - The waiter returned that progress JSON and the step raised `unexpected chunk status: {'phase': 'store_ready'}`. - Invent/resume was skipped. `store_ready`, `advance_timeout`, and `advance_error` are progress, not a finished chunk. ## What changed - `wait_chunk_result` keeps polling through those phases. It returns only when a **fresh** `STATUS_FILE` (seen `STATUS_FILE=missing`, then `STATUS_FILE={...}`) is `BOOTSTRAP_FORCED`, `BOOTSTRAP_PARTIAL`, or `dry_run`, or when RC is a real exit code and output has stopped moving. A dead chunk (`RC=137` with no further output) is recorded as `BOOTSTRAP_PARTIAL` and the budget loop continues instead of aborting the run. - An early `BOOTSTRAP_PARTIAL` written at `store_ready` is provisional and is not treated as done while RC is still missing, so a live chunk is not cut off. SIGKILL cannot be caught; that file is what the waiter reads after OOM. - Guest writes `BOOTSTRAP_PARTIAL` immediately after `store_ready` (before the advance loop) and on SIGTERM/SIGINT. It does not arm Bitfinex and does not claim SAFE. - New `workflow_dispatch` input `chunk_seconds` (string, default `"180"`). The runner clamps it to **at most 150** before passing `MAX_SECONDS` to the guest. Above 150 the guest switches from 256 records / 8MiB to 1024 / 16MiB, which makes the OOM worse. Effective budget for the default input is 150. ## How Ops runs this (no merge) ```bash gh workflow run fly-force-receipt-bootstrap-once.yml \ --ref cursor/force-bootstrap-wait-chunk-harden-0ca0 \ -f apply=true \ -f expected_epoch=epoch-v22-51e7a8d95b4a233813fa \ -f expected_revision=37f3a57a36db \ -f max_seconds=3600 \ -f chunk_seconds=150 ``` `chunk_seconds=180` is also safe: the workflow clamps anything above 150 down to 150. Do not pass a value expecting the 1024-record step.

author: atimics
body:
## What

Every character and creature becomes one Blender-built skinned GLB, posed at runtime by the motion code. This PR has the design and the first migration (goblins).

1. **Design doc:** `docs/design/unified-characters.md`. It covers the skeleton families (humanoid 18 bones, quadruped 19, dragon designed at exactly 32), the GLB contract, the runtime contract, and the migration order: goblins, then dragons, then NPCs, then pig. Pigs do not exist in the sim yet, so the doc lists the sim hooks a pig needs.
2. **Goblins migrated:**
   - `build_creature_library.py` builds each goblin in the humanoid skeleton with rigid one-bone weights. The shapes, sizes and palette slots follow the old C rig. It exports one skinned GLB per variant. `paint_channels` gains per-part value pins (dark pupils and mouth).
   - New `src/locomotion/cc_character_skin.[ch]`: `CcSkeletonFamily` bone tables, and `CcHumanoidPoseFromBipedRig`. This function turns the goblin creature rig (pelvis and legs) plus a body plan into a `CcHumanoidPose` in model space. The hero's `CcHumanoidSkinPoseResolve` then poses it. Goblins share the hero solver.
   - The runtime has one generic path: `LoadSkinnedCharacter` checks the family bones and caches the rest frames. `PoseSkinnedCharacter` writes the bones, keeps the "clamped to bind pose" guard, and uploads the frame. Quadrupeds now go through it too, with the same math as before.
   - Goblin callers draw with a continuous gait phase instead of 8 stepped poses.
   - Catalog, manifest and validator: goblins are `skeleton: humanoid`. The validator checks that the bone set has at most 32 bones, that no vertex has more than 4 weights, and that every humanoid joint matches the runtime idle pose (the same table that `character_skin_tests --print-bind` prints).

## Deleted

- 24 goblin held-pose GLBs and their catalog entries
- `DrawGoblinRig`, `DrawGoblinHair`, and the goblin branches of `DrawCreatureMuscleLimbs`
- `BIPED_POSES` and the held-pose goblin builder

## Frames (game size and review sheets)

`docs/reviews/unified-characters-goblins-2026-09-25/` has before and after frames for the cave, the creature reel, the mine contest and the review sheet, plus a new stride sheet. The README there says what to look for. Known differences:
- The skinned shader reads a bit darker and flatter than the old world-shader draw. The goblin paint is one value step higher to keep faces readable.
- The raider's spear now tilts with the arm swing.

## Checks

- `make blender-creature-assets blender-creature-assets-check`: passes (10 variants, 26 assets). Only the goblin GLBs and the .blend changed; the other creature exports are byte-identical.
- `make blender-exports-check`: passes. `validate_character_paint_channels.py`: passes.
- `cmake --build --preset play` and `ctest` (with `ulimit -s 65520`): 241 of 244 pass. The 3 that fail (`crisis_contested_succession`, `long_history_recovery`, `scrivendays_calendar_and_evidence`) are sim-hash checks. They fail the same way locally on a clean export of `origin/main`, so this PR did not cause them.
- `renderer_regression_tests --creature-captures`, `--carriage-graphics`, `--graphics`: pass. The quadruped animal sheet is unchanged.
- Web preset build: passes.
- No `clamped to bind pose` or `not drawn; rig pose failed` lines in the captures.
- Research artifacts: 1.1 MB.

Not merged: this is for human review.

author: grinidx
body:
These come from reviewing a second skill built on Wikipedia's *Signs of AI writing* (`de-ai-writing`). Dan picked three items to take: the watch-list gaps, vocabulary by model era, and plain-word swaps. Every item was checked against Wikipedia's raw text, not that skill's copy.

**Added**
- **B1:** *has generated debate about*, *prompted broader reflection on*.
- **B5:** *several sources* when only one or two are cited; *such as* before a list that is actually complete; and the general weasel forms from Wikipedia's weasel-words page (*widely regarded*, *research has shown*).
- **B7:** *refers to*, and opening lines that define their own title ("X refers to…").
- **D6** stock and paired headings (*Awards and recognition*, *X and Y*) and **D7** tables too small to need a table. Both are marked *needs company*.
- **Wordlist:** an era column on the AI vocabulary (GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-5, per Wikipedia). It also states that the era weighs evidence in detect mode and never decides what a rewrite keeps. Plus the stiff synonyms (*authored*, *relocated*, *utilised*, *attempted*, *passed away*), with an exception: *passed away* stays where it was chosen for a grieving reader.

**Not added:** *ventured into … as* and *began his career as*. That skill included them, but Wikipedia's guide does not have them.

**Evidence**
- `tells-wikipedia-2026` failed every run on both models before the change, and passes every run after it.
- Judged by Codex, Opus kept its meaning in 51 of 51 outputs and Sonnet in 46 of 51. The Sonnet misses are the known residuals.
- The first draft made one thing worse: Sonnet read the era column as permission to keep an older word (*delve*). That draft did not ship; the era note above now rules that reading out.

The "three additional nodes" assertion now accepts "three nodes" and "three more nodes". It still catches a dropped node count, and the mutation suite confirms it (9/9).

Production-readiness items 5 and 6. **Stacked on #10** (and so on #7–#9); the new work is the last commit.

**Public dev tenant:** migration 11 disables the seeded `dev` tenant, whose API key is the public string `dev-token`, on every database. `sluice-cli enable-dev-tenant` turns it back on for local development, with a warning. The README quick start now includes that step.

**Dashboard key:** the API key was compiled into the JavaScript bundle (`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_TOKEN`, defaulting to `dev-token`). Now viewers sign in with a tenant key. It's checked against the API, kept in `sessionStorage` for that tab only, a 401 anywhere returns to sign-in, and Sign out clears it.

- Corrects the crash-failover range to the measured 1.5–2.6s (etcd lease expiry, load-dependent). A 2.51s run on a loaded laptop broke the old 2.5s test limit; the limit is now 3s, which still catches a real regression like the old 5s lease.

author: ace2932
body:
Adds `docs/power-chain-fmea.md`, a one-page FMEA of the power chain: 15 rows sorted by severity. Each row has the failure mode, its effect, how it is detected today, a v6 bodge and v7 fix, a bench check with a pass criterion, and a blank **Measured** column to fill in on the bench.

Net claims were checked against a `kicad-cli sch export netlist` of the current schematic. No KiCad files are touched.

**Headline (PC-01, sev 5):** Q1's gate network (D1 anode, R_gs1, C_gs1) lands on `BATT_NEG`, which is Q1's **drain**. The cause is the `Q_NMOS_GSD` symbol, which labels pin 2 "S" (`01_battery.kicad_sch:1104-1111`), while the IRLB3034's pin 2 is D. With the pack reversed, D1 forward-biases and Q1 turns on as a source follower. Bodge: move 3 SMD ends onto Q1.3. The bench test is in the row.

Also:
- The E-stop and hardcut both fail open when V5_AUX is lost (PC-04).
- The hardcut is not latched and has only 0.28 V of hysteresis, so pack rebound can cycle it (PC-07).
- Hardcut does not disconnect the pack (PC-08).
- #244's inrush goes through the body diode, not the channel (PC-10).
- Trip points with hysteresis are 12.96/13.06 and 12.42/12.70 (PC-11).

Inline `⚠ superseded by` notes (nothing deleted) in `docs/order-list.md`, `docs/pre-power-on-validation.md` and `hardware/wiring/README.md`.

author: primowork
body:
## מה זה עושה

שני שלבים ממפת דרכים רחבה יותר לשימור לקוחות, שגדלו על אותו PR פתוח:

**תובנות בדשבורד הלקוחות** - `/staff/customers` מציג עכשיו ארבעה מדדים חדשים: אחוז לקוחות פעילים ב-30 הימים האחרונים, ביקורים בממוצע לחודש ללקוח פעיל, השעה/יום העמוסים ביותר (לפי שעון ישראל, לא UTC), והתחייבות הפרסים הפתוחה (כמה משקאות חינם העסק חייב כרגע).

**ייצוא לאקסל** - כפתור חדש מוריד CSV עם כל הלקוחות הרשומים.

**Web Push ללקוחות (opt-in) + שידור ידני מהצוות** - עד עכשיו ה-push שימש רק לאישור ניקובים בצד הצוות. עכשיו לקוחות יכולים להפעיל התראות מהכרטיס האישי שלהם, ולצוות יש כלי חדש בדשבורד לשדר הודעה חופשית לכל מי שנרשם ("יש עוגה טרייה היום!"). זו תשתית מוכנה לקמפיין החזרת לקוחות אוטומטי בעתיד (דורש עוד החלטה נפרדת על מנגנון תזמון בפרודקשן - לא בסקופ כאן).

## למה ככה

- `createdAt` נשמר כ-`timestamp(3) without time zone` שמייצג בפועל UTC. שעת/יום העומס דורשים המרת אזור זמן כפולה: `("createdAt" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Jerusalem'` - אומתתי ישירות מול השרת המקומי לפני שהוטמע (UTC 07:42 → ישראל 10:42, תואם קיץ).
- לקוחות פעילים + ביקורים ממוצעים מגיעים משאילתת `groupBy` אחת, לא שתיים. התחייבות הפרסים מחושבת מ-`currentStamps` הקיים, בלי שדה חדש במסד.
- CSV מתחיל ב-BOM כדי שאקסל יזהה UTF-8 ויציג עברית נכון. `Content-Disposition: attachment` + `Link` רגיל, בלי fetch+blob.
- `CustomerPushSubscription` הוא מודל נפרד מ-`PushSubscription` של הצוות (תוספת נטו) - לקוח מזוהה ע"י ה-id הבלתי-נחוש שלו בנתיב, לא session, כמו כל endpoint ציבורי אחר. `NotificationSubscribe.tsx` הפך לגנרי (subscribeUrl+טקסטים כ-props) כדי לשרת גם צוות וגם לקוח בלי כפילות קוד.
- `sw.js` מבחין בין push של בקשת ניקוב (כפתורי אישור/דחייה, פותח את דשבורד הצוות) לבין broadcast ללקוחות (בלי כפתורי פעולה, פותח את הכרטיס האישי) לפי שדה `kind` בפיילוד.
- `Date.now()`/`Math.random` הועברו לפונקציות עזר נפרדות ולא נקראים ישירות בגוף רינדור - כלל `react-hooks/purity` חדש שכבר נתקלנו בו בסבבים קודמים.

## בדיקות שבוצעו

- `npm run build` ו-`npm run lint` נקיים בכל שלב.
- מדדי התובנות אומתו ישירות מול שאילתות SQL זהות שהרצתי ב-`psql` (10 לקוחות, 10 ניקובים, 7 פעילים=70%, התחייבות=2, שעת שיא 15:00 ביום שישי) - הצילום מסך תואם בדיוק.
- ייצוא ה-CSV נבדק בפועל (Playwright + `acceptDownloads`): BOM תקין, עברית תקינה, נתונים תואמים ל-DB.
- Web Push: שידור אמיתי דרך ה-API עם subscription מדומה מוכיח שכשל שליחה בודד לא מפיל את כל הבקשה ולא נתפס בטעות כ-endpoint שפג תוקף. `POST`/`DELETE` על `/api/customers/[id]/push-subscription` נבדקו עם לקוח לא קיים (404), גוף לא תקין (400), והזרימה התקינה (201/200). **לא נבדק** subscribe אמיתי מדפדפן - מגבלת סביבה ידועה כבר מ-PR קודם (`pushManager.subscribe` נתקע בסביבת ה-sandbox הזו), לא באג בקוד - הבדיקה האמיתית הנותרת היא מכשיר אמיתי.

author: maralcbr
body:
Ticket 12 of the Apple Silicon convergence plan (#512): the disposable-aarch64-root seam for package resolution, ownership and version transitions.

`tools/package-resolution/check` downloads the live Arch Linux ARM (core, extra, alarm, aur), asahi-alarm and pkgs.omarchy.org edge/aarch64 databases for each platform fixture (Apple with the Asahi repositories, generic aarch64 and Qualcomm without them) and resolves each set in a throwaway pacman root. It never touches the host's pacman state and runs as a normal user on any Arch or Arch Linux ARM host or container. Per platform it checks:

- the closure resolves, with no declared conflicts between its packages
- no forbidden repositories are configured, and non-Apple closures contain no Mac-only packages
- which package `pacman -S linux` selects, with every package that provides `linux`. This fails if a Mac-only package is selected off Apple, and on Apple it also reports the choice with linux-aurora installed.
- nothing in the non-Apple repositories depends on a Mac-only name
- no file in the closure has two owners
- equal-version and locally-newer installs are kept by `-Su` and replaced by an explicit `-S`, while `-S --needed` skips the equal one

Packages that aren't published yet (omarchy-mac, omarchy-mac-boot, m1n1-aurora) and `obs-studio` (not built for aarch64) are skipped with a reason. The run reports when they start resolving.

What it shows against today's databases:
- On generic aarch64 and Qualcomm, `linux` resolves to `core/linux-aarch64`, but `omarchy/linux-aurora` still provides `linux` (reported until ticket 06 drops the provide).
- On an empty Apple root, `linux` resolves to `asahi-alarm/linux-asahi`. With linux-aurora installed, it resolves to linux-aurora through the provide.
- hyprland, hyprtoolkit, hyprland-guiutils and xdg-terminal-exec come from ALARM `extra` rather than `[omarchy]`, because `[omarchy]` is last in the aarch64 repository order.

## Testing

- `test/check-test.sh` builds synthetic repositories with `repo-add`, including one in ALARM's older desc+depends layout. It shows each check passing on a clean set and failing on its fault: a Mac package in a generic closure, two owners for one file, a Mac kernel selected for `linux`, an Asahi repository on generic, conflicts (including one met through a versioned provide), unknown or unresolvable transition packages, and a files database from another snapshot.
- The new `Package resolution` workflow runs shellcheck, the self-test and the live check. The live check runs in an `archlinux:base` container with `Architecture = aarch64` forced, so no Mac or arm64 runner is needed. It runs on push, on PRs and daily. It's green on this branch (about a minute).
- Not run on an Arch Linux ARM host: the M2 Max was unreachable while I worked on this.

Second review: three rounds. The first two found six issues, all fixed with regression tests: locale-dependent parsing, the conflicts that `-Sp` skips, platform-name path traversal, conflicts met through a provide, `.db`/`.files` snapshot skew, and transition resolution errors being treated as skips. The third round confirmed the fixes.

author: droodotfoo
body:
## What was wrong

`Raxol.Headless.handle_info({:DOWN, ...})` (`lib/raxol/headless.ex:355-362`) dropped a session when its lifecycle exited, but never called `stop_synchronizer/1`. The `Raxol.MCP.ToolSynchronizer` is started with `start_link` from Headless, so it is linked to Headless, not to the app. After the app died on its own (crash, `Directive.stop()`), the synchronizer kept running with its `[:raxol, :runtime, :view_tree_updated]` telemetry handler attached and the session's MCP tools and `raxol://session/<id>/context|widgets` resources registered, for a session `Headless.list/0` no longer reported. Only `stop/1` (`:336-347`) stopped it.

Finding from the runner-map audit in #1079.

## Reproduction

New test in `test/raxol/headless_test.exs` ("stops the session's tool synchronizer when the lifecycle dies"): starts `Raxol.MCP.Registry` if it isn't already running, starts a session, reads the lifecycle and synchronizer pids from Headless state, monitors both, kills the lifecycle, then waits for the synchronizer's `:DOWN` and asserts the session's context resource and `tool_sync_<id>_*` telemetry handler are gone.

On master it fails: `assert_receive {:DOWN, ^sync_ref, ...}` times out with an empty mailbox.

## Change

The `:DOWN` handler now splits the sessions into those owned by the dead lifecycle and the rest, and calls `stop_synchronizer/1` on each dropped session. It skips `stop_lifecycle/1` because that process is already dead. There's no double stop: `stop/1` deletes the session before the lifecycle's `:DOWN` arrives, so that `:DOWN` matches nothing. `stop_synchronizer/1` already catches `:exit`, so a synchronizer that has already exited doesn't crash Headless.

## Manual testing

- [x] `mix test test/raxol/headless_test.exs:259` on the unfixed code: 0/1 passed (synchronizer `:DOWN` never arrived)
- [x] `mix test test/raxol/headless_test.exs test/raxol/headless_resize_test.exs`: 32 passed
- [x] `mix test test/raxol/headless test/property/headless_monitoring_property_test.exs test/cross_terminal/headless_golden_test.exs`: 57 passed (4 properties, 53 tests)
- [x] `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean
- [x] `mix credo --strict lib/raxol/headless.ex test/raxol/headless_test.exs`: no issues
- [x] `MIX_ENV=test mix dialyzer --format short`: `Total errors: 134`, none in `lib/raxol/headless.ex`

body:
Two unrelated pieces of work share a branch because the generated GraphQL
files (`src/gql/`, `schema.gql`) carry both, and splitting a codegen
output by hand is not sound. They are separate commits — review them one
at a time.

## d505ecc — overview dashboard and console shell

- Serve real counts from the admin GraphQL API: users, saved charts,
  logins, active sessions, over a chosen window, each paired with the
  preceding window so the page shows movement rather than a bare total.
- Move the account block from the topbar into the sidebar; `topbar.tsx`
  is gone.
- Give the login page its own backdrop and Google button.
- `docs/local-admin-access.md` records how to reach `/api/admin` locally.

## ecd5f11 — user list filtering and sorting

- Filters: role, email verification, joined range, balance range.
- Sort: joined date, balance, email — accepted as an enum member that
  maps to a column, never as a column name from the client.
- `genCount` and `lastActiveAt` are deliberately not sortable: both are
  correlated subqueries, so ordering by them would make Postgres compute
  them for every user before applying `LIMIT`.
- Toolbar collapsed into icons. Search expands in place; dates and
  balance open in popovers; sorting moved off the column headers into one
  menu. Active filters show as removable chips.

### One bug worth naming

A nullable GraphQL argument arrives as `null`, not `undefined`. Testing
absence with `!== undefined` turned every unused filter into
`column = NULL`, which matches no row — the list came back empty on every
page load. Absence is now tested with a guard that treats both alike, and
the DTO types say `T | null` so the compiler stops claiming otherwise.

## Test plan

- [x] `nx run-many -t typecheck lint test -p @org/dashboard @org/backend`
      — 11 backend specs, 23 dashboard specs
- [x] Every filter and sort exercised against the local database through
      GraphQL **variables**, not inline literals — the literal path does
      not reproduce the null bug
- [x] Rejects bad input: unknown sort field, malformed date, negative
      balance
- [x] Toolbar rendered in jsdom: search opens and searches, sort menu
      lists and applies all six orders, clear button appears only when
      a filter is on
- [ ] Not checked in a browser — a stale Chrome instance held the
      devtools profile lock for the whole session

author: sigarone
body:
## What

Make `GroupSession.decryptFromGroupOrThrow` all-or-nothing: a frame that does not decrypt leaves the receive chain (chain key, last-seen index, next index, skipped-key cache contents and order) exactly as it was. A valid skip-ahead frame still decrypts and commits exactly as before.

## Why

Before this change the skip-ahead branch stepped the receive chain and filled the skipped-key cache **before** the frame's AEAD tag was checked, and the late-delivery branch removed its cache entry and re-appended it around the check (so a failure changed cache order). `GroupSenderChain` is a `final class` and `GroupChatService.session()` returns a cached, live `GroupState`, and every `persist(state)` snapshots all receive chains, so a frame that failed verification could leave the in-memory chain (and a later persisted snapshot of it) different from before.

## Change (minimal, `GroupSession.swift` only)

- Skip-ahead and the in-order step now run on a scratch `GroupSenderChain` copy (`work`); chain key, cache, last-seen and next index are written to the live chain in one commit block, after the AEAD tag has verified.
- Late delivery: the cache entry is removed only after its tag verifies (no remove/re-append on failure).
- Unchanged: wire format, AAD, nonces, `MAX_SKIP_AHEAD`, cache cap, TTL, expiry/LRU eviction rules and their order on the success path.

## Tests (`GroupSessionAtomicDecryptTests`, engine test target)

State equality is checked byte-for-byte through `GroupSessionSnapshotCodec.encode`.

- Frame with a high chain index and filler tag (with and without a matching nonce): decrypt fails, snapshot identical, genuine frames still decrypt afterwards and the chain ends where an undisturbed run ends.
- Loop over 16 failure kinds (bad tag in-order / skip-ahead, bad nonce, bad ciphertext, index jump beyond the window and beyond the cache cap, entries past TTL, replay of current / older frame, late frame with bad tag / nonce / ciphertext, wrong sender id, malformed wire) plus a loop over many indices on one state: snapshot never changes.
- Valid skip-ahead inside the window: frame delivered, skipped keys stored with the expected keys/nonces/expiry, late frames served from the cache, in-order delivery continues; skip-ahead past the cache cap evicts the oldest entries; a committed skip-ahead still drops expired entries.

Note: there is no Swift toolchain on the authoring machine, so these were written against the real API by reading it; the CI simulator lane is their first compile/run.

## Serialization of the cached `GroupState` (finding, nothing changed here)

- Chat path: `GroupChatService` is `@MainActor`; its cached `sessions[groupId]` states are only reached through main-actor-isolated methods.
- Call path: `GroupCallController` owns a separate `GroupSession` (no vault) and a separate call-scoped `GroupState` (group id = call id), and every access (decrypt, encrypt, sender-key install, key reads) is under its own `NSLock`.
- The two paths therefore do not share a `GroupState` instance today. `GroupState` / `GroupSenderChain` themselves carry no lock, so the commit block is not self-guarded; it is safe only because callers confine each state to one actor / lock.
- Follow-up (not done here, on purpose): if a future caller shares one state across threads, add a per-state lock (or an actor) around decrypt/commit. The 1:1 ratchet's skipped-key path and the Android/Desktop equivalents of this ordering were not audited in this PR.

body:
## What

- **Settings > Scheduled tasks** and `lumi schedule` (`lumi/schedules.py`): a saved prompt, project, model, permission mode and time limit that runs at set times through Task Scheduler (Windows), a LaunchAgent (macOS) or crontab (Linux), so the app needn't be open.
- Each run is an unattended `lumi run`: policy, budgets, exclusions, the audit log, the guardrails and the sandboxes apply, and a schedule never passes `--trust-project`.
- Results are kept per schedule (the last 30) under `~/.lumi/schedules/<id>/`. A run writes only its results, never `schedules.json`, so it can't undo an edit made while it ran.
- `running.json` keeps a schedule from running twice at once. **Run now** starts `lumi schedule run <id>` in its own process and claims the run for it with a one-time token, so the page shows "Running now" at once and a second click is refused.
- `security.scheduled_tasks` (Privacy & security, lockable by policy) turns the feature off: nothing can be added, resumed or run now, and a run the OS still starts is refused and recorded. A schedule can't be saved with a permission mode the policy doesn't allow.
- Docs: new [scheduled tasks guide](docs/scheduled-tasks.md), nav and index entries, a headless cross-link, the enterprise policy key, an AGENTS.md rule, and Unreleased.

## Validation

- Full `pytest`: 3,977 passed, 4 skipped; `ruff check .` clean; `node --check` on both scripts; UI node tests pass.
- `tests/test_schedules.py` (17 tests) uses a fake registrar and mocked `schtasks`/`crontab`/`launchctl`. No real scheduled task was registered.

author: crazz-e
body:
Closes #271.

## Problem
`daemon.js` parsed both flags as `parseInt(v) || default`. I reproduced the result on main with the real daemon:
- `--deadline-ms 3000000000`, `-1` or `1.5` reached the CHECK and PUSH_PR step deadline, which then fired in 0–2 ms. The dispatcher re-forwards that deadline to every worker.
- `--interval-ms` did the same to the dispatcher's and the scanner's poll timers.
- `abc`, `0` and `Infinity` fell back to the default silently.

This has never fired in production, because the systemd unit passes neither flag.

## Fix
- **Validation:** each flag must be an integer in [1, 2^31−1]. Anything else exits 2 with a message that names the flag, the value and the allowed range. The check runs before the lock, in every mode.
- **Same fix in `scripts/usage-report.js`:** `--top=` gets the same treatment.
- **Help text:** the default deadline covers CHECK and PUSH_PR only.

## Verification
- **Callers:** I checked every caller in production and tooling. Nothing passes these flags except the dispatcher's own forward, which always validates.
- **Opus verifier:** PASS, 13/13 mutants killed. I re-checked that disabling the validation turns all 4 new tests red.
- **Gate, in three environments** (normal, `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, empty `HOME`):

body:
Closes #5417

## 触发条件（逐字读数，2026-09-25 现取）

**现象**：`chore/flaky-ledger` 的 PR 上，`pull_request` run 的结论是 **`action_required`** —— run 被创建、却**零 job ⇒ 零 check-run**（`gh pr checks` 里根本看不到它），必须显式 `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/approve` 才会真的跑。⇒ 台账 PR 拿不到 required 的 checks（`mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`）；而 `Flaky Ledger Reconcile` 的**自己那条 PR 腿**也在队列里（run `36116660786` `action_required`）⇒ 本该兜底的腿是死的，只剩被 GitHub 节流到 2~5.5h 的定时腿。

「偶发」的两条实测形态（同一 push `425732992` = 台账 PR #5563）：

| # | 逐字读数 | 证据 run |
|---|---|---|
| ① | `ℹ️ tip=425732992180fada5f187ae10e4f67ea49c61904 暂无待批准 run（尚未创建或已批准）⇒ 本轮零动作，下一轮触发会重试（历史待批准 98 个均为**陈旧推送**，批准它们对 required 判定无贡献）`；同刻 `state=OPEN mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED autoMerge=armed / check 数=0` | triage `36116623413`（步骤⑤，09:07:26Z；push 在 09:07:0xZ） |
| ② | `🔓 历史待批准 102 个，其中属于分支 tip=425732992180fada5f187ae10e4f67ea49c61904 的 4 个 ⇒ 只批准这 4 个（被 GITHUB_TOKEN 抑制 ⇒ 无 job ⇒ 无 check）：[36116660804, 36116660821, 36116660826, 36116660877]` | reconcile `36118293816`（09:25:32Z） |

⇒ ① **单发一次 approve 撞上「GitHub 还没把这批 run 建出来/标成 action_required」⇒ 脚本按诚实读数退出 `0`、workflow 绿** ⇒ 台账 PR 停在 **0 个 check**，直到 **09:25:31Z**（**18 分钟**后）被**另一条** workflow 的兜底轮次顺手批上（逐条：`gh api …/runs/36116660804/attempts/1 ⇒ conclusion=action_required`、当前 `run_attempt=2`、`run_started_at=09:25:31Z`）。
⇒ ② 该次推送 tip 上**共 10 个** run 在队列里，机制只批 **4 个**（沿用了「重跑白名单」口径）—— 另外 6 个 `[36116660775, 36116660779, 36116660786, 36116660817, 36116660823, 36116660846]`（Mechanism Liveness / PR Issue Link Check / Flaky Ledger Reconcile / Post-Merge Verify / Drift Audit / Deploy Reconcile）**至今**仍是 `action_required`。

**被证伪的假设（有据，别再按它修）**：issue 正文推测的「由 `migao-flaky-bot` **署名的提交**所触发的 run」**不成立** —— 同一次推送 `0d2b2112a`（同为 bot 署名）里，3 个 run 直接执行（`…/runs/36118807935/attempts/1 ⇒ failure`），4 个进队列（`…/runs/36118808148/attempts/1 ⇒ action_required`）。真正的驱动是**这个 PR 由 `GITHUB_TOKEN` 创建**（`gh pr view 5563 --json author ⇒ app/github-actions`）⇒ 批准门槛作用在 **PR/run** 上，与**提交署名无关** ⇒ 「换个署名/身份」不是修法。
（判据自证坐标：只读一律 `git show origin/main:<path>`；run/日志读数取自 `gh api repos/zhaokai-mgzn/migao/actions/...`。）

**与 #5477 / #5480 / #5549 的关系**：三者的根因分别是「弱断言扫描集两侧口径」「点号 worktree + 部分交付悬挂」「required 腿时长」，与本单（审批队列 + 单发 approve）**不同因** ⇒ 未重复修，也未改它们的判定语义。

## 改了什么

1. `.github/scripts/flaky_ledger.py`
   - `approve` 新增 `--wait-seconds`：**幂等轮询**至 tip 的审批队列清空（每轮只批「本轮新出现的 id」⇒ 重复批准不会重复发 POST）；**窗口用尽仍非空 ⇒ 非零退出**，逐条打 run 链接 + `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>/approve` 人工出口（判据「可归因 + 可处置」）。
   - 缺省 `--wait-seconds 0` ⇒ **既有语义（单轮 + 退出 0）一字未动**，窗口由 workflow 显式给（既有的四态红证继续钉住它）。
   - 新子命令 `approval-queue`（**只读**：不发 approve、不碰 PR、不写台账）：把停在 `action_required` 的 run 分成 **机制面 / 按设计不批（重跑白名单外，**不在** required 集合）/ 陈旧推送** 三类，每条带链接与人工出口命令；取不到事实 ⇒ 三态退 `3`（未跑 ≠ 通过）。
2. `.github/workflows/flaky-triage.yml` 步骤⑤：接线 `--wait-seconds "${APPROVE_WAIT_SECONDS:-60}"`，保留 `::error::` fail-closed 出口；回读 `run_attempt` 降级为**审计读数**（不再兼任判据）。
3. `.github/workflows/flaky-ledger-reconcile.yml`：新增 `always()` 的**审批队列读数**步（`approval-queue --min-age-minutes 10`，`tee` 进 job summary；退 `3` ⇒ 红）。用 `always()` 的理由：上游一红时，正是要看「队列里有没有卡住的 run」。

**明确不做**：不自动批准白名单外的 run（它们不是 required，批了只会给台账 PR 添红 —— 现在**有读数**并给出人工入口）；不新增/放宽任何 required 判据；不绕过平台门槛（批准 = 放行**首次执行**，run 仍要真的跑完 required 检查才允许合并）。

## 红证（实跑读数）

- **把修复前的实现喂给新判据**（`git show origin/main:.github/scripts/flaky_ledger.py` / 两条 workflow 装载后跑同一批）：
  - ① 幂等重试 ⇒ `SystemExit(2)`（旧 argparse **不认** `--wait-seconds`）；② fail-closed ⇒ `SystemExit(2)`；③ 队列读数 ⇒ `KeyError('approval_queue_reading')`（读数面不存在）；④ workflow 接线 ⇒ 2 条违规：`triage 的 approve **没给窗口**…`、`reconcile 没有 approval-queue 读数步…`；⑤ 冻结真实队列（push `425732992` 的 10 个 run）：旧口径**会批 4 个**、**永远不批 6 个**。
- **注入式红证**（把修复点单点变异回去 ⇒ 判据必红，已实跑）：窗口去掉 ⇒ `未在窗口内重试到「迟到出现的 run」…`；fail-closed 改回 `return 0` ⇒ `…却退出 0 ⇒ 非 fail-closed`；把面外条目并进机制面 ⇒ `「按设计不批」分类不符`；摘掉 triage 的 `--wait-seconds` / 改名 reconcile 的读数子命令 ⇒ 接线判据红（只认**调用形态**：注释里「提及」不算）。
- 本地：新文件 `11 passed`；同批受影响守卫（flaky 家族 + 声明门禁 + 弱断言盲区 + 红证巡检 + 来源文件名陷阱）`295 passed`；`./check-ui-regression.sh` ✅；`./verify-all.sh gate` ✅（1 通过 / 0 失败）。

## 固化声明

- **判据**（CI job = required 的 `ci workflow helper unit tests`，`pytest tests/unit_ci_workflows -q`）：
  - `tests/unit_ci_workflows/test_flaky_ledger_approval_wait.py::TestApprovalQueueFix::test_wait_retries_until_late_runs_appear`（迟到出现的 run 必须批上）
  - `::test_window_exhausted_is_fail_closed`（窗口用尽仍非空 ⇒ 非零退出 + 链接 + 人工出口）
  - `::test_approval_is_idempotent_within_the_window`（同一 run 只批一次）
  - `::test_reading_splits_the_queue_into_three_classes`、`::test_reading_cli_is_actionable`（三类分开报 + 可行动）
  - `::test_workflows_carry_the_retry_and_the_reading`（两条 workflow 的**调用形态**接线）
  - 类级元守卫（注入式红证）= 同文件 `::TestEveryJudgmentCanGoRed::test_red_proof_dropping_the_wait_window` / `::test_red_proof_dropping_the_fail_closed_exit` / `::test_red_proof_mixing_the_out_of_scope_runs_into_the_mechanism_bucket` / `::test_red_proof_dropping_the_workflow_wiring`
- **回归时怎么红**：删掉 `--wait-seconds` 接线、把窗口判据改回「单发一次」、把 fail-closed 改回 `return 0`、把读数步摘掉/改名，或让「面外」条目混进机制面 ⇒ 上述判据逐条红。`approve` 的既有四态（空候选快速路径 / tip 解析不到 fail-closed / tip 无候选 / 恰好批 tip 那一批 + `--json-out`）继续由 `tests/unit_ci_workflows/test_flaky_triage.py::TestApproveFixRedProofs` 钉住（本 PR 未放宽它们，只更新了 3 处**因源码改写而失效的注入锚点**）。
- **未固化项（照实登记，不粉饰）**：
  1. 白名单外的 6 个 run **仍停在队列里**（按设计：不在 required 集合，批了只会给台账 PR 添红）—— 现在**有读数**（读数步显式列为「按设计不批」+ 人工出口命令），但**不自动批**；这是本单的取舍，不是遗漏。
  2. `flaky-ledger-reconcile.yml` 的 `pull_request` 腿**自己**仍会进队列 ⇒ 该腿可能不执行，兜底仍依赖定时腿（GitHub 节流 2~5.5h）+ 别的 PR 触发的轮次；**谁看**：本次新增的队列读数步 + P3 值班单。
  3. 「平台**为什么**把某些 workflow 放进队列、某些不放」**未取证**（观测到的只是形状：同一次推送 4 个进、3 个不进）。本单按「**只要是队列里的就批（白名单内）/就报（其余）**」处理，不依赖那条未取证的规则；若将来平台语义变化，读数步会先出声。

author: kaku-san
body:
Implements the captain's intent from the relaunch brief.

## A) External wallets only

- `loginMethods` is wallet-only; the Privy config no longer offers email.
- The connect sheet has a single choice — "Connect Phantom or Solana wallet" — and no "Continue with email"; copy never promises an embedded/email wallet.
- `embeddedWallets.createOnLogin` stays `off`, and the removed `createWallet()` path is gone.
- The wallet picker lists external wallets only (`selectableSolanaWallets` filters out Privy embedded wallets), and `selectedSolanaWallet` never auto-selects or honours an embedded address.
- An authenticated legacy embedded-only session is refused for every signature (`signTransaction`/`signMessage`/`signAndSendTransaction`) with **"Connect an external Solana wallet (Phantom, Solflare or another compatible wallet) to invest, cash out or claim."**, and the sheet shows that refusal with `data-embedded-only="true"` instead of a "You're connected" card.

## B) Cash-out settling

Traced `request_withdraw` → keeper fulfil/settle → USDC, plus the timeout in-kind/claim path:

- `POST /api/nav-vault/[id]/claim/prepare` (`prepareNavClaim`) already existed server-side but had **no frontend caller** — that was the gap leaving a timed-out cash-out without a next step.
- New `src/components/cash-out-claim-panel.tsx` wired into the position detail: a reserved withdrawal now shows its observed next step — the keeper converting to USDC, or, once the request timeout passes, a **Claim in kind** action that prepares and signs the chunked owner claim and re-reads the position.
- `src/lib/frontend/cash-out-claim.ts` derives that view from the observed operation (`requestId`, `phase`, server `nextAction`), never inventing state; malformed/finished/deposit operations never show a claim action.
- The positions list names the claim step and stops the endless pending loader for an owner-claimable request.
- The duplicated `confirmSignature` in `vault-flow.tsx` is extracted to `src/lib/frontend/confirm-signature.ts` and shared.

No keeper, program, slice or on-chain bound changes; no UI redesign beyond settling + wallet-only.

## Tests

- `tests/privy-wallet-selection.test.mts`: external-only filtering, embedded never auto-selected, embedded-only session detection, refusal copy.
- `tests/public-index-ux.test.mts`: the picker lists external wallets only and an old Privy email session gets the external-wallet refusal.
- `tests/cash-out-claim.test.mts` (new): request view model, claim-key binding, and rendered converting/claimable panels.
- `tests/nav-vault-api.test.mts`: an open request becomes owner-claimable in kind after its timeout, and the claim route prepares and delivers it (reserved USDC + stock legs), with the pre-timeout refusal.

Local: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (343 pass), `npm run lint` (0 errors), `npm run build` all green.

`no-mistakes` review could not run: the configured pipeline agent (Codex) is out of quota until Sep 30, 2026; the rebase step completed and the failure is the agent binary, not this change.

## Summary
Templates rebuilt from the updated vm-templates repo lock the `ansible` build account (no password, no key) and disable root SSH login. This role only put SSH keys on **root**, so a newly deployed VM (e.g. `r10-test-01`) had no account anyone could log in to.

author: nachopal
body:
Fixes #141

## What changes

Settings > **AI assistants (MCP)** now shows the bearer token **exactly once**, then never again.

- **One-time reveal.** The "Copy your token now" card appears only after the response that generated the token (first switch-on, or **Regenerate token**). It now says you won't see the token again, and it has a **Done** button. The token is dropped for good when you press **Done**, close Settings (`forgetMcpToken`, called from `setPopoverOpen`), receive any later server answer (for example switching off and on), or reload. It lives only in one closure variable and is never written to localStorage or sessionStorage.
- **Masked hint afterwards.** `maskMcpToken` builds `xbo_mcp_ab12…9f3c` (prefix, plus the first and last 4 of the 43 random characters) when the token is generated. Only that hint and the hash are stored. The panel shows `Active token xbo_mcp_ab12…9f3c, created 2026-09-25.`, with the hint in code type. Existing installs don't need to regenerate: a row from before this change that holds only the last 4 characters is shown in the same shape (`xbo_mcp_…wxyz`), and a row with no hint shows `Active token created <date>.`
- **Snippets always use a placeholder.** Every Connect-from snippet (Claude Code, Codex, JSON) carries `<YOUR_TOKEN>`, and `snippet()` no longer accepts a token at all. The Codex snippet keeps `bearer_token_env_var`, and its note says to set `XBOOKMARKS_MCP_TOKEN` to your token. A note under the snippet, always visible, says to paste the token you copied, or regenerate if you lost it.
- **Server:** as before, only `PUT /api/mcp` (first switch-on) and `POST /api/mcp/token` return the plaintext.

## Tests

- `mcp.test.ts`: after a generate and a regenerate, none of the 12 parameter-less `/api` GETs contains either token, whole or as its random part. The stored row holds neither. Also covers the hint format, and legacy rows (last-4 hint, or no hint) still verifying.
- `mcp-settings.test.ts`: no client's snippet ever contains a token, even when one is passed. Also covers the `<YOUR_TOKEN>` placeholder, `tokenLine`/`tokenLineParts`, and the status line never naming the token.
- `mcp-token-view.test.ts` (new, jsdom running the real `app.js` + `index.html`): a regenerated token is revealed once, Copy token copies it, and every client's snippet stays on the placeholder and stays copyable. After closing and reopening Settings, **Done**, switching off and on, or a reload (a new JSDOM against the same fake server), the token is nowhere in the DOM, localStorage or sessionStorage. A mutation check (removing the forget-on-close) fails these tests.

`npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (104 files, 1606 tests) and the building-frontends checker (PASS, with 4 existing `0.7rem` warnings in rules this change doesn't touch) all pass.

## End to end (throwaway seeded DB, port 5741, headless Chrome)

1. Switched MCP on in Settings: the token was revealed, and **Copy token** copied it.
2. Reloaded: only the hint showed. The snippets had `<YOUR_TOKEN>`, and the token was absent from the DOM, both storages, `GET /api/mcp` and `/api/setup`.
3. The copied token worked through the MCP SDK client (`library_stats`).
4. **Regenerate token** revealed a new token once. The old token got a 401 from the SDK client and the new one worked.
5. **Done** removed the token from the page.

I checked screenshots in light and dark at desktop and phone widths. They are not committed.

body:
Implements the A1 offline diagnostic foundation and A2 local Kafka lab using a pinned Confluent Docker image.

author: benjaminshafii
body:
## What is this about?
The PR template and the `open-a-pr` skill get two new sections: how the change is implemented, and what else changed along the way.

## What problem does it solve?
Reviewers had nowhere to read how a change fits together, so technical detail leaked into the plain-language sections. Drive-by fixes in the same diff went unmentioned and surprised reviewers.

## What was the situation before?
The body had five sections. Paths, tool names and flags ended up in "What is this about?", and unrelated edits were only visible by reading the whole diff.

## How is this implemented?
- `.github/pull_request_template.md`: adds `## How is this implemented?` and `## What else changed?` between "situation before" and "Release note"; word budget ~200 → ~250.
- `.opencode/skills/open-a-pr/SKILL.md`: the same two sections in the shape, with guidance (2–5 bullets; technical detail lives here; `none` when nothing else changed).

## What else changed?
- The skill's intro no longer says "four questions".

## Release note
none

No E2E; template and skill text only. `collect-release-prs.mjs` still reads only `## Release note`, so changelog parsing is unaffected.

author: jameskermode
body:
Fixes #321. Also documents the limitation in #322; that issue stays open.

## Bug
`SinclairCrack.get_potential_energy()` computes its far-field term E2 relative to a reference state (`x0`, `E0`, `f0bar`). That state was taken only once, in `__init__`: the u = 0 continuum (plus Cauchy–Born) field at the construction K. `rescale_k()` changed K but kept the old reference. So after `rescale_k` both the energy and its α-derivative were wrong, and the tip force no longer matched −dE/dα by finite differences.

## Fix
The reference is now taken in a new `_set_energy_reference()`, called from both `__init__` and `rescale_k`. It builds the u = 0 state at the current (α, K), records the reference, and then restores u. As a side effect, `self.atoms` is up to date after `rescale_k`, which wasn't the case before.

I didn't snapshot `self.atoms` directly inside `rescale_k`, as #321 suggests. `rescale_k` doesn't call `update_atoms`, so `self.atoms` is out of date at that point. Also, the `__init__` reference is defined at u = 0, not at the current u.

Not covered: arc-length continuation with `variable_k=True` also changes K without refreshing the reference. It only uses forces, not `get_potential_energy`, so it isn't affected.

## Also: #322 docstring
The `CubicCauchyBorn` docstring now says that the ±0.5 sublattice split is only valid for centrosymmetric (diamond-type) crystals, not zincblende ones.

## Test plan
- [x] New `tests/test_sinclair_energy.py`: an EMT Cu crack built at 0.8 k1g and rescaled to 1.2 k1g gives the same `get_potential_energy` (to 1e-8 eV) and the same dE/dα as one built at 1.2 k1g, with a random u. **Fails without the fix**: energies differ by 1.25 eV.
- [x] Crack and Cauchy–Born tests (`test_cauchy_born_corrector`, `test_sinclair_*`, `test_crack`, `test_cubic_crystal_crack`): 20 passed
- [ ] CI
