author: hansblitzz
body:
Zwei Wünsche vom Telefon:

1. **Ein Knopf, dann viele Beutel.** Umziehen, Ernten, Kontamination und Entsorgen als Knöpfe in der Kamera: einmal antippen, dann jeden Beutel scannen, bis der Knopf wieder aus ist. So einfach, dass es jeder ohne Erklärung benutzt.
2. **Fehler, die sagen, was los ist** — und was hilft. Anlass: „Unbekannter Barcode: 1000587" über einem Etikett, das der Server kannte; geholfen hat nur, die App neu zu starten.

## Die vier Knöpfe

Unter dem Kamerabild, als beschriftete Kacheln (2 × 2). Der leuchtende Knopf zeigt, was läuft, seine Zahl, wieviele Beutel es schon waren.

| Knopf | Tippen | Jeder Scan danach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Umziehen** (blau) | fragt einmal: „Wohin kommen die Beutel?" | zieht den Beutel dorthin; der Knopf zeigt das Ziel, z. B. „→ Zelt 1" |
| **Ernten** (orange) | an | öffnet das Gewicht; nach dem Speichern (Enter reicht) zurück in die Kamera |
| **Kontamination** (rot) | an, wie bisher | sammelt; zweiter Tipp oder ✓ öffnet das Formular für alle |
| **Entsorgen** (hell) | an | bucht den Beutel als entsorgt, **ein Scan pro Beutel** |

- Nochmal tippen = aus, mit Meldung „Umziehen beendet — 12 Beutel nach Zelt 1".
- **Umziehen:** ein Platz-Etikett mitten im Umzug wechselt das Ziel (war ein Fehler). Ein Beutel ohne Platz im System (nie eingelagert oder als entsorgt gebucht) → „hat im System noch keinen Platz. Nochmal scannen, dann kommt er nach Zelt 1." Ein Beutel, der schon am Ziel steht → „schon in Zelt 1 — nichts zu tun" (gelb statt rot).
- **Ernten:** „Speichern & weiter" öffnete bisher die grüne Handscanner-Hülle; am Telefon musste man für jeden Beutel die Kamera neu aufmachen.
- **Entsorgen:** die Doppel-Bestätigung (jeden Beutel zweimal scannen, drei Sekunden dazwischen) fällt weg — auch für das gedruckte REMOVE-Etikett. Die Bestätigung ist der Knopf; ↩ nimmt den letzten zurück. Ein schon entsorgter Beutel bekommt keinen zweiten Eintrag.
- **Klebt:** schließt sich die Kamera mitten in der Reihe (Anruf, Sperre, Tipp daneben), nimmt „Scannen" **Umziehen und Ernten** bis 15 Minuten danach wieder auf, mit Hinweis. **Entsorgen nie** — wer später nach einem Beutel sehen will, soll ihn nicht versehentlich wegbuchen.
- Die Zielliste ging **hinter** dem Kamerabild auf (beide `z-index: 200`, die Kamera steht in `index.html` dahinter) — deshalb tat das „TO"-Feld scheinbar nichts. Jetzt liegt sie darüber; solange sie offen ist, liest die Kamera nichts.
- Weniger auf dem Bildschirm: die Reihe „ACTION – TO – 0" steht nur noch, wenn ein gedrucktes Etikett einen Vorgang ohne Knopf gesetzt hat (ADD, MOVE_BATCH). Die Taschenlampe verschwindet auf Telefonen ohne Lampe wirklich (`hidden` wirkte wegen `display: flex` nicht).

## Warum das Etikett „unbekannt" war

Ohne Verbindung zum Server antwortet der Service Worker auf `/api/data` mit **503 und `{error:'offline'}`**. Das ist gültiges JSON, und `applyData()` hat es als Stand übernommen: alle Listen leer, auch das Barcode-Register — bis die nächste Abfrage durchkam oder die App neu startete. Ein kurzer WLAN-Aussetzer reichte.

- `loadData()` und `pollSync()` nehmen nur noch eine gute Antwort an.
- Unbekanntes Etikett, Charge, Kultur oder Platz → der Scanner holt **erst den Stand vom Server** und versucht es noch einmal. Erst dann heißt es „nicht im System".
- Aus dem Hintergrund zurück, oder Ereignisstrom neu verbunden → sofort nachfragen statt bis zu 30 s warten. Eine hängende Abfrage bricht nach 60 s ab, statt alle weiteren zu sperren.

## Meldungen

Jede Fehlermeldung im Scanner sagt, was los ist und was hilft (de/en/pt), mit Namen statt Kürzeln („Zelt 1" statt `TENT1`), ohne Etikettennummer:

| Vorher | Jetzt |
| --- | --- |
| Unbekannter Barcode: 1000587 | Etikett unbekannt, und der Server ist nicht erreichbar. WLAN prüfen, dann nochmal scannen — hilft das nicht, die App neu starten. |
| Unbekannter Barcode: 1000587 (nach dem Nachfragen) | Dieses Etikett gibt es im System nicht (mehr) — die Charge wurde gelöscht, oder das Etikett kommt von einem anderen Server. |
| Unbekannter Barcode: 4006381333931 | Das ist kein Meistertracker-Etikett (Produkt-Barcode?) — das Beutel-Etikett scannen. |
| X hat keinen bekannten Standort — erst mit ADD platzieren | X hat im System noch keinen Platz. Nochmal scannen, dann kommt er nach Zelt 1. |
| MOVE rejected: bag X was moved by another user. Current zone: … | X ist laut System inzwischen in Zelt 2 — nicht umgezogen. Stand ist aktualisiert, nochmal scannen. |
| Scan gespeichert lokal, Server-Sync fehlgeschlagen: … | X NICHT gespeichert — der Server hat es nicht angenommen. WLAN prüfen, dann nochmal scannen. (Grund) |
| Unbekanntes Format: … — Barcode prüfen. | Barcode nicht lesbar („…") — nochmal scannen. Kommen immer falsche Zeichen, ist beim Scanner die Tastatur falsch eingestellt. |
| Kamerafehler: … | Die Kamera startet nicht — App neu starten, dann nochmal. (…) |

Fehler bleiben 7 s stehen statt 4, die Meldung in der Kamera hat Platz für drei Zeilen. „Scan gespeichert lokal" stimmte übrigens nie — der Eintrag verschwand mit der nächsten Abfrage; jetzt geht er gleich weg.

**Service-Worker-Cache auf v56**: neues `app.js` und neues `index.html` gehören zusammen. Die drei neuen Knopf-Bindungen sind zusätzlich abgesichert, falls eines davon doch aus dem Cache kommt.

## Offen, bitte entscheiden

- **Entsorgen ohne Doppel-Scan** gilt auch für das gedruckte REMOVE-Etikett am Handscanner. Wenn ihr dort die Doppel-Bestätigung behalten wollt, sag Bescheid.
- **15 Minuten** für das Wiederaufnehmen von Umziehen/Ernten sind geschätzt.

## Geprüft

- Neue `test/scan-in-serie.test.js` (57 Tests): Umziehen (Zählen, „schon da", Einlagern beim zweiten Scan, Zielwechsel per Platz-Etikett, Zähler bleibt beim selben Ziel), Entsorgen mit einem Scan und ohne Doppelbuchung, Ernten zurück in die Kamera (Enter und beide Knöpfe; Handscanner unverändert), die Knöpfe an/aus mit Zahl und Meldung, gesammelte Kontamination geht beim Umschalten nicht verloren, Wiederaufnehmen (Umziehen/Ernten ja, Entsorgen nie, nach 15 min nicht), Nachfragen vor „unbekannt" für Etikett, Charge, Kultur und Fremdes, die 503-Antwort wird nicht übernommen, 304/200/force/Warten auf laufende Abfrage. Gegengeprüft: zwei absichtlich eingebaute Rückschritte fallen durch.
- `test/scan-einstieg.test.js` an die Knöpfe angepasst.
- Gesamte Suite: 2070 Tests, 0 Fehlschläge. ESLint 52 Warnungen vorher, 52 nachher. Prettier sauber. `mobile-audit` 0/0/0.
- **Am Telefon angesehen** (390 px, offline gerendert mit dem echten Markup und Stylesheet): alle Zustände — neutral, Umziehen mit kurzem und langem Ziel, Ernten, Entsorgen, Kontamination, längste Fehlermeldung. Die Kacheln füllen 358 px in zwei Reihen, kein Name abgeschnitten, die Werkzeugreihe passt mit und ohne Lampe.
- **Nicht** auf einem echten Telefon mit echter Kamera getestet.

Part of #170.

## What now works

- **The box reads a sentence.** Where Maple's route plans, `installMock({ route })` leaves a `plan` lookup on the handle (beside `shape`, over the real `fetch`), and `createMockClient()` asks it 500 ms after typing pauses, abandoning the request before. Each recorded call goes with the names in its last answer (`items [id, origin], total`), never a value.
- **The calm-UI gate** (`readPlan`): below 0.4 confidence nothing; `none` → "That doesn't name a state this page's data can be in."; the runner-up within 0.15 → two chips; otherwise one chip, `Empty · 3 calls`. No numbers, nothing moving while a plan is on its way.
- **A chip** puts its calls in its state beside the rest of the draft, and the sentence goes into the recipe's `request`. Clear drops it.
- A route without a planner (404) turns the field back into the key filter for the page's life; `plan: false` keeps it one. Failures are swallowed.
- **The Next (tRPC) example mounts the box**, through a dynamic import behind the inlined `MAPLE_MOCK` flag, so its production build carries none of it.

## Proof in Chromium

Playwright presses `m`, types the sentence into the box inside its shadow root, clicks the first chip, clicks *Apply and reload*, and reads the reloaded page.

| Example, mode | Sentence | Chip | Recipe after Apply | Reloaded page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Next, `MAPLE_PREVIEW=1 next build && next start` | "no projects yet" | `Empty · 3 calls` | the three `project.*` calls `empty`, `request: "no projects yet"` | "No projects yet.", count 0, banner "Mock on: project.slow is empty and 2 more" |
| Next, same | "make the header blue" | none; the "doesn't name a state" line | — | — |
| Next, `next dev` | "the project count fails" | `Error · 3 calls` | three calls `error` | banner "…fails and 2 more" |
| Next, `next build && next start` | — | no box on the page | — | — |
| Vite, `MAPLE_PREVIEW=1` build + `vite preview`, `/` (inside `<Maple />`) | "no reviews yet" | `Empty · 1 call` | `rest:GET /api/reviews` `empty`, with `request` | banner "Mock on: GET /api/reviews is empty" |
| Vite, same, `/mock.html` (box alone) | "no reviews yet" | `Empty · 1 call` | same, `route: "/mock.html"` | same banner |

Screenshots in the first comment.

`pnpm test`: 1511 passed (new: `client-plan.test.ts`, 22 cases, `routePlan` over msw including a 404 and a 500). `pnpm test:browser`: 483 passed (5 new box cases). Lint, prune, format, typecheck, build and both `verify` pass.

## Numbers

- `@maple-kit/ui/mock` alone: **7.0 KB** gzipped of its 7 KB budget. The next addition to the box will need room made or the budget argued.
- The box on top of the overlay: 2.9 KB of 4 KB.

## Not exercised

- A real model behind the box: both examples here planned with the keyword planner. The jev path is proven route-down in #201, not from the box.
- The keyword planner's reading is rough: "the project count fails" concerns all three `project.*` calls, since sharing one word of two lands exactly on `p = 0.5`. The eval slice measures this; nothing here tunes it.
- The two-chip case and the unsure case in a real example page (they are in the browser suite, against a fake plan).
- A plan arriving after the box closed, and screen-reader announcements of the chips (`mk-live` only).
- `maple mock plan` is the next slice.

## Summary

Fixes gridded-raster precipitation authoring and precompute readiness for issue #371.

The reported `Imported Raster Data` group is the native HEC-RAS authoring layout; it is not an extra/wrong path. HEC-RAS preprocessing must transform it into the shallow solver-facing `Precipitation/Values` and `Precipitation/Timestamp` datasets. The previous precompute workflow could return or terminate at an early signal before that materialization completed, allowing the solver to start without usable rainfall.

## Changes

- add `RasPrecipHdf` and `PrecipRasterImportResult` for native gridded-raster payloads
- preserve source units and distinguish rate, interval-amount, and cumulative semantics
- support first-timestep duration and precipitation ratio explicitly
- orient grids north-up/west-first and validate CRS, spacing, variables, timestamps, and units before model edits
- write the unsteady HDF before changing `.u##` text and create a missing sidecar
- require fresh `.tmp.hdf/.b/.x` artifacts plus aligned, nonempty solver-facing rainfall datasets before preprocessing succeeds
- accept materialized rainfall as the readiness signal under Wine when the BCO marker/process observation is transient
- preserve mapped-drive paths in gridded DSS configuration
- validate AORC NetCDF existence before cloning storm unsteady files
- warn when precipitation-sidecar attributes cannot be read
- expand notebook 924 into native authoring, precompute, final-HDF, runtime-message, and visual validation
- add a detailed follow-up plan for HEC-RAS 5.x–7.x capability research, format routing, and AORC/MRMS/forecast workflow qualification

## Validation

- focused automated suite: **173 passed, 1 skipped** (optional native 6.3.1 specimen), 1 environment warning
- notebook metadata validation: **140 notebooks, 0 errors** (pre-existing catalog warnings remain)
- `git diff --check`: clean
- Windows / HEC-RAS 7.0, executed notebook 924:
  - native source payload: 5 timesteps × 30 raster cells
  - temporary plan HDF materialized aligned rainfall datasets
  - final HDF: 18,066 mesh cells with positive cumulative rainfall
  - final mean/max rainfall: 0.535/0.673 in
  - nonzero hydraulic response; peak mesh depth 9.718 ft
  - runtime messages report precipitation processing completed without precipitation-specific errors

author: s0urledd
body:
Five findings from the earlier code audit, each confirmed and fixed with a regression test:

1. Network feed first FAULT: a suspect-point fault before the span hid a validator's real first fault; LIMIT 20 could miss it; settling (withdrawable) faults were published; ties were unstable. Now one pass over genuine, settled faults, suspect points computed once.
2. Probe budget state was written on every exit, so an unreadable or newer file was replaced by an empty one and the next start skipped the cool-down. Now written only when changed.
3. Export key rotation: on a re-signed day the old key stayed current in /v1/exports/pubkey; verification used only the current key, so older exports failed after a rotation. Now all listed keys are kept and the .sig fingerprint picks the key.
4. Scan gaps: two pruned-height payments in one block recorded overlapping ranges. A covered height is recorded once; existing states are deduped on resume and ingest.
5. sentinel-anchor no longer defaults to mocha-4: the chain id is read from the node (and must match -chain-id), or -chain-id is required.

author: jackyhkust
body:
Add SGLang-Diffusion (SGL-D) CI support for LTX-2.5: the runner LTX CLI plumbing plus one default benchmark config mirroring the xDiT LTX-2.5 default.

#### Background

We benchmark LTX-2.5 through SGLang-Diffusion (`sglang generate`). The existing `.ci/integrations/sgld/runner.py` lacked the LTX-2.5-specific CLI knobs (pipeline class selection, VAE parallel-decode control, the diffusion VAE decoder, and model-variant selection), and there was no SGL-D LTX-2.5 benchmark config. This ports the net-new LTX-2.5 support from our private build so SGL-D and xDiT are directly comparable.

The decode-side performance of this path depends on two SGLang changes that are still in review upstream:
- sgl-project/sglang#40755 — LTX-2 sequence-parallel: skip the no-op self-attention mask so the fused attention backend runs under Ulysses.
- sgl-project/sglang#41240 — LTX-2.5: balance tile-parallel diffusion decode by tile volume (LPT) instead of round-robin.

#### Goals

- Make LTX-2.5 runnable and benchmarkable through the SGL-D CLI path in CI.
- Keep the config knob-for-knob comparable with `benchmark_configs/xdit/ltx2_5.yaml` (`ltx2_5.default`).
- Default the decode path through the diffusion decoder (the path the two sglang PRs above target). It runs today; those PRs improve its SP / decode performance rather than gate correctness.

#### Tasks

- [x] `runner.py`: add `--pipeline_class_name`, `--vae_parallel_decode_mode`, `--vae_use_parallel_decode`, `--use_diffusion_decoder`, `--model_variant`; add `_maybe_local_snapshot()` so model-variant / diffusion-decoder paths resolve a local snapshot dir (a bare HF repo id is a false-negative for the pipeline's subfolder checks); wire these into `run_cli` and `run_api`.
- [x] `benchmark_configs/sgld/ltx_2_5.yaml`: one default config (`ltx_2_5.default.gfx950`), t2v 1024x1536, 121f, distilled 8-step, ulysses 8, decode via the diffusion decoder (`use_diffusion_decoder`), mirroring the xDiT default.
- [x] Reference the two pending sglang PRs inline (`ltx_2_5.yaml` header and the `--use_diffusion_decoder` arg in `runner.py`).

#### Tests

- [x] LTX-2.5 distilled, CLI `sglang generate`, diffusion decoder, on gfx950 (MI355X, ROCm 7.1, `aiter`, bf16): the full i2v / t2v x ulysses{1,8} distilled matrix (121f, g1.0, seed 42) runs to completion via `/app/.ci/runner.py`, exit 0, native h264 + aac mp4 out on every cell.
- [x] Also verified on **NVIDIA B200 (sm_100)** with **sglang v0.5.20** (torch 2.13.0+cu130) — the SGL-D CLI harness and the `LTX2Pipeline` path are not gfx950-specific:
  - The CLI path (`run_type: cli`) emits no `attention_backend`, so `attention_backend: aiter` in the config is a no-op on the CLI path (consumed only by the API path). On NVIDIA, sglang auto-selects `dynamic_cudnn_sdpa` (confirmed in logs), so the same config file runs unchanged on both gfx950 and NVIDIA.
  - `LTX2Pipeline` is pinned via `--pipeline-class-name` and loads the LTX-2.5 distilled checkpoint; the pinned distilled 8-step sigma schedule is applied.
  - The full distilled matrix (i2v / t2v x ulysses{1,8}, 121f, g1.0, seed 42) runs to completion via `/app/.ci/runner.py`, exit 0, native h264 + aac mp4 out on every cell — same `--use_diffusion_decoder` decode path as the shipped default.

Environment note: the older `amdsiloai/pytorch-xdit-sgld:v26.8-custom-nvidia` image cannot run this — its bundled sglang (`gateway-v0.3.1`, ~0.5.10-dev) predates the LTX-2.5 transformer and fails to load the checkpoint (`scale_shift_table` 9-vs-6, missing `caption_projection.linear_2`). B200 verification used a v0.5.20-based image, matching this PR's decode-side sglang dependency.

This PR changes only the SGL-D integration runner and one benchmark config; it does not touch Dockerfiles or public images.

#### Other

Companion to the private LTX-2.5 SGL-D work; verbose LTX-specific comments were trimmed per review feedback before this public port.

author: dinkycoder
body:
Follow-up to #1. It targets `chore/bootstrap`, so merge this first and #1 then carries it into `main`.

## Summary

### 1. `guard.py` hardening (`fix(hooks)`)
I probed the first version with commands it should block, and it missed in every category:

| Category | Commands that got through before |
|---|---|
| Secrets | `grep`/`sed`/`awk`/`more`/`cp`/`base64` on `.env`; `python -c "open('.env')"`; `printenv`, bare `env`; PowerShell `gc .env`, `Select-String`, `Get-ChildItem env:` |
| Mainnet | `--rpc-url https://mainnet.base.org`, `base.llamarpc.com`, `--chain base`, `cast send` after `&&` |
| Sealed set | `ml/eval/./sealed`, `cd ml/eval && cat sealed/…`, `seal*` and `ml/eval/*` globs |
| Raw sanctions data | No rule at all. `>`, `rm`, `sed -i`, `xargs rm` and `git checkout --` all got through. |

**How the checks work now:**
- Checks match what a command *names* (a path, host or variable), not which program reads it.
- Each command is checked in three forms: as written, with quotes stripped and slashes normalized, and with backslash escapes removed. That catches tricks like `.e""nv` and `ml\eval\sealed`.
- Any flag or variable that picks an RPC or chain must name Sepolia or a local node.
- A command that mentions `data/sanctions` may only use read-only programs and no write redirects.
- Decode-and-run patterns are blocked: `base64 -d | sh`, `eval`, `iex`, `-EncodedCommand`, and `b64decode`/`Buffer.from(…,'base64')` combined with an interpreter.

**It now fails closed.** Invalid JSON, a missing or non-string `command`, or any exception exits 2. Claude Code runs the command on every other exit code, so before this change a crash let the command through.

**One false-positive fix:** `8453` used to match as a substring, so it also blocked Base **Sepolia**'s `84532` and `eip155:84532`.

**Known false positive (by design):** a `git commit -m` message that mentions `.env`, `sealed` or `mainnet` gets blocked. Commit with `-F <file>` instead. Exempting commit messages would let `-m "$(cat .env)"` through.

**Known gaps.** This guard only sees the command string, so it can't catch:
- scripts that read `.env` themselves
- paths built from variables (`f=.en; cat ${f}v`)
- recursive searches over the whole tree (`grep -r KEY .`, `git grep`)

The real fix for the sealed set is to keep it out of the checkout entirely. That's your decision and isn't part of this PR.

### 2. Docs check (`fix(docs)`)
- **The bug:** `docs-map.yml` required `README.md` to change whenever `docs/sprint/CURRENT.md` changed. But the README block is generated from the frontmatter only, so ticking a sprint checkbox failed `check_docs` and turned the required `test` check red.
- **The mapping is gone.** `docs-map.yml` now explains why generated blocks aren't mapped.
- **New `gen_readme.py --check`:** it writes nothing and exits 1 if a generated block is stale. CI runs it before `check_docs`.
- **`check_docs.py` no longer crashes without `gh`:** a missing `gh` now counts as "no bypass label".
- **Docs updated:** `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `CURRENT.md`, and the `readme-sync` and `ship` skills now list `--check`.

This PR changes `CURRENT.md` without touching its frontmatter, so it also exercises the fix directly.

## Test plan
- [x] Tests written first and confirmed failing against the old code (57 guard cases; 4 docs-tooling cases)
- [x] `python -m pytest -q`: 103 passed (Linux, Python 3.11)
- [x] `python scripts/gen_readme.py --check` and `python scripts/check_docs.py` pass
- [x] CI `test` check green on this branch
- [x] On Windows: `.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q`: 103 passed; `gen_readme.py --check` and `check_docs.py` pass
- [x] Live session, secrets: `Get-Content .env` (PowerShell) and `grep KEY .env` (Bash) were both blocked with "secret access is blocked". This also confirms the PowerShell tool sends its command in `tool_input.command`.
- [ ] Live session, other categories: one probe each for mainnet, the sealed set, and raw sanctions data

## Summary

Three explicit changes from this feedback round.

### 1. Content font: Public Sans → Inter

You flagged 16px/Public Sans as looking too big and asked to try Inter at
14.5px instead. Sakura's UI chrome (buttons, chips, labels, dialogs)
already used Inter, so `--content-font` now matches it exactly instead of
switching families between chrome and content — Public Sans stays as the
fallback. Font-size drops from 16px to 14.5px; line-height recomputes to
14.5×1.25=18.125px automatically, and the four dot/handle
vertical-centering formulas move from 20px to 18.125px to match.

### 2. Depth indentation: one character further

Per your attached mockup — a child's bullet should begin under the
parent's *second* character, not its first. Measured the actual width of
"T" (matching your example text, "To-Be Process…") at the current
font/size via `canvas.measureText`: ~8.86px. Added that to the existing
23px step (from the earlier recursive-alignment fix) to get 32px. Verified
live: every child's bullet now sits ~9px past its parent's text start,
consistently at every depth. Inline note/remark/Q&A alignment (which
reuses the same per-depth constant for its own row, not a child's) stays
correctly aligned automatically. Updated
`depth-indent-recursive-alignment.spec.ts`'s expectation to match.

### 3. Wider title/editor margins

`#editor-title-row` and `#editor-pane` padding widened to match the
breathing room in your reference screenshot: top padding on the title row
20px → 34px, and left/right gutter on both 26/14px → 40/24px.

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean

author: bihius
body:
Closes #263

## Summary

Learning mode: Guard Proxy proposes rule exclusions for likely false positives, and an admin approves or rejects each one. Nothing is ever applied automatically.

1. Put a policy in **detect only**. A nightly job analyzes the last 24 h of events of every active detect-only policy. **Analyze now** on the policy page runs the same analysis on demand, for any policy.
2. **Every** rule match in every event is grouped by *(rule, matched target)*, not only the event's primary rule. It reuses the Coraza message parser from #293, and anomaly-evaluation rules drop out naturally because they match no variable.
3. A group with at least 3 events becomes a pending suggestion, scoped to the narrowest path prefix covering its events (`/api/users/1` + `/api/users/2` → `/api/users/`). Targets already covered by an existing exclusion are skipped.
4. **Confidence 0–100** that the group is a false positive, weighted by:
   - distinct clients (35)
   - volume (20)
   - hours with events (20)
   - share of events where the rule fired alone (25)

   Rationale per signal is in `tuning_service.confidence_score` and `docs/waf-rules.md`. New suggestions below 30 are not created: single-client bursts tripping several rules are attacks, and listing them invites approving one or poisoning the window.
5. **Review** opens the #264 exclusion form pre-filled; the admin can narrow it, then **Approve** creates the exclusion and resolves the suggestion in one transaction. **Reject** is permanent: re-analysis never re-proposes it. Pending suggestions are refreshed, not duplicated.

### Backend
- `TuningSuggestion` model + migration `ecc951b4c672`. It reuses the Postgres `targettype` enum (`create_type=False`) and adds `suggestionstatus`. Checked upgrade → `alembic check` → downgrade → upgrade on SQLite and Postgres 16.
- `GET /policies/{id}/suggestions` (any user; `?status=` defaults to `pending`), `POST …/analyze?window_hours=` (admin), `POST …/{sid}/approve` (admin, body = the exclusion to create), `POST …/{sid}/reject` (admin). 404 for an unknown policy or suggestion, 409 when the suggestion was already reviewed.
- Nightly `analyze_learning_policies` job in the existing APScheduler. One run reads at most 20 000 most recent events.

### Frontend
- A **Tuning suggestions** card on the policy detail page. It shows rule, target, scope, confidence badge (likely FP / review / unlikely FP) and evidence (events, clients, last seen, **View events** link to the log viewer filtered by rule and time range), with Review/Reject for admins. It is read-only for viewers.
- `RuleExclusionFormModal` gains `createExclusion` / `submitLabel` so approval goes through the approve endpoint.

### Docs
`docs/waf-rules.md`: a new "Learning mode" section and API cheat-sheet rows. The target-types table is also updated; it had gone stale after #293 (new target types, `target_value` must be `null` for single-value targets).

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest --cov=app` (751 passed), `uv run mypy app/`, `uv run ruff check app/`
- [x] `pnpm run type-check`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm exec vitest run` (192 passed)
- [x] Integration tests: suggestion from repeated single-rule matches; every rule in an event considered; single-client attack burst not suggested; re-analysis refreshes instead of duplicating; approve creates the admin-edited exclusion, reject is permanent, second review → 409; already-excluded targets skipped; admin-only writes, 404s; nightly job analyzes only detect-only policies and only the 24 h window
- [x] Mutation checks: counting every match as "rule fired alone", dropping the detect-only filter, and removing the confidence threshold each make a test fail
- [x] **End to end on the local stack (HAProxy + Coraza + backend + UI):**
  1. Switched "Lab Baseline" to detect only. 8 clients (separate containers, distinct IPs) searched Juice Shop for phrases like `cat /dev/null mug`; one of them also sent SQLi/XSS/traversal. All passed through: detect only.
  2. Ran the real scheduled job function in the backend container: top suggestion **932160 on `ARGS:q`, scope `/rest/products/search`, 9 clients, confidence 68**; the attacks scored ≤ 39.
  3. UI: Review → pre-filled form → Approve → exclusion listed, suggestion gone, **Apply config** lit; Reject on another; **Analyze now** → "0 new, 4 updated", nothing re-proposed.
  4. Back to **block**, applied from the UI: the false-positive search → **200**, same input on another path → **403**, SQLi on the same path → **403**.
  5. Local state reverted (exclusion and suggestions deleted, policy in block mode, config re-applied).

## Not included
- The issue's "reminder for policies stuck in detect-only > 7 days" (a risk mitigation, not an acceptance criterion) — can follow separately.
- The ADR: `notes/` is gitignored, so it cannot ship in the PR.

## Summary

Explicit, repeated request from the site owner: a technically-accurate but stiff, literal, word-for-word translation reads as machine-generated, not as something a culturally-fluent human would write for a wedding invitation whose whole identity rests on royal dignity, warmth, and 100% authentic cultural tradition — and that mismatch should be treated as seriously as a factual mistake, not a mere style preference.

## Changes

- Added a shared `BRAND_VOICE` instruction block naming the actual site ("Helasiritha") and giving concrete per-language guidance: the traditional ceremonial register for formal Sinhala wedding invitations/sannasa scrolls, the classical elegant register for formal Tamil invitations, and the dignified formal register of traditional South Asian English wedding invitations — explicitly warning against a stiff calque of the source language's grammar.
- `buildPrompt` (new translations) now embeds this, and its own confidence self-critique now also flags translations that lean too literal/mechanical rather than reading as native-speaker-fluent.
- `buildAuditPrompt` (the quality-audit feature) gained an explicit 7th check category, **VOICE**: flags a version that is technically correct but robotic/mechanical/a structural calque of another version, even when the meaning matches. Its correction guidance was refined so a voice-only fix rewrites just the offending language into natural phrasing (preserving its meaning) rather than treating a different, already-natural language as the thing that must change.

Nothing about the JSON response shape changed — this is a prompt-engineering change.

## Test plan

author: kumilingus
body:
## Description

Runs the browser suite under a restrictive Content Security Policy, fixes two places the library silently lost styles under one, and gives applications a way to switch off the only inline style it injects. **2122 of 2122 pass under the policy.**

Closes the "Test CSP" item on the board.

## How the policy is applied

Karma serves two documents. `client.html` is the runner frame and carries an inline `<style>` of its own, so it stays unrestricted. `context.html` is where the tests execute and has no inline style, so it takes the header:

```
default-src 'self';
script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval';
img-src 'self' data:;
style-src 'self' 'report-sample'
```

`default-src 'self'` covers `connect-src`, `font-src`, `media-src` and the rest in one line, so the suite proves the library reaches for nothing off-origin as well as that it writes no inline styles.

Two directives are relaxed, both deliberately. `script-src` allows inline and eval, because `context.html` carries Karma's own bootstrap and its instrumentation evaluates code; the library uses neither `eval` nor the `Function` constructor anywhere in `src`, but this harness cannot be the thing that proves it. `img-src` allows `data:`, which was the only thing `default-src 'self'` broke on its own, two paper background tests using data-URI images, and which real policies normally permit.

`'report-sample'` matters more than it looks. Without it the browser names the directive and nothing else, so a failure reads `style-src-elem` with no indication of what was blocked.

## What the policy found

**`V.attr('style', ...)` silently did nothing.** It wrote a `style` attribute, which `style-src-attr` drops. It now assigns through the CSSOM, matching what the `style` presentation attribute already did via `.css()`. Elements outside the HTML and SVG namespaces expose no `style` and keep the attribute.

| write | violation | applied | reads back as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setAttribute('style', 'fill:red')` | yes | no | `fill:red` |
| `style.cssText = 'fill:red'` | no | yes | `fill: red;` |

Two behaviour changes come with it: a declaration reads back normalised, and an invalid one yields an empty attribute rather than the verbatim string.

**`util.svg()` silently lost markup styles.** It parses with `DOMParser` and reads `node.style`, which the policy leaves empty, so `style="..."` in any markup string vanished. It now re-applies the raw attribute through the CSSOM before reading. The resulting JSON is applied later through the `style` presentation attribute, which is CSSOM regardless, so this repairs data loss rather than working around a check.

## The paper stylesheet

`dia.Paper` injects one rule as an inline `<style>`, giving elements inside a `scalable` group `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`. That element is subject to `style-src-elem`, so under a policy it is dropped and reported, and today there is no way to opt out short of subclassing.

`injectScalableGroupStylesheet` turns it off:

```js
new dia.Paper({ injectScalableGroupStylesheet: false });
```

It is not marked deprecated. It is the supported way to be policy-clean until v5, and it goes when the thing it disables goes. `stylesheet` itself is deprecated, because injecting CSS is what cannot work under a policy. v5 drops both, and the migration is in the doc comment: add the rule to your own CSS, or set `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` on the elements inside the group that need it.

Two tests pin both sides, so removing the default in v5 is a deliberate act rather than drift.

### Why not make the stylesheet itself policy-safe

An earlier revision adopted it as a constructed stylesheet, which the CSSOM exempts from `style-src`. It worked, and it was the wrong answer. It dodged the policy rather than letting the application decide, it kept a feature alive that is on its way out, and it left `@joint/format-svg` with no stylesheet to clone, since the export relied on the `<style>` living inside `paper.svg`. Keeping the element and letting people switch it off needs no companion change anywhere else.

## Notes

- Each CSP test discards anything reported before its own subject runs, since every test builds a paper.
- `Attributes > textWrap takes external CSS into account` injects a stylesheet of its own to prove external CSS is honoured, and moves to a constructed sheet, which is a test concern rather than a library one.
- The suite is unchanged without the policy: one failure, the guard test, which asserts the policy is in force and so must fail when it is not.
- Joint's inline styling is otherwise CSP-exempt by design, because it goes through `.css()` and the CSSOM. Worth knowing that a strict `style-src` therefore gives an application less control over diagram content than it might assume.

## Not done here

Violations are asserted by the four tests in `test/jointjs/csp.js`, not across the whole suite. A global QUnit `afterEach` attributing a violation to the test that caused it does work, and I tried it: it finds thirteen more violating tests, every one a fixture with a literal `style="..."` in its markup rather than library code, and it takes the run from 8.7 to 30 seconds because each test needs a macrotask for reports to arrive.

It also surfaces something the narrow tests hide. `util.svg()` still emits a report at parse time even though it recovers the data afterwards, so a real application would see reports at its endpoint despite rendering correctly. Avoiding that means keeping the `style` attribute out of the parsed DOM entirely, which is a larger change than this PR.

## Tests

- `grunt karma:joint` under the policy: 2122 of 2122 pass
- `grunt karma:joint` without it: 1 failure, the guard test
- `karma:vectorizer`, `karma:geometry`, `yarn test-server`, `yarn test-ts`: pass
- `@joint/react` Jest in jsdom: 1069 pass
- `eslint`: clean

author: danielcarletti
body:
## Problem

- A CDC table reset from the app or the API can lose its rows when a sync of the table is still finishing.
- The resync button, a table-mode switch, re-enabling a table's sync, and Repair CDC all reset right after asking the running sync to stop, or with no stop request at all.
- A cancel only asks the workflow to stop. The loader still applies batches the sync queued, and the final one hands over, flipping the table to streaming with `reset_pipeline` still set.
- The next streaming run then wipes the table and replays only the change buffer.
- #106270 fixes the same race for TRUNCATE and slot recovery inside capture. This layer covers the request paths, which cannot wait for a later capture run by themselves.

## Changes

- When a sync of the table could still hand over, these paths pause the table's schedule and set `cdc_reset_pending` with `trigger`, instead of resetting.
  Capture then finishes the reset once the sync stops (#106270), unpauses the schedule, and starts the new snapshot.
- With no sync in the way, they reset at once, as before.
- A failed stop check also hands the reset to capture, because capture retries it.
- Re-enabling a table leaves its schedule paused while its reset is pending, so no sync runs on the old state first.
- Capture merges its own reset into the pending key under the row lock, so a request's `trigger` survives a TRUNCATE in the same run.
- After handing a reset over, the request starts a capture run right away, and recreates the capture schedule if it is gone (`trigger_cdc_extraction_schedule`).
  Otherwise the last capture run could have looked for resets just before the key was written, and a missing schedule would never finish the reset. A source marked broken, or with capture paused after a non-retryable error, is left to Repair CDC or resume, which restart capture themselves.
- Every write that stages a reset bumps a `generation` on the key, and capture drops only the reset it finished.
  Field equality could not tell an identical reset, staged while the snapshot was starting, from the finished one, and the table would keep a paused schedule with no reset left to unpause it.
- The admin resync and `resync_schemas_non_billable` refuse instead, with "A sync of this table is still stopping. Retry in a minute."
  They start their own non-billable run, which capture cannot start for them.
- `hand_reset_to_capture_if_sync_running` in `cdc/snapshot_lane.py` holds the shared check. The API reaches it through the lazy `source_management` facade.
- Not changed: `migrate_cdc_source_to_buffered --rollback` still resets right after a cancel. #105912 deletes that command.

## How did you test this code?

- `test_a_reset_is_left_to_capture_while_the_tables_sync_can_still_hand_over` covers the resync, table-mode switch, and re-enable requests with a sync still stopping. It checks for a pending reset, a paused schedule, no reset, and no trigger.
- `test_repair_cdc_cancels_running_cdc_jobs` now also checks that Repair CDC leaves the busy table to capture and does not resume or trigger its schedule.
- `test_a_pending_reset_finishes_before_the_read_once_the_sync_stopped` gains a case where capture starts the snapshot for a reset a request handed over.
- `test_a_cdc_reset_is_refused_while_the_tables_sync_can_still_hand_over` covers the admin resync refusal.
- `test_a_reset_staged_while_the_snapshot_was_starting_is_left_pending` also stages an identical reset through the real request-side merge. That case fails without the generation.
- `test_triggering_capture_recreates_a_schedule_that_is_gone` and the hand-over test cover the capture trigger.
- Each new case fails with its fix removed.
- Not run: an end-to-end check against a real Temporal cancel and loader.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

`docs/internal/cdc-buffered-ingress-runbook.md` lists the request paths that hand a reset to capture, the capture run they start, the reset generation, and the admin refusal.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

- Stacked on #106270, which adds the capture side of `cdc_reset_pending`.
- Skills: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/stacking-prs`.
- CodeRabbit CLI: three findings.
  - Fixed: re-enable unpaused the schedule while the reset was pending.
  - Fixed: capture rebuilt the pending key from a stale in-memory config.
  - Rejected: fail the hand-over when the schedule pause fails. No reset is staged until capture pauses the schedule itself and raises if it cannot. A sync that starts meanwhile cannot hand over into a staged reset. Raising would also fail a table-mode switch after the new mode is saved, leaving the new table unseeded.
- Bot review follow-ups: CodeRabbit's outside-diff "guarantee a capture run" finding and its identical-reset race are both fixed in fc17350 (capture trigger, reset generation); CodeRabbit CLI on that commit: no findings.
- Everything here comes from the repository. No customer data.

This PR closes the rest of set 6 and sets 4 and 5 of `packages/ui/docs/audits/2026-09-24-DASHBOARD-REFINEMENT-AUDIT.md`, and changes one `QuerySummary` label. The three parts are separate commits. One branch carries them, so they share one PR.

## Set 6: the engine inputs (S17, S19, S21, S15)

- **S17.** A column change or an out-of-range entry clamped two entries onto one cell. `resolveLayout` now holds back a clamped entry that covers another entry, and places it in a new row under the lowest tile. An entry that overlaps as saved keeps its place. The rule reads the moved entries in saved order (row, column, id), so the order of the array changes no cell. `placeEntries` applies the same rule before the tiles register, so the server markup follows it. After the tiles register, the reading order follows the painted rows.
- **S19.** A repeated id resolved to the first entry, but the server and the DOM order read the last. The store now reads the first entry of each id in each view, and `mergeLayout` drops a later duplicate on the next commit.
- **S21.** A deeply nested filter overflowed the stack in the parse. `isQueryNode` in the query module now reads groups to the `MAX_DEPTH` of `parseQuery` (32 levels). A deeper filter fails the guard, so the dashboard parse reports `invalid-filter` and the grid column filter reads no filter. The query module plan states the new limit.
- **S15.** Two tiles with one id shared one registration. A development `console.error` now names the id. StrictMode and a swap of two ids stay silent.

## Sets 4 and 5: the gestures (R01, S10, S07, S08, S06, S04, S05)

- **R01.** The drag hook and the resize hook share `measureGesture` and `endGesture`.
- **S10.** An `onValueChange` that throws no longer leaves the gesture in the settle phase. The gesture still gets one end event, and the error goes back to the app.
- **S07.** A gesture refuses to start while another gesture is live.
- **S08.** An edit exit or an unmount ends a live drag or resize. The resize releases its listeners, and the dnd-kit drag ends through its own cancel path. A resize whose tile unmounts ends too. A lift that edit mode ends in the same task cancels the sensor after the sensor attaches its keydown listener.
- **S06.** A drop over a layout that changed from outside ends as canceled, so it does not revert the change or restore a removed entry. `mergeLayout` appends a cell only for a mounted tile.
- **S04 and S05.** The board registers an Escape layer and the grabbing cursor while its gesture is a drag. An Escape during a drag in a dialog cancels the drag and leaves the dialog open. A tile looks lifted only for a drag that the board owns, so a refused or canceled dnd-kit drag shows and says nothing.
- **Tests (T05, T06, T07, T09).** A pointer resize suite, pointer drag cases, a node suite for the drag announcements with keyboard end-event cases, a declined drop, a default hydration, and `active` server markup.

## The summary label

A rule whose operator the field does not list showed the raw value, for example `isEmpty` on a `number` field after a blank dashboard selection. The label now comes from the operators of the field, then from the defaults of the field type, then from the other built-in sets. So `isEmpty` reads `is Empty`, and `equals` on a `date` field whose operators leave it out reads `on`. A parity test holds the evaluator operators and the built-in sets equal. The dashboard scope TSDoc no longer tells an app to list `isEmpty` in the operators of a field.

## Verification

- Each behavioral test failed on the code before its fix. Tests that pin correct behavior only, as guards, are named as such in the commit bodies.
- Two review rounds read the commits, and the later commits fix what they confirmed.
- `biome check .`, `knip`, `turbo run check-types`, the `boundary` project (170 tests), the dashboard and query suites (496 tests, plain and under `vitest.compiler.config.ts`), the grid column filter suite, and the 4 browser dashboard suites pass. The branch merges `main` at `bcaf8c6`.

## Not in this PR

- When `onValueChange` throws, the drop gets no live-region narration.
- A lift that S07 refuses during a live resize still holds the arrows, Space, and Escape in dnd-kit until the user drops or cancels it. The tile shows and says nothing.
- The synthetic `resize` that ends a dnd-kit drag also reaches each other resize listener of the window, and a drag of another `DndContext`.
- `QueryBuilder` sets no depth limit, and `evaluateQuery` and the SQL formatter recurse with no cap.
- The Escape defect of S04 is still open on the other dnd-kit surfaces: kanban, the sortable list, and the grid group manager.

author: xroche
body:
The bounded resolve armed its deadline on the wall clock. A backward NTP step therefore extended the resolve by the size of the step, and `--timeout` stopped firing for that long. That is the #606 wedge the deadline exists to prevent. chrony steps rather than slews past its `makestep` threshold, one second on a default install, and a step at boot can be far larger.

`mtime_monotonic()` is the DNS self-test's own clock, promoted to the engine and now shared with it. The rate limiter's window gets it too. The DNS cache does not, because `t_dnscache.stored` is compared against a wall-clock age and a backward step has to expire those stamps.

A test may not step the host's clock, so `01_engine-dnstimeout` reads the source the way 133 does for gmtime. A deadline armed on one clock and compared on the other is caught at runtime by the existing self-test.

Closes #1769

body:
Redesigns all eight Security pages after the pattern the Overview, Docker, Backups and account pages settled on: identity lines, product marks, lit cards for destinations, and one clear section per idea.

**Overview** opens on how the panel is reached as an identity line (Tailscale's own mark on a tailnet-only panel, the grade in its verdict's colour, the allowed ranges, interfaces, this host's tailnet address and the reader's own address as facts, the posture's verdict and check count at the right end). The five area tiles say what they count with the products themselves; the Findings header carries the count and check time instead of repeating the verdict.

**Firewall** opens on the backend by name with the enable switch beside its state; the rule count moved out of the Rules header, whose only command is now Add rule.

**SSH** opens on sshd with its port, what it was read from, the socket holding the listener and the managed file, with the verdict and recent jobs at the line's end; the keyed accounts are drawn as people.

**Intrusion** opens on fail2ban as its own mark (the project's, from homarr, added to `public/logos/` with its NOTICE entry). Jails are lit cards that open their sheet, each drawn as the service it watches (nginx's mark for `nginx-http-auth`, a glyph for `sshd`) with banned/failing/total in fixed measures. Offenders and the ban log draw addresses as their network and jails as their service.

**Connections, Logins, Network** stay tables of readings (§16): every address is drawn as the network it is on (Tailscale's mark for the tailnet), a peer's processes as their products, a network device as what made it (Tailscale, Docker), an interactive login as the person's initials, and an attacker's attempts as a meter against the most persistent address.

New `components/security/marks.tsx` holds `jailProduct`, `interfaceProduct`, `Address` and `ProcessList`. `product-logo.tsx` registers the fail2ban mark and the fail2ban/apache process aliases.

author: arthexis
body:
Parent issue: #230

## PR 3 — Backlog, migrated-database replay, and delivery models

This PR adds read-only replay sources for migrated/current-generation Arthexis SQLite databases and accelerated replay through the simulator.

### Implemented
- Require a generation-2 migrated database rather than interpreting arbitrary legacy schemas.
- Filter replay by historical charger identity.
- Stream transactions in deterministic order with bounded fetch batches.
- Derive OCPP 1.6 StartTransaction, MeterValues, and StopTransaction events from retained transaction/meter evidence.
- Preserve historical payload timestamps and ordering while decoupling replay timing from the original wall clock.
- Maximum-speed execution sends events back-to-back with no historical sleeps.
- Rebind target-CSMS transaction IDs: StartTransaction captures the runtime ID and subsequent MeterValues/StopTransaction use that ID.
- Replay retained InboundProtocolRequest rows only when they are OCPP 1.6 charge-point→CSMS requests with a usable stored payload.
- Never replay CSMS→charge-point retained requests as charger traffic.
- Add explicit replay pacing policies:
  - maximum speed
  - fixed interval
  - burst size + burst pause
- Keep the replay database read-only.
- Add coverage for deterministic ordering, charger filtering, current-generation validation, inbound direction/version filtering, pacing validation, and accelerated execution.

## Field-test status

**Ready for field testing of the implemented migration/replay path, but not complete.**

The current implementation is sufficient to use a migrated/current-generation database as replay input and exercise historical transaction traffic at accelerated speed. This is appropriate for the next non-destructive field rehearsal together with the migration workflow from #276.

### Missing

A true **live reconnect-and-drain** test is still missing. That behavior must run through the active network simulator transport, not the in-process dispatcher. The older persistent `ocpp simulator open/authorize/status/close` worker from merged PR #231 is no longer present on current `main`, so this PR deliberately does not resurrect that stale command/worker implementation.

That remaining network-facing transport work should stay tracked under parent issue #230 and can be completed after the first field rehearsal informs the exact operator/transport requirements.

## Validation
- Quality: green
- Secret Scan: green
- Package/Clean Install: green
- Python 3.10/3.11/3.13: green

## Status

This PR is a mergeable P3 implementation checkpoint. **Merging this PR does not complete #230.** The parent issue remains open for the missing reconnect/drain transport work, later load/resilience reporting, and any field-test findings.

Implements the current PR 3 checkpoint of #230.

author: yojahny55
body:
## Summary

claude-wp-builder can now build a WooCommerce store from a recorded decision. A validated `store` block in `.wp-create.json` says what the store sells (`catalog`, `store` or `full`); `/wp-woo-setup` writes it and brings WooCommerce in line with it; three store profiles make `/wp-create` do the same for a new site. Stripe keys live in `wp-config.php`, not the database. Everything is proven against a real WordPress 7.1.2 + WooCommerce 11.1.2 in the fixture, including a real Store API order.

Stacked on #149 (`feat/store-fixture`); retarget to `main` once that merges.

## Changes

- **Manifest** (`bin/lib/manifest.mjs`): a strict `store` block validator, three Stripe test-key secrets (env `WP_CREATE_STRIPE_TEST_*` or `.wp-create.local.json`, never the committed manifest), a `Store tier` context row.
- **`plugins/store-kit/`** (new, bundled, PHP 7.4 floor) + `bin/store-kit-sync.sh` (copy in, never downgrade):
  - catalog mode — nothing purchasable, cart and checkout redirect to the shop;
  - Stripe API keys supplied from `STORE_KIT_STRIPE_*` constants and stripped from every save, including the copy Stripe writes inside its webhook data;
  - webhook-secret constants only seed an empty field, so a secret Stripe rotates is saved (SEC-040 reports it) and an admin notice asks to update the constant;
  - a constant whose prefix does not match its mode (e.g. `sk_live_` in a test constant) is refused.
- **Profiles + skill**: `templates/profiles/woo-{catalog,store,full}.json`, `skills/wp-woocommerce/` with one reason row per recommended plugin and an avoid list; `validate-profile` learns the `store` key and the `bundled` source.
- **Setup** (`skills/wp-woocommerce/scripts/woo-lib.php`, `woo-setup.php`): converges admin defaults, HPOS, identity, pages (with Polylang languages), shipping, tax, Stripe in test mode, checkout rate limit, Turnstile, visibility, catalog mode.
  - Never overwrites a value the owner changed; `force` takes it back — except launch state (coming soon, Stripe enabled/test mode, cash on delivery), which is never written on a store that has orders.
  - Report-only on an existing store with orders and no setup record.
  - Reports (never deletes) zones, methods and rates it created that the block no longer names.
  - Secrets never appear in output; a secret setting shows only a `sha256:` fingerprint.
- **SEC-040@2** reads the stored option row instead of `get_option()`, so a key injected by a filter is not reported as at rest.
- **Commands**: `/wp-woo-setup` (new: gate, sync, record, keys never in chat, dry run, apply, report); `/wp-create` marks dev sites `WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=local`, installs bundled plugins, and chains store setup for store profiles. Store profiles stop with one clear line on anything but native WP-CLI.
- **CI**: the integration job provisions the store fixture (`WP_FIXTURE_STORE=1`) and runs `wp-woo-setup-integration.sh`; timeout 15 → 20 minutes.

## Environments

Store profiles need native WP-CLI. Docker, DDEV, Lando and wp-env all run WP-CLI in a container that mounts neither this plugin's scripts nor the host project path, so `/wp-create` and `/wp-woo-setup` stop on anything but `native` before syncing store-kit, with one line saying why.

## Test plan

- [x] `WP_FIXTURE=1 bash tests/checks/wp-woo-setup-integration.sh` — PASS, 120 assertions: refusals, dry run, first run, second run `0 set`, client edit and `force`, launch state held on a store with orders, block edits, checkout type both ways, Polylang override, missing keys, a Store API order ($53.00, processing, in the HPOS table, emails sent), Turnstile failure, the 4th-attempt rate limit, SEC-040's own snippet, report-only, catalog, stale rows reported and not deleted.
- [x] New offline checks: `wp-config-store.sh`, `store-kit.sh`, `woo-lib.sh`, `wp-woo-setup.sh`; extended `wp-profiles.sh`, `audit-gateway-credentials.sh`, `wp-create-profile-enforcement.sh`.
- [x] Every new assertion shown red by mutation and green after a byte-for-byte restore.
- [x] Full offline suite: only the two checks that already fail locally on `main`; `bin/doc-sync-check.sh` and `ci-skip-accounting.sh` pass.
- [ ] CI: PHP 7.4 lint of `plugins/` and the new scripts (no 7.4 binary was available locally).
- [ ] CI integration job green within 20 minutes.

author: hugocasa
body: ## Summary A variable carries an optional `account` id linking it to an OAuth account. The variable API accepted any id, but a variable's link decides which account a read refreshes through. This records who connected each account and checks it when a variable is linked. A variable may now link an account only if: - the caller connected that account (`account.created_by`), or - the caller can already read a variable that links it. ## Changes - **Migration:** adds a nullable `account.created_by`. Existing accounts stay NULL, so they can be linked only through a variable the caller can already read. - **Recording the creator:** both places that create accounts set it: the resource OAuth connect (EE companion, `oauth2_ee.rs`) and the native trigger connect flow. - **The check:** `create_variable`, and `update_variable` when the `account` changes, now run `require_account_link_allowed`. Existing flows keep working. The resource and MCP connect flows create the account and then link it as the same user, and relinking an account you can already read is unchanged. EE companion: windmill-labs/windmill-ee-private (branch `oauth-account-link-ownership`). ## Test plan - [x] On a local instance, as a non-admin member: - [x] linking an id that does not exist yet is refused; - [x] linking an account whose variable was deleted is refused for others and allowed for its creator; - [x] linking an account another member's unreadable variable uses is refused. - [x] Connecting an account records `created_by`. - [x] `SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo check` with `private`: the EE insert is cached. - [ ] Resource OAuth connect on an EE build (AppConnect): creates the account, then the variable, as the same user. Left in draft: adds a migration and changes an auth path, so it wants a human look before ready. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Restricts which OAuth accounts a variable can link to, so only the account's creator—or a caller who can already read a variable linked to it—may link. Previously any account id was accepted, even though reading a variable refreshes through the linked account and exposes its token. **Migration** - Adds nullable `account.created_by`; existing accounts keep NULL, so they can only be linked through a variable the caller can already read. **The check** - `create_variable` and `update_variable` (when the account changes) now require the caller be the creator or have read access through a linked variable. - Both account-creation paths record the creator: the native trigger connect flow and the EE resource OAuth connect in the companion branch `oauth-account-link-ownership`. Written for commit 14dd45dc37601d64cc78a0e8964c99979f05ce3e. Summary will update on new commits.

author: acolomba
body:
## Summary

This change makes every Pi launch in the repository use the Pi version that `package-lock.json` pins. It makes `npm run check` pass on macOS, where it hung and then failed. It also commits the agent configuration that `scripts/init.sh` writes and removes a stray macOS file.

### Pinned Pi runtime

Before this change, `scripts/pi.sh` and the two live-UAT canaries ran the `pi` on `PATH`. On a developer machine that can be a different version: Homebrew had Pi 0.87.1 installed where the lockfile pins 0.86.1. The e2e smoke already ran the pinned Pi from `node_modules`.

A new module, `tests/pi-runtime.ts`, finds the CLI of the installed `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` package. The e2e smoke, both canaries, and `scripts/pi.sh` use it and start Pi with `node <cliPath>`. None of them look up `pi` on `PATH`. Run `npm ci` first.

`scripts/pi.sh` no longer installs the companion extensions with `npm install -g`. It installs pinned versions of pi-mcp-adapter, pi-subagents, and @quintinshaw/pi-dynamic-workflows into a private npm prefix (the directory where npm installs packages). The default prefix is `~/.cache/pi-claude-marketplace/pi-runtime`, and `PI_CM_RUNTIME_PREFIX` overrides it. The script refuses a prefix inside the checkout before it creates any directory. It installs with `--legacy-peer-deps`. Pi supplies its own core packages to the extensions that it loads, so the prefix does not need a second copy of Pi. pi-subagents starts subagents from the running Pi entry point, so subagents also use the pinned Pi.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` no longer lists Pi as a prerequisite and has a new section on `scripts/pi.sh`. `tests/live-uat/README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` describe the change. One fallow duplicate exemption is removed, because the canaries no longer share that code.

### `npm run check` on macOS

Before this change, `npm run check` hung on macOS in `tests/bridges/hooks/stage.test.ts`. With that fixed, 54 other unit tests failed. CI runs on Linux, where all of them pass.

The macOS temporary directory is a symlink: `/var` points to `/private/var`. Child processes, `write-file-atomic`, and the TypeScript compiler report the resolved path, while the tests built paths from the unresolved one. In `stage.test.ts`, a fake `realpath` waited for a path that never arrived, so a promise never settled and the file hung. The tests now create their temporary roots by the resolved path. The unused-type-member gate script now resolves its project root and contracts path too.

Some tests expected Linux behavior. `unlink` on a directory fails with `EPERM` on macOS and `EISDIR` on Linux, and the macOS file system ignores letter case by default. These tests now accept the macOS result. A new test forces a case-sensitive platform. It covers the discovery branch that only Linux hosts reached, and it gives the same result on every host.

Twenty tests used `fs.watch` to make a change in the middle of an operation. The change removed a record, corrupted a file, or locked a directory. macOS delivers file events late, so the change arrived after the operation. These tests now make the change at an exact point through the state I/O, the functions that read and save `state.json`. `updateMarketplace`, `createPluginUpdateOperations`, and `selectReinstallTargets` now take an optional replacement for those functions. #210 used the same pattern for marketplace remove. `withStateGuard` takes the same optional argument as `withLockedStateTransaction`. Production callers pass none of these, so production behavior does not change. Each rewritten test fails when its injected change is removed.

The shifted source lines moved 22 coordinates in `scripts/check-unused-type-members.contracts.json`. Prettier re-indented the two `withStateGuard` callbacks in `update-swap.ts`. `git diff -w` shows the real change there.

### Agent configuration and `.DS_Store`

`scripts/init.sh` runs `codegraph install` and `fallow agent install`. These commands register the `codegraph` and `fallow` MCP servers (tools that an agent can call) for Claude Code and Codex. They also add the `codegraph prompt-hook` to Claude Code. Each run left uncommitted changes in `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/config.toml` and an untracked `.mcp.json`. This change commits that output.

The change also removes `tests/domain/fixtures/hash-stability/sample-plugin/.DS_Store` from git. `.gitignore` already ignores `.DS_Store`, but this copy was committed before that rule existed. Test results do not change, because the hash walk skips `.DS_Store` (`HASH_WALK_SKIP` in `domain/version.ts`).

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/pi.sh -- --version` prints 0.86.1 while `pi` on `PATH` is 0.87.1.
- [x] `scripts/pi.sh -- --offline --help` loads all four extensions without errors.
- [x] `scripts/pi.sh` refuses four prefixes: the repository root, a relative path inside it, a `..` path that leads back into it, and a symlink into it. It creates no directory for any of them.
- [x] `scripts/pi.sh` installs the companions into a new prefix outside the checkout and runs Pi.
- [x] The e2e runtime smoke (`tests/e2e/pi-runtime-smoke.test.ts`) passes.
- [x] `pre-commit` passes on the changed files, and the `fallow audit` verdict is `pass`.
- [x] `npm run check` passes on macOS (Node 26.10): 7,244 unit tests at 100% coverage, 36 integration tests, and every gate.
- [x] Each rewritten race test fails when its injected change is removed.

author: weter11
body:
## Phase 12 — Target Schedule Orchestration

Adds the single application-level entry point for the whole target scheduling pipeline:

```text
TargetSchedule[]
        ↓
TargetPlanner
        ↓
TargetSchedulePolicy
        ↓
TargetScheduleApplicationService
        ↓
TargetScheduleSlotPersister
        ↓
ProgramScheduleRepository
```

**Phase 12 adds no scheduling semantics.** Every semantic decision was already owned by a
component from Stage 2 to Stage 11; this stage connects them in order and stops.

### What it adds

- `TargetScheduleOrchestrator` (`domain/usecase`) — performs exactly three statements:
  `TargetPlanner.plan(...)` → `TargetSchedulePolicy.decide(...)` →
  `TargetScheduleApplicationService.apply(...)`.
- `TargetScheduleOrchestrationRequest` — an immutable value carrying every input one pass needs:
  `programId`, `revisionId`, `schedules`, `window`, `selection`, `existing`, `sources`, `asOf`,
  `pauses`, `programDayBindings`.
- `TargetScheduleOrchestrationResult` — keeps all three semantic boundaries whole
  (`TargetPlan`, `TargetScheduleDecision`, `TargetScheduleApplicationResult`) instead of
  flattening them.
- `AppContainer.targetScheduleOrchestrator`, wired beside `targetScheduleSlotPersister` and
  `targetScheduleApplicationService`. It receives only the application service.

### The rules this stage keeps

| Rule | Where it lives |
| --- | --- |
| Semantic target computation | `TargetPlanner` (Stage 5) |
| Temporal classification | `TargetSchedulePolicy` (Stage 6) |
| Presentation → persistence application | `TargetScheduleApplicationService` (Stage 11) |
| Composition of those three only | `TargetScheduleOrchestrator` (Stage 12) |

- `TargetPlan.planned` is **not** a substitute for `TargetScheduleDecision.created`. The decision
  itself reaches application, so exactly `decision.created` is processed.
- The orchestrator does not filter past/paused/future dates, does not reimplement `isPaused`, and
  holds no second temporal policy. The policy's result is authoritative.
- `request.existing` is forwarded unchanged into both the planner and the policy — never sorted in
  place, filtered, rebuilt, or used to infer execution.
- `request.sources` and `request.selection` are forwarded unchanged.
- The orchestrator constructs no `ProgramDayId`, no `TargetOccurrencePresentation`, no `WorkoutSlot`,
  no `SlotId`, no `targetOccurrenceKey`, no UUID and no random value. Slot identity remains the
  Stage 10 persister's.
- It never touches `ProgramScheduleRepository`, a DAO, an entity, Room or SQLite.
- Typed failures (`TargetOccurrencePresentationException`, `TargetSlotPersistenceException`, planner
  and policy validation failures) propagate unchanged. No catch-all, no empty result.

### Legacy isolation

The target orchestrator does **not** replace the legacy scheduler. `ProgramScheduler.kt`,
`SlotPlanner.kt` and `ScheduleCalendar.kt` are untouched, there is no injection in either direction,
and there is no fallback between the generations. Both contours coexist; the cutover is future work.

### Revised guards (inverted, not relaxed)

Three previous-stage guards asserted an *absence*. Each is now a closed one-element caller list
naming `domain/usecase/TargetScheduleOrchestrator.kt`, with the legacy-contour negatives kept:

- `TargetScheduleArchitectureTest.oldSchedulerSourcesRemainOutsideAndStageTwoHasExactlyOneProductionCaller`
- `TargetPlannerArchitectureTest.stageFiveHasExactlyOneProductionCallerAndItIsTheStageTwelveOrchestrator`
- `TargetSchedulePolicyArchitectureTest.stageSixHasExactlyOneProductionCallerAndItIsTheStageTwelveOrchestrator`

A second consumer still fails each pin. Stage 7's and Stage 10's pins are unchanged.

### Verification

Base: `origin/main` `ddd83f1` (merge of PR #313).

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| base JVM suite | 265 classes / 2336 tests / 0F / 0E / 0S |
| branch JVM suite (`cleanTest`, `--rerun-tasks`) | 267 classes / 2362 tests / 0F / 0E / 0S |
| focused Stage 12 suites | 26 tests / 0F / 0E / 0S |
| `scripts/program-stage12-red-mutations.sh` | control GREEN, caught 17, missed 0, source restored byte-identically, exit 0 |
| `compileDebugKotlin`, `compileReleaseKotlin`, `assembleDebug` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL |
| `git diff --check` | clean |

Documentation: `docs/PROGRAM_TARGET_SCHEDULE_ORCHESTRATION.md`.

## Summary

This pull request consolidates major UX refinements, mobile interaction architectural upgrades, player enhancements, and security improvements from `v5.1.0` through `v5.1.10`.

### 📱 Mobile (SP) Interaction Architecture: Top Segmented Subtabs
- **Replaced Accordion Stacks with Segmented Controls**: Converted stacked accordion cards in `PlaylistTab`, `SearchTab`, and `DownloadMgrTab` into clean, iOS/Spotify-style top segmented controls (`SegmentedTabs`).
- **Semantic Accent Colors**: Each subtab features its own distinct semantic theme with delicate glow shadows:
  - Red (`from-red-500 to-rose-600`): Playlists / Online Search / Local Explorer
  - Blue (`from-sky-500 to-blue-600`): Playlist Details / Album Details / Download History
  - Amber / Purple / Emerald: Daily Recommend / Artist Details / Browser Cache
- **Smooth Auto-Navigation**: Selecting a playlist, album, or artist automatically switches to the respective detail subtab without jarring jumps.
- **Zero-Flicker State Preservation**: Inactive subtabs remain in the DOM via `class:hidden`, preserving search queries, input fields, scroll positions, and loaded data with 0ms switching latency.
- **Accordion Card Flat Mode**: Added `flat?: boolean` prop to `AccordionCard` so that nested components render flat, edge-to-edge cards without redundant headers when inside segmented views.

### 🎧 Audio Player & UI Enhancements
- **Track Source Reveal Shortcuts**: Added desktop double-click and mobile long-press on track source badge to open/reveal local audio files directly in the system file explorer.
- **Player Bar Like Button**: Integrated persistent heart/like toggle button into both desktop and mobile player bars.
- **Immersive Lyric Player**: Refactored action layouts with jitter-free fixed action slots, song comment modal, and netease red heart counter.
- **Offline Audio PWA Range Support**: Implemented HTTP 206 partial content support for browser cache streams, fixing seek/scrub playback on iOS/Safari.
- **Volatile Blob URL Sanitization**: Auto-clean stale blob URLs on startup to avoid playback failure on refreshed sessions.

### 🔍 Search & Playlist Filters
- **Pinyin Search Matching**: Unified local filtering across playlist tables and search results with Chinese pinyin and initials matching (`pinyin-match`).
- **Unified LocalSearchBox**: Extracted standard reusable search box eliminating double clear ("x") icons.
- **Playlist Management**: Added "Remove from playlist" modal with optional local cache deletion.

### 🛡️ Security & Architecture
- **Secret Scanning**: Replaced external `gitleaks` binary dependency with project-local `secretlint` npm package in git hooks.
- **Component Line Budget (<500 lines)**: Split and refactored views to strictly adhere to the project's single-file <500 lines architecture rule.

author: antoncl
body:
Closes #2227

## Why
In a reference peek card, long summary values (tags, aliases) ran past the card's right edge, and rows sat side by side ("Aliases …" with "Role supporting" crammed beside it).

`PeekCard.svelte`'s `.peek-summary` is a two-column grid (`auto 1fr`), but each label/value pair was wrapped in an unstyled `.peek-summary-row` div. The grid's items were therefore whole rows, which filled the two columns alternately. And a `1fr` track has `min-width: auto`, so a `nowrap` value widened the column past the 260px card and `text-overflow: ellipsis` never applied.

## What
- `.peek-summary-row { display: contents; }`: label and value become the grid's cells, one aligned line per field.
- `grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr)`: a long value truncates with "…" inside the card.
- The value carries its full text as a `title`, so it is readable on hover.

## Verification
- Frontend: svelte-check clean, 3563 tests passed, build ok.
- New test: a long summary value carries its full text as its hover title. (Grid layout is CSS that happy-dom doesn't lay out, so the layout itself was checked in the browser.)
- **Browser-verified** on a scratch project with a scratch config, hovering a connection whose target has long aliases: Aliases / Role / Pronouns render one aligned line each, and the alias list ends in "…" inside the card.
