author: graph1ks
body:
## Why
Real-display acceptance rejected two worlds:
- `laser-canopy-grid` read as flat 2D beams repeatedly occupying the same screen-space rig rather than a club/disco laser canopy
- `sparks` read as four small repeating fireworks/fountains

## Laser Canopy
- replace flat rig-to-floor fan geometry with explicit projected 3D room coordinates
- add perspective dance floor, ceiling truss rails and depth slices
- build the hero canopy from transverse, longitudinal and deep diagonal beams at distinct X/Y/Z endpoints
- add projected fixture pods at multiple depths
- keep beam geometry/time ownership autonomous; audio is light/material response only
- route semantic `VisualPalette` roles into the world

## Sparks
- replace four fixed ballistic emitters with a fullscreen procedural spark-storm shader
- multiple directional flow strata span the full frame and move autonomously
- Cinema adds quieter depth strata rather than merely more opacity
- secondary rising embers and close glancing seams add depth without discrete fountain sources
- transient envelope affects hot emission only, never direction/speed/coordinates
- semantic `VisualPalette` retained

## Regression contracts
- reject flat bass-steered laser fan geometry
- require projected 3D canopy room/depth structure
- reject fixed Sparks emitters, ballistic `sparkPosition`, gravity fountain loops and `Math.random`
- require shader-based distributed flow and time-owned geometry

Real-display acceptance remains required after CI.

author: anugram
body:
#191, second half: **redaction runs on the web engine, through the policy written once**, and a differential holds the web to the native engine on every recorded case.

**Stacked on #198** (base: `refactor/redaction-over-a-handle-trait`). Retarget to `main` and rebase once #198 merges.

## What it is

- `web/redact.rs` implements `redact::graph` over the JS bridge. `WebQpdf` implements `PageRedactor` with the native body, `redact::redact_page`: same steps, sharing rules, read-back through a fresh document. **Every method makes the call its native twin makes and drains exactly when it does.**
- Web-only, and each with its own test:
  - keys are copied into the engine heap (memoised); a refused copy is **latched** and the next drain reports it, as qpdf reports its own failures (`PdfObject::key` cannot return one);
  - the web handle's two writes that take a second handle refuse one from another session with an error — with the check removed, the handle-id collision overflows the stack, reproducing the native measurement on the web path.
- One new `qpdf.wasm` export, `qpdf_oh_set_array_item`, through every layer (trait, fake, binding import, JS glue, types, export list); `engines/qpdf-not-exported.toml` is empty again. **+2,496 raw / +642 brotli** on `qpdf.wasm`, measured as an A/B link whose control is byte-identical to the shipped artifact.
- The base Rust module grows **1,902 bytes raw** (353,600 → 355,502) — the new bridge import and its glue, because `JsQpdf` implements the whole bridge trait; **none of redaction's eight needles** is in it.
- The no-engine `expect(dead_code)` gates #198 added are gone (the web calls the policy in every build); what remains is item-by-item with its own reason.

## How it is held to native

`qpdf/web_differential_tests.rs` implements `QpdfBridge` over the native C API, one call for one call, reproducing `bridge-qpdf.js`'s handling of each answer, and runs `WebQpdf` over it — so the web's own Rust (session, handles, key cache, latch, drains, write) runs over the qpdf the native engine links. Cases come from `tests/redaction/outcomes.tsv` itself:

- **463 of 463 redaction outcomes and 107 of 107 rotation vectors identical** on the two engines (output + report digests, or the full error);
- **every web outcome is the one the golden pinned**, errors included (212 redactions among them) — engine-level outcomes equal the golden's operation-level ones on every case, measured;
- **each engine, and only it, is asked**: the bridge counts documents opened per case — native must open none, the web at least one unless a pre-engine ceiling refused the input (12 bomb fixtures);
- **nothing is left in the engine heap** after the run;
- **5 mutations planted in the web half, each caught** (20–209 of 570 outcomes diverge): packed object streams on write, an integer off by one, `remove_key` inert, a prefix-keyed key cache, swapped identity halves.

**What it cannot see**: the JS glue and `qpdf.wasm` themselves. The browser-level comparison needs a redaction entry point in a wasm binding and a worker op, which #137 owns; it is recorded there (issue comment) and in the ADR.

## Gates

- `check-redaction-not-in-base.sh`: its probe now runs the whole operation over the web engine, so **all eight needles have a compiled positive** (three had only planted ones). No shipped module reaches them.
- `check-wasm-exports.sh` in all three directions: the new pair passes; the old artifact is refused naming the function; the new artifact against the old exemption is refused as stale.

## Reviews (both, before the push, each in its own worktree)

**Neither found a leak, a memory-safety bug or a privacy leak.** The security review failed a key copy at every possible point across all 212 redactions (8,840 runs): every one refused, none returned a smaller removal. What they found was checks that could not fail — all fixed in `44270e1`, each with its mutation asserted, recompiled and killed:

- **The differential could not tell which engine ran.** The code review made `WebQpdf::redact_page` call native and all five tests stayed green; the probe meant to rule that out passes for native too. My ADR draft said "a harness that asked native twice could not pass" — false. Now the bridge's open count is checked per case, and the same mutation fails **451 of 463** cases (the other 12 are pre-scan refusals).
- It compared only the redactions with the golden and gated on "> 0" → now every outcome in full, with the exact count, plus a heap-leak assertion.
- **The web open's page ceiling and measured-memory check** could be deleted with everything green → tested (the first memory test sat inside the check's noise margin; the check was right, the test wrong).
- **The web's four drains** had no tests → held, with the same free-standing-null latch the native tests use.
- `write` didn't read the marshalling latch → it does; the header now states the three error paths where the mirror isn't exact (all fail closed).
- The new JS forwarder had no test → a vitest, which fails when two arguments are swapped.

**Left open for you, not decided here** (security review): the removed exemption argued against exporting an array-mutation primitive while no shipped path can run redaction. Its written removal condition (a web `Steps` impl) is met, but its reason holds until #137, and `qpdf.wasm` on every page carries the export meanwhile. Reverting that one line of `build-wasm.sh` + the toml entry is cheap if you'd rather hold it until #137.

Filed from the reviews: #199 (decoded page content is freed without being wiped on the web path — no read-back path found; a gap in an existing posture).

## Verification

`tools/ci-local.py --changed` at `800dcbd`, on a still tree: **24 of 24 jobs passed** (it selected every job). Two earlier runs failed `doc`, both the same class: a public doc comment linking to a private item — the first run of this branch was also stopped mid-way by me because I'd started review fixes, so its result was void.

## Not a route

No wasm binding entry point (#137), no page (#136); #125 still blocks the tool.

author: ndelangen
body:
Part of #1318 (PR 3 of 3: F24). Map: #1310.

## What changes

- One capture-status authority: `assetCaptureStatusSchema` (`z.enum(['scheduled', 'in_progress', 'error'])`) in `src/shared/asset-publishing/captureStatus.ts`. `PublicAssetCaptureStatus` is its `z.infer`, `assetPublishingValidator.captureStatus` is `zodToConvex` of it, and `cardbackPresetSchema.captureStatus` takes it directly. The three restatements (`convex/assetPublishingStatus.ts:7`, `collaborativeAccessValidators.ts:122`, `cardbackPresets.ts:58`) are gone. The Rulebook first page keeps `'failed'` (decision on question 3).
- `publicationStatusFor` derives `'error'` from the jobs it already reads, ranked in progress, then scheduled, then error. `presetFor` drops its second `publication_jobs` read.
- A `CardbackPresetMemo` sits beside `deckBacks` in `cataloguePage`, `listByTypes` and `browsePage`. `getPage` passes one memo to its entry, its preset list and `resolveBackHref`. The memo travels separately from `DeckBackPresentation`, so `getPage` still never passes a presentation.
- `factionDefinition` reads both shared cardback hrefs through `publishedFace`, and the `presetFor` import goes. `publishedFace` builds the same `publishedHref(type, id, cache_token)` as the projection, and `.unique()` throws on a duplicate publication just as the projection's `take(2)` guard did.
- The faction page keeps showing "Current" (decision on question 2). The Files badge is now one `switch` (`filesBadge`) that routes `'error'` back to the publication's own status, replacing the two ternary chains.

## Before and after

No visible change, so the proof is contract tests (red at the base, green at the head) and a page story that is green on both sides.

| Check | Base `2e90071e8ad` | Head |
|---|---|---|
| `convex/assetPublishingStatus.test.ts` › projects failed work as an error capture (the one pinned value that moves, `null` to `'error'`) | red: `captureStatus: null` | green |
| `src/app/ui/content/assetPublishingStatus.test.ts` › reads a failed replacement capture as the publication it leaves in place | red: `'Saved. Public assets are current.'` | green |
| `convex/assetPublishingStatus.test.ts` › shows pending work ahead of error work | green | green |
| Story `Factions` › `DetailKeepsCurrentBesideAFailedReplacement` (a current sheet plus an error job reads "Current" and "Public assets are current.") | green | green |

Bite tests at the head:
- Routing `'error'` to "Unavailable" in `filesBadge` turns the story red (`Unable to find an element with the text: Current`), so the seeded error job does reach the page.
- Ranking error ahead of pending in `publicationStatusFor` turns "shows pending work ahead of error work" red.

### Preset read counts

Measured with a throwaway convex-test file (deleted, not committed) that counted `queryStream` syscalls on `cardback_presets`, and on `publication_assets` and `publication_jobs` with `asset_type = 'cardback-preset'`. The fixture has five preset-mode decks over three keys plus one custom deck.

| Read | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| `getPage`, preset-mode deck | 24 | 12 |
| `getPage`, custom deck | 16 | 12 |
| `listByTypes(['deck'])`, 5 preset decks, 3 keys | 20 | 9 |
| `browsePage('deck')`, same fixture | 20 | 9 |
| `cataloguePage`, 4 preset decks among the 5 newest, 3 keys | 16 | 9 |
| `factionDefinition` | 8 | 2 |

A listing now costs at most 12 preset reads in total (4 presets times 3) however many decks it holds.

## Deploy window

The window exists. Convex deploys before the browser bundle, and `assetPublishing` reaches the faction page unparsed (`src/app/db/factions.ts:163`), so a tab on the previous bundle computes `captureStatus ?? status` and shows "Unavailable" (neutral tone) for a faction whose sheet has an error job. That badge contradicts the rest of the old page: its body copy still reads "Public assets are current." and the download link stays. No stale-data refresh prompt fires, because nothing on that path goes through `parseClientBoundary`. It lasts until that tab reloads: open tabs have no upper bound, and a new visitor meets it only between the Convex step and the bundle step of `deploy-main.yml` (58 seconds on #702). It affects only factions with a `faction_sheet` job in error, which `/__jobs` lists. The editor copy on an old bundle is unaffected in practice, because a save deletes the error job before the "Saved" copy shows. The Cardback preset admin page already read `'error'`.

## Gates

Node v22.16.0, each run on its own and exit code read directly.

| Gate | Exit |
|---|---|
| `bun run typecheck` | 0 |
| `bun run lint` | 0 |
| `bun run format:check` | 0 |
| `bun run check:app-layout` | 0 |
| `bun run check:css-orphans` | 0 |
| `bun run check:css-vars` | 0 |
| `bun run check:prose` | 0 |
| `bun run knip` | 0 |
| `bun run test` | 1, see below |
| `bun run publisher:typecheck` (for parity; `workers/publisher` unchanged) | 0 |
| `bun run game:typecheck` (for parity; `workers/game` and `src/shared/play` unchanged) | 0 |
| Storybook: `src/app/routes/factions.stories.tsx`, `src/app/routes/assets.stories.tsx`, `src/app/routes/_app/assets/presets.stories.tsx`, `src/app/ui/content/**`, `src/app/widgets/deck-editor/**` | 0 (17 files, 98 stories) |
| `bun run publisher:release:verify` | 0, no renderer-manifest diff |

`bun run test`: 2851 of 2853 pass on the second run. The two failures are first-test timeouts at 5000 ms in files this diff does not reach: `src/app/routes/_app/profiles/$profileSlug/edit.test.tsx` and `delete.test.tsx` (the first run also timed out `workers/game/load-limits.native.test.mjs`). The machine's load average was 35 to 41 from parallel sessions. At the base (`2e90071e8ad`) the profile folder passed once and then failed with the same two timeouts on a second run under that load. CI is the clean signal for them.

The renderer manifest did not change: `src/shared/assets/cardbackPresets.ts` gains an import, and neither it nor the new `captureStatus.ts` is in the renderer closure.

## Not run

- The three hosted browser flows (regular, `--public-controls`, `--private-banks`). This PR touches `convex/playCatalogue.ts`, which Play's catalogue capture reads. The nightly queue runs them for every PR, so they were not run here.
- `bun run game:test`: `workers/game` and `src/shared/play` are unchanged. `factionDefinition` returns the same values, and `playCatalogue.captureReads.test.ts` passes unchanged.
- No base-and-head image composite, since nothing visible changes.

## Deviations from the ticket

- `factionAssetPublishingCopy` keeps every string, but it gains one line that reads `'error'` as no capture. Without that line, the "saved" branch (`captureStatus ? ... : 'Saved. Publication scheduled. ...'`) would treat the new truthy `'error'` as a live capture and drop "Publication scheduled." The new copy test pins this.
- `toListEntry`'s positional `owners` parameter becomes a `{ owners, presets }` memo object, so `getPage` can pass presets without passing a presentation.
- `presetFor` is now private to `convex/lib/cardbackPresets.ts`. `presetFromKey` and `resolveBackHref` take the memo as a required argument, and `cardbackPresets.list` wraps its handler (`(ctx) => listCardbackPresets(ctx)`), so the query's args object is never taken as a memo.
- Beyond the one expectation the ticket names, `assetPublishingStatus.test.ts`'s ordering test becomes a two-row `test.each` (in progress over pending, pending over error), with the lower-ranked job inserted first. The ticket also asked for the new copy test and the page story.
- The ticket's verification section asks this PR to run the hosted flows locally. Tonight's instruction hands them to the queue instead.
- Vitest browser mode served the story runs on its own port (63315), not the assigned 6073 and 6074. No Storybook dev server was started.

## After the independent review

Head `b66805043c9`.

- Must-fix, applied: the `assetCaptureStatusSchema` JSDoc claimed one spelling for every as

author: eserlan
body:
## 🎯 Purpose

Slice 3 of the Session Journal (eserlan/Codex-Cryptica#3402), tracked as eserlan/Codex-Cryptica#3408. Follows slices 1 (#3422) and 2 (#3429), both merged. While a journal is running, dice rolls, card draws and table results are added to it automatically, so the journal becomes a record of play and not only typed notes.

## 🛠️ Changes

- **Shared event.** New `JOURNAL:CAPTURE` event on the existing `@codex/events` bus, defined in `session-journal-engine`. Any feature can publish a journal entry through it without importing the journal, so a new capture source needs no journal-side change.
- **One emitter.** Every dice roll, table roll (and per-part re-roll), deck draw, Oracle `/roll` and stat sheet field roll already ends in `DiceHistoryStore.addResult`, so that is where the event is published: exactly once per recorded result, and none of the roll tools' own code changed. The event is local to the tab (it never sets `metadata.sync`).
- **Listener.** `SessionJournalCapture` (wired like the Oracle's listener, in `listeners/session-journal-events.ts`) appends events to the active journal one at a time in the order they arrived. With no active journal, in guest mode, or for a malformed event it quietly does nothing, and a failure while saving is logged and never reaches the roll.
- **Pure logic in the engine package.** `capture.ts` builds the one-line summary and a small structured `sourceRef` (formula and total, table source and result, cards drawn) and enforces bounds: summary 500 characters, result text 1,000, 30 cards, 4 KB per reference, no table resolution chain.
- **Current section moves into the store** (`activeSectionId`, in memory only) so typed notes and captures land in the same section, even while the panel is closed.
- **Entry display.** New `JournalEntryRow.svelte`: automatic entries carry a label and icon (Dice roll, Card draw, Table result, generic fallback for unknown types) so they are told apart from typed notes without relying on colour.
- Help copy updated. Spec, plan, tasks and contract for slice 3 under `specs/163-session-journal/` (User Story 6, FR-024–035).

## 🧪 Testing

- New tests, each with success and negative paths: engine capture logic (30 engine tests, 90% coverage on the package), emitter, listener, current-section store behaviour, entry row and view, the listener's wiring, and an end-to-end chain (real roll history → real bus → real listener → real journal store) covering ordering, a burst, no journal, an ended journal and a reload.
- The roll tools' own existing tests (262 web tests, 314 oracle-engine tests) pass unchanged.
- `lint:changed` and `svelte-check` (0 errors) pass; `bunx fallow audit` verdict `pass`. `codex-review` run on the diff with nothing to fix.
- **Live check in the running app:** with the panel closed, the dice roller, a table roll and the Oracle `/roll` command were each captured once, in order, with the right label; a typed note kept its place; ending the journal stopped capture with no error or message and the roll still worked; everything persisted across a reload.
- **Not checked live:** deck draws (the test vault has no deck; covered by unit and end-to-end tests) and a live burst (the dice roller ignores rapid repeat clicks while it animates; ordering is covered by tests).

## ⚠️ Notes

- Rolls in the solo Adventure prompt and in the Map (VTT) view do not go through the shared roll history, so they are not captured yet. They would publish through the same event.
- Each captured entry is a journal write, and journal writes already mark the vault as changed for cloud backup. With cloud backup on, frequent rolls therefore schedule more (debounced) full backups than typed notes did. Worth watching; not changed here.

## 🏷️ Release Labeling

- `minor`

body:
Closes #89

> **Stacked on #83** (→ #81 → … → #69 → #100 → …). The base is `test/map-domain-scoped-tests`, so this diff shows only 24. Rebased onto 19 in the 01–27 integration; 24's tree is unchanged. Record comments now name both tracks' placements.

Adds the L1 → L2 topic hierarchy beneath `24 Autonomous Organizations`. It is **structural only**: no exposition, no L3, no UI/explorer changes.

## Hierarchy
**15 L1 topics, 88 L2 placements:**
Organizations · Organizational Membership · Roles & Authority · Organizational Structure · Organizational Governance · Organizational Decision-Making · Organizational Policies · Treasuries · Organizational Budgeting · Organizational Workflows · Autonomous Operations · Accountability & Auditability · Disputes & Emergency Controls · Organizational Lifecycle · Inter-Organizational Coordination.

## Reuse
- **Taught here with their own layer, so preferred here:** Organizations (21) and Treasuries (14).
- **34 further placements, each still preferred at its home:**

| Source | Concepts |
|---|---|
| 08 | Roles, Authority Boundaries |
| 10 | Resource Allocation |
| 14 | Mandates, Separation of Powers, Working Groups, Councils & Committees, Governance Models, Constitutions, Proposals, Voting, Decision Rules, Veto Rights, Spending Controls, Treasury Management, Budget Allocation, Grants, Accountability, Transparency, Dispute Resolution, Emergency Powers, Pause Mechanisms, Guardians, Incident Response |
| 20 | Human Oversight |
| 21 | Authority Escalation ("Escalation"), Policy Constraints, Revenue, Capital Allocation |
| 22 | Collective Decision-Making, Conflict Resolution, Task Assignment, Negotiated Agreement |
| 23 | Audit Trails |

- **Disputes & Emergency Controls** consists entirely of existing 14 and 22 concepts. They're the same safeguards, applied at organization level.
- **New concepts:** 67 (13 L1 + 54 L2).

## Kept distinct (41 tested pairs)
- **Membership:** Organizational Membership · Coalition Membership. Member Exit · Exit Rights. Membership Tokens · Token Holders.
- **Governance:** Organizational / Hybrid / Cross-Organizational Governance · Governance Models.
- **Policies:** Organizational Policies, Operating Procedures · Execution Policies. Organizational Compliance · Policy Constraints. Policy Updates · Rule Changes.
- **Workflows:** Organizational Workflows, Workflow Definitions · Execution Planning, Plans. Approval Workflows · Multi-Party Approval. Spending Approvals · Human Approval. Handoffs · Task Delegation.
- **Accountability:** Accountability & Auditability, Liability · Accountability. Auditability · Audit Trails. Responsibility Attribution · Attribution.
- **Treasury:** Treasury Custody · Key Management. Runway · Solvency.
- **Autonomy and lifecycle:** Organizational Autonomy · Autonomy Levels. Organizational Lifecycle · Contract Lifecycle. Formation / Alliances / Dissolution · Coalition Formation / Dissolution. Restructuring · Reorganizations.

## Boundaries
- **vs 23:** 23 is the control plane of *one action* (runtime authorization, sandboxing, execution policies). 24 is the *persistent organization*: its policies, approval workflows, decision rights and accountability. 23's Audit Trails and 20's Human Oversight are placed here because the concepts are the same.
- **vs 25:** 24 covers organizations *composed of actors* and how they run. Operating a protocol itself autonomously is left to 25; protocol upgrades and parameter changes stay in 14 and aren't placed here.

## Verification
- **Commands:** `npm test` 235/235, `tsc`, lint, `git diff --check`, `next build` and the OpenNext build all pass.
- **Tests** (domain-scoped, per #83):
  - Exact 24 tree, order and no L3.
  - Reuse and preferred placements within 24's scope; 41 distinct pairs.
  - No new content; unique IDs.
  - 20–23 unchanged; explorer context, ancestry and `24` as the containing L0.
- **No earlier domain's tests changed.** Only the global registries changed: concept count, authored topics, `POPULATED_L0`, and the preceding-subtree test (which now also covers 14 and 23).
- **Responsive sanity** (production build, 320/1280, all 15 L1 contexts, 656 rows): no clipping or overflow. The longest L2 rows take 4 lines at 320px (e.g. "Organizational Decision-Making › Collective Decision-Making"), as in 10 and 22.

Not merged or deployed.

## What

author: transfix
body:
**Track 1c** of the nav_stats intrinsic-stats build (follows #421, #422). Adds the **epistemic** counterpart to the motion stats — belief coverage + sense-churn — additive/off-by-default.

### What lands
- `nav_coverage {explored_frac, visible_frac, believed_free_frac, phantom_frac}` + `episode_nav_stats.coverage` + `nav_scorecard.mean_coverage`.
- **`compute_coverage(truth, belief, everseen, lastvis, planes, cells)`** — a **pure reducer** over the belief rasters (plane-major; `truth` is one shared plane broadcast per cell): explored = ever seen, visible = in view, believed_free = belief FREE, phantom = believed OCCUPIED where truth is FREE. Null/empty → all zero. Kept **out of the collector** so the collector stays raster-free (mirrors the `min_clearance` caller-provides pattern).
- `veh_nav_stats.sense_flips` (`int64_t`) + `nav_samplers.sense_flips` per-step feed; collector sums the per-agent delta. `nav_scorecard.mean_sense_flips`.
- JSON: episode nested `"coverage"` + per-veh `"sense_flips"`; scorecard nested `"mean_coverage"` + `"mean_sense_flips"`.

### Portability (Track 2 will mirror this in `grl_snam`)
Both are bit-identical to the Python twin given matching inputs. The grl-snam survey confirmed all four rasters + the `flips[]` count exist on the Python side (`(M,H,W)` shape, real `last_visible`). The header **pins the shared contract** so the twin can't desync: the `to_occupancy` binarization literals (`p_thresh 0.5` / `band 0.15` / optimistic), the plane-major + broadcast-truth flattening, the `int64` width (LP64 == Windows/LLP32), and the divide-by-total mean convention (deliberately distinct from the finite-only `min_sep` rule).

### Parity
5 pinned corpus cases stay **byte-identical**; new `CoverageReducerAndSenseFlips` case pins the feature against hand-computed values (explored 5/8, visible 2/8, believed_free 5/8, phantom 2/8; corpus mean_coverage 0.5, mean_sense_flips 5).

### Review
4-lens adversarial review (parity / numeric-indexing / serialization / portability): **no functional defect** — the `truth[c]` shared-plane indexing, phantom/free logic, denominator, and null guards all verified correct; JSON re-parsed cleanly. It surfaced the `long`→`int64` Windows-width fix and three contract-spec gaps (unpinned binarization literals, implicit plane-major/broadcast obligation, divide-by-total vs finite-only) — all fixed here as type/doc hardening so the Track 2 twin has exact values to implement against.

### Test
```
8/8 nav_stats_test pass (5 pinned + formation + progress + coverage)
```

author: 50thycal
body:
## What
### Commit 1: scale, adapt, tables, simpler Adaptive timeline

**Scale one round to later rounds.** Each scripted round's panel has a *Scale R{n} to later rounds* tool.
- You pick the last round to fill and how much each round adds: `+N units`, or `+%` compounding.
- Every round up to that one becomes a copy of this round, with the same weapons, positions and timing, and growing counts.
- A live preview shows the sequence (`30 → 34 → 38 … → 58`) and warns which already-scripted rounds it will replace.
- If the last round you pick is past the end of the region, those rounds are added.
- Implemented as two pure helpers: `extrapolateRound` and `scaledCount`.

**Adapt to player.** There is a region-wide switch in the planner's top bar and a per-round switch on each scripted round.
- Flipping the region switch clears per-round overrides.
- An adapting scripted round multiplies its counts by **granted budget ÷ neutral budget**. This is the same signal the Auto enemy's budget follows.
- The multiplier is clamped to ×0.5–×2 (`scriptScaleFor` in `evolution.ts`).
- Round 1 has no player signal yet, so it fires as written.
- The preview shows the multiplier it applied.

**Tables** (new `src/ui/tableKit.ts`)
- Tap a header to sort: ascending, descending, then back to the original order. The sort is kept across redraws.
- The first column stays frozen when you scroll sideways on a phone.
- Applied to the All-rounds, library, sweep-persona and pattern-compare tables.
- **All rounds** now opens a round only from its round button, so a stray tap on a row no longer jumps. It also has short headings, variant tags and a Total column.

**Adaptive timeline, simplified**
- An intro explains that the tab only affects Auto rounds, and what a credit buys in this region.
- Only the weapon types the region uses are listed; *Show all weapons* reveals the rest.
- Unit caps, tactic ladders, beats and unbuilt variants sit behind *Show advanced rows*.
- Weapon prices read `5cr · ~78 per round`.

### Commit 2: difficulty curve, before → after, set pieces

**Difficulty across rounds**
- *Play every round* previews each round once in the worker, with the same seed and defender.
- It draws one bar per round showing **hits on ships**, with ships sunk as a red tag and the number fired underneath. Tapping a round opens it.
- The bar shows hits rather than losses because a well-defended region can sink nothing for several rounds while still pressing harder each round. A losses bar would stay flat there.
- One series, one axis.
- Once it has run, the All-rounds table gains a sortable *Lost* column. After any edit the chart dims and its button reads *Re-run (changed)*.

**Before → after**
- *Pin this result* keeps the current preview's tally on screen.
- On later edits to the same round (same seed and defender), a small table shows Pinned / Now / Change for fired, shot down, hits and ships lost.
- Changes are coloured by whether they made the round harder or easier for the player.
- A one-line summary sits above the table, e.g. "12 unguided missiles salvo → 12 unguided missiles stream".

**Set pieces**
- Save a scripted round's attacks under a name, using an inline field rather than a pop-up.
- Add a saved set piece to any round of any region from a picker; choosing an entry adds it immediately.
- Stored on the device in `platform/workshopStore.ts`. Saving under an existing name overwrites it, and *Manage* lets you delete.
- The new test caught a bug where two saves in the same millisecond got the same id; that is fixed.

## Data contract
- New optional fields `RegionAuthoringDef.scriptAdapt` and `RegionRoundMilestone.adapt`. Both are additive, so the schema stays v1.
- These compile to `RegionDef.scriptedAdaptive` and are copied onto the enemy economy.
- Set pieces live in their own device store, not in region JSON.
- Packaged regions are unchanged.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 725 passed. New tests cover extrapolation, percent compounding, extending the region, runtime counts after scaling, adapt on/off/override, round 1, the round trip, and set-piece save/reuse/overwrite/delete.
- `npm run build`: clean.
- `node e2e/workshop.mjs`: OK. It now covers the scale tool, table sorting, rows not jumping, the round button, the region adapt switch, the pin before/after table, dropping a set piece into another round, and the difficulty curve plus the *Lost* column.
- Two e2e adjustments:
  - The matrix-scroll check runs at 900px, because the slimmer matrix now fits a 1400px desktop.
  - The map-tap step scrolls the map into view first, because the taller side panel had pushed it partly off screen.

body:
## Что и зачем

Владелец выбрал вариант «спрашивать». Если в форме или при правке ввести дату раньше сегодняшнего дня сообщества, бот ничего не отправляет в Meetups. Он показывает кадр A-16: сходка сразу уйдёт в архив, и есть две кнопки, «Сохранить дату» и «Ввести другую». Граница проверяется по дню, как у архива Meetups. Поэтому сегодняшняя дата в уже прошедший час вопроса не вызывает, ведь сходка останется в «Ближайших».

Ответ после публикации и после правки больше не обещает «видна в списке», если сходка на самом деле в архиве. Это и был дефект из PER-174. Правило записано в `docs/services/telegram-bot.md`, раздел «Прошедшая дата сходки», и в список обязательных угловых случаев под номером 19.

## Отклонения от плана

Отдельного плана не было, развилку закрыл выбор владельца. Отклонений нет.

## Осталось открытым

- Ревью корректности заметило: у сходки `held` с будущей датой ответ «Опубликовать» тоже обещал бы список. Находку оспариваю: признак `archived` ставится только в ответе на публикацию из предпросмотра формы, а там сходка всегда `planned`. Повторная публикация из A-10 рисует карточку, а не текст про список.
- Ревью стандартов предложило вынести повторяющийся приём `...(flag ? { flag: true as const } : {})` в хелпер. Находку оспариваю: это принятая в коде идиома под `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, и хелпер на три места читался бы хуже самой записи.

author: cprussin
body:
Three checks that failed under parallel load and passed on their own, none of
them for anything a branch had changed — #587 met `--test file_index` in CI
with a diff holding no Rust at all. Each is the same mistake in a different
language: a stopwatch standing in for a wait. None of them is fixed by a
longer number.

`#592` landed while this was being written and took the second half of the
file_index story with it — the lost-write window is closed at the source now,
and what is left here is the half it does not reach.

## What each race was

**`tests/file_index.rs` — asking before there is anybody to answer.** A
`search_files` that lands before the index thread has published anything is
answered with *nothing at all*, deliberately, so that an empty list is never
said on a desktop with no index to search (the `SearchFiles` arm in the
compositor says why). There is no reply to read, so `Chrome::wait_for` sits
out its whole patience, and `asked_until_settled` — a loop built to ask again
— dies inside its first turn with its own deadline never so much as read. The
check now waits for the compositor to say the walk has published, which it
does at the first announcement and every one after, and costs nothing on a
machine that was going to win the race anyway.

**`tests/handshake.rs` — a count read before the thing being counted.** It is
the one test in that file with no accepted chrome to wait on first, so its
count started a two-second read timeout at the reconfigure — against the
config watcher's own two-second coalescing cap, which this fixture hits *every
time*: the run directory it writes the config into is also where the session
document, the chrome socket and the cache live, so it never goes quiet and the
reload always rides the cap. Measured on an idle machine, the desktop arrives
between 1.94s and 1.99s in sixty-eight runs out of sixty-eight. Two timers
started together, and the loser reported the compositor for never describing
the desktop. The first description is waited for now; only the duplicate is
still read off a timeout, because a second description is what must *not*
come, and it rides the same walk of the broadcast list as the first.

**`scripts/test-dev-shell.sh` — fixed sleeps for another process.** Every "and
then it reloads" case slept a second and a half for a loop that ticks a tenth
of a second and forks a `stat` and a subshell per turn. Measured, that
handover costs a third of a second idle and one and a half loaded — the whole
budget — which is exactly `wanted: 3 / got: 2`; a little further up, the burst
case read naught reloads and blamed the coalescing. The sleeps become polls on
the condition, bounded rather than deciding: a wait that runs out says nothing
and lets the expectation after it report what it found, so one fault prints
one failure. `dev-shell-reload.sh` now takes its baseline stamp *before*
announcing itself, so the line the test waits on means a build made after it
is one the loop will see — the old order left a window in which a build was
swallowed by the baseline, and `sleep 0.5` was the bet that bash got there
first.

The two waits that cannot be waits stay bounded and say so, because an absence
has no arrival to wait on. The baseline case gains an expectation that the
loop was watching at all: it asserts that nothing happened, so a loop that
never started would have satisfied it, and a check that passes by asking the
question of nobody is worse than one that fails.

Nothing is ignored, retried, slept longer or loosened. The handshake assertion
still reports the same total in the same words.

## Each one reproduced first, and then held

Reproduced under load before anything was changed, and then confirmed against
a window widened on purpose, so the old check fails deterministically and the
new one passes:

| Check | Widened how | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file_index` | index thread held 3s | 5 of its 5 subjects fail, `NeverCame` after 20s each | 10 of 10 pass |
| `handshake` | broadcast held to 8s | fails with the reported words, `described 0 times` | passes |
| `test-dev-shell.sh` | load average ~84 | fails every run | 4 of 4 pass |

Under load without any widening, at the level that first produced them:
`file_index` fails 2 runs in 32 before and 0 after; the handshake count's
reported failure goes from 22 occurrences to none.

## Checks

`./scripts/check.sh shell rust typescript` from the repo root: **87 passed, 0
failed, 0 skipped**, three times over, on this branch rebased on `a6b0625`.
`test-dev-shell.sh` also got faster — 14.5s to 9.9s — because it no longer
sleeps past events it could have waited for.

Nothing under `packages/domicile-engine/patches/`, `CHROMIUM_PIN` or
`engine-release.nix` is touched, and no engine release is needed.

## One thing seen and not fixed

At loads where the compositor cannot start at all — 128 of them on 4 cores,
where 80 fail to publish a session inside the fixture's 20s — the config
watcher sometimes reloads *twice* for one `reconfigure`, because the fixture's
staging write and its rename land more than the watcher's 150ms settle apart,
and the desktop is broadcast twice. It is pre-existing and not in scope here:
it hits `a_chrome_that_agrees_again_after_a_refusal_is_let_back_in_once` and
`a_chrome_that_takes_its_agreement_back_stops_getting_the_desktop`, neither of
which this touches, at the same rate before and after.

**Guidelines audited:** `docs/guidelines/TESTING.md`,
`docs/guidelines/ERRORS.md`, `docs/guidelines/CONTROL_FLOW.md`,
`docs/guidelines/FUNCTIONS.md`, `docs/guidelines/FILES.md`,
`docs/guidelines/RUST.md`, plus `AGENTS.md` on American English and on a skip
reading as loudly as a failure. Change complies with all rules.

Two notes below the line. TDD, for a change whose subject is a check rather
than a behavior, was run as the mandate's shape rather than its letter: each
flake was reproduced and watched to fail for the right reason before anything
was edited, and then — where a window could be widened — turned into a
deterministic red that the fix turns green, which is the table above. No new
test cases were added beyond the one the baseline case needed to stop passing
vacuously, under parsimonious coverage: the checks that exist were made honest
rather than joined by more.

`docs/guidelines/RUST.md` asks for the three Rust checks under `nix develop
.#full` for a change touching `domicile-compositor`. There is no `nix` in this
container, so they ran in the core shell with a real linkable `libxkbcommon`
installed, through `check.sh`, which reports `cargo test` as run rather than
skipped — the 0-skipped line above is what says so.

author: yutapr0117-design
body:
`#240` で「件名フィルタは固有名詞に盲目である」と書いたので、**固有名詞そのもので数え直した** —— 506 か月のアーカイブから `For Approval:` 形式の件名を全部抜いて提出名へ正規化すると **146 件**が得られ、**96 件をドシエが一度も言及していない**（`#242`）。

**優先順位は通数ではなく「委員が名指ししたもの」から**とし、Piana 氏が 2023 年に挙げた 3 件（CC0 / MXM / W3C）を追った。

## 🔴 主な発見

- **`#241` 我々の「記録に在る唯一の日本発の提出」は誤りだった。** IPA Font License v1.0（2009）が在り、**承認されている**。**提出したのは森・濱田松本法律事務所の弁護士**が IPA を代理して。**有利**（日本発の承認例が在る）と**不利**（通った方には弁護士が付いていた＝B1）が同時に出る。
- **`#243` OSD を書いた本人が「OSD は著作権・人格権・特許を区別しない」と述べていた。** Perens 氏 2009 —— *"It applies equally to all of those."* **`#236` の「OSD は特許許諾を要求していない」という読みへの、最も強い反対。** ⚠ 撤回ではなく**重みの配分が変わった**（しかも Perens 氏は両側に居る）。
- **`#244`** 同じ 1 文が**人格権**にも及ぶ —— §12 の「mission creep」側が成り立ちにくくなる。
- **`#245` 「特許について沈黙してよい」の根拠が、発言から実際の承認へ変わった。** W3C（2017・copyright-only と明言して提出・承認）。**同じ反対者が線の両側に居る。**
- **`#246`** 特許の反対が実際に持ち出される条（**OSD 1 / 7**）を提出文が名指ししていなかった → 49 語足した。

## 逆側

- **`#242` の 96 件を「未読 96 件」と読んではならない** —— OpenMDW は誤検出（我々が略称で書いていた）。上位 23 件を手で確かめて 21 件が本物。**候補リストであって census ではない。**
- **「沈黙は許される」は運用であって規則ではない**（Piana 氏 2017 *"must be resolved"*）。
- **B15 に逆側が付いた** —— OSI はフォントのライセンスを承認しており、線は「コードか否か」ではなく *"tied to software"* に引かれている。⚠ 線の位置は不明のまま。
- **2001 年の *"resubmit it"* を我々の処方として読んではならない**（B14 の下では投稿が通っていない）。

## 変更

- `rounds/` に 3 スレッド（IPA Font 41 通 / MXM 59 通 / W3C 25 年分 72 通）= 14 file を逐語保存
- register `#241`〜`#246`（240 → 246）
- `review-precedents.md` §1.110 / `review-doctrine.md` §1.111・§1.112 / §1.105 の「唯一」を撤回
- `AS-OF.md` に 4 行 / bottleneck **B15** に逆側

body:

_Requested by **Kenji** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01G5g3ABQ3pMKVG7fKZnmv3x?thread=cmsg_01G5g3ABQ3pMKVG7fKZnmv3x5rdmaKQQcgfXqGLvCvbzE5)_

Before: 計測ガジェットの面積（`geodesicArea`）は、辺が長いほど小さく出ていました。GeographicLib（WGS84 の測地線多角形）と比べると、東京・大阪・札幌の三角形で −7.4%、100 km の三角形で −0.37%、赤道から北緯 50° の大三角形では −19% でした。北極を囲むリングでは、南極側の面積（地球のほぼ全部）が出ていました。

After: 差は東京・大阪・札幌で −0.011%、100 km の三角形で −0.00016% になりました。北極を囲むリングも正しい側の面積が出ます。

旧式は Chamberlain–Duquette の台形の式で、辺を (λ, sinβ) 平面の直線とみなしていました。計測の線は大円（`measure.js` の `gcPoints`）で描いているので、数字と線の形が合っていませんでした。コメントの「辺形状の差は二次＝数百km級でも無視できる」は、実測では成り立っていませんでした。

How: 緯度を authalic 緯度 β に写し、半径 R_A の球の上で辺を大円とした球面過剰を辺ごとに厳密に足します。辺ごとの過剰は tan(E/2) = tan(Δλ/2)(t1+t2)/(1+t1·t2)（t = tan(β/2)）で求めます。極を囲むリングでは、全球の面積との小さい方を返します。`tests/geodesic.mjs` には GeographicLib 2.1 の参照値 8 件を加えました。緯線に沿う矩形の検定は、縁を細かく刻んで渡す形に直しました（大円の辺では緯線の縁にならないため）。`npm test`（ortho-core）はすべて通っています。

同じ種類の近似は `packages/geopbf/src/extension/spatial.js` の `area` にもあります。ただし、あちらは頂点の密なデータの面積を求めるものなので、この PR では触っていません。

author: micka420-collab
body:
## Why (handoff V2 Alpha, item E)

The Aiguillage (routing) learns from a single signal, the counter-review outcome, and that is deliberate. But one average cannot say *why* a model succeeds or fails. Item E asks that the Genome keep real facts apart, and that absence stays absence.

## What

A **read-only register**: facts per **model × task category**, folded from the retained event journal.

| Fact | Source | Attributed to |
|---|---|---|
| delivered / assigned | `task_assigned`, `task_done` | the current assignment on that node |
| retries · failures · refusals · interruptions | `task_retry`, `task_failed`, `task_rejected`, `task_requeued`/`task_cancelled` | the current assignment on that node |
| Evaluator corrections | `task_retry {source:'evaluator'}` | the last delivered production |
| cross-review opinions (valid / contested) | `contre_expertise_verdict` | the **proven** model (`producteurModele`) when present, otherwise the last production |
| human review | `task_reviewed` (last state per production; cleared by a correction) | the last production |
| median Worker time | `task_done.durationMs` | the delivering assignment |
| provider cost | — | always `"unknown"`, never estimated |

Reading rules:
- **No ranking and no score.** Rows are sorted by model name, then by category.
- **Absence stays absence.** An assignment with no declared model goes to `sansModele`, not under any model. An outcome whose assignment has left the journal window is attributed to nobody. A full window is reported (`fenetre.tronquee`).
- **Known limit (documented in the module):** in a drone race, `task_assigned` carries only the primary's model, so a win by another drone is attributed to no model.

**The routing and its reward are untouched.**

## Code

- `src/shared/registre-genome.ts`: a pure projection.
- `GET /api/genome` (authenticated).
- `store.evenementsParTypes` (bounded, chronological).
- Essaim: a "Genome · facts per model" panel, hidden when an older Queen lacks the route. The existing Essaim screen tests stub the new probe, and the panel test cuts the network (guard `sans-vraie-connexion`).

## Tests (+11)

- 7 unit tests covering: separation of facts, retry vs. correction attribution, human review cleared by a correction, absence, an outcome from another node, the proven model beating the commanded one, failure vs. refusal vs. interruption, sorting, and a truncated window.
- A real Queen and a real `HiveNodeClient` declaring a model: the first attempt fails, the second delivers. The register reads `affectations 2, reprises 1, rendus 1`, and the route answers 401 without a token.
- The **V2 Alpha scenario is extended**: the Evaluator correction goes to `claude-code-model` (the first production), exactly one human approval (the final production), reviewer opinions are filed, and cost is `unknown` on every row. I checked with a temporary mutation that this assertion really runs.
- 3 screen tests covering the column facts, absence, the full window, and the read error.

## Checks

- Local runs: typecheck, dashboard typecheck, lint, build, `git diff --check`, and `npm audit` (0 vulnerabilities) are all clean.
- Full suite: 6042 tests, 6027 passed locally (15 skipped locally, 14 in CI), 0 failed.
- Badges and `DEFINITION-DE-SORTIE.md` are updated to 6042 / 6028 / 14 on main `2cf6e22`.

author: devnexsler
body:
## Summary

Parity-first split of `OutboundActionService` (`service.py` 1,826 -> 971 lines). No behaviour change; not deployed.

**New modules**
- `record.py` — `OutboundActionRecord` + the `ActionStore` seam (both still re-exported from `service.py`), plus `require_action`, `is_due`, `action_result`. The new modules import this instead of the service.
- `stale_context.py` — the needs_confirmation -> yes / no / revise question.
  - Pure core: `execute_answer`, `implicit_revise`, `check_confirmable`, `revised_request`, `asks_on_block`, `waive_shown`, `asks_about_unshown`, `needs_confirmation`, `refusal`.
  - One I/O class, `StaleContextQuestions`, covering the store, the traffic probe and the context loader: `confirm`, `after_execute`, `answer_and_drive`, `reask`, `block`, `waive_shown_inbound`, `ask_about_unshown_inbound`.
  - The service passes in how an answered successor goes through the send gate (`drive_answered`) and the terminal traffic block.
- `recovery.py` — reconcile, the provider-outcome pre-check, exhaust and manual review.
  - Pure plans: `plan_exhaust`, `plan_manual_review`, `plan_recover_acceptance`, `plan_expire_dispatch`, `plan_start_reconciliation`. Each is a tuple of `Claim` / `Transition` / `DefinitiveFail` / `Complete` steps.
  - One executor, `apply_plan`, and `ActionRecovery`.
  - `exhaust` no longer tracks `lease_held` by hand: where the lease is taken is part of the plan.

**Duplicate code merged**
- The "traffic gate -> preflight/prepare or dispatch" tail was written out in `execute`, `_confirm_successor` and `prepare`. It is now one function, `_drive()`.
- The claim -> dead_letter -> manual_review tail shared by `exhaust` and `_manual_review` is now one helper.
- The claim + unknown -> reconciling pair in `reconcile` and `_provider_outcome` is now one plan.

**Traffic methods (step 3) were not moved.** `stale_context.py` builds on `traffic_control.py`, and traffic's enforce path asks `stale_context`, so moving store I/O into `traffic_control.py` would create an import cycle. See the report for the clean follow-up.

## Parity

`legacy_service.py` is the pre-split service, frozen and imported only by the parity tests. `tests/unit/outbound_gateway/parity.py` runs each scenario through both services with every collaborator instrumented. It compares the full trace: public results, the store call sequence with its arguments and returned rows, adapter / probe / loader calls, and log records. UUIDs are normalised.

- `test_parity_stale_context.py` covers:
  - all 96 existing tests (60 service + 36 stale-context), replayed with their own assertions on both sides;
  - 4,032 generated rows: every state x stale detail x decision x due x 12 agent touches, with confirmation on and off;
  - 600 generated conversations that include ledger failures and flag toggles.
- `test_parity_recovery.py` covers:
  - all 60 existing service tests;
  - 2,688 generated rows over a compare-and-set ledger that behaves like the SQL;
  - exhaust ladders failing at each step;
  - a plan-lease invariant.
- A mutation check showed the parity layer catches changes the existing suite misses. A different lease owner in `reask` gave 19 parity failures while the existing tests stayed green. An extra claim in the exhaust ladder gave 15 parity failures while the existing tests stayed green.

## Verification
- `uv run --frozen pytest tests/unit/outbound_gateway -q`: 936 passed, 5 skipped. The existing 651 are unchanged; the other 285 are the new parity tests.
- ruff and pyright are clean on the touched files.
- Real-data replay (`scripts/replay_provider_requests.py --compare replay_base_20260925.json --days 30` in the worker container, read-only): 310 compared, 309 identical. The only change is the known a648bd51 (empty sender account, 09-16, terminal).

author: bsikar
body:
Part of #1478. One slice: what the unclaimed reaper reports about a pass that stops midway.

## The gap

`UnclaimedReport.Steps` documents itself as "counts completed steps by name, so a pass that keeps stopping at the same place says so rather than only counting failures". It did not do that. `Reap` added all four step names at once, and only on the success path, so a reservation that stopped midway contributed nothing to the map even though the steps before the failure had really run against the forge, the hypervisor and the bench.

The consequence is an operator-facing one. A pass the forge refuses at `revoke_registration` and a pass that walks all three systems and only fails to close the row both report an empty `Steps` map and a `Partial` count. Those are different outages and the report could not tell them apart.

## What this does

Counting moves into `revoke`, one step at a time as each completes, and the four-at-once loop in `Reap` goes away. The rules that were already pinned stay pinned: the step that failed is not counted, nothing after a failure runs, the row stays in the queue, and a reservation that finishes the sequence still counts each step exactly once.

A reservation skipped because a job claimed it under the reaper counts no steps, since nothing was done to it.

## Deliberately not done

No `StoppedAt` tally. Which step a reservation stopped at is already derivable from the counts plus `Partial`, and a second map is a reporting-shape decision rather than a fix to a stated contract. If the pass report should name the stopping step directly, that is its own slice.

## Verified

`gofmt` clean, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/...`, `go test ./internal/... -count=1` (all packages) and `go test ./ -count=1` pass on this box.

Not verified: the postgres integration tests need a live database this box does not have, and no lab hardware ran.

The Airflow 3 job runs on one Python version only. Its job is to catch API breakage between Airflow 2 and 3, and Python-version coverage already comes from the 2.11 matrix. The dependency cache key now includes the Airflow version so the two jobs don't restore each other's environments.

author: dawsontoth
body:
The three system tables mTLS certificate verification caches into — `hdb_certificate_cache`, `hdb_crl_cache` and `hdb_revoked_certificates` — no longer expire rows through an `@expiresAt` attribute. Each row carries its expiry as record metadata, and [one declaration per table](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-7d722d983785dba028401155938cbc3099c3594c927c734aff2fc94db2bc43d7R27) stores a table-level `expiration`, [applied on every writable start before worker threads](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-01680253cab1229d8cdc4eff0a56337accf055e871c4ab4d87cb5b4879590445R199) (as #2823 does for `hdb_oidc_token_use`) and on the verification path. A node that never verifies a certificate now holds the full shape instead of the primary-key stub, so the replication handshake stops logging the missing attributes and the rows replicated to it are removed once they expire. Stacked on #2823; GitHub retargets it to `main` when #2823 merges.

Moving the expiry exposed three ways a revoked client certificate could be accepted when certificate verification is enabled (it is off by default), all fixed here:

- **A cached verdict never went stale on RocksDB.** The verdict source [returned its expiry as a field](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-8691965c63d00e69e2b340d7200ca5c0f2bf925868fea3d0939844d77abc553bR73), which a source fill does not store, so every verdict was cached with no expiry. Only the `@expiresAt` sweep removed them, and on RocksDB it throws (#1481). A certificate revoked after its first verification kept being accepted.
- **A revoked certificate on an overdue CRL read as good, on both engines.** Revoked rows [expired at the CRL's `nextUpdate`](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-64e65204a8b6c7bd07673968649743e995a6fbf4b871b093ad7ad2c01d4de622R521), so past it the lookup found nothing: the grace-period branch in `performCRLCheck` was unreachable, and a CRL downloaded after its `nextUpdate` but inside `gracePeriod` reported the certificate `good`.
- **On LMDB, the first check after a CRL download read a revoked certificate as good**, and cached that verdict for `cacheTtl`: the revocations were staged in the verdict fill's transaction, [whose LMDB reads do not see them](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-64e65204a8b6c7bd07673968649743e995a6fbf4b871b093ad7ad2c01d4de622R278).

## For the human reviewer

1. **Requirement.** As specified, with one addition taken on purpose: the CRL grace period. The #2823 session handed that bug over and withdrew its own task, because choosing the revoked rows' stored expiry is the fix. Stacked on #2823 because it shares the `initialize()` block, the "System table bootstrap" design section and #2823's `threads: 0` change to `scheduleCleanup`.
2. **Table-level `expiration` values.** They are the fallback for a row written without an expiry of its own; every writer here sets one. Verdicts get [3 600 s](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-7d722d983785dba028401155938cbc3099c3594c927c734aff2fc94db2bc43d7R20), the shorter of the two methods' default `cacheTtl`, which is what a verdict replicated from a peer still on the old build receives. CRLs get 86 400 s, CRL's default `cacheTtl`. Revocations get [691 200 s](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-7d722d983785dba028401155938cbc3099c3594c927c734aff2fc94db2bc43d7R23) (the 7 days assumed for a CRL without `nextUpdate` plus the default 24 h grace), deliberately long, because a fallback shorter than a revocation's window would admit a revoked certificate early.
3. **Revocations [live until `crl_next_update + gracePeriod`](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-64e65204a8b6c7bd07673968649743e995a6fbf4b871b093ad7ad2c01d4de622R521)**, the window `performCRLCheck` already honors; its decision logic is unchanged. Consequence: past `nextUpdate`, a revoked certificate stays revoked through the grace period without the CRL being refetched, so a `certificateHold` that a newer CRL releases takes effect up to `gracePeriod` late. That is the direction the grace branch was written for.
4. **How a CRL download is stored and decided.** The rows are replaced all or nothing in a transaction of their own, with no per-row `catch`: a failure leaves the previous set and surfaces as no verdict (fail-closed rejects), where before a swallowed insert could leave a partial set that read as good, and [a revoked entry without a serial number now fails the CRL](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-64e65204a8b6c7bd07673968649743e995a6fbf4b871b093ad7ad2c01d4de622R528) instead of being skipped. [Checks on one thread share one download per distribution point](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-64e65204a8b6c7bd07673968649743e995a6fbf4b871b093ad7ad2c01d4de622R394), so a burst of checks against one CA (which the next item makes certain right after the upgrade) runs one replacement per worker instead of one per connection, whose conflicting commits could exceed the retry limit. A shared download [keeps its deadline until the response body is read](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-64e65204a8b6c7bd07673968649743e995a6fbf4b871b093ad7ad2c01d4de622R425): the timer used to be cleared once the headers arrived, so a responder that stalled mid-body held its check with no deadline, and with sharing it would also hold every later check against that CA. [The check that downloaded the CRL decides from that CRL's own revocations](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-64e65204a8b6c7bd07673968649743e995a6fbf4b871b093ad7ad2c01d4de622R278). Planning review had overruled that in-memory decision in favor of re-reading the committed rows; review round 2 showed the re-read can see another worker's older generation of the same CRL and report the certificate good, so it is adopted for the downloading check, with [a test that fails without it](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-2495a68059c4dbda4f6cc01e778b38b4466dad7c9b1c6aa38bd1a57ec0e656dcR704). Replacements from two workers that fetch different generations are still unordered: #2834.
5. **Verdicts cached before this change are never read again, and are evicted once.** They have no stored expiry, and a table's `expiration` applies only to new writes, so `createCacheKey` now [hashes a key version](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-e9b2f0ef284115103c6aa22917899a1eebfcd5579b49a08b61a4124d3e9f4dddR323): every client certificate is verified once more after the upgrade, and old and new nodes use disjoint verdict keys during a rolling upgrade. The first declaration on a node then [evicts the old verdicts](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-7d722d983785dba028401155938cbc3099c3594c927c734aff2fc94db2bc43d7R86) locally (not a replicated delete). If an eviction fails, or the first start stops partway through the scan, the rows left only occupy space, since nothing reads them. Retrying would need a node-local record that the reclaim finished, which I judged not worth adding for a one-time cleanup; review rounds 3 and 4 flagged this, and it stays open.
6. **Declared on every writable start, including nodes that never use mTLS.** A failed declaration or backfill [is logged and the next start retries](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/2835/changes?w=1#diff-01680253cab1229d8cdc4eff0a56337accf055e871c4ab4d87cb5b4879590445R201), as for #2823. The first start after the upgrade pays for the evictions and the revoked table's index backfill (measured below).
7. **Review coverage.** Round 1 had codex, gemini, cursor-grok and the Harper domain adjudicator. Rounds 2 and 3 ran without codex (it needs `codex login` on this machine) and without the adjudicator (Claude's weekly quota), so I triag

author: markokraemer
body:
## The problem

Two defects with one cause: nothing ever told a long-lived box to converge its binaries, and the three turn-start preparations disagreed about which requests they applied to.

## The asymmetry that governs the design

**Config BLOCKS the turn. Binaries MUST NOT.** Config changes what the agent *is*, so `convergeBeforeTurnStart` awaits and a stale box pays a measured 10,287–10,907 ms. The daemon, the CLI, the managed-skill overlay and OpenCode are ~96 MB, ~104 MB, ~373 KB and ~167 MB. A box one turn behind on the CLI is the state that already exists today; a box that makes the user wait for those bytes is a regression.

So the asset lane **detects and schedules**. It never applies, and it is never awaited on the send path. That sentence is in the module header of `runtime-assets/manifest.ts` and in `turn-start-convergence.ts`, because every later reviewer will want to "just await it".

## Proven causes

**1. Binaries never converge on a long-lived box.** `scheduleRuntimeAssetsReconcile` has exactly two non-test call sites — `harness/open-code/boot.ts` (`runtimeReadyTail`) and `harness/open-code/control.ts` (`POST /kortix/refresh`) — and `requestAgentSwapIfIdle` is reached only from the tail of that same pass. `runtime-assets.ts` refuses a swap below `AGENT_SWAP_MIN_UPTIME_MS = 5 * 60_000`. The boot pass fires seconds after `opencode-ready`, so it always answered `too-young`, and no later pass existed. A box staged a daemon update and never installed it, for as long as the box lived.

**2. The API could not tell whether a box was current.** `RuntimeConvergenceReport` described what the last *pass did*: `build` is written even when a half fails, `components` reports outcomes, and `lastConvergence` is in-memory, so every daemon restart reported `build: null`. The persisted truth (`cli_sha256`, `agent_sha256`, `managed_skills_hash`, `staged_agent_sha256`, `opencode_version`) was already on disk in `/opt/kortix/runtime-assets-state.json` and was not surfaced.

**3. `pinned: true` was produced and dropped.** The daemon re-reads the rollback latch from disk on every health call *specifically* so a rollback is visible. `git grep -n runtimeConvergenceReport -- apps/api` returned nothing: `readSandboxConfigState` destructured only the config fields, so a box that crash-looped an update and will not self-heal reported that fact to nobody.

**4. No pre-swap proof, and no rollback at all for OpenCode.** `replaceCli` verified the digest and renamed; nothing executed the binary. `stageAgentBinary` verified the digest; the first thing to run a new daemon was the supervisor, *after* it had replaced the running one. `publishOpencodeNativeLink` symlink-renames `opencode.current` with no retained predecessor, and `seam.restart()` is `lifecycle.restart()` — a hard stop+start, not the config path's verified `reloadVerified`. An OpenCode that installed cleanly and then failed to serve left the box **down**, with nothing to go back to.

**5. `shouldSyncProjectEnvBeforeProxy` was port-8000-only on the client-addressed port.** It answered `port !== 8000 ⇒ false` and never stripped the in-box `/proxy/<n>/` prefix, while `isTurnStartRequest` covers 4096/4097 *and* strips it. Platinum rewrites 4096→8000 and Daytona does not, so **the same prompt got the secret refresh and the connector-grant re-mint on one provider and neither on the other.** `preview.ts` already stated the defect in a comment and documented the divergence as intentional.

### Correcting the premise, before anyone repeats it

The SDK builds `${backendUrl}/p/{externalId}/8000` unconditionally (`packages/sdk/src/core/session/server-store/url-helpers.ts`), and `apps/cli` reaches OpenCode only through the SDK (enforced by `apps/cli/scripts/sdk-boundary.mjs`). **SDK `send()` and `kortix sessions chat` did get the env sync.** The real holes were a prompt addressed straight at `:4096`/`:4097`, a prompt at `/p/<ext>/8000/proxy/4096/...`, and the provider-dependent split between the two call sites.

## What changed

**One predicate.** `isTurnStartEnvSync(port, method, path)` = `isTurnStartRequest` minus `/summarize`, called with `upstreamPort` and `remainingPath` at both sites. `isConnectorGatedTurn` was a byte-identical second copy and is collapsed into it. `shouldSyncProjectEnvBeforeProxy` is deleted; the "ON PURPOSE" comment that documented the divergence is rewritten to say it was wrong. The path set is byte-identical to today — `prompt_async|message|command`, `/summarize` still excluded — and only the port variable and the prefix handling change. `isTurnStartRequest` moved to `projects/turn-start-request.ts`, a leaf with no `config` import, so `pre-prompt-env-sync.ts` can build on it without dragging a `mock.module`-replaced module into the proxy suites.

**Second-order effects, asserted rather than hand-waved:** `generateSessionTitleFromFirstPrompt` and `scheduleOpencodeSnapshotSync` now fire for `:4096`-addressed turns (both fire-and-forget, the title path first-prompt-guarded), and `dropUndeclaredPromptAgent` now runs on that path too — which closes INC-2026-09-15's remaining Daytona hole rather than opening one.

**The box says which bytes it runs.** `runtime.running` is added to the health `runtime` block, read from the state file with the in-memory pass overlaid. No new route, no new probe.

**The API reads it.** `readSandboxConfigState` parses `runtime`; `probeRunningRelease` records the asset verdict from the *same* health GET the config gate already makes. Net new network cost on the turn path: **zero**. `apps/api/src/runtime-assets/running-assets.ts` is the memo, modelled on `config-releases/running-release.ts`, and every entry carries the `manifestFingerprint()` it was computed against — a read against another fingerprint is a miss, which is what stops a rolling deploy re-scheduling a pass the box's epoch guard will refuse.

**A turn-boundary trigger, not a timer.** `session.idle` in `harness/open-code/boot.ts` calls `convergeRuntimeAssetsAtTurnEnd`: a reconcile pass, and — independently, because the binary that needs installing was staged by an *earlier* pass — `applyStagedAssetsIfIdle`. The five-minute floor is waived only there, because a finished turn is the opposite of the session-start hot path it was written to protect. The five config-release AST tripwires stay green.

**Candidate binaries are executed before they replace a working one.** Both the CLI and the agent run from the temp path first. **Exit code, not version string**: `kortix --version` prints a decorated header, so an equality check would assert formatting, not a fact — and a false negative there would freeze CLI updates fleet-wide while looking like a safety feature. `opencode --version` prints a bare version, which is why `installOpencodeVersion` can and does compare it.

**OpenCode gets a rollback.** `opencode.prev` is recorded *before* the install; a restart that does not reach `ok` re-points `opencode.current` at it, restarts, and writes `opencode.pinned`, which the next pass honours exactly as the agent half honours `agent.pinned`. If the predecessor cannot be resolved and a binary *is* serving, the install is refused and the box is left working.

**Two more swap blockers.** `runtime-starting` (`harness.lifecycle.getState() !== 'ok'`) — the turn oracle cannot see a boot, so it answers `false` while the runtime is coming up and a swap would turn a recoverable restart into a dead box. `sse-subscriber` is **off by default** behind `KORTIX_AGENT_SWAP_REQUIRE_UNATTENDED=1`: a swap severs SSE streams, the client reconnects and the ring replays, so the cost is visible but not lossy — and blocking on subscribers would mean a session with one open tab **never** converges, which is the original defect.

**Entrypoint: decided, not left advertised and unconsumed.** Out-of-band repair only, in `components.entrypoint`, in the route description (which previously claimed the control plane installs it — it does not, and never has

body:
## Summary

A content refresh that fixes what was wrong and adds what changed, without cutting anything and without new dependencies. Every skill still works exactly as before (no required CLI, MCP, or plugin).

Where the engine companies publish their own skills or docs (Unity, PixiJS, Roblox), we read them to find bugs and missing pitfalls in ours, verified each point against the engine's primary docs or source, and wrote it in our own words. Nothing was copied.

### Fixes to wrong or outdated content
- **three.js (r184 -> r186):** `THREE.Clock` -> `THREE.Timer` (Clock deprecated in r183), `RGBELoader` -> `HDRLoader` (renamed in r180), `PCFSoftShadowMap` -> `PCFShadowMap` (soft since r182; the old constant now falls back with a warning), CDN and decoder pins bumped.
- **PixiJS (8.19 -> 8.21):** the default `eventMode` is `'passive'`, not `'none'`; `interactive = true` is a deprecated alias, not an error.
- **Roblox DataStores:** limits described with the unified experience-level budget (in-game + Open Cloud, since 2026-07-29) and the new storage limit.
- **Steam:** first titles have a 21-day wait between paying the app fee and release (Steamworks onboarding page).
- **Unity Tilemap:** stale `tilemap.extras@1.6` docs link -> `@6.0`.
- **Yarn Spinner:** example relabelled 3.x and declares its variables before use.

### Improvements
- **Godot physics:** Jolt is the default 3D engine for projects created in 4.6+; adds the documented behavior differences (ray-cast `face_index`, single-body joints, soft limits, kinematic contacts, margins).
- **Unity:** NavMeshLink (OffMeshLink is deprecated in AI Navigation 2.0) plus several physics pitfalls (CCD sweep limits, CharacterController callbacks, raycasts vs triggers, `SyncTransforms`, concave MeshColliders, sleeping bodies).
- **PixiJS:** ticker argument, `globalpointermove` drag, `Texture.from` cache-only, renderer fallback, v8 `ParticleContainer`, teardown with `releaseGlobalResources`.
- **Roblox:** optional Studio MCP section in `roblox-studio-workflow` (manual Studio + Rojo stays the default), UIListLayout flex, Input Action System, new Luau type solver.
- **Unreal:** when to consider StateTree; Behavior Trees are not deprecated.
- **Housekeeping:** version table refreshed (checked 2026-09-25) and skill counts made consistent (73) across the banner alt text, marketplace.json and install docs.

## Testing
- `python scripts/validate-skills.py`: all checks pass.
- three.js changes smoke-tested in Node against the real `three@0.186.0` package (Timer, HDRLoader, loaders, constants).
- PixiJS claims checked against the v8.21.0 source.
- Unity, Unreal and Roblox changes are verified against official docs only; no editor was run.
- `python -m unittest` has one failure locally (`test_repository_markdown_links_are_checked_outside_code_fences`) that also fails on untouched `main` in the same environment, while CI on `main` is green. CI on this PR is the source of truth.

## Not included
- No new skills, no README repositioning, nothing removed.
- PR #16 (Godot headless testing) is separate and still needs a run on real Godot 4.7.2.

author: laurajoyhutchins
body:
## Goal

Make Hyperbolic Time Chamber adversaries exercise realistic competitive behavior rather than letting simplistic or random opponents dominate the curriculum.

## Opponent league

Builds on the opponent league and competence-debt curriculum from #125.

Automatic generations now use:
- max-base-power
- simple-heuristics
- dirty-tricks
- incumbent self-play
- up to three recent archived checkpoints

`RandomPlayer` remains the ordinary local smoke-test baseline but is no longer a training-league member.

Remainder battles rotate across generations, so a small battle budget cannot repeatedly starve later league members.

## Dirty-tricks player

Adds a real poke-env sparring player that prioritizes:
- anti-setup
- priority cleanup
- status
- Taunt / Encore / Disable / Knock Off / Trick-style denial
- trapping and residual chip
- Protect-family stalling under residual pressure
- hazards

When no disruptive line applies it delegates to poke-env's `SimpleHeuristicsPlayer`, preserving normal switching and Tera behavior.

## Teacher opponent realism

The exact-search opponent prior now:
- permits voluntary switching only to a publicly established, surviving, full-health bench Pokemon
- refuses to invent exact HP for a damaged percentage-censored bench
- scores switches from public matchup information rather than arbitrary reconstructed spread details
- may spend Tera when pinned Showdown exposes Tera as legal and the policy has an offensive or defensive reason
- records opponent Tera type as a decision-relevant hidden dependency
- leaves exact turn consequences to pinned Showdown

The strategy mixture itself remains an explicit equal-weight prior. Public replay evidence already enters the self-improvement curriculum directly through #125; this change does not pretend the handcrafted strategy weights are calibrated human frequencies.

## Evidence

All changes are rebased on current main `e5e646f3624d6e1c0dbdd21cfe673f8fc04bde65`, including #127's persistent live Showdown posterior context.

author: philms-org
body:
No migrations. It's safe to merge on its own.

## Problem

`app/globals.css` used Tailwind v3's `@tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities;`, but the project runs Tailwind v4, which ignores them. None of the utility classes the app uses were ever generated, and neither was the base reset (confirmed in the compiled CSS, see #6). Effects:

- Text without an inline `fontFamily` fell back to the browser serif, for example the venue feed rows in #3.
- `<button>`s without an inline `color` used the browser default black. On the dark theme the Profile menu labels ("My Connections", "My Links", …) and the Badges heading measured **1.21:1**.
- `pb-16` never applied on `/main`, so the last ~64px of every tab sat under the fixed tab bar. Profile's Logout button was hidden behind it.
- `.spinner` (History loading states) was never defined, so those loaders showed nothing.

## Fix

Explicit base rules for what the app actually relies on. I didn't turn on v4's full preflight reset, because it would also zero the heading and paragraph margins that the inline-styled screens currently depend on. That's a separate decision.

- `globals.css`:
  - Drop the no-op directives.
  - Put the app font on `html`.
  - Make `button, input, select, textarea` inherit `font-family` and `color`. Inline styles still win.
  - Plain `min-height: 100vh; margin: 0` on `body`.
  - Define `.spinner`, slowed down under reduced motion.
- `/main`: the dead `min-h-screen bg-w-back-gray` / `pb-16` classes become inline styles, and the bottom padding is 64px plus the safe-area inset.
- `layout.tsx` / `global-error.tsx`: dropped the dead classes. `global-error` renders without the root layout, so it gets inline dark-theme styles.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npm run lint` 0 errors · `node scripts/verify-theme-tokens.mjs` OK · `npm run build` passes (placeholder public Supabase env)
- **Before/after audit** with the #6 capture harness: all 15 logged-in screens × dark and light, rendered from the real components against mock data. WCAG contrast was measured from the live DOM.
  - **No screen got worse.**
  - Dark Profile went from 7 failures to 1. The remaining one is the Logout `#D52600`, fixed in the follow-up bugs PR.
  - The dark Home failure is gone.
  - Light-theme counts are unchanged; the muted-grey token is also fixed in the bugs PR.
- Visually checked Profile: menu labels and the Badges heading are readable, and Logout clears the tab bar.

author: bendrucker
body:
The `writing:review` skill's coordinating fork has `context: fork` and `agent: general-purpose` but no `model:`. With `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=opus` set in `user/settings.json`, the fork ran on Opus (or Fable) while the three lens agents it spawns (`content`, `style`, `artifacts`) already ran on Sonnet. Adds `model: sonnet` to the skill frontmatter.

Also switches the lens agents from a `disallowedTools` blocklist to a `tools:` allowlist. Each agent only reads and greps the document; `artifacts` also needs `WebFetch` to check URLs. None edit files or spawn subagents, so inheriting the full tool set added startup token cost with no benefit.

## Evidence

Local usage over the last 30 days: 60 `writing:review` forks ran on Opus across 56 sessions, plus 8 on Fable. Only 3 ran on Sonnet. That's about $166 on Opus/Fable, roughly $2.76 per run; Sonnet rates would put the same runs at roughly $40-70.

## Removal Criteria

Check the session index for `writing:review` forks after this merges: the model family should shift from Opus/Fable to Sonnet, with lower cost per run. Revert if review quality regresses.

author: diogo-santoro
body:
**💡 What:**
Migrates Google Fonts from a render-blocking CSS `@import` to Next.js's highly optimized `next/font/google` module in `src/app/layout.tsx`. Removed outdated CSS variables in `src/styles/globals.css`.

**🎯 Why:**
Loading fonts via `@import` in CSS blocks rendering and slows down First Contentful Paint (FCP). Using `next/font` allows Next.js to self-host the fonts, inject preload tags automatically, and reduce Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) via size-adjust properties. 

**📊 Impact:**
Expected performance improvement for First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Speed Index metrics. Based on local Lighthouse testing, performance score increased significantly (from ~87 to ~97 on a local build).

**🔬 Measurement:**
1. Run `npm run test:lighthouse` to verify performance score improvements.
2. Check Network tab in DevTools: there should be no external requests to `fonts.googleapis.com` or `fonts.gstatic.com`.

author: jakwinkler
body:
In Reflect mode, Trident answers a purge with **HTTP 202**, `status: "deferred"`, `state: "recorded"`. That means the purge is durably queued and gets replayed when reflect ends; a failed write answers 503 `refused` instead (`trident-core/src/server/admin/handlers/reflect.rs`). The module required HTTP 200, so it kept the row and retried it every few minutes. That queued duplicates until the reflect queue was full, and after that genuinely new purges got 503.

Only that exact answer now counts as delivered. 503 `refused`, a 202 without `state: recorded`, and a 200 without the purge schema still don't.
- Unit tests: 23/23.
- The new test fails against the previous code.

This was found by the review of the WooCommerce plugin, which shares the same acknowledgement contract through `qoliber/trident-php` 1.3.0.

author: kaxil
body:
On Airflow 3, importing this package raised `DeprecatedImportWarning` for every class Airflow moved into the Task SDK: `BaseHook`, `BaseSensorOperator`, `Context`, `PokeReturnValue`, `ParamsDict` and `AirflowSkipException`. The old paths still work, but users see the warnings in every DAG that imports a sensor from this package, and the paths will eventually be removed.

The new module `astronomer/providers/utils/compat.py` imports each class from `airflow.sdk` and falls back to the Airflow 2 location. All callers now import from it.

The fallbacks are per name because the Task SDK gained these classes in different releases:

| Name | In `airflow.sdk` since |
| --- | --- |
| `BaseSensorOperator`, `Context`, `PokeReturnValue`, `ParamsDict` | 3.0 |
| `BaseHook` | 3.1 |
| `AirflowSkipException` (`airflow.sdk.exceptions`) | 3.2 |

A single `try: from airflow.sdk import ...` would fail as a whole on 3.0 and 3.1 and put everything back on the deprecated paths.

**Why not `apache-airflow-providers-common-compat`:** it requires Airflow >= 2.11, and this package still supports >= 2.6.

mypy runs against Airflow 2, where `airflow.sdk` doesn't exist and `ignore_missing_imports` would type every name as `Any`. So the module declares the Airflow 2 imports under `TYPE_CHECKING`, and the `try` blocks run only at runtime.

On Airflow 3.3, importing every module in the package raises no deprecation warnings.
