author: dj-thank
body:
## 概要

Mac（開発ホスト）でデスクトップ版を操作しやすくし、Mac のアプリメニューから終了したときに制作データの終了処理が飛ばされる不具合を直します。Windows の操作・挙動は変えていません。

## 問題

- メニューのショートカットが Ctrl 固定で、Mac では ⌘S / ⌘Z / ⌘Q が効かない。
- **main では、Mac のアプリメニュー「終了」や OS からの終了要求で JDK 既定の即時終了になり、`closeApplication`（autosave flush、録音・再生・連携の close）が一度も実行されない。**

## 変更後の動作

- macOS: 開く ⌘O / ⌘⇧O、保存 ⌘S、書き出し ⌘E、取り消し ⌘Z、やり直し ⌘⇧Z、終了 ⌘Q。
- Windows/その他: 従来どおり Ctrl+O / Ctrl+Shift+O / Ctrl+S / Ctrl+E / Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Alt+F4（テストで固定）。
- macOS の終了要求は `Desktop.setQuitHandler` で受け、既定の終了を取り消して既存の `closeApplication` を通す。`APP_QUIT_HANDLER` 非対応の環境（Windows 等）では何もしない。
- macOS では AWT 起動前に `apple.laf.useScreenMenuBar` / `apple.awt.application.name`（ja「おとひろい」/en「Earth Song」）/ `apple.awt.application.appearance=system` を設定。起動時に明示された `-D` の値を優先する。
- PAD キー（1234/QWER/ASDF/ZXCV）は修飾キー付きの押下を従来どおり無視するため、⌘ 付きショートカットと衝突しない。

## 確認結果（revision 7dfc7e4、macOS 27.0 arm64、JDK 21.0.12.1）

- `./gradlew :desktop:test`: 234 件成功、失敗 0（新規 `DesktopPlatformShortcutsTest` 5 件を含む）。
- `./scripts/validate_project.sh`: 294 件成功、skip 1。
- 終了経路の比較: `installDist` の起動スクリプトを隔離した `user.home` と `-verbose:class` で起動し、PID 宛てに `NSRunningApplication.terminate()` を送信。`close()` だけが生成する `AutosaveCloseRequest` の読み込みを確認した。
  - main（3dbbbf0）: 約 1 秒で終了コード 0、読み込み **0 回**（終了処理を通っていない）。
  - このブランチ: 約 1 秒で終了コード 0、読み込み **1 回**（終了処理を通っている）。

## 未確認・範囲外

- 画面収録とアクセシビリティの権限がないため、システムメニューバーへの表示・⌘ ショートカットの押下・ダークモードは目視していない。
- Mac での Java Sound の実音・マイク録音は未確認。
- 範囲外: Mac のデータ保存先（現在は `~/AppData/Local` 配下）、Dock 名（非 bundle 起動では `DesktopAppKt`）、Windows 専用機能（WASAPI・loopback・同梱 FFmpeg）。macOS は ADR6 の配布対象ではない。

## ロールバック

このコミットを revert するだけで戻せます。データ形式・保存先は変更していません。

## 人間による確認（Mac）

1. 起動後、メニューが画面上部のメニューバーに出るか。
2. ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z で取り消し・やり直しができるか。
3. 編集後に ⌘Q で終了し、再起動したときに自動保存から復旧されるか。

---

English summary: macOS-host menu accelerators (⌘-based, ⌘Q, ⌘⇧Z) with unchanged Windows bindings, and the macOS app-menu/OS quit request now runs the owned shutdown instead of the JDK default exit, which skipped the autosave flush on main.

author: whysobad
body:
While working on adding a native FreeBSD job to the CI, I noticed that some of the non-blocking TCP socket tests assert that a non-blocking `connect` must not complete immediately. 
This assertion is not guaranteed to hold when executing natively (once rust-lang/miri#5308 is merged, it's also no longer guaranteed to hold for Miri executions). Thus, those tests now assert that a non-blocking `connect` either succeeds immediately or "fails" with an EINPROGRESS. 

Sadly https://github.com/rust-lang/libs-team/issues/212 decided against `Result::is_ok_or` so we now have this less readable assertion.

author: claudechen95
body:
Follow-up to #275. The branch-naming line was ambiguous in a way that nearly caused a real bug.

## What happened

#275 was pushed on `jaipal/test-stability-and-prompt-cache` by a session authenticated as `claudechen95`, with commits authored by `yunc1995@gmail.com`. Asked why the branch carried someone else's name, the obvious answer looked like "use your own username" — and that would have been wrong.

## Why it would have been wrong

`jaipal/` is not a convention. Five executable places match on that exact literal:

| where | what it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/lib/claims.mjs:150` | `isTicketBranch` = `^jaipal/<ticket>-.+$` — **how a session claims a ticket** |
| `scripts/lib/run-report.mjs:131` | same regex over `refs/heads` and `refs/remotes/origin` |
| `scripts/lib/reconcile-status.mjs` | a matching branch is what moves a ticket to In Progress |
| `.claude/commands/work-ticket.md:24` | `branchExists` greps `*jaipal/tac-xxx-*` |
| `Bash(git checkout jaipal/:*)` | the permission rule |

The first is load-bearing. A branch under a different prefix does not register as a claim, so a build run would start a ticket a local session already has — precisely the 2026-09-17 TAC-396 incident CLAUDE.md already records under "Two sessions must never work one ticket".

Secondary effects: the ticket never moves to In Progress, and `branchExists` misses the branch so a session creates a second one for the same ticket.

## What this changes

Documentation only. The line now says the prefix is a protocol token, lists the five matchers, and explains the failure mode.

**Deliberately not fixed here.** The right answer is to generalise the matchers to `^[\w.-]+/<ticket>-` so the prefix becomes a genuine personal namespace — but that has to land in all five places at once. Changing one breaks the thing the others protect. Worth its own ticket.

## Verification

`tsc` clean, `eslint` clean, `scripts/lib` suite 609/609. No behaviour change.

author: enumeratio
body:
The Plausible contract (design/plausible.md §3, §6): each family declares what it is, so the sampler can derive everything from the declaration.

- **`@enumeratio/plausible`**, a new leaf package: seeded mulberry32 streams per key, bigint draws, edge-biased integers and the size ramp. collections' properties import it; bench and the oracle sampler can follow.
- **`FamilyKernel.declared`**: carrier, params (axis or param, with a minimum), the cost of each operation, and a `work` bound wherever it enumerates. The enumerating helpers supply the bound themselves: `indexedFamily` its count, the permutation-class filters n!, necklaces and bracelets base^size. "count ≤ budget" alone isn't safe (Baxter(10) filters 3.6M permutations to find 326k).
- **Declared now**: every family the old runner's lists named, the enumerative ones those lists missed, and the numeric-sets spike. PlanePartitions counts by MacMahon's recurrence instead of enumerating.
- **`scripts/sampleable.ts`** derives each family's instance: the address `(params, rank)` is the proxy, `unrank` the interpretation, shrinking generic.
- **Guards**: `plausible-contract.test.ts` checks each declared family and ratchets the undeclared ones (`plausible-undeclared.json`, which only shrinks; a new family must declare). A census test walks the engine, so every declared collection is a family or exempt with a reason, and a declared carrier matches the catalogue's.

author: pachaninm-lab
body:
## Что сделано

Найдено при оценке ASVS V3.7.2. Три маршрута демо-входа — `/api/auth/demo`, `/api/auth/demo/role/[role]`, `/api/auth/demo/instant/[role]` — принимали параметр `to` и проверяли его через `raw.startsWith('/')`. Значения `//evil.example` и `/\evil.example` начинаются с одного слэша, но по алгоритму WHATWG URL, который реализует любой браузер, разрешаются в **чужой origin**.

**Production не затронут:** `demoLoginAllowed()` безусловно проверяет `NODE_ENV` первой, и флаг это не отменяет. Дефект реальный в тестовых контурах, где демо-вход включён явно, и именно такой шаблон проверки копируется в следующий маршрут.

**Исправление:**
- `resolveSameOriginRedirectTarget()` проверяет **разрешённый** origin, а не префикс строки;
- у `instant` адрес уходит не в `Location`, а во встроенный скрипт `window.location.replace()`, поэтому нужны ещё два шага:
  - `toPathAbsoluteReference()`: после удаления dot-сегментов `/.//evil.example` даёт pathname `//evil.example`, и в относительной ссылке это снова protocol-relative адрес — такое отклоняется;
  - кодирование строкой JavaScript вместо HTML-сущностей. Внутри `<script>` сущности не раскодируются, и каждый `&` в query приходил в браузер как `&`; теперь адрес доходит целым и не может закрыть элемент скрипта.

## Тип прохода
- [ ] E01 data layer
- [ ] QA / smoke
- [ ] UI / дизайн
- [ ] Bank / money
- [ ] Docs / ops
- [ ] Hosting / deploy

Проход: security, ASVS V3.7.2 / V1.5.3 (#4459).

## Риск
- [ ] Низкий: 1–3 файла, поведение не менялось
- [x] Средний: затронута runtime-логика — только в маршрутах демо-входа, выключенных в production
- [ ] Высокий: деньги, банк, споры, доступы, навигация

## Проверка
- [x] Read before write выполнен
- [x] UI не деградировал — UI не затронут
- [x] Деньги/статусы не разъехались — не затронуты
- [ ] Mobile 375px — экран не затронут
- [ ] web/API/API-ovdc success — ждёт CI на этом head

Локально на head `6b580a2b2c451aef57fdff5535dbee7407132167`:
- тесты хелперов и всех трёх маршрутов: `Location` и сам сгенерированный литерал вместе с тем, куда он реально ведёт; `/.//evil.example`; сохранение `&` в query; невозможность закрыть `<script>`; отказ в production;
- мутации: вернуть проверку префиксом — падают тесты каждого маршрута; убрать защиту `//` — падают 3; вернуть HTML-экранированный литерал — падают 7;
- CI web-unit: 25 файлов, 668 тестов — все зелёные; `tsc` web — 0;
- `node --test scripts/security/*.test.mjs` — 144/144; `p7-autopilot-guard` с `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` — PASS; `check-production-hosting-authority` — PASS.

## Hosting (REG.RU)
- [x] Изменения идут через main
- [x] `процент-агро.рф` на виртуальном сервере REG.RU — единственный production-host (Netlify и Vercel выведены из эксплуатации)
- [x] Merge, зелёный CI или опубликованный GHCR-образ не считаются доказательством, что production изменился
- [ ] Если менялся hosting/config — не менялся
- [x] Если менялся product/UI — deploy-поведение не менялось скрыто

**Virtual-server deployment state: not required** для production-поведения: маршруты там выключены. Не развёрнуто.

## Что нельзя было трогать
- `demoLoginAllowed()` и его fail-closed поведение в production — не тронуты.
- UI, адаптеры, AI gateway, БД/миграции, lockfile — не тронуты.

## Scope, файлы, ограничения
- **Scope:** `docs/platform-v7/autopilot/scopes/open-redirect-demo-login-4459.json`. Написан мной, **требует ратификации владельцем**.
- **Changed files (9):** `lib/server-request-security.ts`, три маршрута, два теста, `ci.yml`, реестр покрытия (`serverRequestSecurity.test.ts` перенесён из исключений в CI), манифест.
- **Known limitations:** CSRF-токен в `instant` по-прежнему берётся из `Math.random`, а cookie ставятся из скрипта без `HttpOnly`. Это только демо; не менялось, чтобы не расширять шаг.

## Следующий безопасный шаг
1. Независимое ревью **этого exact head**. Автор реализации ревьюером быть не может. **Не выполнено.**
2. Self-audit владельца на exact head. **Не выполнено.**
3. Ручной merge с полным SHA.

author: akvasha
body:
> **Draft, and red on purpose. This PR cannot merge in this state and is not asking to.** It lands #384's two harness changes and the seven comment repairs they force, and it exists so the 25 failures are produced by CI rather than asserted by me. **Stage 2 has since begun inside this same diff** — commits 6 to 11 adjudicate the first three files and take the tip to 15 reds. An earlier revision of this line said the adjudication "is not in this diff"; that was true when it was written and stopped being true at commit 6, and a branch whose whole subject is prose falsified by its own changes should not leave its own summary in that state.

## What this is

#384's plan splits the harness work into two independent changes to `test/helpers/syncplay-min-election-server.ts`:

- **Half B** — the reference server sends a join-time `State`, because upstream does: `Watcher.__init__` schedules one through `reactor.callLater(0.1, …)` (`server.py:737`), the `LoopingCall` it starts fires its first tick immediately (`server.py:841-843`), and the *other* immediate tick — the one `setRoom`'s `_resetStateTimer` forces — is swallowed by `sendState`'s `isLogged()` guard (`server.py:858-860`), so the reference emits exactly one. Delivered through the existing `sendState` helper so the frame pays the link delay like every other `State` rather than arriving instantly; that detail is the difference between modelling upstream and modelling a faster-than-light server.

  ⚠️ **It went in the `Hello` branch, not in `seat()`, and #384's terminology line says `seat()`.** Stating the deviation rather than quietly taking the better placement: `seat()` has **no call site inside the helper** — the `Hello` branch reaches its watcher through `this.watchers.get(username)`, on a watcher the *test* seated before the client ever connected. So a `State` emitted from `seat()` would fire at fixture-setup time, before any handshake, which is neither join time from the client's view nor a model of a `callLater` scheduled by `__init__` *after* login. The `Hello` reply is the login, so that is where the frame belongs. #384's body wants its terminology line corrected; I have not edited it in this PR, because the correction is worth reviewing on its own rather than arriving inside a diff.
- **Half A** — `w.lastUpdatedOn = Date.now()` moves **above** `if (!ps) return` in `applyState`, so a state frame carrying no playstate still stamps the watcher. Upstream stamps unconditionally at `server.py:877` inside `updateState` (`:875`).

Each half is its own commit so either can be reverted alone. Then **three** commits repairing **seven** comments these halves make false — see below. That is not optional tidying: it is the branch falsifying its own prose, and leaving it would ship exactly the defect class #395 and #407 exist to record. Commits 6 to 10 begin stage 2, adjudicating the first three files: the sixth clears `two-peer-ignore-counters`' two reds, the seventh `two-peer-episode-change`' four, the eighth pays off a disclaimer the seventh deliberately left standing, the ninth clears `two-peer-adoption`' four, and the tenth and eleventh correct, in turn, a sentence the ninth got wrong about its own repair and a sentence the tenth got wrong about the fix it guards.

## The failures are the point, not a regression

The two halves alone red **25 failed / 1834 passed across 10 files** (main is 123 files / 1859 green). Every failure is a two-peer expectation written against a reference server that did *not* send a join-time `State` and did *not* stamp unconditionally. Deciding which encode real behaviour and which encode the old harness is stage 2, one file at a time; **commits 6, 7 and 9 do the first three files, so the tip now reds 15 failed / 1844 passed across 7 files.**

The red count also does not match #384's own C1/C2 table (14 failed / 1822 passed / 6 files). That table was measured before **#404** seeded a playing `MinElectionServer` room with a setter; with the seed in, the same two halves red 25 across 10 files. The table is not wrong, it is stale, and the tip is the number that counts.

Two further measurements worth having on the record, because both correct something written down earlier. Both were taken on commits 1 and 2, before commit 6 adjudicated this file, so the line numbers they quote are that tip's, not the current one's:

- **`test/services/syncplay-two-peer-ignore-counters.test.ts:266` red as the C3 shape, not the shape I predicted on #384.** Measured: `expected [ 1500, 2500, 3500, 4500, 5500, 6500 ] to deeply equal [ 2500, 3500, 4500, 5500, 6500, 7500 ]` — and the expected side was `:266` verbatim at that tip. My earlier figure predated #404's setter seed; with the seed in, commit 1 is "Half B and the pairing fix without Half A", which is exactly the configuration round 13 says yields C3's reds.
- **#384's own prediction for Half A does not reproduce.** The issue body says Half A clears `:266` so execution reaches `:278`. Measured at commit 1 and again at commit 2: `:266` still reds with the same diff, and the two censuses are byte-identical apart from `Start at` and `Duration`. Recorded rather than accommodated — the prediction is wrong, not the measurement.

## Commit 6 — stage 2's first file, and why one of its two reds needed the scenario changed

Both reds in `test/services/syncplay-two-peer-ignore-counters.test.ts` are caused by **Half B alone** — Half A is inert in this file, measured at both helper snapshots — and neither is a production defect. The mechanism in both is the one stage 2 expects: the join-time frame moves the host's mirror anchor a second earlier, which moves the `min()` position election.

- **`abandons our window when a peer-initiated forced update crosses it`** was an expectation that encoded the old harness, and is renumbered 1 → 2. The periodic broadcast at t=4000 now arrives at 4050, one slice *before* the press is classified, so the window is not open and the frame is foreign: the t=4000 election moved from us (winning by 49 ms) to the joiner (winning by 951 ms). It moves nothing — `|102.049 − 103.95| < 3` — so `seekWrites` is untouched.
- **`drops the foreign periodics that land while our change is unacked`** needed its **scenario** changed, not its numbers, and this is the part worth reviewing. Under a join-time `State` the host becomes the room's laggard from t=6000, so the old press at t=8000 puts all three in-window periodics in a stretch where they are self-`setBy` and die at `src/main/syncplay.ts:2097` — *before* the ack guard at `:2098` is reached. The press moves to t=4000, putting the window over the broadcasts at 3000, 4000 and 5000, all still the joiner's.

**Why that is not a stylistic preference.** A naive renumber — expectation updated to `[1500, 2500, 3500, 4500, 5500, 6500]`, `advance(8)` kept — was built as a counterfactual and measured: it passes clean **and passes with the ack guard deleted** (`if (!localChangeAcked) {` → `if (false) {`, applied in memory, never to a repo file). Renumbering alone would therefore have retired this file's only coverage of `:2098` while looking green. author: arcanada
body:
## A2-383 — the Datarim import is on the audit record

### What
`POST /sync/datarim/:projectId/import` now writes one route-level `activity_log` row per import that reaches the write phase:

- `action: sync:datarim_imported`, `actor_type`/`actor_id` = the key's agent, `workspace_id` of the project, `task_id: null`;
- payload: `projectId`, `outcome` (`completed` | `failed`), `created[]` (`taskId`, `title`, `status`), `updated[]` (`taskId` plus `{from, to}` for each of `status`, `priority` and `dueDate` that changed), `unchanged` count, and `error` when `failed`.

It is written through `ActivityService.log`, the same form `migration.transition` uses. No new schema and no migration.

### Why
After #194 every import write goes through `TasksService`, so the per-task rows (`task:created`, `task:status_changed`, `task:updated`) exist. They look identical whichever route caused them, though. From the log alone it was still impossible to answer "was the import used, by whom, and on which project". This row answers that. `task:updated` carries only new values; this row also records the old ones.

The writes are one `TasksService` call each, not one transaction. If a write fails part-way, the row is still written with `outcome: failed`, listing exactly what was applied before the failure, and the original error is rethrown. A refused import (404/403/409/400, all decided before the first write) writes no row, which is unchanged behaviour.

The title-match ambiguity (`findFirst` without `orderBy`) was already closed by #194: `findMany take 2` returns 409 `AMBIGUOUS_TITLE`. No change was needed here.

### Tests
- `test/sync-import-scope.e2e.spec.ts` (real HTTP and Postgres): an import that creates one task, moves one and leaves one unchanged produces exactly one row, and the test checks the row's **full content** with `toEqual` (actor, project, ids, old → new). A refused import (403 in-workspace, 404 foreign) produces no row.
- `test/sync.service.spec.ts`: completed payload, failed-midway payload, and no row on refusal.
- Red control: each of the following mutants turns tests red:
  - dropping the audit write on success: 2 red (unit and e2e);
  - recording the new status as `from`: 2 red;
  - dropping the audit write on failure: 1 red.
- Full `pnpm test` on a local PG16 passed apart from `mutation-evidence`, which was red before the rebind as expected and passes 30/30 after it.

### Rule 12 (re-issued by A2-387 after merging main)
`main` moved (#195, A2-382), so the branch now carries a merge commit `5eec076` instead of a rebase (the PR was open and being read). The only conflict was `apps/api/test/assembly/mutation-results.json`. Both sides were rebinds on different bases, so neither was taken. It was recomputed with the harness's own `gitSupplement()`/`buildBinding()`. The new `trackedTreeWithoutEvidence` differs from both sides, and a second rebind reports `changed: false`. The pre-merge canary and receipt of A2-383 were removed, because their range no longer applies.

- Commit order: merge+rebind `5eec076`, then canary `7a8aa11`, then receipt `b7b878b`.
- Canary `receipts/canary/A2-387-sync-import-audit-candidate-5eec076.json`, run on the local candidate `5eec076`: 76 verified / 2 not_measured / 0 failed.
- `receipts/graph/A2-387-sync-import-audit.json`: `verify.py`, graph at the new base `99938af`, range `..7a8aa11`. Result: **13 verified, ADMITTED**, with 30 structural exclusions.
- `admit_change.py gate 99938af..b7b878b` returned ADMIT. Red control in a separate detached worktree at `7a8aa11` returned REFUSE `RECEIPT_MISSING`, rc 5.
- Local PG16 on the merged head: `sync*` + `outbox*` 208/208 (8 suites), `mutation-evidence` 30/30.

body:
Spec nueva: `06-analisis-financiero/sistema-multisuperficie` (hallazgo H-D5 de la prueba en producción de la fase A2).

## Problema
- Financiero exigía 📊 Producción, que simula el sistema de superficie única. En la prueba D5 ignoró sin avisar los 7.552 kWh/año publicados desde Vista 3D y pasó a modo manual con 5.695 kWh/año.
- Aun con Producción, Financiero mezclaba dos sistemas: la energía venía de Vista 3D, pero los kWp y los módulos, de superficie única (8,06 kWp y 128 módulos, en lugar de 6,37 kWp y 34 módulos). Con eso, el CAPEX, el TIR y el payback correspondían a otro sistema.

## Cambios
- **Publicación:** nueva clave `multisup_sistema`, calculada con el mismo diseño y en el mismo momento que la energía:
  - potencia DC: Σ módulos × Pmax del panel de cada superficie;
  - módulos y potencia por referencia de panel;
  - reparto mensual de la energía según la POA de cada superficie;
  - `completo`: si todas las superficies tienen grupos de strings.
  
  Se publica en los tres orígenes (simplificado, bypass y físico) y se guarda con el proyecto.
- **💰 Financiero:**
  - Con el modo multi-superficie activo ya no exige 📊 Producción. Toma la energía, los kWp y los módulos de Vista 3D.
  - Pide un costo por cada referencia de panel.
  - Si falta algún grupo o la publicación es anterior a este cambio, muestra 🔴 y no calcula.
  - El Presupuesto (superficie única) queda desvinculado por defecto, con un aviso 🟡.
- **🔋 Baterías:** balance mensual con el reparto mensual publicado. El balance horario queda deshabilitado, con aviso.
- **🌿 CO₂:** muestra los kWp y módulos del sistema multi-superficie.
- **💼 Presupuesto:** avisa que todavía usa el sistema de superficie única. El Presupuesto por superficie (H3) queda para su propia Spec.
- **Aviso fijo de energía retirada** (pedido en la prueba D6): si un cambio de panel o de diseño eléctrico retira la energía publicada, el motivo y las superficies afectadas quedan visibles en «🔗 Integrar al análisis financiero» hasta volver a publicar. Desactivar a mano no deja el aviso.
- Actualizados la persistencia, la invalidación, el Asistente, los contratos del director y el registro de decisiones.

## Validación
- Las pruebas nuevas fallan contra `main` y pasan con este cambio.
- Suite completa: `1755 passed`.
- `physics-guard` limpio y auditoría SDD sin faltantes.
- Prueba de humo con AppTest:
  - **Escenario D5 sin Producción:** Financiero muestra 6.37 kWp (34 módulos) y un costo por panel. Baterías y CO₂ usan el sistema publicado. Con un sistema incompleto sale 🔴 y no se calcula.
  - **D6:** el aviso de energía retirada sigue visible tras un rerun y desaparece al volver a publicar.

author: kaxil
body:
`ExternalDeploymentSensor` and `AstroHook` only worked against Airflow 2 deployments. The hook hard-coded `/api/v1`, which Airflow 3 removed, and it ordered runs by `execution_date`, which Airflow 3 renamed.

The hook now asks the target deployment which API it serves, with an unauthenticated `GET /api/v2/version`. A 404 means Airflow 2, and the hook uses `/api/v1`. Any other error is raised. The result is cached on the hook instance.

On `/api/v2`, `get_dag_runs` orders by `-run_after` rather than `-logical_date`. Manually triggered and asset-triggered runs on Airflow 3 can have a null logical date, but every run has `run_after`.

With no host on the connection, the base URL now comes from `AIRFLOW__API__BASE_URL` (Airflow 3) before `AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__BASE_URL`.

I checked every sync and async method against `apache/airflow:2.11.2` and `apache/airflow:3.3.2` running `airflow standalone`, from clients on both versions. The runs included a run ID with `+` and `:`, and an Airflow 3 run with a null `logical_date`.

## Design rationale

**Why probe instead of adding a connection field for the API version:** the version is a property of the target deployment. A user who upgrades that deployment shouldn't also have to edit every connection that points at it. The connection form also hides `extra` for this hook. The probe is a single unauthenticated GET, and it only runs once per hook instance.

**Cost of the probe:** it runs once per hook instance. `ExternalDeploymentSensor` pokes once in `execute()` and then defers, and the trigger reuses one hook across its polling loop. So a deployment sees one extra unauthenticated GET per task try and one per trigger start. Caching the version across hooks would need a module-level cache keyed by URL, and that goes stale when the target deployment is upgraded. Each public method also resolves the connection once, so a secrets backend sees one lookup per call. Before this change it saw two.

## Gotchas

The example DAG `example_external_deployment_task_sensor.py` and the integration scripts still call `/api/v1` through `HttpSensor`. They target the Airflow 2 integration deployment, so I left them alone.

author: softjey
body:
## Problem

On Node < 20 (e.g. Node 18 from `apt` on Ubuntu 24.04 / Debian 12) every CLI command, including `install-hooks`, crashed before any of our code ran:

```
node_modules/string-width/index.js:19
const zeroWidthClusterRegex = /^(?:\p{Default_Ignorable_Code_Point}|...)+$/v;
SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression flags
```

`ink` pulls in `string-width@8`, whose module-level regexes use the `v` flag (Node 20+). `engines` is only a warning in npm and npx ignores it, so users got a stack trace into `node_modules` instead of a reason.

## Fix

`src/cli/bin.ts` checks the running Node against `engines.node` from `package.json` before importing the CLI (now a dynamic `import()`), and exits with:

```
claude-profiler needs Node.js >=22, but this is Node.js 18.20.8.
Upgrade Node (e.g. `nvm install 22`, or see https://nodejs.org/en/download) and run it again.
```

The hook script and the live collector don't load `ink` and are unaffected.

Also bumps the version to 0.1.3 for release.

## Verified

- `pnpm verify` passes
- `npx node@18 dist/cli/bin.js` prints the message above, exit code 1
- Node 22+ behaviour unchanged

author: mmmries
body:
## Summary

The generative suite's backup-and-restore action from #236, cold-copy variant. The cluster is backed up with a file-level copy of the stopped server right after op *k*, the program runs to *n*, the backup is restored into a fresh cluster, and ops *k+1..n* replay against the restored database. The restore must converge and must never pause a transform.

This checks the assumption behind the 2026-09-24 decision on #236 ("no restore-specific handling"). Trellis keeps its catalog, staging ring, `replication_progress` and targets in the database it reads. A restore therefore rolls all of them back to one point, and a cold copy also brings the slot back where the restored progress row expects it.

The `pg_basebackup` variant is held for #558. That restore has no slot, so it goes through the #310 pause, then a resume, then a fresh backfill. `BackupKind` has a `TODO(#558)` where that variant goes, and the runner marks the point where its pause/resume check would replace the no-pause check.

## What changed

- **testkit:** added `TestCluster::cold_backup()`. It stops the server with a fast shutdown, copies the data directory (`cp -Rp`) into a `ClusterBackup` temp dir, then restarts the server. Also added `TestCluster::from_backup(&ClusterBackup)`, which starts an independent cluster on a copy with no `initdb` and no migrations, and `TestCluster::database_dsn(name)`. `restart` now shares a `while_stopped` helper with `cold_backup`. The backup dir uses the `trellis-testkit-<pid>-<n>` naming, so the orphan reaper removes it if the test process is killed. `Drop` deletes it.
- **generative backend:** added a `BackupRestore` trait, implemented for `TestCluster`, so `run` still names no cluster type. Added `ManualBackend::connect_to_restore(dsn)`, which builds a backend over the restored database and starts an equivalent engine client with the same slot and publication names and client options. It does **not** re-run `install`.
- **model/generate:** added `RestorePlan { backup_op, kind: BackupKind::ColdCopy }` and `restore_plan_for(program)`.
- **run:** added `run_convergence_with_restore`. It installs the program, then runs each op with the usual per-op check, taking the backup right after op *k* is applied and before the quiesce, so that op's change is usually still in flight. After op *n* it stops the original engine, restores, and drops the backup copy. It then checks the restore at *k* in this order:
  1. No transform is paused (`RunError::PausedAfterRestore`).
  2. The restored source tables equal the original's after *k* (`RunError::RestoreDiffers`). This is the "cloned oracle": the SQL oracle recomputes from the source, which the backup carries.
  3. The targets converge to the oracle.

  It then replays *k+1..n*, running the no-pause check and the convergence check after each op.
- **tests:** added `generative/tests/backup_restore.rs`, with one `#[ignore]`d property and three hand-built pins (backups at the first, a middle and the last op). Every run in that file takes a file-level gate, one at a time. A restore starts a second cluster while the first is still up, and testkit caps a process at four live clusters. Without the gate, `-- --include-ignored` left the three pins and the property each holding one cluster and blocked forever waiting for another. Added a testkit harness test showing that a cold backup restores data and slots as of the backup, independently of the original, and that both temp dirs are removed on drop.
- **docs:** `generative-test-suite.md` §7 item 5 now lists the built action, and §8 records the decision. The intake failure-mode table has a new row for a cold-copy restore, and the "restored from a backup" row now reads "a backup that carries no slot". `transforms.md`'s note on automatic pauses says the same.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p testkit --test harness`: 6 passed, including the new `a_cold_backup_restores_data_and_slots_as_of_the_backup`.
- `cargo test -p generative --test backup_restore`: 3 pins passed.
- `cargo test -p generative --lib restore`: 3 unit tests for the no-pause check (pass, the empty-list panic, and a control).
- Control experiment, not committed: I dropped the slot on the restored database before starting the engine. The mid-program pin then failed with `PausedAfterRestore { op_index: 3, paused: [("t1", "paused"), ("t2", "paused")] }`, which shows the no-pause assertion bites. Before the pause check was moved ahead of the oracle comparison, the same experiment showed up only as an unexplained divergence.
- `PROPTEST_CASES=40 cargo test -p generative --test backup_restore property_ -- --ignored`: 1 passed (40 cases, 403s). No divergence found.
- Review mutation checks, not committed:
  - Taking the backup just *before* op *k* while the plan still says *k* makes all three pins fail with `RestoreDiffers` at *k*. A restore that silently loses a committed op is caught.
  - Probing the restored targets against the oracle before the first quiesce shows them diverged in all three pins. Op *k* really is in flight in the backup, so the restored engine has to finish it.
- Source-table equality at *k* is exact, not approximate. Op *k* commits before the backup's fast shutdown, the next op isn't applied until the server is back, and the engine never writes source tables. The comparison snapshot is taken after the original's quiesce, but only engine-owned tables change in that window.
- `cargo test -p generative --test backup_restore -- --include-ignored` (with `PROPTEST_CASES=3`): hung past 150s before the gate, and passed in 52s after it. `PROPTEST_CASES=15 ... property_ -- --ignored`: passed.
- An interrupted run's leftover `trellis-testkit-*` dirs, a data-only backup dir among them, were removed by the next run's orphan reaper.
- `verify` (review, on eb239ac over upstream/main c055ff9): `passed=1812 failed=0 ignored=16`, `VERIFIED: tree b49f5260bc green`.

## Limitation

Each property case copies the whole shared cluster twice: once for the backup and once for the restored cluster. That includes all of `pg_wal`. A deep run's peak disk use is therefore about three times the cluster's size, which matters on the nightly's tmpfs quota (#526/#527) if this property is ever added there.

Refs #236 (stays open for the `pg_basebackup` variant, held for #558).

body:
`auth._store_path()` resolves an unset `STRANDS_DASH_AUTH_STORE` to
`~/.strands_dashboard/auth.json` - the passkey records and the `jwt_secret`. Every
reader goes through `_load`, which **writes**: with no store it creates one; with an
unparseable one it renames the operator's file aside and writes a fresh secret, killing
every live session token. Sixteen modules redirected it in a fixture of their own, no
two agreeing on the rest of the family.

One fixture in `tests/conftest.py` points the store at `tmp_path/auth.json` - the path
all sixteen chose, so their helpers are unchanged - and unsets the family in one sweep.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `isolated_store` fixtures | 16 | 1 (the session's) |
| `tests/` LOC | 581,506 | 581,473 |
| `dashboard/auth.py` under `-k dashboard` | 525 stmts, 8 missed, 98% | identical, same lines |
| `-k dashboard` | 1,265 passed | 1,270 passed |

The new pin declares no fixture; its last cell re-runs a sibling in a child session
carrying `RP_ID`. **5/5 red** without the fixture. Gate: ruff, mypy,
`check_whole_tree_graders.py` 6,577 passed. #3818 0.8-0.9.

---

### Round 1

The required check on `cfc92799` was red: `11566 passed, 1 error`, the error a
teardown `TypeError: vars() argument must have __dict__ attribute` on
`tests/test_robot_factory.py::TestRunDeviceConnectAsciiOutput::test_a_failed_bring_ups_report_is_ascii_too`.
Moving the redirect into the session reordered fixture teardown onto a latent crash in
the shared Device Connect restore (`tests/_device_connect_real.py::_agree`): a name a
test blocks by registering `None` in `sys.modules` was read as a module. `main` is
green because nothing there reaches that ordering.

`eb04c400` - one concern, one commit: `_agree` skips a `None` entry (a blocked name
holds no attributes, the same reading `restore` already makes), and
`tests/test_device_connect_stand_in_is_not_handed_back.py` gains one cell that blocks
an import under the probe prefix and runs the restore - red on `cfc92799`, green here.
The fragment records the second half. `+38` lines, no production code touched.

The push dismissed the prior approval; the diff the approval covered is unchanged
beyond those three files.

author: marcospaulo
body:
Train engine-8: five green PRs merged with `--no-ff` into one sha for CI's gate. Main fast-forwards to the train's last sha once CI is green on it.

- #60 `perf(speculative)`: `--spec-draft-mtp-swa N` gives the MTP draft head a sliding attention window. It is off by default: `0` is the whole context, as before.
- #61 `perf(kv-cache)`: a cache without a sliding window keeps no partial state, so context checkpoints stop copying the MTP draft's whole KV. Off switch: `LLAMA_KV_PARTIAL_STATE_LEGACY=1`.
- #63 `perf(cuda)`: flash attention's mma kernel reads only the KV steps a Q tile sees. Its stream-k blocks split only those steps, and the fixup runs one block per output tile. Off switch: `GGML_CUDA_FATTN_LIVE_TILES_LEGACY=1`.
- #65 `perf(kv-cache)`: the KQ mask takes a group of 64 cells before the batch whole from the sequence's bits, instead of scanning every cell's position and sequence set on the host. Off switch: `LLAMA_KQ_MASK_SEQ_BITS_LEGACY=1`.
- #66 `perf(server)`: the drafters read the slot's own token list, not a copy made every round. Off switch: `LLAMA_SPEC_PROMPT_COPY_LEGACY=1`.

The TORAD.md rows for the five, and #58's served number at 245,760 tokens, are the train's docs commit, `7621029c0`. Main was fast-forwarded to it.

## Measured (one slot at 245,760 tokens unless marked)

- #60: no net gain with this head, so rig keeps it off. Rounds are 11.8-14.9 % faster, but acceptance drops 0.60 -> 0.47-0.52 and decode moves -1.7 to +3.8 % (Q4_0-head pack, -np 4, one conversation).
- #61: a checkpoint holds 43.9 MiB against main's 318.0, created in 11-13 ms and restored in 5.9-7.0 ms. At one slot against `main`, with the train's other changes, a resumed question's first token 1,546.0 -> 781.2 ms (-764.8 ms, 95 % CI -771.7 to -757.9).
- #63: -0.84 % a round at one slot, where every tile is live; +18.50 % a round with four slots taking turns; perplexity 6.9811 against 6.9842. Engine-9's `1959364de` takes back about half of the one-slot cost.
- #65: +21.8 % with MTP, +6.46 % without.
- #66: +1.12 %; text, drafts and acceptance identical 4/4.
- Whole train against main, rig's one-slot argv, fresh server per leg: **+25.3 % a round.** 7616f8272 against 3fe9adde4, RTX 5080, rig's `slots = 1` argv at `-c 262144`, MTP n_max 3 with the draft vocabulary, the cold 245,755-token prefill, then 23 questions resumed from checkpoints, 512 greedy tokens each, legs B C C B:
  - a round 26.929 -> 21.494 ms (+25.29 %, 95 % CI +24.99 to +25.59);
  - decode 101.25 -> 126.40 tok/s (+24.85 %, CI +20.96 to +28.86);
  - resumed first token 1,546.0 -> 781.2 ms;
  - acceptance 0.5696 -> 0.5684 (CI -0.0322 to +0.0293);
  - the cold prefill 205.3 -> 198.9 s;
  - each engine's two legs identical in text, drafts and acceptance 24/24.
  The host was shared (load 25): main's legs differ by 8 % (105.44 and 97.05 tok/s) and engine-8's by 0.12 %, so main's host work per step carries part of the gap.

## Checked on this sha

The fork's CI runs actionlint, gitleaks, a supplementary scan, the title check and zizmor. It builds nothing and runs no tests, so the tests ran on a rented RTX 5070 Ti at 7616f8272:
- `test-kv-mask`: 8,560 masks, 0 failures.
- `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` from 2,048 cells: 248/248.
- Three MTP chat requests: text, drafts and acceptance identical 3/3/3.
- Perplexity at 16,384 tokens (wikitext-2 test, 4 chunks): 6.9811 with #63's list, 6.9842 without, 8.1078 with a broken pre-pass (the check can fail).

author: jotarodriguezv
body:
## Summary
- Al revisar el bug de las paletas, el usuario notó que en la pantalla de TV los logos salen con un recuadro alrededor en vez de transparentes. Comprobado con datos reales (solo lectura): el logo de Skipper tiene sus 4096 píxeles muestreados en alfa 255 — el archivo nunca tuvo canal alfa que perder, probablemente porque se exportó desde una herramienta (como Canva gratis) que no ofrece fondo transparente real.
- `quitarFondoDelLogo` reconoce un color de fondo sólido mirando el borde entero de la imagen (no solo las esquinas) y lo quita con un relleno por inundación desde los bordes hacia dentro, deteniéndose en cualquier color distinto — así no se come el mismo color si aparece suelto dentro del dibujo (el blanco dentro de una "O"). El alfa de cada píxel se gradúa según su distancia de color al fondo, para que el borde antialiasado quede suave.
- Si el borde no tiene un color claramente mayoritario (foto, degradado, logo que llega a las cuatro esquinas) o si el logo ya trae transparencia real, no se toca nada: mejor dejarlo como está que arriesgarse a comerse parte del dibujo.
- Se aplica solo al subir el logo (`handleLogoUpload`), junto con `conservarTransparencia`. El texto de la zona de subida ahora recomienda subir el logo con fondo transparente, porque esto es una heurística de mejor esfuerzo, no un sustituto.

## Verificación
- Probado contra los 5 logos reales de restaurantes que no tienen transparencia hoy (leídos de producción, sin escribir nada): el fondo se quita limpio en los 5, incluida una tarjeta redondeada de diseño (Ojo Cerrado) que queda intacta.
- El único restaurante que ya tiene transparencia real (Lobster Boat) se deja sin tocar, como debe ser.
- `npm test`: 1479/1479 en verde, con 5 pruebas nuevas para `quitarFondoDelLogo` (fondo conectado al borde, color suelto dentro del dibujo que no se toca, transparencia real que se respeta, borde sin color mayoritario que no se arriesga, y el suavizado del borde antialiasado).

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test`
- [x] Verificado visualmente en el navegador contra los logos reales de producción (lectura, sin subir nada)

author: vishutdhar
body:
A trial redesign. If it isn't wanted, close this PR and `main` stays on `97e59ea`.

## Why
The first commit on this branch (`26dbdcf`) looked generated. It had a dark ground with a terracotta accent, a stat strip, numbered section labels, cards, gradient washes and fade-ins on every section. The later commits replace it with a design built from the subject itself. Vishut's work is taking a process that is out of control and bringing it back into control, so the page opens with that result.

## What changed
- **The one bold element is a staged scrap-rate chart** for GM Spring Hill, on a real 0–6% axis:
  - a red line at 5% before, a dashed stage break, and a green line at 0.5% after, with "$15 million saved a year";
  - no invented samples, control limits or dates;
  - a note saying the lines are stage levels.
- **Colour carries meaning.** Red appears only on the before line. Green appears only on the after line, the Email me button and the contact email.
- **Type.** One self-hosted family, Archivo, replaces DM Sans and DM Serif Display. It uses the width axis, is left-aligned on a 12-column grid, and uses sentence case.
- **Theme.** Light "drafting film" paper (`#F2F4F3`) is now the default, with a complete dark theme. Going back to a dark default is a one-line change in `theme-init.js` and `script.js`.
- **Sections.** Results, Experience, What colleagues say, About (with Education), Outside work, Contact.
  - Experience keeps all 30 original bullets word for word; the key ones are shown and the rest sit in `<details>`.
  - All 8 recommendations are word for word. Each employer links to its recommenders, and each result links to its role.
  - The claims from the original project cards are kept in the Results lines.
- **Motion** (`d726513`, `691ea64`):
  - **One unprompted moment:** the chart draws itself once, as a sequence:
    1. the axes;
    2. the red 5% run;
    3. the dashed stage break and the drop;
    4. the green 0.5% run;
    5. the saving.

    On short screens it runs in two halves as the chart scrolls into view.
  - **Motion in response to visitor actions:**
    - expanding a role animates to its real height, with the +/− morph;
    - following a "Recommended by", Results or chart link draws a marker bar on the target;
    - the theme change wipes down from the nav;
    - a sliding nav indicator;
    - the mobile menu rows arrive in order;
    - press and focus states.
  - **Deliberately not added:** section fade-ins, card lifts, parallax and number counters. The frontend-design skill calls these the generic defaults.
  - Reduced motion, no-JS and print all show the finished state immediately. Nothing keeps animating after the page settles, and there is no layout shift.
- **Also updated:** the social card (`assets/og/`, `og-image.png`), `icon.svg` and `apple-touch-icon.png` are redrawn to match.
- **Unchanged:**
  - All old anchors still work (`#home #about #experience #projects #apps #education #testimonials #contact`).
  - The CSP is unchanged: no inline styles or scripts, and fonts are self-hosted.
  - Contact obfuscation still works.

## How it was made
Following the frontend-design skill:
1. Three independent design directions were drafted.
2. A judge panel chose one: a hiring manager, a design critic and a front-end engineer.
3. The chosen direction was built.
4. It went through three critique-and-fix rounds covering the skill's tells, visual design, and function, accessibility and content fidelity.
5. The motion pass then had its own plan, build and three critique rounds, judged from recorded animation frames.

## Verification (headless Chromium)
- No horizontal overflow from 320 to 1440px. No console or CSP errors.
- Checked and working:
  - nav clicks and highlighting (Contact included), Back, and direct hash links;
  - the theme cycle, including quick repeated presses;
  - the mobile menu with Escape;
  - print with every collapsed section expanded;
  - the no-JS view.
- WCAG AA contrast for text colour pairs in both themes.
- All 8 recommendations match the original site word for word.
- At 1440×900, the name, role, credential, Email me and the whole chart fit in the first screen. On a 390×844 phone, Email me fits in the first screen.
- Not tested: a physical iPhone, Safari or Firefox. The fallback for browsers without the View Transitions API (theme wipe) is untested there.

author: himynameisdave
body:
Rewrites the three rule docs in `docs/rules/` to match the layout of [eslint-plugin-unicorn's rule docs](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/main/docs/rules/comment-content.md).

Each doc now has:

- A `# rule-name` title.
- A 📝 description line (same as `meta.docs.description`).
- A ⚠️ line listing the presets that turn it on (`recommended`, `strict`, `all`), using eslint-doc-generator's default emoji for each.
- Plain paragraphs covering why, what gets reported, what's supported, and when not to use it. The Bun and Node API links now sit inside the text instead of a References list.
- An `## Examples` section with `// ❌` / `// ✅` pairs, including alias, namespace, `fs.promises` and CommonJS cases, plus one ✅-only case for an API the rule skips.

**Removed:**

- The "Options" section. None of the rules take options, and the header already shows the presets.
- The "Suggestions / autofix" section. Unicorn only adds a 🔧/💡 line when a rule can fix things, so leaving it out means "no fix". The reason there's no fix is now in the text.
- The "Bun compatibility" section. It was the same in every doc, and the README's Compatibility section already covers it.

**Not included:** the header is written by hand. Unicorn generates its header with `eslint-doc-generator`, but I didn't add that tool, so I also left out its "auto-generated, do not edit" comments.

**Testing:**

- Ran every example against the built plugin with ESLint: each ❌ block reports once and each ✅ block reports nothing.
- `bun run format:check` and `bun run lint` pass.
